items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Affine factorization of equal weight parameters
items.statement: In N67's setup, equality of the two expressions for omega holds iff wtilde(rhobar,tau)=w2^-1 s w1 for some finite Weyl s.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Extremal intersection is a single obvious weight
items.statement: Under N67's hypotheses, if wtilde(rhobar,tau)=t_(s^-1(lambda+eta)) for finite Weyl s, then W?(rhobar) intersect JH(sigma(tau)bar tensor W(lambda)) consists of exactly the obvious weight corresponding to s. In the proof the forced equality is w=w1, not the printed w=w2 (E5).
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Admissibility produces an obvious common weight
items.statement: Under N67's genericity and compatibility hypotheses, if wtilde(rhobar,tau) belongs to Adm(lambda+eta), then Wobv(rhobar) intersect JH(sigma(tau)bar tensor W(lambda)) is nonempty.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Herzig weights lie in one auxiliary tensor type
items.statement: For a3h_eta-generic chosen bartau presentation, take the eta-compatible Deligne–Lusztig representation R with wtilde(R)=wtilde(bartau)t_(-eta-w0 eta). Then W?(bartau) is contained in JH(Rbar tensor W(eta)); -eta-w0 eta is central.
items.note: Route owner: ModularRepresentationsOfFiniteReductiveGroups. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Universal Iwahori group scheme
items.statement: Over X=Spec Z[v], construct the smooth affine Bruhat–Tits group scheme G with connected fibres from cyclic n-tuples of invertible matrices satisfying D_i A_(i-1)=A_i D_i, where D_i has v in its ith diagonal position. If v maps to a regular element t in R, its R-points are the invertible matrices upper triangular modulo t. Use the tuple functor for arbitrary bases.
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Evaluate the same group scheme in shifted power-series and Laurent-series rings before forming the fpqc quotient.

uses.where: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII route brief in this packet
uses.how: Supply the integral GLn Iwahori carrier, rather than replacing it by a matrix subgroup on bases with v-torsion.

api.name: UniversalIwahori.of_tuple
api.statement: For n>=1 and a Z[v]-algebra R with v↦t, construct a point from a cyclic n-tuple A_i∈GL_n(R) satisfying D_i A_(i-1)=A_i D_i, with D_i the specified diagonal matrix.

api.name: UniversalIwahori.ext
api.statement: Two points are equal iff all their matrices A_i are equal; projection to A_0 alone is not asserted injective on arbitrary bases.

api.name: UniversalIwahori.mul_apply
api.statement: The i-th matrix of the product is A_i B_i; identity and inverse are computed componentwise.

api.name: UniversalIwahori.map
api.statement: Apply a Z[v]-algebra homomorphism to every matrix entry; preserve the relations, identity maps and compositions.

api.name: UniversalIwahori.matrix_equiv_of_regular
api.statement: When t is a non-zero-divisor, projection to A_0 gives the group equivalence with invertible matrices upper triangular modulo t.

api.name: UniversalIwahori.unit_parameter_equiv
api.statement: When t is a unit, the preceding matrix condition is vacuous and gives GL_n(R), with the other A_i recovered by the diagonal conjugations.

tests.name: UniversalIwahori.rank_one
tests.statement: For n=1 over any R, the tuple relation is automatic and UniversalIwahori(R)≃R×.

tests.name: UniversalIwahori.regular_lower_entry
tests.statement: Over R=Z[t] with v↦t and n=2, A_0=I+E_21 is not a point in the regular-parameter matrix description, since 1 is not divisible by t.

tests.name: UniversalIwahori.unit_parameter
tests.statement: Over Q with v↦1 and n=2, every A_0∈GL_2(Q) gives a unique point, and every matrix in its tuple equals A_0.

items.name: Universal positive and full loop groups
items.statement: At v->t in a Noetherian ring R, L+G(R)=G(R[[v-t]]) and LG(R)=G(R((v-t))), using the map that sends v to the formal variable v inside these rings. They are represented by a scheme and an ind-group scheme. For Noetherian R use matrices upper triangular modulo v; v is regular in these completed rings. T maps in by constant diagonal matrices, and determinant takes values in the Gm loop group.
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Use the positive subgroup inside the full loop group to define left cosets and prove uniqueness of factorization.
Use coefficientwise maps, determinant, and the exact shifted variable in chart and Frobenius-matrix constructions.

api.name: UniversalLoop.positive
api.statement: For q=v-t, evaluate U01 on R[[q]] via v↦q+t, not via v↦t; the full loop group uses R[[q]][q⁻¹] with the same map.

api.name: UniversalLoop.positive_to_full
api.statement: Localization at q gives a natural group homomorphism L+G(R)→LG(R); in the Noetherian matrix description it is injective.

api.name: UniversalLoop.matrix_mem
api.statement: For Noetherian R, membership means invertibility over the indicated series ring and vanishing of lower entries modulo v=q+t; the latter condition is not reduction modulo q unless t=0.

api.name: UniversalLoop.map
api.statement: A Z[v]-algebra map R→S induces coefficientwise maps, with the formal q variable sent to the target shifted variable, commuting with the positive-to-full map and with identity/composition.

api.name: UniversalLoop.constant_diagonal
api.statement: Map T(R) to L+G(R) by the constant diagonal matrix, compatibly with multiplication and coefficient maps.

api.name: UniversalLoop.det_mul
api.statement: Determinant is a natural group homomorphism LG→LG_m; on constant diagonal matrices it is the product of diagonal entries.

tests.name: UniversalLoop.special_full
tests.statement: For R=k a field, t=0, LG(k)=GL_n(k((v))) because v is invertible in the Laurent ring; L+G(k) is the standard upper-Iwahori subgroup.

tests.name: UniversalLoop.special_positive
tests.statement: For n=2,t=0, I+vE_21 belongs to L+G(k), whereas I+E_21 belongs to LG(k) but not L+G(k).

tests.name: UniversalLoop.unit_parameter_positive
tests.statement: For t∈R×, q+t is a unit in R[[q]], so L+G(R)=GL_n(R[[q]]) in the Noetherian setting.

items.name: Universal affine Grassmannian and bounded pieces
items.statement: The fpqc quotient L+G\LG is represented by an ind-projective X-ind-scheme Gr. Its fibre off v=0 is the GLn affine Grassmannian and at0 the standard Iwahori affine flag variety. LGdet=d requires det(A)=(v-t)^d times a power-series unit. L+M consists of matrices over R[[v-t]] upper triangular modulo v. Bound A by (v-t)^-h L+M, h>=0; its determinant-d quotient is projective over X and exhausts the determinant-d piece as h grows. Quotients of R-points inject into sheaf-quotient points, not necessarily surject.
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Bound the determinant component to obtain projective targets for finite-type open charts.
Provide the fpqc quotient in which differential and Schubert loci intersect.

api.name: UniversalGrassmannian.quotient
api.statement: Construct the fpqc sheaf quotient of LG by LEFT L+G translation, with quotient map q; descend any invariant morphism to an fpqc sheaf uniquely.

api.name: UniversalGrassmannian.coset_injective
api.statement: The natural map L+G(R)\LG(R)→Gr(R) is injective; no surjectivity for arbitrary R is part of this API.

api.name: UniversalGrassmannian.det_height_mem
api.statement: An LG representative A is in the (d,h) piece iff det A=q^d u with u∈R[[q]]× and q^h A∈L+M(R), where h>=0.

api.name: UniversalGrassmannian.bounded_inclusion
api.statement: For h<=h', multiplication by q^(h'-h) on the height condition gives compatible inclusions Gr^(d,<=h)→Gr^(d,<=h'); identity and composition hold.

api.name: UniversalGrassmannian.bounded_quotient
api.statement: The bounded piece is the fpqc quotient of its left-stable LG locus; it is projective over X and its filtered union is Gr^det=d.

api.name: UniversalGrassmannian.fiber_comparison
api.statement: The restriction to X0 is the GLn affine Grassmannian and the zero fibre is the standard affine flag variety, with the quotient maps identified.

tests.name: UniversalGrassmannian.rank_one_height
tests.statement: For n=1 over a field with t=0, Gr^(d,<=h) has its unique point [v^d] if d+h>=0 and is empty otherwise.

tests.name: UniversalGrassmannian.left_translate
tests.statement: For h∈L+G(R), the representatives A and hA have exactly the same image in Gr(R) and the same determinant/height membership.

tests.name: UniversalGrassmannian.determinant_component
tests.statement: Over a field with t=0, diag(v,1,...,1) is in determinant component 1, not component 0; multiplying by a positive loop cannot change that integer.

items.name: Negative loop subgroup
items.statement: L--G consists of invertible matrices polynomial in(v-t)^-1, lower unipotent at(v-t)^-1=0 and upper triangular modulo v/(v-t). The positive, full and negative loop groups are formally smooth over X in the source's Noetherian test-ring setting.
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Give the negative factor and its square-zero Lie module in the direct splitting.
Act on affine-element charts by left multiplication.

api.name: NegativeUniversalLoop.of_matrix
api.statement: For Noetherian R and q=v-t, construct a negative loop from an invertible matrix over R[q⁻¹] whose value at q⁻¹=0 is lower unipotent and whose lower entries vanish modulo v/q=1+t/q.

api.name: NegativeUniversalLoop.ext
api.statement: Two negative loops are equal iff their Laurent matrices, equivalently every polynomial coefficient, are equal.

api.name: NegativeUniversalLoop.group
api.statement: Identity, multiplication and inverse preserve both conditions; the inclusion into LG is a group homomorphism.

api.name: NegativeUniversalLoop.map
api.statement: Coefficient maps preserve the two conditions and commute with the inclusion into LG, identity and composition.

api.name: NegativeUniversalLoop.positive_intersection
api.statement: Use U05: an element simultaneously in L+G and L--G is the identity; this is a uniqueness assertion, not global factorization of LG.

api.name: NegativeUniversalLoop.chart_action
api.statement: Use U11 for the left L--G-action on U(z); trivialize only after choosing an actual chart point over the base in question.

tests.name: NegativeUniversalLoop.special_lower_constant
tests.statement: For n=2,t=0 over a field, I+cE_21 is a negative loop for every c, because v/q=1 and the value at q⁻¹=0 is lower unipotent.

tests.name: NegativeUniversalLoop.upper_constant
tests.statement: For n=2 over Q, I+E_12 is not a negative loop: its constant value is not lower triangular.

tests.name: NegativeUniversalLoop.nonzero_parameter_lower
tests.statement: For n=2,R=Q,t=1, I+(1+q⁻¹)E_21 is a negative loop, but I+E_21 is not, since the required lower-entry divisor is 1+q⁻¹.

items.name: Unique positive-negative factorization
items.statement: Multiplication L+G times_X L--G -> LG is a monomorphism. Consequently L--G -> Gr is a monomorphism. Proof uses intersections of nonnegative and strictly negative Laurent degrees and v-regularity.
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Square-zero loop Lie modules
items.statement: For R->S with square-zero kernel J, define Lie LG(J), Lie L+G(J), Lie L--G(J) by the corresponding matrix-entry and triangular conditions with coefficients J. M->1+M identifies these with the respective congruence kernels; conjugation factors through the S-valued group.
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Split and correct infinitesimal errors in positive-negative factorization.
Supply tangent vectors with the correct lower-entry divisibility and the adjoint action.

api.name: LoopSquareZeroLie.of_matrix
api.statement: For a Noetherian square-zero extension R→S with kernel J, construct each full/positive/negative Lie module from J-valued entries with exactly the corresponding support and triangular conditions.

api.name: LoopSquareZeroLie.congruence_equiv
api.statement: M↦I+M gives an additive-group equivalence with the kernel of the corresponding R-points→S-points map; its inverse is g↦g-I.

api.name: LoopSquareZeroLie.mul_eq_add
api.statement: For M,N with entries in J, (I+M)(I+N)=I+(M+N) and (I+M)⁻¹=I-M because J²=0.

api.name: LoopSquareZeroLie.adjoint_descends
api.statement: Conjugation of the kernel by an R-valued group element depends only on its image over S; use the S-module structure J=J/J².

api.name: LoopSquareZeroLie.split
api.statement: Use U07 to obtain unique negative and positive projections; their sum is the identity and both cross-composites vanish.

api.name: LoopSquareZeroLie.map_extension
api.statement: A commuting morphism of square-zero extensions maps Lie entries and congruence kernels compatibly; maps preserve identity, composition and the two projections.

tests.name: LoopSquareZeroLie.upper_split
tests.statement: For R=k[ε]/ε²,t=0,J=(ε), the Lie vector ε(v⁻¹+v)E_12 splits as negative εv⁻¹E_12 plus positive εvE_12.

tests.name: LoopSquareZeroLie.lower_split
tests.statement: For the same extension, ε(1+v)E_21 splits as negative εE_21 plus positive εvE_21; the lower-entry positive cutoff is degree 1, not 0.

tests.name: LoopSquareZeroLie.zero_kernel
tests.statement: For J=0 all three Lie modules and all three congruence kernels are trivial.

items.name: Positive-negative Lie splitting
items.statement: For a square-zero extension of Noetherian Z[v]-algebras with kernel J, Lie LG(J)=Lie L--G(J) direct-sum Lie L+G(J), using Laurent positive/negative decomposition separately in upper and v-divisible lower entries.
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Artinian formal etaleness at a point
items.statement: A morphism of functors on Noetherian rings is formally etale at x:Spec k->F in this section if every compatible Artinian local thickening Spec A->G with residue field k admits a unique lift to F. For representable locally finite-type morphisms with locally Noetherian target this implies etaleness; it is deliberately weaker than the unrestricted formal-lifting definition.
items.note: Route owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: State the unique lifting conclusion for the non-finite-type loop factorization functors.
Upgrade the lifting property for bounded finite-type charts, then combine with monomorphism for an open immersion.

api.name: ArtinianEtaleAt.iff_unique_lift
api.statement: At x∈F(k), require for every local Artinian A with identified residue field k and every y∈G(A) reducing to f(x), a unique z∈F(A) reducing to x with f(z)=y.

api.name: ArtinianEtaleAt.lift
api.statement: For such a compatible diagram, return its unique lift, its two compatibility equalities, and uniqueness.

api.name: ArtinianEtaleAt.iso_invariant
api.statement: Natural isomorphisms of source and target preserve the property at the transported point.

api.name: ArtinianEtaleAt.comp
api.statement: Compose lifts for F→G→H to obtain the unique lift at x when the two factors have the property at x and f(x).

api.name: ArtinianEtaleAt.base_change
api.statement: Pullback of a morphism with the property at x has it at every point lying over x, with the other fibre-product coordinate fixed.

api.name: ArtinianEtaleAt.of_formallyEtale
api.statement: For affine representable functors, unrestricted formal etaleness supplies this restricted property by iterated square-zero lifting. Reuse Algebra.FormallyEtale.comp_bijective and iff_comp_bijective at the pinned Mathlib commit, not a replacement definition of formal etaleness.

api.name: ArtinianEtaleAt.finite_type_upgrade
api.statement: For representable functors with locally Noetherian target and locally finite-type morphism, the property at all field-valued points implies etaleness, as in Remark3.2.5. No upgrade for arbitrary functors or from a lone field point is asserted.

tests.name: ArtinianEtaleAt.identity
tests.statement: The identity natural transformation on any functor has the property at every field-valued point; the unique lift is the supplied A-point.

tests.name: ArtinianEtaleAt.affine_line_fails
tests.statement: For A=k[ε]/ε², the projection A1_k→Spec k at the origin has distinct lifts x↦0 and x↦ε, so it fails the unique-lift property.

tests.name: ArtinianEtaleAt.open_lift
tests.statement: The open immersion Gm_k→A1_k has the property at x=1: any A-element reducing to 1 is a unit and has a unique lift to Gm(A).

items.name: Formal etaleness of loop factorization
items.statement: L+G times_X L--G -> LG and L--G -> Gr are formally etale in U08's sense. Lift across successive square-zero ideals using formal smoothness, then correct by U07; uniqueness comes from U05.
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Affine-element chart functor
items.statement: For z=w t_nu in the dual affine group, U(z) consists of A for which A(v-t)^-nu w^-1 is polynomial in(v-t)^-1 and lower unipotent modulo(v-t)^-1, and A(v-t)^-nu is upper triangular modulo v/(v-t). It is a subfunctor of LG. Its bounded determinant part intersects LGdet=sum(nu),<=h.
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Turn the two matrix conditions into a negative-loop torsor and finite-type coordinate equations.
Use bounded charts as open immersions and transport the extended-torus action.

api.name: AffineElementChart.of_matrix
api.statement: For z=w t_nu and q=v-t, construct A from A q^-nu w^-1∈GL_n(R[q⁻¹]) lower unipotent at q⁻¹=0, and A q^-nu upper triangular modulo v/q. Keep this order of w and q^-nu.

api.name: AffineElementChart.ext
api.statement: Chart points are equal exactly when their matrices are equal; the map to LG is a monomorphism.

api.name: AffineElementChart.map
api.statement: Coefficient maps preserve both conditions and the chart-to-LG map, with identity/composition laws.

api.name: AffineElementChart.bounded_coefficients
api.statement: Use U12 to identify the determinant/height-bounded chart with its displayed coefficient scheme, including empty nonpivot ranges and the determinant equation.

api.name: AffineElementChart.negative_torsor
api.statement: Use U11 for the left negative-loop action and uniqueness of the element carrying one chart point to another; an R-point must be supplied before identifying the torsor with L--G(R).

api.name: AffineElementChart.open_map
api.statement: Use U14 to identify the bounded chart as an open subfunctor of the matching bounded determinant component.

tests.name: AffineElementChart.identity_height_zero
tests.statement: For n=2,z=1,h=0, over any Noetherian Z[v]-algebra the bounded chart has the sole matrix I; both off-diagonal coefficient ranges are empty.

tests.name: AffineElementChart.swap_height_zero
tests.statement: For n=2,w=(12),nu=(0,0),h=0, the bounded chart is empty over a nonzero ring: its (2,1) pivot would require exponent -1 outside the range.

tests.name: AffineElementChart.special_swap_section
tests.statement: For n=2,t=0,w=(12),nu=(1,0),h=0, the matrix [[0,1],[v,0]] belongs to the chart and has determinant -v.

items.name: Chart torsor and formal etaleness
items.statement: Left multiplication makes U(z) an L--G torsor, and U(z)->Gr is a formally etale monomorphism. Point sets may be empty over a given base; no global trivialization is presumed.
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Explicit bounded chart equations
items.statement: For Noetherian R, A in U(w t_nu)det,<=h has A_ij=v^[i>j] sum_(k=-h)^(nu_j-[i>j]-[i<w(j)]) c_(ij,k)(v-t)^k, pivot c_(w(j)j,nu_j-[w(j)>j])=1, and det A=det(w)(v-t)^sum(nu). Empty coefficient ranges contribute zero. These equations represent the chart by a finite-type affine scheme. Do not impose a nonemptiness inequality on every nonpivot entry: the sentence following the proposition is too strong (source issue E7).
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Distinguished chart section
items.statement: For a nonempty bounded chart, its v=0 fibre has a section over Z represented by w v^nu. Distinguish this section from a choice of an arbitrary matrix representative over nonzero v.
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Identify the contracting fixed section and the precise point whose branch is tested.
Form products of the special-fibre sections; require the section to meet the local model.

api.name: DistinguishedChartSection.of_nonempty
api.statement: For a nonempty bounded z=w t_nu chart, construct the zero-fibre section over Spec Z represented by w v^nu.

api.name: DistinguishedChartSection.matrix
api.statement: For a Noetherian ring R with t=0 the section has (i,j) entry δ_(i,w(j)) v^nu_j and determinant det(w)v^sum(nu).

api.name: DistinguishedChartSection.map
api.statement: The section commutes with coefficient change along Z→R→S and with inclusions into larger height bounds.

api.name: DistinguishedChartSection.grassmannian_image
api.statement: Its image is the affine flag point [w v^nu] under U03's zero-fibre comparison; no representative with nonzero t is chosen by this definition.

api.name: DistinguishedChartSection.model_membership
api.statement: A distinguished point of a local model exists precisely when this ambient section factors through that closed model after the chosen parameter specialization; membership is additional data, not automatic.

api.name: DistinguishedChartSection.fixed
api.statement: Use U28: the contracting action on a nonempty bounded chart has this section as its fixed subscheme.

tests.name: DistinguishedChartSection.identity
tests.statement: For z=1,n=2,h=0 the section is I in the unique-point chart over the zero fibre.

tests.name: DistinguishedChartSection.swap
tests.statement: For w=(12),nu=(1,0),h=0 the section is [[0,1],[v,0]], not diag(v,1)w.

tests.name: DistinguishedChartSection.base_change
tests.statement: Reducing the integral section for w=(12),nu=(1,0) to any field gives the same two displayed monomial entries and no new choice of representative.

items.name: Bounded charts are open
items.statement: U(z)det,<=h -> Grdet=sum(nu),<=h is an open immersion, via finite type plus formal etaleness and monomorphism.
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Universal differential condition
items.statement: LGnabla is the subfunctor of LG times An of pairs(g,a) with v g' g^-1 + Ad(g)Diag(a) in(v-t)^-1 L+M. Its left L+G invariance makes the quotient a closed sub-ind-scheme Grnabla of Gr times An, ind-proper over X times An. A common scalar shift of all coordinates of a yields the isomorphism in Remark3.3.2 with the hyperplane a_n=0 times A1.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Descend the matrix differential condition to the LEFT quotient before intersecting Schubert varieties.
Use the exact simple-pole equation in flag coordinates and remove the common scalar parameter without changing the locus.

api.name: UniversalDifferentialLocus.expression
api.statement: For q=v-t, set Φ_a(g)=v(dg/dv)g⁻¹+g Diag(a)g⁻¹, differentiating with coefficients of R and t constant.

api.name: UniversalDifferentialLocus.mem_iff
api.statement: A pair (g,a) lies in LG∇ iff q Φ_a(g) belongs to L+M(R), including its lower-entry divisibility by v.

api.name: UniversalDifferentialLocus.left_translate
api.statement: Use the corrected U16 identity Φ_a(hg)=v h'h⁻¹+Ad(h)(Φ_a(g)) for h∈L+G; the integral derivative assertion is v h'∈L+M, not h'∈L+M.

api.name: UniversalDifferentialLocus.quotient
api.statement: The invariant condition descends to the closed sub-ind-scheme Gr∇ of Gr×An; a local representative satisfying it gives a point independently of positive-loop trivialization.

api.name: UniversalDifferentialLocus.scalar_shift
api.statement: For n>=1, (g,a)↦(g,a-a_n(1,...,1),a_n) identifies LG∇ with its a_n=0 slice times A1, with inverse adding the scalar; the same comparison descends to Gr∇.

api.name: UniversalDifferentialLocus.map
api.statement: Coefficient change commutes with the formal derivative, Φ, the closed condition, and the quotient maps; preserve identity and composition.

tests.name: UniversalDifferentialLocus.rank_one_monomial
tests.statement: For n=1,g=q^m,m∈Z, Φ_a(g)=m v/q+a and qΦ_a(g)=m v+a q∈R[[q]], so every such pair satisfies the condition.

tests.name: UniversalDifferentialLocus.lower_derivative
tests.statement: For n=2,R=Q,t=0,h=I+vE_21, h'=E_21 is not in L+M but v h'=vE_21 is; Φ_0(h)=vE_21.

tests.name: UniversalDifferentialLocus.common_scalar
tests.statement: For g=I in rank n, Φ_(a+c1)(I)-Φ_a(I)=cI and multiplication by q puts that difference in L+M; scalar shift cannot change membership.

items.name: Descent of the differential condition
items.statement: For h in L+G, v(hg)'(hg)^-1+Ad(hg)D=v h'h^-1+Ad(h)(v g'g^-1+Ad(g)D), which lies in(v-t)^-1 L+M whenever the original expression does. The printed calculation and claim h' in L+M are corrected in E12; the integral term is v h'.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Global Schubert variety and orbit projection
items.statement: s_lambda is represented by(v-t)^lambda. SX(lambda) is the irreducible closed right-L+G-stable orbit closure; its open stratum excludes smaller dominant weights in the Weyl polytope. Off v=0, the orbit quotient L+G_lambda\L+G identifies with this stratum and maps to P_lambda\GLn by reduction modulo(v-t); the map is an iterated affine-space bundle. P_lambda has vanishing root entries where <lambda,alpha^vee><0.
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Select the lambda Schubert bound and project the generic open orbit to the correct LEFT parabolic quotient.

uses.where: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII route brief in this packet
uses.how: Keep the underlying Schubert/orbit geometry separate from differential equations and their closure.

api.name: GlobalSchubertOrbit.section
api.statement: Construct s_lambda by the diagonal matrix q^lambda, q=v-t; form the scheme-theoretic right-positive-orbit closure S_X(lambda).

api.name: GlobalSchubertOrbit.stabilizer
api.statement: The right stabilizer of s_lambda is L+G∩Ad(q^-lambda)(L+G); the orbit map is from L+G_lambda\L+G, not the reversed quotient.

api.name: GlobalSchubertOrbit.open_stratum
api.statement: Remove the smaller Schubert loci indexed by integral weights in Conv(lambda) outside W lambda to obtain S_X°(lambda).

api.name: GlobalSchubertOrbit.generic_orbit
api.statement: Over X0 the orbit quotient is S_X0°(lambda), and S_X0(lambda) is the constant usual GLn Schubert family. Weyl-conjugate weights give the same generic Schubert variety.

api.name: GlobalSchubertOrbit.flag_projection
api.statement: Over X0 send the class of g to its reduction modulo q in P_lambda\GLn, where root entries of P_lambda vanish when <lambda,alpha∨><0; prove independence from the stabilizer representative.

api.name: GlobalSchubertOrbit.affine_bundle
api.statement: The flag projection is an iterated affine-space bundle, with affine root coordinates as in the proof of U19. Do not call it an isomorphism until the differential equations of U19 are imposed.

tests.name: GlobalSchubertOrbit.zero_weight
tests.statement: For lambda=0, the Schubert orbit is the identity section, its stabilizer is L+G, P_lambda=GLn and the generic flag quotient is a point.

tests.name: GlobalSchubertOrbit.GL2_minuscule
tests.statement: For lambda=(1,0) in GL2 over a field on X0, P_lambda is the upper Borel, the flag quotient is P1, and the open Schubert orbit projects isomorphically to it.

tests.name: GlobalSchubertOrbit.GL2_nonminuscule
tests.statement: For lambda=(2,0) in GL2 over Q on X0, the open Schubert orbit has dimension 2 whereas P_lambda\GL2 has dimension 1; the orbit projection before imposing ∇ is not an isomorphism.

items.name: Naive universal local model
items.statement: Mnv_X(<=lambda,nabla)=Grnabla intersect(SX(lambda) times An). Its chart Unv(z,<=lambda,nabla) is the intersection with U(z) times An, equal to the sufficiently bounded-chart intersection.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Use the actual scheme-theoretic intersection for flag comparison, smoothness and a finite chart presentation in Elkik lifting.
Provide the ambient model in which the top generic differential component is closed.

api.name: NaiveUniversalModel.intersection
api.statement: Define Mnv_X(<=lambda,∇) as the fibre product of the closed Gr∇ locus and S_X(lambda)×An over Gr×An, with both projections.

api.name: NaiveUniversalModel.lift
api.statement: A test-scheme morphism to the ambient factors through Mnv exactly when it factors through both closed loci; the factorization is unique.

api.name: NaiveUniversalModel.chart
api.statement: Pull back the open chart U(z)×An to Mnv; for h sufficiently large to contain the Schubert bound this agrees with the bounded-chart intersection.

api.name: NaiveUniversalModel.base_change
api.statement: The scheme-theoretic intersection and its chart commute with base change, including non-flat coefficient specialization, as fibre products; this assertion is not made for U21's closure.

api.name: NaiveUniversalModel.proper
api.statement: Mnv is proper over X×An because the differential condition is closed in the proper Schubert bound; the chart is affine of finite type with the induced equations.

api.name: NaiveUniversalModel.generic_flag
api.statement: Use U19 only on the top open stratum over X0 after inverting h_lambda!, and U23 for smoothness of the whole generic naive model after inverting (2h_lambda)!.

tests.name: NaiveUniversalModel.zero_weight
tests.statement: For lambda=0 the model is X×An: its only Grassmannian coordinate is the identity and Φ_a(I)=Diag(a) satisfies the condition.

tests.name: NaiveUniversalModel.rank_one
tests.statement: For n=1 and lambda=(m), the Schubert bound is the section q^m; the naive model is X×A1 since m v+a q has no pole.

tests.name: NaiveUniversalModel.intersection_not_union
tests.statement: For any test scheme T, a T-point of Mnv is a Grassmannian point together with both compatible Schubert and differential factorizations, not a choice of one of them.

items.name: Open differential stratum is a flag variety
items.statement: For dominant lambda, after inverting h_lambda!, the orbit projection identifies Mnv_X0 intersect(Sopen_X0(lambda) times An) with(P_lambda\GLn) times X0 times An. The triangular recursion solves positive Laurent coefficients from constant coefficients using invertibility of t and integers1,...,h_lambda.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Reduced generic universal decomposition
items.statement: After inverting h_lambda!, the reduced Mnv_X0(<=lambda,nabla) is the disjoint union of(P_lambda'\GLn) times X0 times An for dominant lambda'<=lambda. Keep the localization; the proof removes each open proper component successively.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Universal local model as a closure
items.locator: Definition3.3.6, PDF65; the introduction's Definition 1.4.1 (PDF 9) is its specialization at a
items.statement: MX(lambda,nabla) is the closure of the lambda open differential stratum over X0 inside the naive universal model (equivalently inside Gr times An). Imposing the differential equation before closure differs from imposing it after closure. A later flatness/base-change argument is needed to identify specializations with closures formed after specializing.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Compare closure before and after parameter specialization without assuming that the operations commute.
Supply the horizontal closure used in generic-flatness and product-specialization arguments.

api.name: UniversalClosureModel.closure
api.statement: Take the scheme-theoretic closure of Mnv_X0∩(S_X0°(lambda)×An) in Mnv_X; retain the closed immersion into the naive model.

api.name: UniversalClosureModel.minimal
api.statement: Any closed subscheme of the ambient through which the top generic differential stratum factors contains this closure scheme-theoretically.

api.name: UniversalClosureModel.affine_contraction
api.statement: On an affine open Spec B, if I0⊂B[1/v] defines the restricted generic stratum, the closure ideal is the inverse image of I0 under B→B[1/v].

api.name: UniversalClosureModel.parameter_regular
api.statement: Multiplication by v is injective on each affine coordinate ring of this closure, since that ring injects into its localization. This alone does not assert flatness over all the additional parameters.

api.name: UniversalClosureModel.generic_comparison
api.statement: Restriction back to X0 recovers the top generic component in the factorial-localized setting of U19/U20; no other generic naive component is added.

api.name: UniversalClosureModel.specialization_map
api.statement: After specialization at a field-valued parameter, the closure formed after specialization maps by a closed immersion to the specialized universal closure; equality requires the additional flatness/comparison input used in U31.

tests.name: UniversalClosureModel.zero_weight
tests.statement: For lambda=0, closing X0×An inside X×An gives X×An, so universal and naive models coincide.

tests.name: UniversalClosureModel.saturation
tests.statement: For B=k[v,x] and generic ideal (x)⊂B[1/v], the closure ideal is (x); using (v x) instead introduces an unwanted vertical component.

tests.name: UniversalClosureModel.closure_specialization_failure
tests.statement: For Y=Spec k[a,v,x]/(a x-v), the closure of Y|D(v) is Y. At a=0, its fibre is Spec k[x] supported at v=0, whereas the closure of (Y|D(v)) at a=0 is empty. This is a test of the closure operation, not an asserted counterexample among LLHLM local models.

items.name: Torus fixed points of global Schubert varieties
items.statement: Over X0 the torus-fixed subscheme of SX(lambda) is supported on sections s_mu for integral mu in the Weyl polytope Conv(lambda); this is a support assertion, not an assertion that the fixed scheme is reduced.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Generic universal naive model is smooth
items.statement: For dominant lambda, Mnv_X0(<=lambda,nabla) becomes smooth over X0 times An after inverting(2h_lambda)!. Proof reduces to torus-fixed points by properness of the non-smooth locus, then bounds diagonal and root tangent coefficients by the displayed recursion. Combined with U20 it removes the reduction qualification in that decomposition after this stronger localization.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Elkik lifting for a fixed chart presentation
items.statement: Fix lambda,z and a finite presentation of Unv(z,<=lambda,nabla)[1/(2h_lambda)!] over X times An. There are N>2r and r depending on the presentation such that, for any t-adically complete t-torsion-free ring A with a base map v->t, every compatible A/t^m point with m>=N lifts to an A point agreeing modulo t^(m-r). No uniqueness or agreement modulo t^m is claimed; torsionfreeness supplies the non-Noetherian I=A specialization of Elkik used here.
items.note: Route owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.
proofSteps: Choose r from the universal conductor-weighted Jacobian identity, before any test-ring base change.
Use completeness to absorb the approximate-equation error into a unit and obtain t^r∈H_B(a).
Apply the non-Noetherian torsionfree specialization Z06 with N=2r+1. The corrected point agrees modulo t^(m−r), not necessarily t^m.
Elkik's original lemma has standing Noetherian hypotheses; Z06 provides the actual adaptation required by this statement.

items.name: Equal-characteristic closure model
items.statement: For a field k with(2h_lambda)! invertible and a in k^n, first specialize the naive family at a and then take the closure of its lambda flag component over X0_k; call this M(lambda,nabla_a). It is flat over A1_k. The map to MX(lambda,nabla) specialized at a is an isomorphism over X0, but need not be an isomorphism on the whole fibre without a generic-base-change argument.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Work with the closure formed after fixing a, so the family is flat over A1_k before using contraction.
Supply the canonical comparison to a universal-model specialization, with both required flatness hypotheses visible.

api.name: EqualCharacteristicClosure.of_parameter
api.statement: For k a field with (2h_lambda)! invertible and a∈k^n, close the top flag component over X0_k in the specialized naive model.

api.name: EqualCharacteristicClosure.generic_flag
api.statement: Over X0_k this closure is (P_lambda\GLn)×X0_k via U19; this identification is fixed before taking the closure.

api.name: EqualCharacteristicClosure.torsion_free
api.statement: On each affine chart its ring embeds into its v-localization, which is flat over k[v,v⁻¹] by the generic flag description. Consequently the chart ring is torsion-free over k[v], so the model is flat over A1_k.

api.name: EqualCharacteristicClosure.comparison
api.statement: Construct the closed immersion into MX(lambda,∇) specialized at a, compatible with the identity on the generic flag component; do not assert it is globally an isomorphism for arbitrary a.

api.name: EqualCharacteristicClosure.chart
api.statement: Pull back U(z) to the equal-characteristic closure. Distinguished points require an actual factorization of the ambient section through this model.

api.name: EqualCharacteristicClosure.power_base_change
api.statement: For e>0 construct the base change along v↦v^e and the inherited distinguished point; use U30, not a general preservation claim, for its unibranchness.

tests.name: EqualCharacteristicClosure.zero_weight
tests.statement: For lambda=0 and any allowed a, the equal-characteristic model is A1_k and its comparison with the universal specialization is an isomorphism.

tests.name: EqualCharacteristicClosure.rank_one
tests.statement: For n=1,lambda=(m), after fixing a the model is A1_k with generic representative (v-t)^m; every e-power base change is again A1_k.

tests.name: EqualCharacteristicClosure.discard_vertical_torsion
tests.statement: The affine closure helper applied to B=k[v,x]/(v x) with its entire D(v) locus returns B/ker(B→B[1/v])≃k[v]. Thus x, killed by v, is removed before the flat-family conclusion.

items.name: Unibranch points and normalization
items.statement: A point y is unibranch when the normalization of the reduced local ring is local. Under finite normalization its fibre is then a single point, equivalently connected. For a REDUCED excellent Noetherian local ring, unibranchness is equivalent to its completion being a domain. The printed remark omits reducedness (source issue E9); dual numbers show why it is necessary.
items.note: Route owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Pass from a connected finite normalization fibre to a unibranch point.

uses.where: LLHLM23 Theorem3.7.1 and existing source finding E9
uses.how: Use completed-local-domain conclusions only with reduced excellence, never discard nilpotents silently.

api.name: UnibranchLocalPoint.iff_normalization_local
api.statement: For a nonzero local ring A in the finite-component setting, unibranch means that A_red has one minimal prime and its integral closure in its fraction field is local; equivalently the normalization of the reduction is local.

api.name: UnibranchLocalPoint.reduction
api.statement: Unibranchness of A is equivalent to that of A_red; it is not a reducedness predicate.

api.name: UnibranchLocalPoint.finite_fiber
api.statement: When normalization is finite, a point is unibranch iff its set-theoretic normalization fibre is a single point, equivalently connected.

api.name: UnibranchLocalPoint.completion_domain
api.statement: For a REDUCED excellent Noetherian local ring A, A is unibranch iff its maximal-ideal completion is a domain. Use U26/E9's corrected hypothesis.

api.name: UnibranchLocalPoint.local_iso
api.statement: A local-ring isomorphism identifies reductions, normalizations and the unibranch predicate; transport is compatible with identity and composition.

api.name: UnibranchLocalPoint.geometric_distinction
api.statement: Geometric unibranchness additionally requires the normalization residue extension to be purely inseparable. Do not identify it with ordinary unibranchness or infer arbitrary field-base-change stability from the latter.

tests.name: UnibranchLocalPoint.normal_local
tests.statement: For a field k, k[[x]] is a normal local domain, is unibranch, and its completion is itself.

tests.name: UnibranchLocalPoint.dual_numbers
tests.statement: For A=k[ε]/ε², A_red=k and its normalization is local, so A is unibranch; A is already complete but not a domain.

tests.name: UnibranchLocalPoint.node
tests.statement: For A=(k[x,y]/(xy))_(x,y), normalization of the reduction has two points above the closed point; A is not unibranch and its completion k[[x,y]]/(xy) is not a domain.

items.name: Extended torus and chart action
items.statement: Tdual times Gm acts on the universal Grassmannian by right diagonal multiplication and loop rotation v->r^-1v, with the induced scaling of t. On the z=w t_nu chart use (D,r)A=Ad(w)(D^-1) A(r^-1v) r^nu D. It preserves the chart and its bounded pieces. The chart-to-Gr map is equivariant for the original target action precomposed by theta_nu(D,r)=(r^nu D,r), not in general for the untwisted action (E43). In the chart-preservation calculation r^nu(v-rt)^-nu=(r^-1v-t)^-nu; the final right-hand exponents in both printed identities need minus signs (E44). The chart action and the corrected contracting weights of U28 are unchanged.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Calculate the corrected positive coordinate weights and contract to the distinguished section.
Transport the action through power base change while tracking the common base parameter.

api.name: ExtendedTorusChartAction.act
api.statement: For z=w t_nu, D diagonal and r∈R×, send A(v) over parameter t to Ad(w)(D⁻¹) A(r⁻¹v) r^nu D over parameter r t.

api.name: ExtendedTorusChartAction.one_mul
api.statement: The identity pair acts identically and successive actions compose by multiplication in T∨×Gm; include the induced scaling of the base t in this statement.

api.name: ExtendedTorusChartAction.chart_preserved
api.statement: The matrix conditions preserve U(z) and every bounded subchart. The chart-to-Gr map is equivariant for the original target action precomposed by θ_nu(D,r)=(r^nu D,r); it is not generally equivariant for the original action with unchanged (D,r). See E43.

api.name: ExtendedTorusChartAction.map
api.statement: Coefficient maps carry the action to the action of the images of D and r, with identity and composition laws.

api.name: ExtendedTorusChartAction.coefficient_weight
api.statement: For the cocharacter r↦(Ad(w⁻¹)(r^mu),r^N), the coefficient c_(ij,k) in U12 scales by r^[N(nu_j-[i>j]-k)+mu_(w(j))-mu_i], and t scales by r^N; this is the corrected E8 convention.

api.name: ExtendedTorusChartAction.contracting
api.statement: Use U28: for regular dominant mu and N>h_mu, pivots have weight zero, every nonpivot coefficient has positive weight and t has positive weight, giving the A1-monoid extension and its fixed section.

api.name: ExtendedTorusChartAction.scaled_inverse
api.statement: In the chart-preservation calculation r^nu(v-rt)^-nu=(r⁻¹v-t)^-nu. Both occurrences of the exponent on the final right-hand sides in Lemma3.4.6's proof must be -nu, as recorded in E44.

tests.name: ExtendedTorusChartAction.identity_pair
tests.statement: With D=I and r=1 the matrix and its base parameter t are unchanged.

tests.name: ExtendedTorusChartAction.section_fixed
tests.statement: At t=0, Ad(w)(D⁻¹) w(r⁻¹v)^nu r^nu D=w v^nu, so the distinguished section is fixed for every D,r.

tests.name: ExtendedTorusChartAction.GL2_corrected_weight
tests.statement: For w=1,nu=(0,0),mu=(1,0),N=2,t=0, the chart matrix I+cE_21 transforms to I+r cE_21. The nonpivot coefficient has weight +1, not -1.

tests.name: ExtendedTorusChartAction.twisted_equivariance
tests.statement: Over Q,t=0,w=1,nu=(1,0), take A=[[v,v⁻¹],[0,1]],D=I,r=2. The chart action yields C=[[v,2v⁻¹],[0,1]], whereas the original target rotation yields B=[[v/2,2v⁻¹],[0,1]]. Since CB⁻¹=[[2,-2v⁻¹],[0,1]] is not positive, their left cosets differ. Rotation followed by right diag(2,1), i.e. θ_nu, yields C.

items.name: Contracting chart action
items.statement: Choose regular dominant mu and N>h_mu. The one-parameter subgroup r->(Ad(w^-1)(r^mu),r^N) gives a contracting action on every bounded z chart and has distinguished section z as its fixed subscheme when nonempty. Direct substitution in U27 gives coefficient weight N(nu_j-[i>j]-k)+mu_(w(j))-mu_i. The proof prints the opposite mu-signs (source issue E8); with the corrected weights all nonpivot variables have positive weight.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Contraction gives a unibranch vertex
items.statement: For an irreducible variety M over an algebraically closed field with an A1 multiplicative-monoid action whose unique Gm-fixed point is x, M is unibranch at x and its completed local ring is a domain. Normalize, lift the action, and use the0-action map to show the finite normalization fibre is connected. Reducedness comes from the variety hypothesis.
items.note: Route owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Equal-characteristic unibranchness after power base change
items.statement: Under U25's hypotheses, if z_k lies in M(lambda,nabla_a), then for every integer e>0 its base change under v->v^e is unibranch at z_k. The preimage of the z chart in the normalization's v=0 fibre is connected. The contraction lifts after composing its scaling cocharacter with the e-power map.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Normalization fibres in a flat family
items.statement: For the universal family restricted to U in An and its e-power base change, assume both M_U and the normalization of M_U,e in its X0 part are flat over X times U. At a geometric special-fibre point in a distinguished z section, the normalization fibre is supported at one point; the normalization preimage of the z chart in that fibre is connected. Both flatness hypotheses are retained.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Flatness across a principal divisor
items.statement: For an A[v]-algebra B, if v is regular in B, B[1/v] is flat over A[v,1/v], and B/v is flat over A, then B is flat over A[v], in the local-criterion setting used by the finite-presentation family. Before stating this for unrestricted B, audit the cited local flatness criterion's finiteness hypotheses.
items.note: Route owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Generic flatness of the universal family after shrinking the base
items.statement: Lemma 3.5.5. Assume Setup 3.5.1: X = A^1 = Spec Z[v] with zero section 0 : Spec Z → X and X^0 = Spec Z[v, 1/v]; S is an integral finite type Z-scheme whose generic point has characteristic 0; M → X × S is a finitely presented map such that the base changed family M^0 = M ×_X X^0 → X^0 × S is smooth, M is the Zariski closure of M^0 (in particular v ∈ O(M) is a regular element), and M is normal. Then there is a non-empty open subscheme U ⊂ S such that the base change M ×_{X×S} (X × U) → X × U is flat. Proof (PDF74): v is regular in M. Let M_0 be the S-scheme M ×_X {0}. Since S is integral, generic flatness ([75, Tag 0529]) gives a non-empty open U ⊂ S such that M_0 ×_S U is flat over U. M^0 → X^0 × S is smooth, hence flat. Conclude by Lemma 3.5.4 (U32).
items.note: Route owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Generic flatness under weaker hypotheses than Setup 3.5.1
items.statement: Remark 3.5.6. The proof of Lemma 3.5.5 shows that the lemma holds under much less restrictive conditions than Setup 3.5.1. One only needs a finitely presented map M → X × S (X = A^1 = Spec Z[v], X^0 = Spec Z[v, 1/v]) such that S is integral, v is regular in M, and M^0 = M ×_X X^0 → X^0 × S is flat. Then there is a non-empty open subscheme U ⊂ S such that M ×_{X×S} (X × U) → X × U is flat.
items.note: Split from U33. The argument is the proof of Lemma 3.5.5 word for word. It uses generic flatness of M_0 = M ×_X {0} over the integral S ([75, Tag 0529]), the flatness of M^0 over X^0 × S (now a hypothesis), and Lemma 3.5.4 (U32). Lemma 3.5.4 applies the local flatness criterion ([75, Tag 00MD]) to Noetherian local rings, which is why U32 asks for an audit of its finiteness hypotheses. In both applications S is an integral scheme of finite type over Z (a non-empty open of the base in Theorem 3.7.1, and A^{n,J} over Z in Theorem 7.3.2), so the Noetherian case is enough. E85 already uses Lemma 3.5.5 with this remark to correct the cross-reference in Remark 3.4.1.

uses.how: Theorem 3.7.1 proof, PDF78: "the first item can be arranged by Remark 3.5.6". After shrinking to a non-empty open S_j, M_j ×_{X×S} (X × S_j) → X × S_j is flat.

Theorem 7.3.2(2) proof, PDF154: Remark 3.5.6 is applied to M_{X,J}(λ′,∇) → X × A^{n,J} to make its base change along (−p, a_τ) O-flat for each λ′, so that M(λ′,∇_{a_τ}) is that base change (first bulleted property).

items.name: Geometrically S1 special fibres after shrinking
items.statement: In Setup3.5.1 (S integral finite type with characteristic-zero generic point, M finitely presented, normal, closure of its smooth X0 part), additionally assume flatness over X times S. After shrinking S nontrivially, the v=0 fibres are geometrically S1. First spread geometric normality of M's generic fibre over S; quotient by the regular element v.
items.note: Route owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Codimension-one regularity under uniformizer specialization
items.statement: In Setup3.5.1 with flatness, there is a nonempty etale U->S such that a DVR map Spec R->X times U sending v to a uniformizer yields an R1 base change M_R. Spread geometric integrality of special components and their principal generators in height-one localizations; the displayed base arrows in the printed statement need correction to X times U and Spec R.
items.note: Route owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Normality spreads to generic DVR specializations
items.statement: In Setup3.5.1 there is a nonempty open U in S such that for every complete DVR R and map Spec R->X times U sending v to a UNIFORMIZER, M_R is flat over R and normal. Combine U33,U34,U35 and Serre R1+S2. In the proof, an etale lift may require a faithfully flat unramified DVR extension; completeness alone does not supply a residue-field point. Normality then descends. The unrestricted higher-valuation claim is false, as x^2-v with v->varpi^2 shows.
items.note: Route owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Quasi-finite horizontal subscheme through a section
items.statement: Let M->X times S be flat finite type between finite-type Z-schemes, with S irreducible and characteristic-zero generic point, and s:S->M0 a section. There is a nonempty open U in S and a closed Z in M restricted over X times U, flat and quasi-finite over X times U, containing s restricted to U. The proof needs a horizontal curve through the generic section point, then spreading and generic flatness.
items.note: Route owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Uniform bounded-extension lift of a section
items.statement: Under U37's hypotheses there are e and nonempty open U such that for any complete DVR R mapping to X times U with v of positive valuation, the point induced by s lifts after a finite DVR extension R'/R of degree<=e. Use the finite flat connected piece of the quasi-finite horizontal subscheme and normalize it.
items.note: Route owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Product universal local model
items.statement: For finite J and dominant tuple lambda, take the product over the common X of MX(lambda_j,nabla), with parameters in(An)^J. Distinguished sections and charts are products indexed by z in Wtilde-dual^J. The shared X coordinate is not duplicated into independent deformation parameters.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Keep a single ramification parameter v while allowing a separate coefficient tuple a_j in each factor.
Distinguish the finite scheme fibre product from its later completed local and adic tensor-product constructions.

api.name: ProductUniversalModel.of_factors
api.statement: For finite J form the fibre product over X of the models MX(lambda_j,∇), with structure map to X×(An)^J and projections to each factor.

api.name: ProductUniversalModel.lift
api.statement: For a test scheme T→X, compatible T→MX(lambda_j,∇) maps with this same map to X give a unique T→product; the coefficient maps a_j may differ.

api.name: ProductUniversalModel.ext
api.statement: Two maps into the product are equal iff their composites with all factor projections are equal.

api.name: ProductUniversalModel.reindex
api.statement: A bijection of finite index sets gives the canonical product isomorphism after transporting lambda and parameter tuples; identity and composition agree.

api.name: ProductUniversalModel.base_change
api.statement: Base change along a single Spec R→X×(An)^J identifies the result with the product over R of the correspondingly specialized factors; the same image of v is used in each.

api.name: ProductUniversalModel.charts_sections
api.statement: Products of the open factor charts give the product chart; ambient distinguished sections are componentwise, and factor through the product model exactly when all factors meet their individual models.

tests.name: ProductUniversalModel.empty_product
tests.statement: For J empty the product in X-schemes is X, with parameter space (An)^empty=Spec Z; it is not an extra copy of Spec Z as a total space.

tests.name: ProductUniversalModel.singleton
tests.statement: For a singleton J the product is canonically the original MX(lambda,∇), with its chart and projection unchanged.

tests.name: ProductUniversalModel.shared_parameter
tests.statement: For two affine factor charts Spec B1 and Spec B2, the product ring is B1⊗_(Z[v])B2 and satisfies v⊗1=1⊗v. The independent-parameter tensor product over Z is not the prescribed construction.

items.name: Uniform unibranchness for product specializations
items.locator: Theorem3.7.1, PDF77–80; stated in the introduction as Theorem 1.4.2 (PDF 10)
items.statement: Fix e>0, n and a finite set of dominant cocharacters. There is a nonempty open U in An depending only on this set,e,n such that, for every finite tuple drawn from the set, complete DVR R and map Spec R->X times U^J sending v to an element of positive valuation<=e, the specialized product model is R-flat and unibranch at each special-fibre point on a distinguished section z. The v-unit case has no such special distinguished points.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Integral adic chart domain for product models
items.statement: Under U40's hypotheses, for a distinguished section z meeting the special fibre, the maximal-ideal-of-R-adic completion of the coordinate ring of its chart in the specialized product is a domain. This is completion of the whole affine chart along the base ideal, not merely its completed local ring at z.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Normalization connectivity controls adic completion
items.statement: For a complete DVR R and finite-type flat R-algebra A with A[1/varpi] a regular domain, if Spec(A^normal/varpi) is connected, then the varpi-adic completion of A is a domain. Finiteness of normalization and excellence give an injection into a normal completed algebra; any nontrivial idempotent there would survive reduction, contradicting connectedness.
items.note: Route owner: DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.
proofSteps: Finite normalization and exact completion give an injection into the normal complete ring B.
If B is not a domain, normal Noetherian component decomposition gives a nontrivial idempotent in B[1/π]. Integrality of an idempotent and normality put it in B.
An idempotent in πB belongs to all π^nB and is zero by separatedness; the same applies to 1−e. Thus a nontrivial idempotent survives in B/π, contrary to L01 and connectedness.
Do not replace connected normalization special fiber by connected original special fiber without justification.

items.name: Completed local product of chart rings is a domain
items.locator: Theorem3.7.1 proof, PDF79–80; [10] LemmaA.1.1 and [54] Proposition2.2
items.statement: In the proof of Theorem3.7.1 after the specified complete DVR extension R′, each completed local chart ring is a Noetherian domain with an R′-point and regular generic fiber. Their completed tensor product over R′, for the sum of maximal ideals, is a domain by the domain-only general-DVR adapter Z12. The separate π-adic affinoid product is Z13.
items.note: Split from the formerly bundled complete-local and affinoid arguments. Original KWII and BLGGT statements were read in this continuation; their exact general-field interfaces are recorded, not silently assumed.

items.name: Pappas–Zhu GLn Iwahori local model
items.statement: Specialize the universal loop construction at t=-p over O. The generic fibre is the GLn affine Grassmannian and the special fibre the Iwahori affine flag variety. For dominant lambda, M(<=lambda) is the closure of the generic Schubert variety through(v+p)^lambda. Its special fibre is the reduced union of cells indexed by Adm-dual(lambda), by Pappas–Zhu9.3 and coherence; this reducedness is not inherited by its differential intersections.
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Supply the bounded ambient scheme in which the flat closure and differential intersection are formed.
Supply the reduced admissible-cell special fibre before imposing differential equations.

api.name: IwahoriLocalModel.mk
api.statement: For the source coefficient DVR O and dominant GL_n cocharacter lambda, specialize t=-p, form the generic Schubert variety through (v+p)^lambda, and take its schematic closure in the bounded universal Grassmannian. Reuse scheme-theoretic image/ideal-sheaf carriers on bounded ambient schemes; do not duplicate their general construction.

api.name: IwahoriLocalModel.generic_fiber
api.statement: After base change to E=Frac(O), recover the usual GL_n Schubert variety S_E(lambda), with the same chosen representative (v+p)^lambda and left-positive-loop convention.

api.name: IwahoriLocalModel.special_fiber
api.statement: Identify the special fibre with the reduced closed union of affine Schubert cells indexed by Adm-dual(lambda), using Pappas–Zhu9.3/coherence. This is the ambient model, not a reducedness assertion for differential intersections.

api.name: IwahoriLocalModel.inclusion_of_le
api.statement: Dominance lambda_prime<=lambda with equal central class induces the corresponding closed immersion of bounded local models; identity and composition agree with the ambient inclusions.

api.name: IwahoriLocalModel.closure_ideal
api.statement: On an affine chart Spec A of a bounded ambient model, if J_E defines the selected generic subvariety, the closure ideal is the inverse image of J_E in A[1/varpi]. Identify the resulting chart with the restriction of the global schematic closure.

api.name: IwahoriLocalModel.flat_base_change
api.statement: For a flat extension of coefficient DVRs preserving the chosen data, prove the closure comparison by exactness of flat tensoring and contraction of the generic ideal. Do not infer this comparison for reduction modulo varpi.

tests.name: IwahoriLocalModel.central_cocharacter
tests.statement: For lambda=(c,...,c), the generic Schubert variety is a point and its model is the section (v+p)^c I over O; its special fibre has one central affine-Weyl label.

tests.name: IwahoriLocalModel.rank_one
tests.statement: For n=1 and any integer c, the model is Spec O at the lattice (v+p)^c; no positive-root coordinates appear.

tests.name: IwahoriLocalModel.central_class_boundary
tests.statement: In GL_2, (1,1) is below (2,0) in the same central class, but (1,0) is not: unequal total cocharacter sums must not be accepted as a dominance inclusion.

items.name: Mixed-characteristic differential locus
items.statement: For a in O^n, require v A'A^-1+Ad(A)Diag(a) in(v+p)^-1 L+M_O. Its left-positive-loop quotient Grnabla_a is closed in Gr_O and is the fibre of the universal differential locus at(-p,a).
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Restrict the same descended differential condition to a generic Schubert cell and to the full bounded model.
Compare its reduction with the zero-parameter locus under right translation.

api.name: MixedDifferentialLocus.expression
api.statement: For a in O^n and a Noetherian O-algebra R, set L_a(A)=v(dA/dv)A^(-1)+A Diag(a) A^(-1), in the source localized completed loop ring. Require (v+p)L_a(A) in L+M_O(R), rather than in an unrestricted matrix ring.

api.name: MixedDifferentialLocus.left_change
api.statement: For h in L+G_O(R), L_a(hA)=v h_prime h^(-1)+h L_a(A)h^(-1). Prove this preserves the prescribed pole/upper-triangular-mod-v condition, including the derivative term.

api.name: MixedDifferentialLocus.quotient
api.statement: Descend the invariant closed subfunctor to the left quotient L+G_O\LG_O using the existing sheaf quotient and the universal differential locus; identify the resulting closed immersion in Gr_G,O.

api.name: MixedDifferentialLocus.specialize_universal
api.statement: Identify this locus with the fibre of the universal construction U15 at (t,a)=(-p,a), retaining the coefficient-algebra category.

api.name: MixedDifferentialLocus.map
api.statement: Under a coefficient-algebra map R→S, send A and the equation coefficientwise to S; prove derivative and matrix-operation compatibility with the source completion/localization maps and identity/composition laws.

api.name: MixedDifferentialLocus.residue
api.statement: Modulo varpi, p=0 and the condition becomes v A_prime A^(-1)+A Diag(a_bar)A^(-1) in v^(-1) Lie I_F, with the prescribed upper-triangular residue condition.

tests.name: MixedDifferentialLocus.identity_matrix
tests.statement: A=I satisfies the condition because (v+p)Diag(a) lies in L+M_O.

tests.name: MixedDifferentialLocus.rank_one_power
tests.statement: For n=1 and A=(v+p)^c, (v+p)L_a(A)=c v+(v+p)a; this checks the v numerator and the sign t=-p.

tests.name: MixedDifferentialLocus.left_gauge_derivative
tests.statement: At p=0 take h=I+v E_21 and a=0. Then v h_prime h^(-1)=v E_21 is nonzero and belongs to Lie I; a change-of-representative formula omitting this term is false.

items.name: Generic differential stratum is a smooth flag variety
items.statement: For any a in O^n, Sopen_E(lambda) intersect Grnabla_a is naturally(P_lambda\GLn)_E. It is closed in the generic Schubert closure, irreducible, projective and smooth.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Flat monodromy local model
items.statement: M(lambda,nabla_a) is the closure of M03 in M(<=lambda). It is projective, O-flat and of relative dimension dim(P_lambda\GLn), and must be distinguished from the naive intersection.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Embed every fixed-Hodge closure into the common naive bound before taking the finite union.
Distinguish the eventual flat-model component theorem from the naive-model component theorem.

api.name: FlatMonodromyModel.mk
api.statement: For dominant lambda and a in O^n, take the schematic closure of S_E^open(lambda) intersect Gr_nabla_a inside M(<=lambda), with its canonical closed immersion.

api.name: FlatMonodromyModel.generic_flag
api.statement: Its generic fibre is the closed differential stratum of Proposition4.1.1, canonically (P_lambda\GL_n)_E. Retain the source parabolic convention: alpha entries vanish when <lambda,alpha_coroot><0.

api.name: FlatMonodromyModel.saturation
api.statement: On a chart with ambient algebra A and a finitely generated ideal I defining the generic equations after localization, the closure ideal is I:varpi^infinity. Equivalently it is the contraction of I A[1/varpi].

api.name: FlatMonodromyModel.flat_projective
api.statement: The saturated quotient is varpi-torsion-free and hence flat over the coefficient DVR; the global closed model is projective. Export relative dimension dim(P_lambda\GL_n), without replacing lambda by a regular weight.

api.name: FlatMonodromyModel.minimal_closed
api.statement: Every closed subscheme of M(<=lambda) whose generic fibre contains the selected generic differential stratum contains this schematic closure.

api.name: FlatMonodromyModel.into_naive
api.statement: The differential condition is closed, so the flat closure factors through Mnv(<=lambda,nabla_a). This factorization is not an isomorphism without additional proof.

tests.name: FlatMonodromyModel.central_dimension_zero
tests.statement: For lambda=(c,...,c), P_lambda=GL_n and the generic differential stratum and its flat closure are the distinguished point/section of relative dimension zero.

tests.name: FlatMonodromyModel.GL2_regular_dimension
tests.statement: For GL_2 and lambda_1>lambda_2, the parabolic quotient has dimension one; for lambda_1=lambda_2 it has dimension zero.

tests.name: FlatMonodromyModel.saturation_removes_vertical_torsion
tests.statement: In O[x], the generic equation varpi*x=0 contracts to (x), not (varpi*x). The naive quotient O[x]/(varpi*x) has a special-fibre line, whereas its generic-fibre closure is Spec O. This is a test of the closure operation, not a claim that this toy scheme is a particular LLHLM local model.

items.name: Naive mixed-characteristic local model
items.statement: Mnv(<=lambda,nabla_a)=M(<=lambda) intersect Grnabla_a. Via flatness of the global Schubert variety, it agrees with specialization of the naive universal model; this extra input is Richarz Theorem1.5 as cited in Remark4.1.4.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Impose the explicit differential equation on each admissible Schubert cell and identify top-dimensional reduced components.
Embed the translated special-fibre intersection in the common zero-parameter flag.

api.name: NaiveMonodromyModel.intersection
api.statement: Define the closed fibre product M(<=lambda)×_(Gr_G,O)Gr_nabla_a, retaining the full scheme structure and its two projections.

api.name: NaiveMonodromyModel.chart_ideal
api.statement: In a common affine chart, its ideal is the sum of the ambient bounded-model ideal and the differential-equation ideal. Do not saturate or radicalize this sum as part of the definition.

api.name: NaiveMonodromyModel.point_criterion
api.statement: For a Noetherian O-algebra R, a point consists of a bounded-model point whose image satisfies equation(4.1) after the required fpqc local representation; equality is equality in the common quotient.

api.name: NaiveMonodromyModel.specialization_universal
api.statement: Use the flatness of the global Schubert variety from Richarz Theorem1.5 as cited in Remark4.1.4 to identify this model with specialization of U21. Equality of generic fibres alone does not establish the integral comparison.

api.name: NaiveMonodromyModel.generic_disjoint_union
api.statement: Use M07 to identify the generic fibre with the reduced disjoint union of (P_lambda_prime\GL_n)_E over dominant lambda_prime<=lambda. This is not the special-fibre decomposition.

api.name: NaiveMonodromyModel.base_change_intersection
api.statement: Base change commutes with this closed fibre product and its projections. A comparison with a newly defined schematic closure after the same base change is an additional assertion.

tests.name: NaiveMonodromyModel.closed_intersection_ideals
tests.statement: On Spec O[x,y], intersecting V(x) and V(y) gives ideal (x,y); using the ideal intersection (xy) would instead describe their scheme-theoretic union.

tests.name: NaiveMonodromyModel.generic_equality_not_integral
tests.statement: O[x]/(varpi*x) and O[x]/(x) have the same generic fibre but different special fibres. Do not deduce flatness of a naive model from M07.

tests.name: NaiveMonodromyModel.nilpotents_retained
tests.statement: A closed intersection can have coordinate ring F[x]/(x^2). The definition retains x as a nonzero nilpotent; passing to F is a separate reduction operation.

items.name: Union of flat Hodge-stratum closures
items.statement: For each dominant lambda'<=lambda, M(lambda',nabla_a) is a closed subscheme of Mnv(<=lambda,nabla_a). Their scheme-theoretic union M(<=lambda,nabla_a) is O-flat and projective.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Supply the flat model with the same generic fibre as the naive differential model.
Pull back its special fibre to the torus torsor and form products over the common coefficient base.

api.name: FlatHodgeUnion.finite_index
api.statement: Use the finite set of dominant cocharacters lambda_prime<=lambda in the fixed central class; record its finiteness before forming the union.

api.name: FlatHodgeUnion.mk
api.statement: Form the scheme-theoretic union of the closed submodels M(lambda_prime,nabla_a) inside the naive model; on a chart its ideal is the intersection of the finitely many defining ideals.

api.name: FlatHodgeUnion.closed_universal
api.statement: Each stratum closure maps by a closed immersion to the union, and a closed subscheme contains the union exactly when it contains every stratum closure.

api.name: FlatHodgeUnion.flat
api.statement: On affine charts, embed A/(intersection I_i) in the finite product of the torsion-free O-modules A/I_i. Deduce torsion-freeness and then DVR-flatness; do not confuse union with a disjoint coproduct over O.

api.name: FlatHodgeUnion.generic_fiber
api.statement: After inverting varpi, finite ideal intersections commute with localization and the union equals the generic naive model of M07, with its reduced disjoint flag strata.

api.name: FlatHodgeUnion.projective
api.statement: The union is a closed subscheme of the projective bounded model and is projective over O; preserve the common ambient immersion under changes of the finite indexing set.

tests.name: FlatHodgeUnion.one_stratum
tests.statement: If lambda is central, only that dominant weight occurs in its dominance interval, so the union is M(lambda,nabla_a).

tests.name: FlatHodgeUnion.two_generic_strata
tests.statement: For GL_2, the dominant weights <=(2,0) are (2,0) and (1,1); the generic union is P^1_E disjoint union Spec E.

tests.name: FlatHodgeUnion.flat_union_nonreduced_special
tests.statement: In O[x], the two flat sections (x) and (x-varpi) have scheme-theoretic union x(x-varpi)=0. It is O-flat, but its special fibre is x^2=0. Thus flat union and reduced generic fibre do not imply reduced special fibre.

items.name: Flat union and naive model have the same generic fibre
items.statement: M(<=lambda,nabla_a)_E=Mnv(<=lambda,nabla_a)_E, the reduced disjoint union of(P_lambda'\GLn)_E over dominant lambda'<=lambda. This proves no equality of the integral models or their special fibres.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Residue tuple genericity
items.statement: A tuple a in R^n for an F-algebra is m-generic when for i!=j its difference a_i-a_j avoids every integer in[-m,m] mapped into R. For integral nu whose translation is m-generic, nu modulo p satisfies this condition. In the affine-cell theorem R is F, so the avoided scalars are units when nonzero.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Make the triangular coefficient scalars invertible when the tuple is defined over the residue field.
Transfer the integral affine-Weyl genericity bound to the residue tuple used in cell coordinates.

api.name: ResidueTupleGenericity.iff_differences
api.statement: For a in R^n over an F-algebra and positive integer m, genericity means a_i-a_j is unequal to the image of every integer c with -m<=c<=m for every i!=j.

api.name: ResidueTupleGenericity.monotone_bound
api.statement: If 1<=m_prime<=m and a is m-generic, then it is m_prime-generic.

api.name: ResidueTupleGenericity.perm_common_shift
api.statement: Permuting all coordinates or adding a common b in R to them preserves and reflects m-genericity.

api.name: ResidueTupleGenericity.injective_map
api.statement: An injective F-algebra map preserves and reflects genericity; for any F-algebra map, genericity of the image implies genericity of the original tuple. Arbitrary maps need not preserve the non-equality condition.

api.name: ResidueTupleGenericity.field_scalar_units
api.statement: If a lies in F^n, every avoided scalar a_i-a_j-c is a nonzero field element, hence a unit; its image remains a unit in every F-algebra. This is the stable open condition used for solving cell equations.

api.name: ResidueTupleGenericity.translation_comparison
api.statement: For an integral nu with t_nu m-generic in Definition2.1.10(2), prove its residue tuple is m-generic as in Remark4.2.3. Retain the source affine-Weyl convention rather than substituting eta-shifted weight depth.

tests.name: ResidueTupleGenericity.boundary_F7
tests.statement: Over F_7 and m=1, (0,3) is generic, whereas (0,1) fails because the difference 1 is forbidden.

tests.name: ResidueTupleGenericity.rank_one_vacuous
tests.statement: With one coordinate there are no pairs i!=j, so the condition is vacuous for every positive m.

tests.name: ResidueTupleGenericity.specialization_failure
tests.statement: Over F_p[t], (t,0) avoids every constant c and is m-generic for every m, but evaluation t↦0 makes the coordinates equal. Nonzero differences over a general algebra must not be treated as units.

tests.name: ResidueTupleGenericity.unit_locus
tests.statement: For a generic tuple already in F^n, extending scalars to F[epsilon]/(epsilon^2) preserves every relevant inverse even though the target algebra is nonreduced.

items.name: Differential affine-cell dimension
items.statement: For positive h, w in Wtilde h-small and a in O^n whose residue is h-generic, Sopen_F(w^*) intersect Flnabla_a is affine space of dimension d minus the number of positive-root critical strips containing w(A0), where d=dim(B\GLn). Proof eliminates all but the top coefficient in each supported root using scalar i+[alpha>0]+<a,alpha^vee>.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Smallness of admissible elements
