items.statement: For w in Adm(lambda), w^* lies in Adm-dual(lambda) and is h_lambda-small.
items.note: Route owner: RootSystemsPartIIDominanceAndDemazure. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Top components of the naive special fibre
items.statement: For dominant lambda and residue a h_lambda-generic, closure of Sopen_F(w^*) intersect Flnabla_a gives a bijection from Admreg(lambda) to the d-dimensional irreducible components of Mnv(<=lambda,nabla_a)_F. Do not infer that the entire special fibre is reduced or equidimensional from this statement.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Affine root subgroups and their conjugation by w̃^*
items.locator: Lemma 4.2.7, PDF84 (U_{α,m} defined in the preceding paragraph, PDF84)
items.statement: For α = α_ik ∈ Φ (i ≠ k) and m ∈ Z, U_{α,m} is the affine root group of G^∨ = GL_n: the unipotent group with ik-entry cv^m, c a constant, and all other non-diagonal entries zero (PDF84). Lemma 4.2.7: if w̃ = s t_ν ∈ W̃ and we set z̃ = w̃^* ∈ W̃^∨, then z̃^{-1} U_{−α,m} z̃ = U_{−s(α), m+⟨ν,α^∨⟩}.
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: The proof of Lemma 4.2.8 (PDF85) applies Lemma 4.2.7 to w̃^{-1} = s t_ν, with (w̃^{-1})^* = z̃^{-1}, to reduce membership in z̃^{-1}I_F z̃ to U_{−s(α),m+⟨ν,α^∨⟩} ⊂ I_F.
The same reduction for z̃^{-1}L^{--}G_F z̃.
Use explicit off-diagonal coordinates and root-height triangularity in the differential equation.

api.name: AffineRootChart.parameter
api.statement: For alpha=e_i-e_k with i!=k and m an integer, send c in R to I+c v^m E_ik in GL_n(R((v))). Reuse Matrix.transvection and its group laws, or TauCeti.GeneralLinear.rootSubgroupPoints evaluated on the Laurent-ring parameter; construct only the affine-loop adapter.

api.name: AffineRootChart.add_inverse
api.statement: For the same alpha,m, x(c)x(d)=x(c+d), x(0)=I and x(c)^(-1)=x(-c); export these as equalities in the common loop carrier.

api.name: AffineRootChart.coefficient_ext
api.statement: The (i,k),v^m coefficient recovers c, so equality of these root-loop points is equality of their parameters.

api.name: AffineRootChart.map
api.statement: An F-algebra map acts coefficientwise and commutes with the root parameterization, with identity and composition laws.

api.name: AffineRootChart.conjugation
api.statement: Lemma 4.2.7: for w=s t_nu and z=w^*, use the source Weyl embedding (PDF88) to prove z^(-1)U_(-alpha,m)z=U_(-s(alpha),m+<nu,alpha_coroot>), including the scalar-parameter map induced by the chosen permutation matrices; fix the Weyl-action convention first (see the M12 statement fix).

api.name: AffineRootChart.membership_bounds
api.statement: Not proved here. The Iwahori and negative-loop membership criteria are Lemma 4.2.8, items M38 (U_(-alpha,m) in z^(-1)I z iff <w(x),alpha_coroot> < m) and M39 (U_(-alpha,m) in z^(-1)L--G z iff m < <w(x),alpha_coroot>). Re-export them from there.

tests.name: AffineRootChart.identity_parameter
tests.statement: c=0 gives I for every exponent, including negative exponents; this point is not excluded by an exact-degree condition.

tests.name: AffineRootChart.GL2_translation
tests.statement: For z=diag(v,1), z^(-1)(I+c v^m E_21)z=I+c v^(m+1)E_21, checking the positive exponent shift for alpha=e_1-e_2.

tests.name: AffineRootChart.root_addition
tests.statement: In GL_2, (I+c v^m E_12)(I+d v^m E_12)=I+(c+d)v^m E_12 because E_12^2=0, over rings with nilpotents as well as fields.

items.name: Unipotent affine-cell subgroup N_z̃
items.statement: For any z̃ ∈ W̃^∨, define N_z̃ := z̃^{-1} L^{--}G_F z̃ ∩ I_F. Here L^{--}G_F(R) = {g ∈ GL_n(R[1/v]) : g mod 1/v is lower unipotent} (Definition 3.2.1 specialized to F, PDF84), and I_F is the Iwahori subgroup.
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Parametrize the Schubert cell by zN_z with the correct left quotient.
Count root supports and order the differential equations triangularly.

api.name: AffineCellSubgroup.mk
api.statement: Define N_z=z^(-1)L--G_F z intersect I_F as a subgroup functor of the common loop group.

api.name: AffineCellSubgroup.root_membership
api.statement: For z=w^*, U_(-alpha,m) is contained exactly when <x,alpha_coroot><m< <w(x),alpha_coroot>, independent of the choice of x inside A0. This is Proposition 4.2.10, proved as M14 from M38 and M39; re-export it from M14.

api.name: AffineCellSubgroup.polynomial_coordinates
api.statement: The (-alpha)-entries are v^(delta_alpha_positive) f_alpha with deg f_alpha <= d_(alpha,w), and f_alpha=0 when d_(alpha,w)<0, keeping zero and lower-degree polynomials (E13). This is Corollary 4.2.12, item M41; re-export it from M41.

api.name: AffineCellSubgroup.cell_map
api.statement: The map N_z→I_F\LGL_n sending N to the left coset of zN is an isomorphism onto S_F^open(z), as in M15; it is not the map N↦Nz.

tests.name: AffineCellSubgroup.identity_cell
tests.statement: For z=e, N_z is trivial and the Schubert cell is a point (its support, M40, is empty).

tests.name: AffineCellSubgroup.GL2_simple_reflection
tests.statement: For the GL_2 permutation matrix z=s, N_s consists of I+c E_12 and the cell is one-dimensional.

tests.name: AffineCellSubgroup.GL2_translation
tests.statement: For z=diag(v,1), N_z consists of I+c v E_21. The coefficient polynomial has bound zero and includes c=0; it need not have exact degree zero.

tests.name: AffineCellSubgroup.exponent_above_bound
tests.statement: For z=diag(v,1) and c≠0, I+c v^2 E_21 lies in I_F but not in N_z, because z(I+c v^2 E_21)z^(-1) has (2,1)-entry c v, which is not in R[v^(-1)]. N_z is a proper subgroup of I_F cut out by the exponent bounds.

items.name: Support of the cell subgroup
items.statement: The support of N_z̃, denoted Supp(N_z̃), is the set of α ∈ Φ such that U_{α,m} ⊂ N_z̃ for some m. The paper writes the subscript as w̃; N is defined only for z̃ ∈ W̃^∨ (Definition 4.2.9), and the definition is applied as Supp(N_{w̃*}).
items.note: Split from M13. The support is defined by containment of whole affine root subgroups. It is used through Corollaries 4.2.15–4.2.16 and in counting the free top coefficients in Theorem 4.2.4.

uses.how: Corollary 4.2.15 characterizes −α ∈ Supp(N_{w̃*}) and computes #Supp(N_{w̃*}).
Corollary 4.2.16 uses −Supp(N_{w̃*}) ⊂ w(Φ^+) to put N_{w̃*} inside w(L^+N̄)w^{-1}.
The proof of Theorem 4.2.4 (PDF86–87) keeps exactly one free coefficient c_{α,d_{α,w̃}} for each −α ∈ Supp(N_{w̃*}), so the dimension is #Supp.

api.name: CellSubgroupSupport.mk
api.statement: For z̃ ∈ W̃^∨, Supp(N_z̃) := {α ∈ Φ : ∃ m ∈ Z, U_{α,m} ⊂ N_z̃}, a subset of the finite root system Φ. It is defined by containment of subgroups, not by a chosen point having a nonzero α-entry.

api.name: CellSubgroupSupport.neg_mem_iff
api.statement: For w̃ ∈ W̃ and x ∈ A0: −α ∈ Supp(N_{w̃*}) iff some integer m satisfies ⟨x,α^∨⟩ < m < ⟨w̃(x),α^∨⟩ (M14), iff ⌊⟨w̃(x),α^∨⟩⌋ ≥ ⌈⟨x,α^∨⟩⌉ (Corollary 4.2.15), iff d_{α,w̃} ≥ 0. The answer does not depend on x ∈ A0.

api.name: CellSubgroupSupport.card
api.statement: #Supp(N_{w̃*}) = #Φ^+ − #{α ∈ Φ^+ : w̃(A0) ⊂ H_α^{(0,1)}} (Corollary 4.2.15). This counts the free top coefficients in Theorem 4.2.4, not the dimension ℓ(w̃^*) of the whole Schubert cell.

api.name: CellSubgroupSupport.neg_subset
api.statement: −Supp(N_{w̃*}) ⊂ w(Φ^+) for the unique w ∈ W with w^{-1}w̃ ∈ W̃^+ (Corollary 4.2.15). This order drives the triangular elimination in Theorem 4.2.4.

tests.name: CellSubgroupSupport.identity_empty
tests.statement: For z̃ = e, N_e = L^{--}G_F ∩ I_F is trivial: off-diagonal entries lie in v^{-1}R[v^{-1}] ∩ R[[v]] or in R[v^{-1}] ∩ vR[[v]], and the diagonal is 1. So Supp(N_e) = ∅.

tests.name: CellSubgroupSupport.GL2_simple_reflection
tests.statement: In GL_2 with z̃ = s (permutation matrix), N_s = {1 + cE_12}, so Supp(N_s) = {ε1−ε2}. Equivalently, α = ε2−ε1 has d_{α,s} = 0 and −α ∈ Supp, while α = ε1−ε2 has d_{α,s} = −2.

tests.name: CellSubgroupSupport.GL2_translation
tests.statement: In GL_2 with z̃ = diag(v,1) = t_{(1,0)}, N_z̃ = {1 + cvE_21}, so Supp(N_z̃) = {ε2−ε1}. Here α = ε1−ε2 > 0 has d_{α,w̃} = 0 and entry v^{δ_{α>0}}f = cv.

tests.name: CellSubgroupSupport.not_pointwise
tests.statement: The identity lies in every N_z̃ and all its off-diagonal entries are 0, yet Supp(N_s) ≠ ∅ in the GL_2 example. The support cannot be read off from one point.

items.name: Affine root subgroups of the cell subgroup
items.statement: Fix x ∈ A0. If w̃ ∈ W̃ and z̃ = w̃^* ∈ W̃^∨, then for α ∈ Φ and m ∈ Z, U_{−α,m} ⊂ N_z̃ if and only if ⟨x,α^∨⟩ < m < ⟨w̃(x),α^∨⟩ (4.3).
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Polynomial coordinates for the cell subgroup
items.locator: Corollary 4.2.12, PDF85 (d_{α,w̃} defined after Proposition 4.2.10, PDF85)
items.statement: Fix x ∈ A0 and w̃ ∈ W̃, and let d_{α,w̃} := ⌊⟨w̃(x),α^∨⟩⌋ − ⌈⟨x,α^∨⟩⌉ (note ⌈⟨x,α^∨⟩⌉ = δ_{α>0}). Let R be a Noetherian F-algebra and α ∈ Φ. Then (N_{w̃*}(R))_{−α} = {v^{δ_{α>0}} f_{α,R}} where f_{α,R} ∈ R[v] has degree d_{α,w̃} (with the convention that f_{α,R} = 0 if d_{α,w̃} < 0). Read 'has degree' as 'has degree at most' (E13): the −α-entries are exactly v^{δ_{α>0}}f with f ∈ R[v] of degree ≤ d_{α,w̃}, including f = 0.
items.note: Split from M14. The paper calls it an 'elementary corollary' and prints no proof. It follows from Proposition 4.2.10 (M14) because N_z̃ is cut out entry by entry: conjugating by z̃ permutes the entries and multiplies them by powers of v. The allowed exponents for the −α-entry are δ_{α>0} ≤ m ≤ ⌊⟨w̃(x),α^∨⟩⌋. The degree wording is already recorded as E13.

uses.how: The proof of Theorem 4.2.4 (PDF86–87) writes f_α = Σ_{i=0}^{d_{α,w̃}} c_{α,i}v^i and eliminates every coefficient except c_{α,d_{α,w̃}}.
That API entry is this corollary and should cite M41.

items.name: Unipotent subgroup parametrizes the Schubert cell
items.statement: N_z is a finite-dimensional affine unipotent group scheme and z N_z -> Sopen_F(z) is an affine-space isomorphism of dimension l(z).
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Support criterion and count
items.statement: For w and x in A0, -alpha lies in Supp(N_w*) iff floor(<w(x),alpha^vee>)>=ceil(<x,alpha^vee>), equivalently <w(x),alpha^vee>>0 and x,w(x) lie in different alpha-strips. For the finite Weyl s with s^-1 w in Wplus, -Supp(N_w*) is contained in s(Phi+), and the support size is d minus the number of positive-root critical strips containing w(A0).
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Triangular cell subgroup
items.statement: For s in M16, N_w* lies in s(L+N)s^-1 where N is the lower unipotent subgroup. This gives the root partial order used in M09's triangular coefficient elimination.
items.note: Route owner: GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Common zero-parameter differential affine flag
items.statement: Flnabla0 is the fpqc sheafification of I A satisfying v A'A^-1 in v^-1 Lie I. It is the zero-parameter differential locus in Fl; use the explicit chosen affine Weyl embedding for right translations.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Provide a common ambient space for translating differential local models with different residue parameters.
Take differential cell closures and compare their intrinsic labels inside one carrier.

api.name: ZeroDifferentialFlag.mk
api.statement: Take the fpqc sheafification of the left-coset presheaf I_F(R)\LGL_n(R) satisfying v A_prime A^(-1) in v^(-1)Lie I_F(R); identify it with the zero-parameter fibre of the universal differential locus.

api.name: ZeroDifferentialFlag.representative_invariance
api.statement: For h in I_F, expand v(hA)_prime(hA)^(-1)=v h_prime h^(-1)+h(v A_prime A^(-1))h^(-1) and prove that the condition is unchanged.

api.name: ZeroDifferentialFlag.closed_inclusion
api.statement: Export its closed immersion in the affine flag ind-scheme and the compatibility of this immersion with fpqc descent and coefficient maps.

api.name: ZeroDifferentialFlag.weyl_points
api.statement: Every chosen affine-Weyl monomial representative z satisfies the condition: v z_prime z^(-1) is a constant diagonal matrix after the permutation conjugation, and lies in v^(-1)Lie I.

api.name: ZeroDifferentialFlag.right_translation_comparison
api.statement: For z=s^(-1)t_mu and a_bar=s^(-1)(mu) modulo p, right multiplication A↦Az identifies the translated a-differential intersection with the zero-differential intersection. It is not an assertion that arbitrary right translation preserves the zero-parameter locus.

api.name: ZeroDifferentialFlag.translation_derivative
api.statement: Use v(Az)_prime(Az)^(-1)=v A_prime A^(-1)+A Diag(s^(-1)(mu))A^(-1), with the right-translation order fixed.

tests.name: ZeroDifferentialFlag.constant_matrix
tests.statement: A constant invertible matrix has derivative zero and satisfies the zero-parameter condition.

tests.name: ZeroDifferentialFlag.monomial_point
tests.statement: For z=diag(v^mu_i), v z_prime z^(-1)=Diag(mu), checking the affine-Weyl fixed-point inclusion in characteristic p.

tests.name: ZeroDifferentialFlag.frobenius_poles
tests.statement: In characteristic p, A=I+c v^(-p)E_12 has derivative zero and lies in the zero-differential flag. The common ambient locus has no uniform pole bound; do not replace it by one bounded local model.

items.name: Translate differential models to the common flag
items.statement: For z=s^-1 t_mu in Wtilde-dual, a integral with a congruent to s^-1(mu) modulo p, right translation identifies Mnv(<=lambda,nabla_a)_F with M(<=lambda)_F z intersect Flnabla0. The same identity holds on each Schubert cell. Thus this right translation is a closed immersion of the naive special fibre into Flnabla0.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Translated differential cells and their closures
items.statement: For w1,w2 in Wplus and s in Wtilde, set Sopen(w1,w2,s)=Sopen_F((w2^-1 w0 w1)^*)s^*. Intersect with Flnabla0, then take its closure inside Flnabla0 to define Snabla0(w1,w2,s). This closure may be strictly smaller than the closure of the entire Schubert cell intersected with Flnabla0.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Compare closures after eliminating the second dominant factor and changing the finite Weyl representative.
Identify the correctly ordered translation with the intrinsic alcove-pair component.

api.name: TranslatedDifferentialCell.open_cell
api.statement: For w1,w2 in Wtilde-plus and s in Wtilde, define the translated locally closed cell S_F^open((w2^(-1)w0w1)^*)s^* inside the affine flag, using the chosen star and embedding conventions.

api.name: TranslatedDifferentialCell.differential_intersection
api.statement: Intersect that locally closed cell with Fl_nabla0 as a scheme fibre product before taking any closure.

api.name: TranslatedDifferentialCell.closure
api.statement: Take the closure of this differential intersection inside Fl_nabla0. In the genericity range the intersection is an affine space, so its schematic closure is reduced and irreducible; retain the distinction from intersecting the closure of the full Schubert cell.

api.name: TranslatedDifferentialCell.dense_open
api.statement: Under M21 hypotheses, the differential cell is a dense open affine space of dimension d in its own irreducible closure; record the immersion and the common ambient map.

api.name: TranslatedDifferentialCell.remove_second_factor
api.statement: Under M22 smallness and genericity hypotheses, identify S_nabla0(w1,w2,s) with S_nabla0(w1,e,s w2^(-1)), preserving the displayed multiplication order.

api.name: TranslatedDifferentialCell.finite_weyl_invariance
api.statement: For w1 in Wtilde1-plus and (n-1)-generic s, M23 identifies the closure at s with the closure at s w^(-1) for w in the finite Weyl group. It does not identify all open cells.

tests.name: TranslatedDifferentialCell.second_factor_identity
tests.statement: For w2=e, the open Schubert label is (w0w1)^* and the right translator is s^*; removing the second factor changes nothing.

tests.name: TranslatedDifferentialCell.order_countercheck
tests.statement: As affine transformations of Z^2, take s(x1,x2)=(7+x2,x1) and w2(x)=x+(1,0). Then s w2^(-1)(0)=(7,-1), whereas w2^(-1)s(0)=(6,0). The two expressions in E14 cannot be interchanged.

tests.name: TranslatedDifferentialCell.closure_intersection_warning
tests.statement: In A^2, let U be the punctured x-axis and C the y-axis. Closure(U intersect C) is empty, but closure(U) intersect C is the origin. This tests the order of operations; the source-specific strictness remains Remark4.3.3(2), not an identification with this toy example.

items.name: Dimension of a translated differential cell
items.statement: If w2^-1 w0 w1 is m-small and s is m-generic, with m positive, the differential cell of M20 is affine d-space. Its closure is irreducible of dimension d.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Closed immersion removing the second dominant factor
items.statement: Let s̃ ∈ W̃ and let w̃1, w̃2 ∈ W̃^+. Assume that for each i ∈ {1,2} there exists a positive integer m_i such that w̃_i is m_i-small. There is a closed immersion S°_F(w̃1, e, s̃w̃2^{-1})^{∇0} ⊂ S°_F(w̃1, w̃2, s̃)^{∇0}.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Removing the second dominant factor under genericity
items.statement: Let s̃ ∈ W̃ and let w̃1, w̃2 ∈ W̃^+. Assume that for each i ∈ {1,2} there exists a positive integer m_i such that w̃_i is m_i-small. If s̃ is (m1+m2)-generic, then the two sides of the closed immersion S°_F(w̃1, e, s̃w̃2^{-1})^{∇0} ⊂ S°_F(w̃1, w̃2, s̃)^{∇0} are equal, hence S^{∇0}_F(w̃1, e, s̃w̃2^{-1}) = S^{∇0}_F(w̃1, w̃2, s̃).
items.note: Split from M22. Proof (PDF90): Proposition 2.1.12 (N19–N21) makes w̃2^{-1}w0w̃1 (m1+m2)-small, and makes s̃w̃2^{-1} m1-generic when s̃ is (m1+m2)-generic. By Proposition 4.3.4 (M21) both sides are then affine spaces of dimension d, so the closed immersion M22 is an equality, and the closures agree. The product is s̃w̃2^{-1}; compare E14 in the proof of Theorem 4.3.9.

uses.how: The proof of Theorem 4.3.9 (PDF92) uses 'By Proposition 4.3.5, S^{∇0}(w̃1,w̃2,s̃) = S^{∇0}(w̃1,e,s̃w̃2^{-1})'.

items.name: Finite Weyl invariance of differential closures
items.statement: Let s̃ ∈ W̃ and w̃1 ∈ W̃1^+. Assume that s̃ is (n−1)-generic. Then, for any w ∈ W, S^{∇0}_F(w̃1, e, s̃) = S^{∇0}_F(w̃1, e, s̃w^{-1}).
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Intrinsic component indexed by an alcove pair
items.statement: Consider (w̃1, ω) ∈ W̃1^+ × X*(T) and assume that t_ω is (n−1)-generic (Definition 2.1.10(2)). Define C_{(w̃1,ω)} := S^{∇0}_F(w̃1, e, s̃) ∈ Irr_d(Fl^{∇0}) for any choice of s̃ ∈ W̃ such that s̃(0) = ω. By Proposition 4.3.6 this does not depend on the choice of s̃. It depends on (w̃1, ω) only up to the equivalence (w̃1, ω) ∼ (t_ν w̃1, ω − ν) for ν ∈ X^0(T). Since w̃1 is (n−1)-small, C_{(w̃1,ω)} is an irreducible closed subvariety of Fl^{∇0} of dimension d.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Identify translated top components independently of the chosen local-model Hodge bound.
Attach a component to a compatible Serre weight and enumerate its obvious fixed points.

api.name: IntrinsicAlcoveComponent.mk
api.statement: For w1 in Wtilde1-plus and (n-1)-generic translation t_omega, choose s with s(0)=omega and take S_nabla0(w1,e,s). The domain includes both the alcove and genericity conditions.

api.name: IntrinsicAlcoveComponent.choice_independent
api.statement: If s(0)=s_prime(0)=omega, express s_prime=s w^(-1) for a finite Weyl element and apply M23 to identify the closed subvarieties in Fl_nabla0.

api.name: IntrinsicAlcoveComponent.central_relation
api.statement: For nu in X0(T), the pairs (w1,omega) and (t_nu w1,omega-nu) define the same closed subvariety, with the induced equality of ambient immersions.

api.name: IntrinsicAlcoveComponent.geometry
api.statement: Export a dense open A^d_F, geometric irreducibility and dimension d of the resulting reduced closed variety, proving the field-extension comparison from this affine chart before using product irreducibility.

api.name: IntrinsicAlcoveComponent.translated_identification
api.statement: Under M25 hypotheses, identify S_nabla0(w1,w2,s) with C_(w1,s w2^(-1)(0)); preserve E14’s corrected order.

api.name: IntrinsicAlcoveComponent.obvious_fixed_points
api.statement: For each finite Weyl w, the chosen affine-Weyl point (t_omega w w1)^* belongs to C_(w1,omega), as in M32. Completeness of this list is not asserted.

tests.name: IntrinsicAlcoveComponent.finite_representative_change
tests.statement: Replacing the chosen s by s u^(-1), for a finite Weyl u, leaves s(0)=omega and the component unchanged even when the corresponding open charts differ.

tests.name: IntrinsicAlcoveComponent.central_shift
tests.statement: In GL_2, shifting w1 by the central translation t_(1,1) and omega by -(1,1) leaves C unchanged; the two operations must be paired.

tests.name: IntrinsicAlcoveComponent.GL2_dimension_fixed_points
tests.statement: For w1=e and omega=(3,0) at p=11, the genericity bound n-1=1 holds, d=1, and both t_omega and (t_omega s)^* give the distinct obvious fixed points after applying the indicated star convention.

items.name: Identify translated closures intrinsically
items.statement: If w1 in W1plus, w2 in Wplus m-small with m>=1, and s is(m+n-1)-generic, then Snabla0(w1,w2,s)=C_(w1,s w2^-1(0)). The first line of the proof reverses the product once; the statement and Proposition4.3.5 fix the order.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Admissible pairs label translated top components
items.statement: For regular dominant lambda, a in O^n, and s=t_mu sfinite(h_lambda+n-1)-generic with a congruent to sfinite^-1(mu) modulo varpi, AP(lambda) bijects the d-dimensional irreducible components of Mnv(<=lambda,nabla_a)_F s^* by(w1,w2)->C_(w1,s w2^-1(0)).
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Torus torsors over the special-fibre flag
items.statement: Let I1 be loops upper unipotent modulo v. The fpqc quotient I1\LGLn maps to I\LGLn as a Tdual-torsor. Pull it back to each local-model special fibre, to Flnabla0 and to C_(w,omega); the last is irreducible of dimension d+n. No global O-model of these torsors is asserted in §4.4; later constructions only provide torsors on chart covers.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Supply the vertical maps in the Cartesian square of product local-model translations.
Lift C_(w,omega) to an irreducible variety of dimension d+n without positing a global integral torsor.

api.name: FlagTorusTorsor.mk
api.statement: Let I1 be the subgroup of I whose reduction modulo v is upper unipotent. Sheafify I1\LGL_n and map to I\LGL_n; identify I/I1 with the split diagonal torus Tdual.

api.name: FlagTorusTorsor.fiber_action
api.statement: The torsor action is left multiplication by I/I1: D acts on [A]_(I1) by [DA]_(I1). Prove normality of I1 in I, representative independence and the torsor isomorphism Tdual×Fl_tilde ≅ Fl_tilde×_Fl Fl_tilde. Distinguish this action from right diagonal translation on the base flag.

api.name: FlagTorusTorsor.pullback
api.statement: For a closed subspace Y of the special-fibre flag, define its lift as Y×_Fl Fl_tilde. Pullback preserves the torsor comparison and commutes with identity/composition of maps of Y.

api.name: FlagTorusTorsor.smooth_dimension
api.statement: The projection is a smooth Tdual-torsor of relative dimension n. For the geometrically integral component C with dense A^d chart, prove its lift is irreducible of dimension d+n via the smooth locally trivial torsor; this does not apply to an arbitrary disconnected Y.

api.name: FlagTorusTorsor.right_translation
api.statement: Right translation A↦Az on both quotients commutes with the left torsor action. Apply M19 to obtain the Cartesian square(4.10), including the restricted differential loci.

api.name: FlagTorusTorsor.scope_special_fiber
api.statement: Only the special-fibre torsors are defined here. Import the later chartwise O-torsors where needed; do not assert that section4.4 constructs a global integral lift.

tests.name: FlagTorusTorsor.identity_fiber
tests.statement: The fibre over the identity I-coset is I1\I≅Tdual, with the usual free transitive left diagonal action.

tests.name: FlagTorusTorsor.left_right_actions_differ
tests.statement: At the identity base flag, right diagonal translation fixes the base point, while left diagonal multiplication on its torsor fibre is free. They are different actions and must not be identified.

tests.name: FlagTorusTorsor.rank_two_dimension
tests.statement: For a GL_2 intrinsic component d=1, its torsor lift has dimension 1+2=3, not one.

tests.name: FlagTorusTorsor.translate_action_commutes
tests.statement: For diagonal D, loop A and chosen z, (DA)z=D(Az), so the lifted right-translation square respects the left torsor action without commuting D past z.

items.name: Product models, components and torsor comparison
items.statement: For finite J take products over O (over F for special fibres). Admissible sets are products, d_J=|J|d, and component varieties C_(w,omega) are products of dimension d_J with torus lifts of dimension d_J+n|J|. If z_j=s_j^-1 t_mu_j and a_j congruent s_j^-1(mu_j), translations give a Cartesian square of closed immersions with both vertical maps smooth Tdual^J-torsors.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Assemble factorwise component labels into the product component indexed by a Serre weight.
Compare all components and their torsor lifts in one product differential flag.

api.name: ProductMonodromyModel.mk
api.statement: For a finite indexing set J, take the products of all bounded/flat/naive local models over the same coefficient DVR O, and products of their special fibres over F.

api.name: ProductMonodromyModel.projections_reindex
api.statement: Export projections and coherent reindexing under bijections of J, with identity/composition and the induced reindexing of lambda,a,w,omega and the product torus.

api.name: ProductMonodromyModel.fiber_comparison
api.statement: Generic and special fibre commute with these finite fibre products. The coefficient base is shared; these are not products over Z and not unrelated completed tensor products.

api.name: ProductMonodromyModel.component_product
api.statement: Define C_(w,omega)=product_j C_(w_j,omega_j), prove geometric irreducibility from the factorwise dense affine charts, and obtain dimension |J|d; the torus lift has dimension |J|(d+n). Irreducibility of arbitrary F-varieties alone is insufficient for this product conclusion.

api.name: ProductMonodromyModel.cartesian_translation
api.statement: For z_j=s_j^(-1)t_(mu_j) and a_j congruent s_j^(-1)(mu_j) modulo varpi in every factor, construct Proposition4.5.1’s Cartesian square. The horizontal maps are closed immersions and the vertical maps smooth Tdual^J-torsors.

api.name: ProductMonodromyModel.admissible_product
api.statement: Identify Adm(lambda) and Admreg(lambda) with the factorwise products, retaining regularity and genericity hypotheses factor by factor rather than only after summing dimensions.

tests.name: ProductMonodromyModel.singleton
tests.statement: For a singleton J, the models, diagrams and dimension formulas agree with the corresponding one-factor construction.

tests.name: ProductMonodromyModel.empty_product
tests.statement: For an abstract empty finite J, the product over O is Spec O, its special fibre is Spec F, the product torus is trivial and both relative dimensions are zero.

tests.name: ProductMonodromyModel.two_GL2_factors
tests.statement: For two GL_2 factors, d_J=2 and the lifted component has dimension 2+2*2=6; the product torus has rank four.

tests.name: ProductMonodromyModel.irreducibility_field_boundary
tests.statement: Spec C is irreducible over R but Spec(C tensor_R C) is a disjoint union of two points. The product argument must use the geometric irreducibility supplied by the affine-space charts.

items.name: Component labelled by a Serre weight and central lift
items.statement: For an(n-1)-deep Serre weight sigma and an algebraic central lift zeta, choose its unique zeta-compatible lowest-alcove presentation(w1,omega) and define C_sigma^zeta=C_(w1,omega). This is independent of representatives. The depth condition is part of the definition's domain.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Label top-dimensional naive-model components by the actual Jordan–Hölder Serre weights under a sufficient genericity bound.
Compare obvious and predicted Serre weights with membership of the inertial-parameter fixed point in C_sigma^zeta.

api.name: SerreWeightComponent.domain
api.statement: Input an (n-1)-deep Serre weight sigma and an algebraic central lift zeta for which a zeta-compatible lowest-alcove presentation exists. Retain compatibility as input, rather than assuming every arbitrary central lift is admissible.

api.name: SerreWeightComponent.mk
api.statement: Choose a representative (w1,omega) of that compatible lowest-alcove presentation and set C_sigma^zeta=C_(w1,omega), using the component construction already made in M24/M28.

api.name: SerreWeightComponent.representative_independent
api.statement: Use uniqueness of the compatible lowest-alcove presentation modulo X0(T)^J and M24’s central relation to prove equality for any two representatives.

api.name: SerreWeightComponent.product_formula
api.statement: For the factorwise presentation, C_sigma^zeta=product_j C_(w_(1,j),omega_j), as in equation(4.12), with all products over the common residue field.

api.name: SerreWeightComponent.dimension_torsor
api.statement: Export the reduced geometrically irreducible closed subvariety of dimension d_J and its previously defined Tdual^J-torsor lift of dimension d_J+n|J|.

api.name: SerreWeightComponent.generic_label_domain
api.statement: When using M30, require a bound that actually makes every constituent (n-1)-deep; use the retained E15 repair max{2n,h_lambda+n-1}. The printed max{2n,h_lambda} is not sufficient to define every proposed label.

api.name: SerreWeightComponent.fixed_point_interface
api.statement: Under M35–M37 hypotheses, obvious weight membership implies the parameter point lies on C; lying on C implies predicted weight membership; the reverse implication needs the polynomial nonvanishing hypothesis. Do not identify all three assertions without that extra condition.

tests.name: SerreWeightComponent.central_equivalent_presentations
tests.statement: Replacing each (w_(1,j),omega_j) by (t_(nu_j)w_(1,j),omega_j-nu_j) with nu_j central preserves the component and product formula.

tests.name: SerreWeightComponent.depth_boundary_E15
tests.statement: In the retained GL_2/F_19 example R_s(7,0), lambda=(6,0), the constituent det^6 is not 1-deep. Under the printed bound its symbol C_(det^6)^zeta is outside this definition’s domain; no default empty component is inserted.

tests.name: SerreWeightComponent.singleton_dimension
tests.statement: For a compatible 1-deep GL_2 weight with one embedding, the component dimension is one and its torus-lift dimension is three.

tests.name: SerreWeightComponent.central_lift_is_data
tests.statement: A Serre weight without a specified compatible algebraic central lift does not determine the particular closed subvariety C_sigma^zeta in the common affine flag under this definition.

items.name: Representation-theoretic component labelling with repaired bound
items.statement: For regular dominant lambda and a Deligne–Lusztig R with a chosen(s,mu) presentation(lambda-eta)-compatible with zeta, assume m-genericity with m>=max(2n,h_lambda+n-1), and a congruent to s^-1(mu+eta) modulo varpi. Then the d_J-dimensional components of Mnv_J(<=lambda,nabla_a)_F(s^-1 t_(mu+eta)) are exactly C_sigma^zeta for sigma in JH(Rbar tensor W(lambda-eta)). The printed bound max(2n,h_lambda) is insufficient for M29's domain and M26's hypothesis; the p19 GL2 test in the reading ledger forces this repair. Preserve it as a source issue, not an unannounced strengthening.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Fixed points detected by the negative-loop chart
items.statement: For finite-type irreducible closed Y in Fl stable under Tdual times loop rotation, fixed point z, and open dense Yopen in Y, z lies in Y iff Y meets L--G z iff Yopen meets L--G z. Use the contracting chart cocharacter and irreducibility.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Obvious fixed points of an intrinsic component
items.statement: For C_(w1,omega), its Tdual^J-fixed points include all(t_omega s w1)^* for finite Weyl tuples s.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Polynomial-generic fixed-point saturation
items.statement: For each restricted affine component w1_j there exists a nonzero integral polynomial P_(w1_j) depending only on it, such that if P_(w1_j)(omega_j) is nonzero modulo p for every j, then the fixed points of C_(w1,omega) are exactly{w^* t_omega:w<=w0 w1}. The proof deforms b v g'g^-1+Ad(g)Diag(a), specializes b=0 to an affine Springer fibre, uses Boixeda Alvarez Theorem3.1, and spreads nonempty chart intersections to b=1. The external fixed-point theorem remains a prerequisite-reading obligation.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Intrinsic component is unibranch at fixed points
items.statement: Each C_(w1,omega) is unibranch at all its Tdual^J-fixed points, by applying the contracting-chart normalization argument to its intersection with the corresponding open chart.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Obvious weight gives a fixed point
items.statement: For sigma(n-1)-deep and rhobar with2(n-1)-generic presentation(s,mu), and their presentations compatible with the same zeta, sigma in Wobv(rhobar) implies wtilde(rhobar)^* lies in C_sigma^zeta.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Fixed point implies a predicted weight
items.statement: Under M35's hypotheses, wtilde(rhobar)^* in C_sigma^zeta implies sigma in W?(rhobar). This implication uses the Bruhat upper bound, without M33's polynomial condition.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Predicted weight gives a fixed point under polynomial genericity
items.statement: Under M35's hypotheses and P_(w1_j)(omega_j) nonzero modulo p in every component, sigma in W?(rhobar) implies wtilde(rhobar)^* in C_sigma^zeta. Keep this additional polynomial condition separate from M35–36's numerical depth.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Tame descent coefficient rings
items.statement: For a fixed1-generic presentation(s,mu) of tau, set r=ord(s0...s_(f-1)), K'/K unramified degree r, f'=fr, e'=p^f'-1, L'=K'((-p)^(1/e')). Gamma'=Gal(L'/K'), Gamma=Gal(L'/K). S_L',R=(W(k') tensor R)[[u']], phi acts by Witt Frobenius, identity on R, u'->u'^p. Gamma' scales u' by the fundamental character; the unramified generator acts on coefficients. v=u'^e', E(v)=v+p, and Gamma invariants give(W(k) tensor R)[[v]]. Retain the J'->J embedding-index projection and sigma_j=sigma0 Frobenius^-j.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Supply the coefficient rings, cyclic embedding indices, Frobenius and descent actions.
Supply the coefficient maps for inverting the Kisin parameter and taking descent invariants.

api.name: TameDescentCoefficients.mk
api.statement: From the fixed 1-generic presentation (s,mu), set r=ord(s_0...s_(f-1)), f_prime=fr and e_prime=p^f_prime-1. Choose the stated unramified extension and pi_prime with pi_prime^e_prime=-p; construct S_Lprime,R=(W(k_prime) tensor R)[[u_prime]] for the source p-adically complete coefficient algebras.

api.name: TameDescentCoefficients.frobenius
api.statement: Define phi by Witt Frobenius on W(k_prime), the identity on R and u_prime↦u_prime^p. Prove continuity and compatibility with the coefficient embedding; do not replace its action on R by absolute Frobenius.

api.name: TameDescentCoefficients.descent_action
api.statement: Gamma_prime scales u_prime by the fundamental character and the chosen unramified generator acts on W(k_prime), fixes u_prime and acts trivially on R. Verify the semidirect-product relation and commutation with phi.

api.name: TameDescentCoefficients.invariants
api.statement: Identify the full Gamma-invariant ring with (W(k) tensor R)[[v]], v=u_prime^e_prime, and carry the Eisenstein factor to E(v)=v+p. Keep the full Gamma invariants distinct from Gamma_prime invariants.

api.name: TameDescentCoefficients.embedding_components
api.statement: For sigma_jprime=sigma_0prime Frob^(-jprime), decompose the coefficient algebra by J_prime=Z/f_prime. Restriction to k is jprime↦jprime mod f, and phi sends the jprime-1 component to the jprime component.

api.name: TameDescentCoefficients.coefficient_map
api.statement: A continuous coefficient-algebra map induces a map of these completed power-series rings commuting with phi, descent and the embedding projections. Establish identity and composition before base changing modules.

tests.name: TameDescentCoefficients.rank_one_extension
tests.statement: For r=1 the unramified extension is trivial, J_prime=J and e_prime=p^f-1; there is still generally nontrivial tame ramification.

tests.name: TameDescentCoefficients.Frobenius_fixes_coefficients
tests.statement: For R=F_p[t], the formal coefficient rule is phi(t)=t whereas absolute Frobenius sends t to t^p. This distinguishes the rule before any completion hypotheses needed for the module category.

tests.name: TameDescentCoefficients.cyclic_target
tests.statement: For f_prime=3, the source of partial Frobenius at target jprime=0 is component 2, not component 1.

items.name: Integral Iwahori and its pro-unipotent subgroup
items.statement: I(R) consists of invertible R[[v]] matrices upper triangular modulo v; I1 has unipotent upper triangular reduction. I=Tdual semidirect I1. For p-adically complete Noetherian O-algebras, R[[v+p]]=R[[v]] and I=L+G_O; for p-nilpotent R, the Laurent rings agree. These comparisons do not hold for arbitrary O-algebras, and Frobenius on the shifted series ring requires the stated completeness.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Identify permissible eigenbasis changes after the orientation conjugation.
Supply the full basis group, its pro-unipotent subgroup and the residual torus action.

api.name: IntegralIwahori.subgroup
api.statement: Define I(R) as the inverse image of the upper-triangular Borel under GL_n(R[[v]])→GL_n(R); define I1 using the upper-unitriangular subgroup, with diagonal entries 1 modulo v.

api.name: IntegralIwahori.diagonal_quotient
api.statement: The diagonal entries modulo v give a surjective homomorphism I→Tdual with kernel I1. Constant diagonal matrices split it, giving I=Tdual semidirect I1 and a unique factorization after fixing the order.

api.name: IntegralIwahori.map
api.statement: Coefficient maps preserve both subgroups and commute with diagonal reduction, the torus section and factorization.

api.name: IntegralIwahori.shifted_series
api.statement: For p-adically complete Noetherian R in the source category, construct the continuous substitution isomorphism R[[v+p]]≅R[[v]]. Explain convergence of every coefficient sum; identify I with L+G_O on this domain.

api.name: IntegralIwahori.localized_shift
api.statement: For p-nilpotent R, the shifted and unshifted Laurent rings identify because v+p=v(1+p/v) has a finite geometric-series inverse. This argument does not give the same Laurent-ring comparison over arbitrary O-algebras.

api.name: IntegralIwahori.Lie_kernel
api.statement: The Lie algebra of I1 has strictly upper-triangular reduction modulo v. In particular, its constant diagonal coefficients vanish; retain this constraint in the infinitesimal gauge calculation K19.

tests.name: IntegralIwahori.unipotent_not_identity
tests.statement: I+E_12 lies in I1 for n=2 although its reduction is not the identity. I1 is larger than the kernel of reduction modulo v.

tests.name: IntegralIwahori.diagonal_excluded
tests.statement: A constant diag(a,1) with a a unit different from 1 belongs to I but not I1.

tests.name: IntegralIwahori.nilpotent_shift
tests.statement: Over Z/125, (v+5)^(-1)=v^(-1)-5v^(-2)+25v^(-3); multiplying by v+5 gives 1. The negative terms must be retained.

items.name: Breuil–Kisin module of bounded height
items.statement: For p-adically complete R, Y^[0,h](R) consists of finite projective rank-n S_L',R modules M with an injective linearized Frobenius phi* M->M whose cokernel is killed by E(v)^h. Embedding decomposition gives partial Frobenius from the j'-1 summand to j'; j' denotes the target embedding.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Add tame descent without changing the bounded-height Frobenius condition.
Express height in oriented matrices and preserve it under semisimplification.

api.name: HeightBoundedKisinModule.mk
api.statement: A datum is a finite projective constant-rank-n S_Lprime,R-module and an injective S-linear map Phi:phi* M→M whose cokernel is annihilated by E(v)^h, with h>=0.

api.name: HeightBoundedKisinModule.linearization
api.statement: Relate Phi to a phi-semilinear map on M using the tensor-product universal property. Preserve the distinction between injectivity of Phi and surjectivity of the underlying semilinear map.

api.name: HeightBoundedKisinModule.height_factorization
api.statement: The height condition is equivalent to existence of Psi:M→phi* M with Phi Psi=E^h and Psi Phi=E^h; use injectivity of Phi for the second identity and uniqueness.

api.name: HeightBoundedKisinModule.partial_Frobenius
api.statement: Decompose Phi into maps phi* M^(jprime-1)→M^(jprime), with the superscript naming the target. Direct sum of these partial maps reconstructs Phi.

api.name: HeightBoundedKisinModule.matrix_height
api.statement: After choosing local free bases, the raw matrix C has integral entries and E^h C^(-1) has integral entries in the localization by E; prove equivalence with the module height condition under the source E-regularity hypotheses.

api.name: HeightBoundedKisinModule.base_change
api.statement: Construct completed coefficient base change, including finite projectivity and the height factorization. Prove injectivity after base change using E-regularity in the target source ring, rather than asserting that arbitrary tensoring preserves injections.

tests.name: HeightBoundedKisinModule.height_zero
tests.statement: For h=0, Psi is an inverse to Phi: the linearized Frobenius is an isomorphism.

tests.name: HeightBoundedKisinModule.rank_one_height
tests.statement: In a free rank-one component with Phi multiplication by E^c, the height bound holds exactly when 0<=c<=h, in an E-regular power-series ring with E a nonunit.

tests.name: HeightBoundedKisinModule.wrong_partial_index
tests.statement: On three cyclic embedding components, a matrix at target 0 acts on phi* M^2; using M^1 fails the coefficient idempotent compatibility.

items.name: Tame descent type on Breuil–Kisin modules
items.statement: Y^[0,h],tau adds a semilinear Gamma-action commuting with Frobenius and M^(j')/u' M^(j') isomorphic to tau-dual tensor R as a Gamma'-representation. Extending Gamma' descent is equivalent to an isomorphism for the unramified generator satisfying its cocycle condition. This functor is a p-adic formal algebraic stack, via CEGS and Caraiani–Levin; the dual type is forced by the contravariant Galois functor.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Choose character eigenbases and descend the oriented matrices to J.
Present the stack by basis changes and descend its associated etale module.

api.name: KisinDescentType.mk
api.statement: Add a semilinear Gamma-action commuting with Phi and require M^(jprime)/u_prime M^(jprime)≅tau_dual tensor R as a Gamma_prime-representation, for every jprime.

api.name: KisinDescentType.unramified_cocycle
api.statement: Starting with Gamma_prime descent, extending to Gamma is equivalent to an isomorphism iota_M:(sigma^f)*M→M satisfying the order-r cocycle and the specified conjugation relation with Gamma_prime.

api.name: KisinDescentType.equivariant_morphism
api.statement: A morphism is S-linear and commutes with both linearized Frobenius and every descent operator. These conditions are preserved by identity, composition and coefficient base change.

api.name: KisinDescentType.type_locality
api.statement: The prescribed type is a local isomorphism condition on the character eigensummands of M/u_prime M. Use the invertibility of |Gamma_prime| to construct projectors; do not infer global free eigenbases from finite projectivity.

api.name: KisinDescentType.forget
api.statement: Forget descent to K03 and retain its height bound. Keep the type condition on the mod-u_prime fibres, not on arbitrary choices of raw Frobenius matrices.

api.name: KisinDescentType.formal_stack
api.statement: Package descent of objects and isomorphisms and import the formal algebraicity theorem from CEGS/Caraiani–Levin with its coefficient hypotheses. The type is tau_dual because the later Galois functor is contravariant.

tests.name: KisinDescentType.trivial_unramified_cocycle
tests.statement: When r=1, the unramified cocycle forces the corresponding descent identification to be the identity after the canonical coefficient identification.

tests.name: KisinDescentType.dual_character
tests.statement: For rank one of tame type chi, the eigenline in M/u_prime M carries chi^(-1), not chi.

tests.name: KisinDescentType.cocycle_required
tests.statement: For a cyclic descent group of order 2 acting trivially on coefficients, a chosen scalar identification c with c^2!=1 does not extend to descent data.

items.name: Eigenbasis with descent compatibility
items.statement: An eigenbasis is an ordered basis in each embedding summand with ith vector carrying character chi_i^-1 from(2.12), compatible with the unramified descent isomorphism up to the permutation s_tau. The bases are chosen relative to the fixed presentation of tau.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Define oriented matrices and their change-of-basis rule.
Refine an eigenbasis to a gauge basis under the genericity and completeness assumptions.

api.name: DescentEigenbasis.mk
api.statement: Choose an ordered basis beta^(jprime) in each embedding summand, whose ith vector has character chi_i^(-1), relative to the fixed lowest-alcove presentation.

api.name: DescentEigenbasis.unramified_compatibility
api.statement: Require compatibility with iota_M with the source permutation s_tau. It is compatibility of the corresponding unordered bases with a specified reordering, not equality of their ordered lists.

api.name: DescentEigenbasis.local_existence
api.statement: After the allowed Zariski localization of the coefficient base, lift the character basis modulo u_prime to an eigenbasis using tame projectors and the source lifting theorem.

api.name: DescentEigenbasis.transition
api.statement: Given beta_2 D=beta_1, characterize D by the descent characters and unramified compatibility. Orientation conjugation turns D into a J-periodic tuple in I; the inverse conjugation reconstructs D.

api.name: DescentEigenbasis.basis_torsor
api.statement: On a locus with an eigenbasis, changes form a torsor for I^J under the established transition equivalence. State the action order using beta_2 D=beta_1.

api.name: DescentEigenbasis.coefficient_map
api.statement: Base change sends every basis vector and its character relation to the corresponding eigenbasis and preserves the unramified permutation.

tests.name: DescentEigenbasis.rank_one_scaling
tests.statement: Scaling a rank-one eigenbasis by a coefficient unit preserves its character, with the cyclic descent compatibility imposed on the full tuple.

tests.name: DescentEigenbasis.permuted_order
tests.statement: If s_tau is the transposition of two distinct character lines, the unramified map exchanges their positions. Requiring the ordered tuple to be fixed rejects a valid eigenbasis.

tests.name: DescentEigenbasis.basis_not_automatic
tests.statement: A finite projective module need not be globally free. The constructor requires a basis or a local trivialization; the module structure alone is insufficient.

items.name: Oriented partial Frobenius matrices
items.statement: Extend alpha to J' by alpha'_(j+kf)=s_tau^-k(alpha_j), put a'^(j')=sum_(i=0)^(f'-1)p^i alpha'_(-j'+i), and s'_or,j+kf=s_tau^(k+1)s_(f-1)^-1...s_(j+1)^-1. For raw Frobenius matrix C^(j'), define A^(j')=Ad((s'_or,j')^-1 u'^(-a'^(j')))(C^(j')). Orientation makes(s'_or)^-1 a' dominant. A depends only on j' modulo f, lies in L+M, and the height condition is E(v)^h A^-1 in L+M. Spell out this construction rather than identifying it with a change of type.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Compute basis changes and define shape.
Convert the normalized Kisin matrix into the etale Frobenius matrix by right multiplication.

api.name: OrientedKisinMatrix.orientation_data
api.statement: Define alpha_prime_(j+kf)=s_tau^(-k)alpha_j, a_prime^(jprime)=sum_(i=0)^(fprime-1) p^i alpha_prime_(-jprime+i), and sor_prime_(j+kf)=s_tau^(k+1)s_(f-1)^(-1)...s_(j+1)^(-1). Keep this order and the empty product convention.

api.name: OrientedKisinMatrix.normalize
api.statement: For the raw target-indexed partial Frobenius matrix C^(jprime), set A^(jprime)=Ad((sor_prime)^(-1) diag(u_prime^(-a_prime)))(C^(jprime)). Construct the descent-invariant entries in the v-loop ring.

api.name: OrientedKisinMatrix.periodicity_height
api.statement: Prove A depends only on jprime modulo f, belongs to L+M, and E^h A^(-1) belongs to L+M. The latter two conditions are equivalent to the height condition for the reconstructed eigenbasis object.

api.name: OrientedKisinMatrix.basis_change
api.statement: If beta_2 D=beta_1 and I_j=Ad((sor_prime)^(-1)u_prime^(-a_prime))(D^(jprime)), then A_beta2^j=I_j A_beta1^j Ad(z_tau,j)(phi(I_(j-1)))^(-1), where z_tau,j=s_j^(-1)v^(mu_j+eta_j).

api.name: OrientedKisinMatrix.reconstruct
api.statement: For a J-periodic tuple satisfying the two Iwahori matrix bounds, reverse the orientation conjugation and equip the free modules with the specified character and unramified descent data. Prove the two constructions inverse up to the basis-preserving isomorphism used in K15.

api.name: OrientedKisinMatrix.etale_matrix
api.statement: In the descended invariant basis, the etale partial Frobenius matrix is A_beta^j z_tau,j. The factor occurs on the right; this is not generally z_tau,j A_beta^j.

tests.name: OrientedKisinMatrix.identity_basis_change
tests.statement: I_j=1 in every component fixes A_j.

tests.name: OrientedKisinMatrix.noncommuting_etale_factor
tests.statement: For A=I+cE_12 and z=diag(v,1), A z has upper-right entry c whereas z A has upper-right entry vc.

tests.name: OrientedKisinMatrix.constant_cyclic_change
tests.statement: In rank one with constants d_j, phi fixes d_j, and A_beta2^j=d_j A_beta1^j d_(j-1)^(-1). For one embedding this scalar action is trivial.

items.name: Compatibility with earlier embedding conventions
items.statement: The earlier LLHL/LLHLM presentation is(s_minus,j,mu_minus,j)=(s_(f-j),mu_(f-j)); its partial Frobenius index is j'-1 for the present target-indexed j'. The orientation, a' exponents and chi characters agree after this translation, and the old star factor becomes s_j+1^-1 t_(mu_j+1+eta_j+1). Use these explicit adapters for all cited earlier lemmas.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Change of eigenbasis is twisted Frobenius conjugation
items.statement: If beta2^(j') D^(j')=beta1^(j'), then I^(j')=Ad((s'_or)^-1 u'^(-a'))D lies in I(R), depends only on j' modulo f, and A_beta2^j=I^j A_beta1^j Ad(s_j^-1 v^(mu_j+eta_j))(phi(I^(j-1)))^-1. Conversely every such periodic tuple in I gives an eigenbasis change.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Shape of a residual Kisin module
items.statement: For M over a field F'/F, its shape relative to the chosen tau presentation is z in Wtilde-dual^J with A_beta^j in I(F') z_j I(F') for every eigenbasis. The change-of-basis formula proves independence of beta.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Place every shape-z field point in the z-gauge open.
Relate shape to Hodge admissibility and transfer it to residual Galois representations.

api.name: ResidualKisinShape.double_coset
api.statement: Over a field Fprime/F, define shape z by A_beta^j∈I(Fprime) z_j I(Fprime) for all j, relative to the fixed type presentation.

api.name: ResidualKisinShape.unique
api.statement: Use the affine Bruhat decomposition to prove uniqueness of z; assemble componentwise uniqueness for the J-tuple.

api.name: ResidualKisinShape.basis_independent
api.statement: Apply K08 and the stated Iwahori containment of the Frobenius-conjugated transition factor to prove independence of beta.

api.name: ResidualKisinShape.field_extension
api.statement: Prove shape is preserved by field extension using the base-change-compatible Schubert-cell decomposition, not a general ring-point double-coset classification.

api.name: ResidualKisinShape.gauge_open
api.statement: A shape-z point belongs to the z-gauge open; the converse asserts more than open membership and must not be exported.

api.name: ResidualKisinShape.admissible_bound
api.statement: Under K24, membership in Y^<=lambda,tau is equivalent to shape in Adm-dual(lambda). Retain the source hypotheses needed to use the local-model diagram.

tests.name: ResidualKisinShape.rank_one_valuation
tests.statement: For n=1 at p=0, A=v^c u with u a power-series unit has shape c; multiplying by I on either side leaves c unchanged.

tests.name: ResidualKisinShape.valuation_boundary
tests.statement: v^c and v^(c+1) have different rank-one shapes over a field.

tests.name: ResidualKisinShape.field_domain
tests.statement: Over F[epsilon]/(epsilon^2), do not define a unique Weyl label merely by reusing the field-point double-coset constructor; families require the chart/stratification interfaces.

items.name: Frobenius contraction on I1
items.statement: For an m-generic presentation(s,mu) and I in I1(R), Ad(s_j^-1 v^(mu_j+eta_j))(phi(I)) is congruent to1 modulo v^(m+1).
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Higher congruence contraction for group elements
items.statement: Assume that τ admits an m-generic lowest alcove presentation (s, μ). Let R be an O-algebra. If I ∈ GL_n(R[[v]]), m ≥ 1, and I ≡ 1 mod v^k, then Ad(s_j^{-1} v^{μ_j+η_j})(φ(I)) ≡ 1 mod v^{(k−1)p+m+1}. The paper states no range for k. 'm ≥ 1' is presumably a misprint for 'k ≥ 1' (see sourceIssues); applications use k ≥ 2.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Higher congruence contraction for matrices
items.statement: Assume that τ admits an m-generic lowest alcove presentation (s, μ). Let R be an O-algebra. If Y ∈ v^k Mat_n(R[[v]]), then Ad(s_j^{-1} v^{μ_j+η_j})(φ(Y)) ∈ v^{(k−1)p+m+1} Mat_n(R[[v]]).
items.note: Split from K11. The paper prints no proof ('leave the rest to the reader'). The entrywise estimate from the proof of (a) gives it: m < ⟨μ_j+η_j, α^∨⟩ < p − m for α ∈ Φ^+, so p > m+1. Then φ(Y) ∈ v^{kp}Mat_n. Ad(v^{μ_j+η_j}) lowers the valuation of a −α-entry by at most p−m−1 and does not lower the diagonal or α-entries, and Ad(s_j^{-1}) only permutes entries. k is an integer. The applications use k ≥ 1. On PDF112 the case k = 0 needs corrected (c) instead (K12, E16).

uses.how: The existence part of the proof of Lemma 5.2.2 (PDF108–109) gets J_i − J_{i−1} ∈ v^{p(i−2)}Mat_n by induction.
The proof of Proposition 5.2.7 (PDF112) uses Y_j ≡ 0 mod v^k ⇒ Ad(A s_j^{-1}v^{μ_j+η_j})(φ(Y_{j−1})) ≡ 0 mod v^{k+1}, which makes the linear map an automorphism plus a topologically nilpotent map.

items.name: Lie I1 Frobenius contraction, corrected
items.statement: The linearization needed subsequently is: if Y modulo v is STRICTLY upper triangular, then Ad(s_j^-1 v^(mu_j+eta_j))(phi(Y)) is divisible by v^(m+1). The printed version only assumes upper triangular and omits phi; Y=identity refutes it. Both repairs are required, and this source issue must be recorded before using the result.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Height-bounded loop spaces
items.statement: For integers a<=b, L^[a,b]G_O requires g in(v+p)^a L+M and(v+p)^b g^-1 in L+M; take its positive-loop quotient Gr^[a,b]. Separately L^[a,b]GLn_F requires v^-a A and v^b A^-1 integral matrices, without Iwahori lower-entry restrictions; its quotient Fl^[a,b] is finite type closed. Gr^[a,b]_F is generally a strict subspace of Fl^[a,b]. Central translation shifts both height bounds.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Present bounded-height Kisin modules by the Frobenius-twisted quotient.
Supply the ordinary residual bounded flags used after translation.

api.name: HeightBoundedLoops.mixed_bounds
api.statement: For a<=b, impose (v+p)^(-a)g∈L+M_O and (v+p)^b g^(-1)∈L+M_O; quotient on the left by L+G_O to define Gr^[a,b].

api.name: HeightBoundedLoops.residual_bounds
api.statement: Separately impose v^(-a)A and v^b A^(-1) in Mat_n(R[[v]]) and quotient on the left by I to define Fl^[a,b]. No upper-triangular-mod-v condition is part of these two ordinary matrix bounds.

api.name: HeightBoundedLoops.central_shift
api.statement: Multiplication by the central scalar (v+p)^m shifts mixed bounds [a,b] to [a+m,b+m]; v^m gives the corresponding residual equivalence.

api.name: HeightBoundedLoops.relax_bounds
api.statement: If a_prime<=a and b<=b_prime, inclusion of bounds induces a closed inclusion of the corresponding bounded quotients, compatible with composition.

api.name: HeightBoundedLoops.finite_type_closed
api.statement: Import/prove the finite-type closed bounded affine-flag construction for Fl^[a,b], retaining its immersion in the ambient affine flag.

api.name: HeightBoundedLoops.special_fiber_comparison
api.statement: Reduction gives a natural subspace Gr^[a,b]_F inside Fl^[a,b], in general strictly smaller. Establish the comparison through the Iwahori matrix bounds rather than declaring the two definitions equal.

tests.name: HeightBoundedLoops.rank_one_interval
tests.statement: For A=v^c over a field, both bounded conditions hold precisely when a<=c<=b.

tests.name: HeightBoundedLoops.central_shift_test
tests.statement: A rank-one exponent c in [a,b] becomes c+m in [a+m,b+m].

tests.name: HeightBoundedLoops.Iwahori_strictness
tests.statement: For n=2 and [a,b]=[0,0], the constant permutation matrix exchanging the two coordinates satisfies the ordinary bounds but is not upper triangular modulo v. Its left-I coset is not in the mixed special-fibre bound.

items.name: Twisted conjugation actions
items.statement: On loop tuples, I acts on A by I^j A^j Ad(s_j^-1 v^(mu_j+eta_j))(phi(I^(j-1)))^-1. The twisted conjugation action without Frobenius uses the same formula with phi omitted. Later residual torus actions agree because phi fixes constants; the full mixed-characteristic I1 actions need not agree.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Form the quotient stack and solve the residual straightening equation.
Distinguish the torus actions in the two chart quotients and the obstruction to gluing over O.

api.name: TwistedKisinAction.Frobenius_action
api.statement: For z_j=s_j^(-1)v^(mu_j+eta_j), define (I star_phi A)_j=I_j A_j Ad(z_j)(phi(I_(j-1)))^(-1). Retain the cyclic predecessor index.

api.name: TwistedKisinAction.ordinary_action
api.statement: Define star by the same formula with phi omitted. Prove the respective domain is preserved using the source genericity and height estimates when those are required.

api.name: TwistedKisinAction.action_laws
api.statement: Prove 1 star A=A and I star (J star A)=(IJ) star A componentwise, for each action, by the homomorphism property of phi and Ad(z).

api.name: TwistedKisinAction.torus_agreement
api.statement: On constant diagonal tuples, phi acts identically, so star_phi and star agree. This equality does not identify either action with ordinary left translation on the chart.

api.name: TwistedKisinAction.straightening_equation
api.statement: In the residual generic domain, solving X=I A Ad(z)(phi(I_prev))^(-1) A^(-1) is equivalent to I=X A Ad(z)(phi(I_prev)) A^(-1). Use the contraction theorem K16 with the retained E17 correction.

api.name: TwistedKisinAction.mixed_gluing_boundary
api.statement: Preserve Warning5.3.2: the quotient change that straightens the residual action need not take values in I1 over a mixed-characteristic thickening. Do not glue the integral local-model diagrams merely from the residual comparison.

tests.name: TwistedKisinAction.one_component_rank_one_torus
tests.statement: For |J|=1 and n=1, constant torus twisted conjugation is trivial, whereas left multiplication by the same scalar generally is not.

tests.name: TwistedKisinAction.Frobenius_not_ordinary
tests.statement: Over F_p[[v]], phi(1+v)=1+v^p, so the full power-series group actions are not identified by their agreement on constants.

tests.name: TwistedKisinAction.negative_poles_in_thickening
tests.statement: For p=11 in R=Z/11^5, v^3/(v+11)=v^2-11v+121-1331v^(-1)+14641v^(-2). Thus 1-v^3/(v+11) has negative Laurent coefficients, unlike its reduction modulo 11. This tests the pole mechanism of Warning5.3.2, without asserting a separately chosen type presentation.

items.name: Quotient presentation of the Kisin stack
items.statement: For a lowest-alcove presentation of tau, Y^[0,h],tau is the p-adic completion of the quotient of(L^[0,h]G_O)^J by twisted Frobenius conjugation of(L+G_O)^J. Eigenbases form torsors locally and exist Zariski locally by prime-to-p descent averaging.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Residual straightening of I1 conjugation
items.statement: For an F-algebra R, A1,A2 in L^[0,h]GLn(R)^J and z=s^-1 t_(mu+eta) with mu(h+1)-deep, tuples I in I1^J satisfying A2^j z_j=I^j A1^j z_j phi(I^(j-1))^-1 biject tuples X in I1^J satisfying A2^j=X_j A1^j. The inverse is a v-adic contraction; this is a residual statement.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Residual Kisin stack as a torus quotient
items.statement: If mu is(h+1)-deep, Y^[0,h],tau_F identifies with the quotient of the I1-torsor lift of Gr^[0,h]_F^J by the(s,mu)-twisted Tdual^J conjugation action, and embeds in the analogous bounded flag quotient.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Gauge opens and gauge bases
items.statement: Residual chart covers from U(z) define an open substack Y^[0,h],tau_F(z); its p-adic open thickening is Y^[0,h],tau(z). M admits z-gauge when its reduction lies there. A z-gauge basis is an eigenbasis with every A_beta^j in Tdual(R)U(z_j)(R). Shape z implies z-gauge over a field, but gauge is an open condition whereas fixed shape is only locally closed.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Produce gauge bases, with torus ambiguity, on the formal open.
Compare chart geometry with the local model and define semisimple Kisin points.

api.name: KisinGaugeChart.residual_open
api.statement: Use the U(z)T chart and the residual quotient presentation to define Y_F^[0,h],tau(z) as an open substack.

api.name: KisinGaugeChart.formal_open
api.statement: Lift this open uniquely to the p-adic formal stack through the identification of its underlying topological space with that of its special fibre.

api.name: KisinGaugeChart.gauge_basis
api.statement: A z-gauge basis is an eigenbasis with A_beta^j∈Tdual(R)U(z_j)(R) for every j. Keep the torus factor on the specified side.

api.name: KisinGaugeChart.existence
api.statement: For the source complete Noetherian coefficient algebras and (h+1)-deep mu, prove that an object in this open admits gauge bases Zariski locally, using K19 and its corrected infinitesimal calculation.

api.name: KisinGaugeChart.uniqueness
api.statement: Under the same hypotheses, gauge eigenbases form the stated Tdual^J torsor. The uniqueness assertion concerns eigenbases satisfying gauge, not arbitrary bases of the underlying module.

api.name: KisinGaugeChart.shape_implication
api.statement: Over a field, shape z implies membership in the z-gauge open. Distinguish this open neighbourhood from the locally closed fixed-shape stratum.

tests.name: KisinGaugeChart.fixed_point_in_chart
tests.statement: The distinguished monomial point z belongs to its own chart and has shape z.

tests.name: KisinGaugeChart.infinitesimal_diagonal
tests.statement: A nonzero constant diagonal infinitesimal matrix belongs to Lie I but not Lie I1; it cannot be used as an I1 gauge correction in K19.

tests.name: KisinGaugeChart.open_not_stratum
tests.statement: A proof of open membership after deformation supplies gauge, not constancy of the Schubert-cell label; fixed shape requires a separate locally closed condition.

items.name: Existence and uniqueness of gauge bases
items.statement: For mu(h+1)-deep, R Noetherian p-adically complete and M admitting an eigenbasis and z-gauge, a z-gauge basis exists and is unique up to Tdual^J(R) scaling (the J'-tuple is constant modulo f). The induction splits Lie LG=Lie L--G direct-sum Lie T direct-sum Lie I1, then inverts identity minus a topologically nilpotent operator. Lie I1 has strictly upper triangular reduction; the proof's printed 'unipotent' is incorrect for a Lie module.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Local model diagram for bounded-height Kisin modules
items.statement: For mu(h+1)-deep and z, the p-completed lifted chart U^[0,h](z) has two Tdual^J-torsor maps: to Y^[0,h],tau(z) by twisted conjugation and to U^[0,h](z) by left translation. Both targets embed openly into the Kisin stack and bounded Grassmannian respectively. The actions are different; the diagrams glue globally over F, but not generally over O (Warning5.3.2).
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Bounded Hodge-type Kisin substack
items.statement: For effective dominant tuple lambda_j in[0,h]^n, Y^<=lambda,tau is the O-flat p-adic formal closed substack with reduced versal rings whose finite-DVR points have Hodge type<=lambda. This is the elementary-divisor condition A_beta^j in the generic Schubert closure SE(lambda_j), established using the graded chi-isotypic pieces of M/E(v)M.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Pull back bounded local models and characterize the possible residual shapes.
Preserve the closed Hodge bound under the semisimplification family.

api.name: BoundedHodgeKisinStack.domain
api.statement: Use an effective dominant tuple lambda with each entry in [0,h]; record the ambient height h and the fixed descent type tau.

api.name: BoundedHodgeKisinStack.flat_reduced_closure
api.statement: Construct the O-flat formal closed substack with reduced versal rings and the prescribed finite-DVR point condition. Generic point data alone is not a substitute for the flat/reduced construction.

api.name: BoundedHodgeKisinStack.DVR_point_criterion
api.statement: For a finite extension Eprime/E with integers Oprime, an Oprime-point belongs exactly when its Hodge type is <=lambda in the source partial order.

api.name: BoundedHodgeKisinStack.elementary_divisors
api.statement: Identify this criterion with A_beta^j in the generic Schubert closure S_E(lambda_j) by the graded chi-isotypic pieces of M/E(v)M. Preserve the (v+p)-adic parameter and the target embedding convention.

api.name: BoundedHodgeKisinStack.chart_pullback
api.statement: Under K22, pull back to U(z,<=lambda) in the gauge diagram; prove equality of the integral closed subspaces using the stated flatness, reducedness and DVR-point detection hypotheses.

api.name: BoundedHodgeKisinStack.bound_inclusion
api.statement: A dominant lambda_prime<=lambda with the same central class induces inclusion of the Hodge-bounded substacks inside the common height stack, compatible with the local-model inclusion.

tests.name: BoundedHodgeKisinStack.rank_one_exact_weight
tests.statement: For a rank-one partial matrix (v+p)^c times a unit, the Hodge weight is c. For lambda=c, its finite-DVR point has the required type.

tests.name: BoundedHodgeKisinStack.wrong_central_class
tests.statement: For rank one, distinct weights do not become ordered merely as integers: the dominance order within a fixed central class is equality.

tests.name: BoundedHodgeKisinStack.generic_points_insufficient
tests.statement: The closed subschemes of Spec O[x] given by (x) and (varpi*x) have equal generic fibres but different integral structures. The latter is not O-flat; the flatness condition in the constructor cannot be omitted.

items.name: Pappas–Zhu local model diagram with Hodge bound
items.statement: For mu(h+1)-deep, lambda_j in[0,h]^n and z, K20 restricts to the lifted chart U(z,<=lambda), with torsor targets Y^<=lambda,tau(z) and the open chart U(z,<=lambda) of M_J(<=lambda). Take p-adic completions throughout. Equality of the reduced flat pullbacks is checked on finite-extension DVR points.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Nonempty Kisin charts are admissible
items.statement: Under K22's hypotheses, Y^<=lambda,tau(z) is nonempty iff z belongs to Adm-dual(lambda).
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Hodge-bound membership detected by shape
items.statement: Under K22's hypotheses, for finite F'/F a module M over F' lies in Y^<=lambda,tau iff its shape relative to tau is in Adm-dual(lambda).
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Etale Frobenius modules with descent
items.statement: O_E,K is the p-adic completion of W(k)[[v]][1/v], and O_E,L' the analogous u' ring. Rank-n finite projective modules over their completed tensor product with R carry semilinear Frobenius whose linearization is an isomorphism, with commuting Gamma descent in the L' version. They form fppf stacks over Spf O.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Receive the proper forgetful map and the generic closed-immersion theorem.
Apply the field-of-norms antiequivalence after forgetting the Kisin lattice.

api.name: EtaleFrobeniusModule.coefficient_ring
api.statement: Form O_E,K as the p-adic completion of W(k)[[v]][1/v], and O_E,Lprime using u_prime. For a source coefficient algebra R use the completed tensor product with R.

api.name: EtaleFrobeniusModule.mk
api.statement: A rank-n object is finite projective over the completed coefficient ring with a phi-semilinear operator whose linearization phi* D→D is an isomorphism.

api.name: EtaleFrobeniusModule.descent_version
api.statement: On the Lprime ring add semilinear Gamma descent commuting with phi; define morphisms by compatibility with both structures.

api.name: EtaleFrobeniusModule.matrix_criterion
api.statement: On a free local chart the linearization is represented by an invertible matrix. This requires invertibility of that matrix, not bijectivity of the coefficient-ring Frobenius.

api.name: EtaleFrobeniusModule.base_change
api.statement: Completed coefficient extension preserves finite projectivity and the inverse of the linearized Frobenius; establish identity and composition with the completion comparison maps.

api.name: EtaleFrobeniusModule.fppf_stack
api.statement: Establish effective fppf descent for objects and isomorphisms and form the formal stack over Spf O, importing the source algebraicity inputs separately.

tests.name: EtaleFrobeniusModule.rank_one_unit
tests.statement: A free rank-one object whose linearized Frobenius matrix is a coefficient-ring unit is etale.

tests.name: EtaleFrobeniusModule.semilinear_not_surjective
tests.statement: On F_p((v)), phi(v)=v^p is not surjective, but the rank-one module with basis e and phi(e)=e has linearization matrix 1 and is etale.

tests.name: EtaleFrobeniusModule.zero_matrix
tests.statement: In positive rank the zero Frobenius matrix does not define an etale object because its linearization is not an isomorphism.

items.name: Forget the Kisin lattice and descend
items.statement: epsilon_tau(M) is the Gamma-invariant part after inverting u' and completing. It defines a map from Y^[0,h],tau to the etale Frobenius stack independent of the chosen presentation. Descent invariants give an equivalence between the etale module stack with L'/K descent and the K-valued one, inverse to scalar extension.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Prove properness, compute the invariant Frobenius matrices and obtain a generic closed immersion.
Use uniqueness of a generic Kisin lift to define representation shape.

api.name: ForgetKisinLattice.invert_complete
api.statement: From a Kisin module, invert u_prime and extend to the p-adically completed etale coefficient ring. Show E becomes a unit there and hence the bounded-height Frobenius linearization becomes an isomorphism.

api.name: ForgetKisinLattice.descent_invariants
api.statement: Take Gamma invariants of the resulting etale module to obtain epsilon_tau(M) over the K coefficient ring.

api.name: ForgetKisinLattice.descent_equivalence
api.statement: Identify etale Lprime-modules with descent and etale K-modules by invariants and scalar extension, including the two natural inverse isomorphisms.

api.name: ForgetKisinLattice.presentation_independent
api.statement: The descended object is independent of the lowest-alcove presentation and eigenbasis; compare presentations through the intrinsic module functor rather than equating their coordinate matrices.

api.name: ForgetKisinLattice.matrix_formula
api.statement: In the invariant basis of K28, the partial matrix is A_beta^j s_j^(-1)v^(mu_j+eta_j), with the cyclic Frobenius convention and this right-factor order.

api.name: ForgetKisinLattice.geometry_hypotheses
api.statement: Export properness using K27 and closed immersion using K29 only with its genericity assumptions. Do not make full faithfulness part of the unconditional forgetful construction.

tests.name: ForgetKisinLattice.E_unit
tests.statement: After inverting v and completing p-adically, E=v+p=v(1+p/v) has inverse v^(-1) sum_(m>=0)(-p/v)^m. Convergence uses the p-adic topology.

tests.name: ForgetKisinLattice.basis_invariance
tests.statement: A change of Kisin eigenbasis changes A z by the usual cyclic Frobenius basis-change formula, so the associated etale object is isomorphic.

tests.name: ForgetKisinLattice.lattice_not_remembered
