tests.statement: The construction forgets the embedded power-series lattice. Uniqueness of such a lattice cannot be inferred from the definition of the etale object; it requires K29 and its hypotheses.

items.name: Properness of the lattice-forgetting map
items.statement: epsilon_tau is representable by algebraic spaces, proper and of finite presentation, using CEGS's bounded-height lattice moduli and descent equivalence.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Etale Frobenius matrix attached to an eigenbasis
items.statement: An eigenbasis beta determines a basis of epsilon_tau(M) in which the jth partial Frobenius matrix is A_beta^j s_j^-1 v^(mu_j+eta_j). This is the explicit compatibility with K08 and is needed to compare different types inside one etale stack.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Generic triviality of Kisin fibres as a closed immersion
items.statement: For h>=0 and tau(h+1)-generic, epsilon_tau is a monomorphism of p-adic formal stacks and hence a closed immersion. This is full faithfulness on all allowed coefficient rings, stronger than uniqueness only at field-valued points.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Pole elimination for etale isomorphisms
items.statement: For R an F-algebra, A1,A2 in L^[0,h]GLn(R)^J and z=s^-1 t_(mu+eta) with mu(h+1)-deep, any tuple I in GLn(R((v)))^J with A2^j z_j=I^j A1^j z_j phi(I^(j-1))^-1 actually lies in I_F(R)^J. The cyclic pole-order inequalities first eliminate negative powers, then force upper-triangular reduction.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Pole elimination for infinitesimal isomorphisms
items.statement: Under the same depth/height hypotheses, for an R-module J and Y_j in Matn(J((v))) with Y_j-Ad(A^j z_j)phi(Y_(j-1)) in v^-h Matn(J[[v]]), all Y_j lie in Lie I_F(J). This lifts K30 across coefficient nilpotents.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Translated bounded flags and shifted torus action
items.statement: Fl^[a,b]_(J,z) is the product of I1\\(L^[a,b]GLn)z_j. For z=sigma^-1 t_(nu+eta) and nu(b-a+1)-deep, the Frobenius-matrix map descends to this flag lift and then to the shifted Tdual^J conjugation quotient, where D acts by D_j A_j z_j D_(j-1)^-1.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Embed the shifted torus quotient into the residual etale stack.
Compare different tame types inside a common translated bound.

api.name: TranslatedBoundedFlags.mk
api.statement: For integers a<=b and a tuple z, form the product over j of I1\(L^[a,b]GL_n)z_j inside the lifted affine flag. This uses I1, not I.

api.name: TranslatedBoundedFlags.parameter_domain
api.statement: For the etale embedding theorem require z=sigma^(-1)t_(nu+eta) with nu (b-a+1)-deep. Record this numerical margin alongside the bound.

api.name: TranslatedBoundedFlags.Frobenius_map
api.statement: Send a tuple represented by A_j z_j to the etale object with those partial Frobenius matrices. Prove independence of I1 representatives by the residual straightening theorem.

api.name: TranslatedBoundedFlags.shifted_torus_action
api.statement: On B_j=A_j z_j the constant tuple D acts by B_j↦D_j B_j D_(j-1)^(-1). Verify identity/composition and descend the etale map through this action.

api.name: TranslatedBoundedFlags.monomorphism
api.statement: Apply K33 to the shifted torus quotient under its depth hypotheses; retain this as a theorem about the quotient, not injectivity of all tuples of matrices.

api.name: TranslatedBoundedFlags.type_comparison
api.statement: For K34 establish the actual inclusion Gr^[0,h]_F w_star(tau) in this translated bound before comparing images. A common ambient name or the existence of two presentations does not supply the inclusion.

tests.name: TranslatedBoundedFlags.cyclic_scalar_action
tests.statement: For n=1 and two embeddings, (b_0,b_1) maps to (d_0 b_0/d_1,d_1 b_1/d_0); their product is invariant.

tests.name: TranslatedBoundedFlags.one_embedding_action
tests.statement: For one embedding the action is conjugation D B D^(-1); in rank one it is trivial.

tests.name: TranslatedBoundedFlags.translation_vs_shifted_action
tests.statement: With two embeddings, changing d_0 but not d_1 changes both partial matrices. Acting by left multiplication on the first matrix alone is a different action.

items.name: Bounded flag quotient embeds in the etale stack
items.statement: Under K32's depth hypothesis, iota_z from the shifted-torus quotient of Fl^[a,b]_(J,z) to the etale Frobenius stack over F is a monomorphism.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Compatibility diagram for different local models
items.statement: Assume a<=b,h>=0; z=sigma^-1 t_(nu+eta) with nu(b-a+1)-deep; tau has(h+1)-deep presentation(s,mu); the translated bounded Gr^[0,h]^J by w*(tau) lies in Fl^[a,b]_(J,z); and lambda_j in[0,h]^n. Then the PZ special-fibre torsor, the Kisin stacks, right translation by w*(tau), the torus quotient and epsilon_tau commute in diagram(5.13). The inclusion is an explicit hypothesis when comparing multiple types.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Fields-of-norms anti-equivalence
items.statement: For R complete Noetherian local over O with finite residue field, etale Frobenius modules over K are exactly anti-equivalent to rank-n continuous R-representations of GK_infinity by the dual of Frobenius-fixed vectors after unramified period extension. Tdd*=V_K* composed with epsilon_tau. The paper explicitly corrects the formula in[59] §2.3; this already-known correction needs a sourceIssues entry with that attribution.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Restriction of tame representations and semisimplification
items.statement: GK_infinity surjects onto the tame quotient of GK, hence restriction is fully faithful on tame representations and tame GK_infinity representations extend canonically. Semisimple finite-characteristic representations are tame. The converse printed identification of tameness with semisimplicity is false without further regular-inertia hypotheses: an unramified nontrivial2x2 unipotent Frobenius representation is tame and nonsplit.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Genericity of a residual Galois representation
items.statement: rho is m-generic if the tame inertial type of rho^ss is m-generic. For tame rho a lowest-alcove presentation means a presentation of its inertial restriction, giving w(rho)=t_(mu+eta)s and w*(rho)=s^-1t_(mu+eta). This definition must not silently discard a nonsemisimple unramified extension.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Classify generic semisimple representations and transfer genericity with a height loss.
Use compatible tame presentations to compare semisimple representation and Kisin shapes.

api.name: ResidualGaloisGenericity.mk
api.statement: Define m-genericity through the tame inertial type of rho^ss. Keep the original representation rho as data, without identifying it with rho^ss.

api.name: ResidualGaloisGenericity.semisimplification_invariant
api.statement: Representations with isomorphic semisimplifications have the same genericity; rho is m-generic iff rho^ss is m-generic.

api.name: ResidualGaloisGenericity.monotone
api.statement: For 0<=m_prime<=m, m-genericity implies m_prime-genericity with the same type convention.

api.name: ResidualGaloisGenericity.tame_presentation
api.statement: For tame rho, a lowest-alcove presentation is a presentation of its inertial restriction; form w(rho)=t_(mu+eta)s and w_star(rho)=s^(-1)t_(mu+eta). This does not encode unramified extension data.

api.name: ResidualGaloisGenericity.semisimplicity_hypotheses
api.statement: Use K45–K47 to deduce semisimplicity for a tame generic representation only with the distinct-inertial-character hypotheses. Retain E19: tameness alone does not imply semisimplicity.

api.name: ResidualGaloisGenericity.height_loss
api.statement: Under K44, an m-generic tau with m>=h+1 yields an (m-h)-generic semisimplified Galois representation from a height-h object; do not export an unchanged m bound.

tests.name: ResidualGaloisGenericity.unramified_Jordan
tests.statement: A two-dimensional unramified representation with Frobenius a nontrivial unipotent Jordan block is tame but not semisimple. Its repeated trivial inertial characters exclude the generic distinct-character hypothesis.

tests.name: ResidualGaloisGenericity.same_semisimplification
tests.statement: A representation and its semisimplification return the same value of the genericity predicate, even when they are not isomorphic.

tests.name: ResidualGaloisGenericity.loss_boundary
tests.statement: For m=h+1 the guaranteed output depth is 1. Replacing it by h+1 overstates the theorem when h>0.

items.name: Semisimple representations from torus-fixed Frobenius matrices
items.statement: For a fixed point z' in the bounded translated flag of Proposition5.4.7 and semisimple rho, rho has a presentation with w*(rho)=z' iff for some D in Tdual^J(F), V_K*(iota_z(Dz')) is rho restricted to GK_infinity. Torus constants account for the unramified extension of the prescribed inertial parameter.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Shape of a residual representation relative to a type
items.statement: If rho|GK_infinity has a Kisin lift M in Y^[0,h],tau(F), define its shape relative to tau to be the shape of M. The generic closed-immersion theorem makes it independent of M; it is undefined if no such lift exists.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Relate the shape of a semisimple representation to admissibility and potentially crystalline nonemptiness.

api.name: RepresentationShape.domain
api.statement: The input is a residual representation rho and a witness M in Y^[0,h],tau(F) with Tdd_star(M)≅rho restricted to G_Kinfinity, under the standing (h+1)-generic type assumption.

api.name: RepresentationShape.mk
api.statement: Assign the shape of the witnessed Kisin module, relative to the specified lowest-alcove presentation of tau.

api.name: RepresentationShape.witness_independent
api.statement: Use the generic monomorphism/closed-immersion theorem for epsilon and the field-of-norms equivalence to identify any two witnessed lifts; their shapes agree.

api.name: RepresentationShape.isomorphism_invariant
api.statement: An isomorphism of the restricted Galois representation transports the witness and preserves shape.

api.name: RepresentationShape.field_extension
api.statement: Base extend the witness and use K09 to preserve shape under a residue-field extension.

api.name: RepresentationShape.no_default
api.statement: Outside the essential image there is no representation shape under this definition. A later theorem producing a lift supplies required data, not a default Weyl element.

tests.name: RepresentationShape.two_witnesses
tests.statement: For two generic lifts of the same restricted representation, the construction produces one label by the uniqueness theorem.

tests.name: RepresentationShape.missing_lift
tests.statement: A bare residual representation and a tame type do not form a valid input unless a Kisin-lift existence witness is supplied.

tests.name: RepresentationShape.presentation_parameter
tests.statement: Changing the lowest-alcove presentation of tau requires the corresponding coordinate comparison; equality of raw Weyl labels is not part of presentation-free Galois isomorphism invariance.

items.name: Semisimple Kisin module
items.statement: M is semisimple of shape z when in the z-gauge diagram its image in the ordinary chart is the torus-fixed point z. Equivalently it has an eigenbasis with A_beta^j in Tdual(F') z_j in every component.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Characterize semisimple Galois representations of the prescribed relative shape.
Construct the semisimplification degeneration while preserving closed height/Hodge bounds.

api.name: SemisimpleKisinPoint.chart_definition
api.statement: Over a finite residue-field extension, a shape-z Kisin module is semisimple when its ordinary-chart image in the z-gauge diagram is the torus-fixed point z.

api.name: SemisimpleKisinPoint.matrix_criterion
api.statement: Equivalently, there exists an eigenbasis with A_beta^j∈Tdual(Fprime) z_j for every j. Preserve the scalar torus factors as unramified data.

api.name: SemisimpleKisinPoint.gauge_independent
api.statement: Under the gauge-basis uniqueness theorem, changing a gauge eigenbasis preserves the fixed-point criterion, so it depends only on the Kisin object.

api.name: SemisimpleKisinPoint.field_extension
api.statement: Base extension preserves the matrix criterion and its fixed-point interpretation.

api.name: SemisimpleKisinPoint.relative_position
api.statement: For the compatible semisimple presentations of K41, the shape is z=w_star(rho) w_star(tau)^(-1); the Hodge criterion uses w_star(tau)^(-1)w_star(rho) in Adm(lambda). Keep these two orders distinct.

api.name: SemisimpleKisinPoint.degeneration
api.statement: Use K43 to construct the cocharacter degeneration to the semisimple object, proving the generic-family identity as a scheme identity before using closedness. A finite list of Fprime-rational nonzero parameters is not a Zariski-density argument.

tests.name: SemisimpleKisinPoint.rank_one
tests.statement: A rank-one shape-c residual object admits A=u v^c with u a unit; the source gauge theorem reduces the gauge representative to a constant torus multiple of v^c, giving the fixed-point criterion under its hypotheses.

tests.name: SemisimpleKisinPoint.torus_factor_retained
tests.statement: Two rank-one etale matrices a v^c and b v^c with a!=b need not define the same unramified representation. The semisimple criterion must not discard the torus factors.

tests.name: SemisimpleKisinPoint.finite_points_not_dense
tests.statement: Over F_q the polynomial x^(q-1)-1 vanishes on every element of F_q^× but is not the zero regular function on G_m. A degeneration identity needs the family over the coordinate ring, not only its rational points.

items.name: Semisimple Kisin modules and admissible type position
items.statement: For tau(h+1)-generic and semisimple rho of GK_infinity, a semisimple M in Y^[0,h],tau with Tdd*(M)=rho exists iff rho admits a presentation with z=w*(rho)w*(tau)^-1 in Gr^[0,h]^J_F. Its shape is z. Furthermore M belongs to Y^<=lambda,tau iff w(tau)^-1 w(rho) belongs to Adm(lambda).
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: A nonzero tame deformation ring forces admissibility
items.statement: For tame ρ, effective λ_j∈[0,h]^n and τ with an (h+1)-generic lowest-alcove presentation as in K41, a nonzero R_ρ^(λ,τ) implies a λ-compatible lowest-alcove presentation of ρ with w(τ)^−1 w(ρ)∈Adm(λ). K48 supplies semisimplicity from the actual height and genericity assumptions; unqualified tame=semisimple is not used.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Semisimplification preserves a Kisin height and Hodge bound
items.statement: For finite F'/F and M in Y^<=lambda,tau(F') (or Y^[0,h],tau(F')), there is a semisimple M' in the same substack with Tdd*(M')=Tdd*(M)^ss. Use a descent-compatible filtration, a cocharacter degeneration over A1 and properness of the lattice map. Density is that of Gm as a subscheme, not the finite set F'^times.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Residual genericity loses at most the height
items.statement: For finite F'/F, M in Y^[0,h],tau(F') and tau m-generic with m>=h+1, Tdd*(M)^ss has an(m-h)-generic lowest-alcove presentation. Reduce to K43, then bound the translation difference by the height.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Framed local lifting ring
items.statement: For a continuous rho:GL->G(F), with L a characteristic-zero nonarchimedean local field and G a split possibly disconnected reductive O-group, liftings to Noetherian complete local O-algebras with residue F form the framed lifting functor represented by R_rho^square. Retain the group/ring hypotheses and do not quotient by conjugacy.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: R_ρ = ⊗̂_{v∈S_p,O} R_{ρ_v} is the local factor of the patched ring R∞ (§6.2, PDF126).
Versal rings at semisimple points are quotients of R_ρ (Theorem 7.3.2(2)).
The primes p_σ(ρ̄) are primes of R_ρ̄ (§9.1, PDF185).
Local deformation problems are quotients of the framed lifting rings (Definition A.3.1).

api.name: FramedLiftingRing.represents
api.statement: R_ρ̄ pro-represents D_ρ̄ : C_O → Sets, A ↦ {continuous r_A : G_L → G(A) with r_A ≡ ρ̄ mod m_A}.

api.name: FramedLiftingRing.completeLocal
api.statement: R_ρ̄ is a complete Noetherian local O-algebra with residue field F.

api.name: FramedLiftingRing.conjAction
api.statement: ker(G(A) → G(F)) acts on D_ρ̄(A) by conjugation; the framed functor is not quotiented by it.

api.name: FramedLiftingRing.baseChange
api.statement: For a finite extension O → O′ with residue F′, R_{ρ̄⊗F′}^{O′} ≅ R_ρ̄ ⊗̂_O O′.

api.name: FramedLiftingRing.pi
api.statement: For a collection (ρ̄_v)_{v∈S_p}, ⊗̂_{v,O} R_{ρ̄_v} represents the product of the lifting functors.

tests.name: FramedLiftingRing.GL1_Qp
tests.statement: For G = GL₁, L = Q_p and p odd, R_χ̄ ≅ O[[Z_p²]] ≅ O[[X, Y]], the completed group ring of the pro-p completion of Q_p^×.

tests.name: FramedLiftingRing.tangent
tests.statement: Hom_F(m/(m², ϖ), F) ≅ Z¹(G_L, ad ρ̄), the continuous 1-cocycles (compare E23).

tests.name: FramedLiftingRing.not_unframed
tests.statement: R_ρ̄ is not the unframed deformation ring: the unframed functor need not be representable when End(ρ̄) ≠ F, while D_ρ̄ always is.

items.name: Type and Hodge-type deformation quotients
items.statement: For GLn and L away from p, R_rho^tau is the reduced O-flat quotient with the prescribed inertial type. For L above p and dominant Hodge lambda and WD inertial tau, R_rho^(lambda,tau) is the reduced O-flat Zariski closure of characteristic-zero potentially semistable points of that exact type; R_rho^(lambda,<=tau) is the reduced union over monodromy types dominated by tau. If N_tau=0 this is the potentially crystalline ring and a versal ring of X^(lambda,tau); a maximal tau gives the usual semistable union.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted. Continuation codex-a71f92 corrects the previously overstrong TypeQuotient.points API: the source defines a closure, not a general iff exact-monodromy statement. No source-paper error is asserted by this extraction correction.

uses.how: R_ρ^{λ+η,τ} ≠ 0 iff w̃(ρ̄,τ) ∈ Adm(λ+η), for generic data (Proposition 6.2.7).
R_ρ̄^τ is a domain at semisimple points (Theorem 7.3.2(2)).
The corrected Theorem A.4.1 uses R_ρ̄^{λ+η,⪯τ} (E33–E34).
Modularity lifting from polynomial-generic local domains (Theorem 9.2.1).

api.name: TypeQuotient.mk
api.statement: R_ρ̄^{λ,τ} is the reduced O-flat quotient of R_ρ̄ whose Spec is the Zariski closure of the E′-points that are potentially semistable of Hodge type λ with WD(ρ)|_{I_L} ≅ τ ⊗_E E′; away from p only the inertial type is imposed.

api.name: TypeQuotient.points
api.statement: An E'-point of the stated exact potentially semistable Hodge/WD type lies in its Zariski closure, hence its map factors through R_rhobar^(lambda,tau). The converse is not inferred from the closure definition for a general WD type with nonzero monodromy; any exact point characterization needs a separate theorem. The potentially crystalline/minimal and full potentially semistable cases have the specific Kisin criteria of Remark6.1.1.

api.name: TypeQuotient.dominated
api.statement: Spec R_ρ̄^{λ,⪯τ} := ⋃_{τ′⪯τ} Spec R_ρ̄^{λ,τ′}, a reduced union.

api.name: TypeQuotient.crys_of_N0
api.statement: If N_τ = 0, R_ρ̄^{λ,τ} is Kisin's framed potentially crystalline ring and a versal ring of X^{λ,τ} at ρ̄; if τ is maximal for ⪯, R_ρ̄^{λ,⪯τ} is the potentially semistable ring (Remark 6.1.1).

api.name: TypeQuotient.dim
api.statement: If nonzero and λ is regular, R_ρ̄^{λ,τ} is equidimensional of Krull dimension 1 + n² + [L:Q_p]·n(n−1)/2 (Kisin).

api.name: TypeQuotient.mono
api.statement: τ′ ⪯ τ implies Spec R_ρ̄^{λ,τ′} ⊆ Spec R_ρ̄^{λ,⪯τ}.

api.name: TypeQuotient.integral_Hecke_factor
api.statement: For a reduced finite flat Hecke target, use A63-A65 to pass from the exact-type characteristic-zero constituents to factorization through the dominated closed union. The field factors are jointly faithful; neither nilpotent nor vertical-torsion targets satisfy this test without more hypotheses.

tests.name: TypeQuotient.empty
tests.statement: If ρ̄ has no lift of type (λ,τ), then R_ρ̄^{λ,τ} = 0.

tests.name: TypeQuotient.GL1
tests.statement: For GL₁, L = Q_p with p odd, and (λ,τ) compatible with χ̄, R_χ̄^{λ,τ} ≅ O[[X]], parametrizing the unramified twists; otherwise it is 0.

tests.name: TypeQuotient.dominated_union
tests.statement: For GL₂ and the Steinberg WD type τ_st, R^{λ,⪯τ_st} contains the crystalline components as well as the exact-type semistable ones, so it differs from R^{λ,τ_st} in general.

tests.name: TypeQuotient.remark611
tests.statement: With N_τ = 0 the quotient agrees with the potentially crystalline ring of [49] (Remark 6.1.1).

tests.name: TypeQuotient.closure_does_not_imply_exact_stratum
tests.statement: For the rank-two nilpotent family N_t=t E12 over a characteristic-zero field, rank N_t=1 for t≠0 and N_0=0. The closure of the rank-one stratum contains the rank-zero point. This is a warning about the closure-to-exact-type inference only, not a constructed family of potentially semistable Galois representations with fixed Hodge data.

items.name: Patched local base rings
items.statement: For finitely many unramified p-adic places, take the completed tensor product R_rho of framed local lifting rings and R_infinity=R_rho completed-tensor R^p, where R^p is nonzero complete Noetherian local, equidimensional and O-flat with residue F. Define R_infinity(lambda,tau) using the Hodge type lambda+eta. The representation sigma(lambda,tau)=V(lambda) tensor sigma(tau) uses lambda, so preserve this shift.
items.note: Route owner: DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Patching functors take values in coherent sheaves on X∞ = Spec R∞.
R∞(λ,τ) ≠ 0 iff R_ρ^{λ+η,τ} ≠ 0 (proof of Proposition 6.2.7).
Minimal patching yields versal cycles on X∞ (Theorem 8.3.5(1)).
Appendix A constructs R∞ with R^p a formally smooth algebra over away-from-p local rings (§A.5).

api.name: PatchedRing.mk
api.statement: R∞ := R_ρ ⊗̂_O R^p, with R_ρ := ⊗̂_{v∈S_p,O} R_{ρ_v} and R^p a nonzero complete local Noetherian equidimensional flat O-algebra with residue F.

api.name: PatchedRing.typeQuotient_ne_zero_iff
api.statement: R∞(λ,τ) ≠ 0 iff R_ρ^{λ+η,τ} ≠ 0, since R^p is nonzero and O-flat.

api.name: PatchedRing.dim
api.statement: dim R∞(λ,τ) = dim R_ρ^{λ+η,τ} + dim R^p − 1 for complete local O-flat factors with residue F.

api.name: PatchedRing.eta_shift
api.statement: The Hodge type of R∞(λ,τ) is λ+η, while σ(λ,τ) = V(λ)⊗σ(τ) uses λ; the shift is part of the definition.

tests.name: PatchedRing.trivial_Rp
tests.statement: If R^p = O, then R∞ = R_ρ.

tests.name: PatchedRing.single_place
tests.statement: If S_p = {v}, then R_ρ = R_{ρ_v} and R∞(λ,τ) = R_{ρ_v}^{λ_v+η_v,τ_v} ⊗̂_O R^p.

tests.name: PatchedRing.no_eta
tests.statement: λ = 0 corresponds to Hodge type η, with HT weights (n−1, …, 0) per embedding, not to parallel weight 0.

tests.name: PatchedRing.nonzero
tests.statement: R∞(λ,τ) ≠ 0 exactly when some product of local lifts of type (λ+η,τ) exists.

items.name: Weak patching functor
items.statement: A weak patching functor is a nonzero covariant exact functor from finite O-module continuous GLn(Op)-representations to coherent R_infinity-modules, taking every stable lattice sigma^circ(lambda,tau) to a maximal Cohen–Macaulay module on X_infinity(lambda,<=tau), and every residual constituent to a maximal Cohen–Macaulay module there or zero. The support includes the monodromy-dominated union.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Weight elimination for any weak patching functor (Proposition 6.2.3).
Existence of a weak potentially diagonalizable patching functor (Proposition 6.2.4(1)).
Nonvanishing criterion (Proposition 6.2.7).
Support of a weak detectable patching functor (Lemma 9.1.10).
Appendix A constructs the exact covariant patching functor (§A.5).

api.name: WeakPatchingFunctor
api.statement: A nonzero exact covariant M∞ : Rep_O(GL_n(O_p)) → Coh(X∞) such that, for every O-lattice σ°(λ,τ) ⊂ σ(λ,τ), M∞(σ°) is maximal Cohen–Macaulay on X∞(λ,⪯τ), and for every σ ∈ JH(σ̄°), M∞(σ) is maximal Cohen–Macaulay on X∞(λ,⪯τ) or 0.

api.name: WeakPatchingFunctor.support
api.statement: Supp M∞(σ°(λ,τ)) ⊆ X∞(λ,⪯τ).

api.name: WeakPatchingFunctor.eq_zero_iff
api.statement: For a finite-length σ, M∞(σ) = 0 iff M∞(σᵢ) = 0 for every Jordan–Hölder factor σᵢ, by exactness.

api.name: WeakPatchingFunctor.generic_indep
api.statement: M∞(σ°)[1/p] is independent of the lattice σ° ⊂ σ(λ,τ): two lattices differ by a finite-length module, whose image is p-power torsion.

api.name: WeakPatchingFunctor.cycle_additive
api.statement: The special-fibre cycle of M∞(σ̄°) equals Σ_σ [σ̄° : σ]·Z(M∞(σ)), by exactness.

tests.name: WeakPatchingFunctor.nonzero
tests.statement: The zero functor is exact but is not a weak patching functor.

tests.name: WeakPatchingFunctor.support_violation
tests.statement: An exact functor with M∞(σ°(λ,τ)) supported on all of X∞, not only on X∞(λ,⪯τ), is not a weak patching functor.

tests.name: WeakPatchingFunctor.jh_zero
tests.statement: M∞(σ°(λ,τ)) ≠ 0 iff M∞(σ) ≠ 0 for some σ ∈ JH(σ̄°(λ,τ)).

tests.name: WeakPatchingFunctor.lattice_change
tests.statement: For lattices σ°₁ ⊂ σ°₂ of σ(λ,τ), M∞(σ°₁)[1/p] ≅ M∞(σ°₂)[1/p].

items.name: Weak minimal patching functor
items.statement: A weak functor is minimal if R^p is formally smooth over O and, for each zero-monodromy inertial tau, the generic-fibre module of every type lattice is locally free of rank at most one on each connected component of the regular generic deformation fibre.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Existence of a weak minimal potentially diagonalizable functor (Proposition 6.2.4(2)).
A weak minimal detectable potentially diagonalizable functor exists (Proposition 6.2.6).
Proposition 6.2.7 assumes a weak detectable minimal functor.
Minimality enters the versal-cycle comparison (Theorem 8.3.5).

api.name: WeakPatchingFunctor.IsMinimal
api.statement: M∞ is minimal iff R^p is formally smooth over O and, for every τ with N_τ = 0, M∞(σ°(λ,τ))[1/p] has rank at most one on each connected component of Spec R∞(λ,τ)[1/p].

api.name: WeakPatchingFunctor.IsMinimal.locallyFree
api.statement: Spec R∞(λ,τ)[1/p] is regular for N_τ = 0, so the maximal Cohen–Macaulay module M∞(σ°)[1/p] is locally free there.

api.name: WeakPatchingFunctor.IsMinimal.toWeak
api.statement: A minimal weak patching functor is in particular a weak patching functor.

tests.name: WeakPatchingFunctor.double_not_minimal
tests.statement: If M∞ is minimal and M∞(σ°) ≠ 0, then M∞ ⊕ M∞ is still a weak patching functor but has rank 2 somewhere, so it is not minimal.

tests.name: WeakPatchingFunctor.minimal_free_rank_one
tests.statement: A functor taking σ°(λ,τ) to a line bundle on each component of X∞(λ,τ)[1/p] where it is nonzero satisfies the rank condition.

tests.name: WeakPatchingFunctor.minimal_only_N0
tests.statement: The rank condition is imposed only for inertial L-parameters (N_τ = 0); WD types with nonzero monodromy are unconstrained.

tests.name: WeakPatchingFunctor.minimal_needs_smooth
tests.statement: If R^p is not formally smooth over O, M∞ is not minimal, whatever its ranks.

items.name: Potentially diagonalizable patching functor
items.statement: A weak functor is potentially diagonalizable when it is nonzero on a type lattice whenever each residual local representation has a potentially diagonalizable lift of the corresponding Hodge type lambda_v+eta_v and inertial type tau_v.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Existence (Proposition 6.2.4(1), via [14, §2] and [56, Theorem 4.3.8]).
Weak potentially diagonalizable functors are detectable for 4n-generic semisimple ρ̄ (Proposition 6.2.6).
Ordinary weights are detected (Proposition 6.2.9).

api.name: WeakPatchingFunctor.IsPotDiag
api.statement: M∞ is potentially diagonalizable iff M∞(σ°(λ,τ)) ≠ 0 whenever each ρ̄_v has a potentially diagonalizable lift of type (λ_v+η_v, τ_v) in the sense of [10, §1.4].

api.name: WeakPatchingFunctor.IsPotDiag.ordinary
api.statement: Ordinary (upper-triangular) lifts are potentially diagonalizable [10, Lemma 1.4.3], so the lifts of Lemma 6.2.8 give M∞(σ°(τ(1,κ))) ≠ 0.

api.name: WeakPatchingFunctor.IsPotDiag.detectable
api.statement: For semisimple ρ̄ with 4n-generic tame inertial parameter, a potentially diagonalizable weak functor is detectable (Proposition 6.2.6).

tests.name: WeakPatchingFunctor.potDiag_implication
tests.statement: The condition is one implication: it does not force M∞(σ°) = 0 when no potentially diagonalizable lift of that type exists.

tests.name: WeakPatchingFunctor.potDiag_FL
tests.statement: Crystalline lifts with Fontaine–Laffaille Hodge–Tate weights are potentially diagonalizable [10, Lemma 1.4.3(2)], as used in Proposition 6.2.6.

tests.name: WeakPatchingFunctor.potDiag_vacuous
tests.statement: If no ρ̄_v has a potentially diagonalizable lift of any type considered, the condition is vacuous.

items.name: Detectable patching functor
items.statement: For semisimple2n-generic rho, a weak functor is detectable when it is nonzero on every obvious Serre weight of rho.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Existence of detectable functors (Proposition 6.2.6).
(1) ⟺ (4) in Proposition 6.2.7 uses detectability through W_obv.
Support equals W?(ρ̄) for weak detectable functors (Lemma 9.1.10).
The global functor is detectable (Lemma A.1.1(2)).

api.name: WeakPatchingFunctor.IsDetectable
api.statement: For semisimple 2n-generic ρ̄, M∞ is detectable iff M∞(σ) ≠ 0 for every σ ∈ W_obv(ρ̄).

api.name: WeakPatchingFunctor.IsDetectable.nonzero_iff_adm
api.statement: For a weak detectable minimal M∞ and a max{2n, h+n−1}-generic tame τ, M∞(σ°(λ,τ)) ≠ 0 iff w̃(ρ̄,τ) ∈ Adm(λ+η) for a λ-compatible presentation (Proposition 6.2.7).

api.name: WeakPatchingFunctor.IsDetectable.support
api.statement: For P-generic ρ̄, {σ : M∞(σ) ≠ 0} = W?(ρ̄) (Lemma 9.1.10).

tests.name: WeakPatchingFunctor.detectable_GL2
tests.statement: For GL₂ and 4-generic semisimple ρ̄, W_obv(ρ̄) = W?(ρ̄) has 2 elements, so detectability means M∞ is nonzero on both.

tests.name: WeakPatchingFunctor.detectable_GL3_shadow
tests.statement: For GL₃, detectability constrains only the 6 obvious weights; nonvanishing on the 3 shadow weights in W?(ρ̄) is a theorem (Lemma 9.1.10), not part of the definition.

tests.name: WeakPatchingFunctor.detectable_needs_generic
tests.statement: The notion is defined only for semisimple 2n-generic ρ̄.

items.name: Minimal patching functor for a set of types
items.statement: For a set S of pairs(lambda+eta,tau) with N_tau=0, a minimal patching functor is a weak minimal one whose generic-fibre module has rank exactly one over the entire Spec R_infinity(lambda,tau)[1/p] for every pair in S and every type lattice. Rank at most one does not imply this full-support property.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Minimal patching functors for a set of types give versal Breuil–Mézard cycles (Theorem 8.3.5(1)).
Theorem 8.4.10(1) constructs minimal functors for generic tame ρ̄.
The proof of Lemma 9.1.10 uses a minimal functor for ρ̄ and S_{0,t}.

api.name: PatchingFunctor.IsMinimalFor
api.statement: M∞ is minimal for ρ̄ and S (types (λ+η,τ) with N_τ = 0) iff it is weak minimal and M∞(σ°(λ,τ))[1/p] has rank exactly one on all of Spec R∞(λ,τ)[1/p], for every pair in S and every lattice.

api.name: PatchingFunctor.IsMinimalFor.cycle
api.statement: For (λ+η,τ) ∈ S, Z(M∞(σ̄°(λ,τ))) = Z(R∞(λ,τ)/ϖ): a maximal Cohen–Macaulay module of generic rank one has the special-fibre cycle of the ring ([23, Lemma 2.2.10], used on PDF169).

api.name: PatchingFunctor.IsMinimalFor.mono
api.statement: Minimal for S implies minimal for every S′ ⊆ S.

api.name: PatchingFunctor.IsMinimalFor.support
api.statement: For (λ+η,τ) ∈ S, Supp M∞(σ°(λ,τ)) = X∞(λ,τ).

tests.name: PatchingFunctor.minimalFor_empty
tests.statement: Minimal for S = ∅ is the same as weak minimal.

tests.name: PatchingFunctor.minimalFor_not_rank_le_one
tests.statement: A weak minimal functor with M∞(σ°(λ,τ)) = 0 on one component of X∞(λ,τ) satisfies rank ≤ 1 but is not minimal for any S containing (λ+η,τ).

tests.name: PatchingFunctor.minimalFor_full_support
tests.statement: If M∞ is minimal for S and (λ+η,τ) ∈ S with R∞(λ,τ) ≠ 0, then M∞(σ°(λ,τ)) ≠ 0.

items.name: Weight elimination for weak patching functors
items.statement: If M_infinity(sigma) is nonzero, then sigma belongs to W?(rho^ss) provided either every local rho_v^ss is(6n-2)-generic, or sigma is(2n-1)-deep and every rho_v^ss is4n-generic. The two alternatives are separate sufficient hypotheses.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.
proofSteps: Write sigma = tensor_v sigma_v over v in S_p and treat the two hypotheses of the statement as genuinely separate cases; the paper proves them by different routes and neither implies the other.

First case, every rho^ss_v is (6n-2)-generic. The patching axioms make M_infinity(- tensor (tensor_{v != v0} sigma_v)) an arithmetic cohomology functor on F[GL_n(k_{v0})] in the sense of the cited weight-elimination paper, and its conclusion gives sigma_v in W?(rho^ss_v) for every v, one place at a time.

Second case, sigma is (2n-1)-deep and every rho^ss_v is 4n-generic. Pick lambda with F(lambda) = sigma and set tau = tau(w, w-hat_h . lambda + eta), which is an n-generic tame inertial type for every w in W. The cited elimination argument produces some w for which rho has no potentially crystalline lift of type (eta, tau) whenever sigma is not in W?(rho^ss).

By the axioms of M_infinity it is then enough that sigma be a Jordan-Holder constituent of sigma-bar(tau). The paper supplies this from the lowest alcove presentation: if (s, mu - eta) is n-generic for tau then F(pi^{-1}(w-tilde) . (t_mu s w-tilde^{-1}(eta) - eta)) lies in JH(sigma-bar(tau)), the depth of mu - eta being exactly what makes t_mu s w-tilde^{-1}(eta) - eta dominant and p-restricted for every w-tilde in W-tilde^+_1.
Blueprint note: the two genericity thresholds (6n-2 against 4n plus (2n-1)-depth) must be carried separately into any formalisation; collapsing them to the weaker one is not licensed by this proof.

items.name: Existence of potentially diagonalizable weak patching
items.statement: If p does not divide2n, every residual L-homomorphism in the section's unramified setup has a weak potentially diagonalizable patching functor. This is a global construction using globalization, potentially diagonalizable lifts and Taylor–Wiles patching, not a formal existence axiom.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.
proofSteps: Reduce to the case that O_p is a domain O_K; the general case follows by completed tensor products over the places of S_p, which is how the section's R_p is built.
Quote the existence input rather than reproving it: by the cited moduli-of-etale-(phi,Gamma)-modules paper a crystalline potentially diagonalizable lift of rho exists, of some type (xi + eta, tau).

Feed that xi and tau into the Taylor-Wiles construction of the cited patching paper. It produces a finitely generated R_infinity[[GL_n(O_K)]]-module M_infinity, from which the functor is defined by M_infinity(sigma) = Hom^cont_{O[[GL_n(O_K)]]}(M_infinity, sigma^vee)^vee.

That this functor satisfies the weak patching axioms is the cited paper's own conclusion. Potential diagonalizability is separate: the residual representation r used there is potentially diagonalizably automorphic, and the proof of the cited weight paper upgrades that to potential diagonalizability of M_infinity.

Blueprint obligation: this is a global construction (globalise rho to a definite unitary group, patch), not a formal existence axiom, so a blueprint owns the globalisation and the patching input, not merely the axiom list.

items.name: Existence of weak minimal potentially diagonalizable patching
items.statement: Under P10, if each rho_v has a potentially diagonalizable lift of a type for which the product potentially crystalline lifting ring is formally smooth, then a weak minimal potentially diagonalizable functor exists.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.
proofSteps: Run the construction of P10 unchanged; the additional hypothesis is used only at the last step.
Assume each rho_v has a potentially diagonalizable lift of type (xi_v + eta_v, tau_v) with R^{xi+eta,tau}_rho formally smooth, and choose that type as the (xi, tau) fed to the patching construction.
Minimality is then immediate from the cited construction: formal smoothness of the local lifting ring at the chosen type is exactly the hypothesis under which the patched module is minimal there.
Record the dependency honestly: minimality here is a property of the chosen type, not of rho alone, so the blueprint must carry the type through.

items.name: Detectability for semisimple generic representations
items.statement: For K/Qp finite unramified, p not dividing2n, and semisimple rho with4n-generic inertia, every weak potentially diagonalizable functor is detectable, and a weak minimal detectable potentially diagonalizable functor exists. Fontaine–Laffaille formally smooth lift existence supplies P11's hypothesis.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.
proofSteps: First assertion. Reprove the cited paper's detectability argument verbatim with one substitution: use Proposition 6.2.3 of this paper in place of the corollary that plays that role in loc. cit. The 4n-genericity of the tame inertial L-parameter is what makes the substitution legitimate.

Second assertion, existence. Each rho_v is Fontaine-Laffaille under the standing hypotheses, so it has a crystalline potentially diagonalizable lift for some Fontaine-Laffaille Hodge-Tate weights, and the corresponding crystalline lifting ring is formally smooth; this is quoted from three cited papers.
That is precisely the hypothesis of Proposition 6.2.4(2), so a weak minimal potentially diagonalizable patching functor exists.

Detectability of that functor is then automatic from the first assertion, since it is in particular weak potentially diagonalizable. Note the logical order: existence is obtained first and detectability is inherited, not imposed.

items.name: Patched nonvanishing and admissibility criterion
items.statement: For semisimple rho with4n-generic inertia, dominant effective lambda_j in[0,h]^n, tau with chosen max(2n,h+n-1)-generic presentation, a stable lattice sigma^circ(lambda,tau), and a weak detectable minimal functor, the following are equivalent: its patched module is nonzero; R_infinity(lambda,tau) is nonzero; R_rho^(lambda+eta,tau) is nonzero; rho admits a lambda-compatible presentation with w(tau)^-1 w(rho) in Adm(lambda+eta). Expand the equivalence into individual implications in the blueprint. No domain claim is involved.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.
proofSteps: Prove the four conditions equivalent as a cycle (1) => (2) => (3) => (4) => (1); the paper's proof is exactly this cycle and no two of the steps share an argument.
(1) => (2). M_infinity(sigma^circ(lambda, tau)) is supported on X_infinity(lambda, tau), so if it is nonzero then R_infinity(lambda, tau) is nonzero.
(2) <=> (3). By the definition of R_infinity(lambda, tau) as a completed tensor product with the local factor, it is nonzero exactly when R^{lambda+eta,tau}_rho is.

(3) => (4). Corollary 5.5.8: nonvanishing of the local deformation ring produces a lambda-compatible lowest alcove presentation of rho with w-tilde(rho, tau) in Adm(lambda + eta). This is the step that consumes the local model theory of sections 4 and 5.

(4) => (1). Proposition 2.6.6 makes W^obv(rho) intersect JH(sigma^circ(lambda, tau)) nonempty; for sigma in that intersection M_infinity(sigma) is nonzero, and exactness of M_infinity lifts this to M_infinity(sigma^circ(lambda, tau)).

Blueprint note: the chosen max(2n, h + n - 1)-generic lowest alcove presentation of tau is a hypothesis of the statement, not a normalisation, and the equivalence is asserted only for a detectable minimal functor.

items.name: Ordinary upper-triangular lifting
items.statement: Let kappa in X1 be(n-1)-deep and rho upper triangular with diagonal characters chi_bar_i having inertia product_j baromega_(K,sigma_j)^(kappa_j,i+eta_j,i). It admits an upper triangular lift with inertia characters chi_i=epsilon^(n-i) product_j omega_(K,sigma_j)^kappa_j,i. Every such lift is potentially crystalline of type(eta,tau(1,kappa)). The proof uses local H2 obstruction vanishing, de Rham extension results, and distinct inertial characters to kill monodromy.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.
proofSteps: Existence of the lift. The (n-1)-depth of kappa forces chi-bar_i not equal to chi-bar_{i'} epsilon for all i < i', so H^2(G_K, chi-bar_i chi-bar_{i'}^{-1}) = 0 and the successive extension problems defining an upper triangular lift with the prescribed diagonal characters chi_i are unobstructed.

De Rham-ness. Along the diagonal the j-labelled Hodge-Tate weights of the lift increase, which is the hypothesis of the cited de Rham criterion; hence the lift is de Rham and so potentially semistable, with Hodge-Tate weight eta by inspection of the diagonal.

Inertial type. D_pst of the lift is a successive extension of the D_pst(chi_i) as I_K-representations, and D_pst(chi_i) is the product over j of omega^{kappa_{j,i}}_j, so the inertial type is tau(1, kappa).

Vanishing of monodromy. The depth hypothesis on kappa makes D_pst restricted to I_K a direct sum of n distinct characters; the monodromy operator N commutes with I_K up to the cyclotomic twist and therefore must vanish. So the lift is potentially crystalline of type (eta, tau(1, kappa)).
Note that the conclusion is about every such lift, not merely one: the last two steps use only the diagonal characters, so they apply to any upper triangular lift with those diagonal entries.

items.name: Ordinary weights detected by potentially diagonalizable patching
items.statement: For kappa,rho as in P14, assume rho4n-generic. Every weak potentially diagonalizable functor has M_infinity(F(kappa)) nonzero. Weight elimination and the singleton obvious-weight intersection isolate F(kappa) from the type lattice.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.
proofSteps: The lift rho-tilde of P14 is ordinary, hence potentially diagonalizable by the cited potential-diagonalizability criterion for ordinary representations. So for a potentially diagonalizable M_infinity, M_infinity(sigma^circ(tau(1, kappa))) is nonzero for any O-lattice in sigma(tau(1, kappa)).

Fix a lowest alcove presentation (w-tilde, omega) of F(kappa), so kappa = pi^{-1}(w-tilde) . (omega - eta). Because rho is 4n-generic that presentation is 3n-generic, which is the depth the next step needs.

Set w-tilde = t_{eta w} w and use Proposition 2.4.5 to write tau(1, kappa) and rho^ss restricted to I_K in compatible lowest alcove presentations. Then w-tilde(rho, tau(1, kappa)) = t_{w^{-1}(eta)}, and Corollary 2.6.5 gives W?(rho^ss) intersect JH(sigma-bar(tau(1, kappa))) = {F(kappa)}: a singleton, which is the crux.

Every other constituent sigma of sigma-bar(tau(1, kappa)) is 2n-deep by Proposition 2.3.7 and lies outside W?(rho^ss), so M_infinity(sigma) = 0 by Proposition 6.2.3. Exactness of M_infinity then forces the nonvanishing to be carried by F(kappa) alone, so M_infinity(F(kappa)) is nonzero.

items.name: Ordinary constituent forces a nonzero lifting ring
items.statement: Under P15's hypotheses, if F(kappa) is a constituent of the reduction of sigma(lambda,tau), then R_rho^(lambda+eta,tau) is nonzero.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.
proofSteps: Combine P15 with the patching axioms: F(kappa) is a constituent of sigma-bar(lambda, tau) and M_infinity(F(kappa)) is nonzero, so by exactness M_infinity(sigma^circ(lambda, tau)) is nonzero for any O-lattice.
The support axiom then gives R_infinity(lambda, tau) nonzero, and hence R^{lambda+eta,tau}_rho nonzero, by the same identification used in P13.
This is the direction of P13's cycle that survives without semisimplicity of rho, which is why the paper isolates it here; do not import the rest of P13's equivalence into the non-semisimple setting.

items.name: Rigid coefficient rings and analytic derivation
items.statement: For a p-adically complete topologically finite type O-flat algebra R, define O^rig_R as the inverse limit of R[[u',u'^m/p]][1/p], with its convergent analytic interpretation. Define the analytic product L=product_{i>=0} phi^i(E(u')/p) and N_nabla=-u'L d/du'. Evaluation at roots of phi^i(E) is available in this analytic ring; it is not an operation on arbitrary R[1/p][[u']].
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Construct the convergent monodromy matrix, evaluate its derivatives and descend the integral ideal.
Bound the analytic error terms after evaluation at v=-p.

api.name: RigidKisinCoefficients.mk
api.statement: For p-adically complete, topologically finite type, O-flat R, form O_R^rig=lim_m R[[u_prime,u_prime^m/p]][1/p] with the source transition maps. Use its injection into R[1/p][[u_prime]] as a comparison, not as equality.

api.name: RigidKisinCoefficients.analytic_product
api.statement: Construct L=product_(i>=0) phi^i(E(u_prime)/p) by convergence on each closed subdisc; prove L=(E/p)phi(L) and L(0)=1.

api.name: RigidKisinCoefficients.derivation
api.statement: Define N_nabla=-u_prime L d/du_prime on the analytic ring. Prove coefficient linearity, Leibniz and compatibility with restriction to subdiscs.

api.name: RigidKisinCoefficients.evaluation
api.statement: For m>=0, construct the map to R[1/p][u_prime]/phi^m(E) by analytic convergence. Prove agreement with polynomial evaluation and with the relevant finite coefficient maps.

api.name: RigidKisinCoefficients.embedding_product
api.statement: Decompose the W(k_prime)-coefficient variant into the J_prime product of O_R^rig, with phi cyclically moving embedding components and N_nabla componentwise.

api.name: RigidKisinCoefficients.locality
api.statement: Use the source sheafiness theorem to glue analytic functions and the module M^rig over Zariski opens of Spf R. Keep the topological finite-type and flatness domain throughout.

tests.name: RigidKisinCoefficients.constant_derivative
tests.statement: N_nabla(r)=0 for coefficient constants r; N_nabla(u_prime)=-u_prime L.

tests.name: RigidKisinCoefficients.product_relation_at_zero
tests.statement: E(0)=p, so every finite product has constant coefficient 1 and the convergent product does too.

tests.name: RigidKisinCoefficients.formal_evaluation_impossible
tests.statement: In E[[u_prime]], E(u_prime) has nonzero constant coefficient p and is a unit. No E-algebra map from this entire formal-series ring to the nonzero ring E[u_prime]/E(u_prime) can send u_prime to its residue class. This rules out extending root evaluation indiscriminately to arbitrary formal series.

items.name: Kisin monodromy operator on a lattice
items.statement: For M over a finite flat O-algebra of height [0,h] with tame descent, there is a unique derivation extending N_nabla on M^rig[1/L], zero modulo u' and satisfying N phi=E phi N. The lattice M^rig is stable precisely when T_dd^*(M)[1/p] extends to a potentially crystalline GK representation of type tau and Hodge–Tate weights in [0,h]. This imports Kisin [48].
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: True monodromy condition
items.statement: A Breuil–Kisin module satisfies monodromy when its rigid lattice is preserved by the unique operator of G02. Keep this condition distinct from the finite truncated equations of G10.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Replace lattice preservation by analytic derivative equations.
Identify the true monodromy substack with potentially crystalline representations under genericity.

api.name: TrueMonodromyCondition.predicate
api.statement: For a finite flat O-algebra and a Kisin module, require N_Mrig(M^rig)⊆M^rig, where the unique derivation is initially defined on M^rig[1/L].

api.name: TrueMonodromyCondition.intrinsic
api.statement: Transport the preservation condition across an isomorphism of Kisin objects, using uniqueness of N and the induced rigid-lattice isomorphism.

api.name: TrueMonodromyCondition.matrix_criterion
api.statement: In an eigenbasis, preservation means the entries of the N matrix lie in the analytic ring; the basis-change formula includes its derivative term.

api.name: TrueMonodromyCondition.jet_criterion
api.statement: For h>=2, use G05: the derivatives of L^(h-1)N of orders 0 through h-2 vanish at E=0. For h<=1 use the stronger integrality bound of G04 directly; do not invent negative-order derivatives.

api.name: TrueMonodromyCondition.Galois_comparison
api.statement: By G02, true monodromy is equivalent to the attached rational G_Kinfinity representation extending to a potentially crystalline G_K representation of the prescribed type and height range. Integral lattice stability is a further step in G25.

api.name: TrueMonodromyCondition.truncation_boundary
api.statement: Relate this condition to the finite ideal G09 only through the precision theorem G11. Their defining ideals are not declared equal.

tests.name: TrueMonodromyCondition.constant_Frobenius
tests.statement: If all raw Frobenius matrices are constant and invertible, the recurrence starts and remains zero; the operator with matrix zero preserves the rigid lattice.

tests.name: TrueMonodromyCondition.height_one
tests.statement: For h=1, G04 places N directly in Mat(O^rig), so lattice preservation holds and the derivative-index set is empty.

tests.name: TrueMonodromyCondition.finite_precision_not_equality
tests.statement: The abstract inclusion I_1⊆(I_infinity,p^N) does not imply I_1⊆I_infinity: in O, take I_infinity=0 and I_1=(p^N). This tests the logic of using the truncation theorem, not an asserted Kisin counterexample.

items.name: Family monodromy recurrence
items.locator: Proposition 7.1.3(2), inductive definition of N_i^{(j′)}, PDF133–134
items.statement: In §7.1 let R be p-adically complete, topologically of finite type and O-flat, let M∈Y^[0,h],τ(R), and work on an eigenbasis chart indexed cyclically by j∈J′=Z/f′Z. Put E(u′)=u′^e′+p and L=∏_{a≥0}φ^a(E/p), so L=(E/p)φ(L). Write C_j for the Frobenius matrix, with C_j and E^h C_j^−1 integral. The recurrence N_(0,j)=0, N_(i+1,j)=E C_jφ(N_(i,j−1))C_j^−1−N_nabla(C_j)C_j^−1 defines the finite iterates. G38–G40 separately give uniqueness, the exact integral increment estimate and convergence to the analytic family operator; no evaluation of arbitrary formal series at u′^e′=−p is allowed.

uses.how: Supplies finite increments for the integral estimate.
Constructs the analytic limit and identifies it by uniqueness.
Gives the ordered expansion consumed by true-versus-truncated monodromy.

api.name: MonodromyIterate.zero
api.statement: N_(0,j)=0 for every embedding j.

api.name: MonodromyIterate.succ
api.statement: Unfold the exact recurrence with Frobenius acting on coefficients and shifting j to j−1.

api.name: MonodromyIterate.increment
api.statement: The difference of consecutive iterates transforms by the homogeneous Frobenius-conjugation map and satisfies G39.

api.name: MonodromyIterate.baseChange
api.statement: Finite iterates commute with continuous O-algebra maps preserving the stipulated coefficient category; then G40 transports the limit.

api.name: MonodromyIterate.limit_unique
api.statement: The analytic limit is characterized by the commutation equation and its zero u′-constant term.

tests.name: MonodromyIterate.constantMatrix
tests.statement: If all C_j are constant in u′, then N_nabla(C_j)=0 and every iterate is zero.

tests.name: MonodromyIterate.cyclicIndex
tests.statement: With two distinct Frobenius matrices, N_(2,0) uses φ(N_(1,1)), while N_(2,1) uses φ(N_(1,0)); replacing both by the same embedding fails the recurrence.

tests.name: MonodromyIterate.heightOne
tests.statement: At h=1, the increment denominator in G39 is p for every i, while its u′-order is p^i; the analytic derivative criterion has no t between0 and−1.

tests.name: MonodromyIterate.noncommuting
tests.statement: For noncommuting C_j, the right product in G41 has decreasing order; reversing it is not an equivalent matrix identity.

items.name: Finite derivative criterion for monodromy
items.statement: Over finite flat O coefficients, monodromy holds iff all derivatives of L^(h-1)N_infty at E=0 of orders 0 through h-2 vanish for every embedding. Frobenius compatibility propagates the criterion to the other zeros of L. The h=1 range is empty.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Closed generic monodromy locus
items.statement: When M is free over the allowed R, the criterion defines a basis-independent Zariski closed locus in Spec R[1/p], compatible with base change among these pairs.

items.name: Integral true monodromy ideal
items.statement: There is a unique ideal I_{M,nabla infinity} with O-flat quotient obtained by closing the generic monodromy locus after flat local trivializations. It commutes with flat base change; arbitrary base change only gives I_M S contained in I_{M_S}. Do not replace that inclusion by equality.

uses.how: Use O-flatness to descend an integral p-adic error equality from the generic fibre.
Glue the true-monodromy closed formal substack and identify its points.

api.name: IntegralMonodromyIdeal.local_contraction
api.statement: On a flat trivializing chart, contract the generic analytic derivative ideal from R[1/p] to R. Equivalently take its p-saturated defining ideal in the integral chart.

api.name: IntegralMonodromyIdeal.flat_quotient
api.statement: Prove R/I is p-torsion-free and hence O-flat; its generic fibre is the closed derivative-equation locus.

api.name: IntegralMonodromyIdeal.unique_gluing
api.statement: The generic locus and O-flatness determine the ideal uniquely. Use that uniqueness and flat local trivializations to glue it without choosing a global eigenbasis.

api.name: IntegralMonodromyIdeal.flat_base_change
api.statement: For flat R→S between the source p-adically complete, topologically finite type O-flat algebras, prove I_M S=I_(M_S).

api.name: IntegralMonodromyIdeal.general_map
api.statement: For an arbitrary map within the same domain, retain only I_M S⊆I_(M_S). Consequently, vanishing of I_(M_S) forces the image of I_M to vanish. The inclusion alone does not prove the converse and no equality is asserted.

api.name: IntegralMonodromyIdeal.zero_criterion
api.statement: I_M=0 iff the source family factors through the flat true-monodromy locus; on a trivializing chart this is vanishing of the generic equations together with the flat closure construction.

tests.name: IntegralMonodromyIdeal.saturation_test
tests.statement: In O[x], contraction of the generic ideal generated by p*x is (x); its quotient is O-flat.

tests.name: IntegralMonodromyIdeal.nonflat_comparison_strict
tests.statement: In R=O[x], I=(x) is saturated. Under R→S=O sending x↦p, I S=(p), whose saturation is S since its generic ideal is the unit ideal. Thus saturation can strictly enlarge after a nonflat map even when both coefficient algebras are O-flat.

tests.name: IntegralMonodromyIdeal.zero_ideal
tests.statement: If the generic derivative ideal is zero and R is O-flat, its contraction is zero.

items.name: Monodromy leading term and error series
items.statement: In the notation of G42, descent removal gives equation(7.6), with P_N(A_j)=(-e′v A′_j−[D_j,A_j])(v+p)^h A_j^−1, leading term −φ(L)^h P_N(A_j), and error Σ_{i≥1}φ^(i+1)(L)^h Z_(i,j). G42 records the complete recurrence and exponent/denominator bound, and G43–G44 give the precision argument.

uses.how: Extract the finite differential equations and compare their parameter with Section4.
Estimate the discarded tail with the correct exponent and lower-triangular precision loss.

api.name: MonodromyLeadingTerm.leading_polynomial
api.statement: Set D_j=Diag((sor_prime,j)^(-1)a_prime,j) and P_N(A_j)=(-e_prime v A_j_prime-[D_j,A_j])(v+p)^h A_j^(-1). Prove it lies in L+M, using the height bound.

api.name: MonodromyLeadingTerm.initial_error
api.statement: Set Z_(0,j)=-P_N(A_j). The derivative of the orientation conjugation is the commutator term, with the displayed minus sign in P_N.

api.name: MonodromyLeadingTerm.recurrence
api.statement: For i>=1 set Z_(i,j)=p^(1-h) A_j Ad(s_j^(-1)v^(mu_j+eta_j))(phi(Z_(i-1,j-1)))(v+p)^h A_j^(-1); retain the cyclic predecessor.

api.name: MonodromyLeadingTerm.series_identity
api.statement: Use G42 to identify p^h Ad((sor_prime)^(-1)u_prime^(-a_prime))(L^(h-1)N_infinity) with -phi(L)^h P_N(A_j)+sum_(i>=1)phi^(i+1)(L)^h Z_(i,j), in the analytic localization.

api.name: MonodromyLeadingTerm.exponent_bound
api.statement: For m-deep data, use Z_(i,j) in p^(-i(h-1))v^(1+m(p^i-1)/(p-1)) Mat(R[[v+p]]). The initial 1 occurs once, not once per term of the geometric sum.

api.name: MonodromyLeadingTerm.precision_interface
api.statement: For h>=2 and m>=2h-3, G43/G44 turn the series bound into the common derivative precision m-2h+3. Include the extra one-power loss for dividing lower-triangular entries by v.

tests.name: MonodromyLeadingTerm.diagonal_monomial
tests.statement: If A is diagonal with ith entry (v+p)^c_i, then its commutator with D vanishes and P_N has ith entry -e_prime*c_i*v*(v+p)^(h-1).

tests.name: MonodromyLeadingTerm.precision_boundary
tests.statement: At m=2h-3 the common precision is zero, so the ideal containment modulo p^0 is vacuous; obtaining a nontrivial mod-p comparison requires a strictly larger margin.

items.name: Truncated monodromy ideal
items.statement: Given an eigenbasis beta, I_{M,beta,nabla1} is generated by derivatives of v^(-[k>l])P_N(A_j)_{kl} at v=-p, of orders 0 through h-2, for every j,k,l. This ideal is basis dependent as presented and is not the true ideal by definition.

uses.how: Connects derivative vanishing to the local-model differential condition.
Provides all integral generators for the precision containment.

api.name: TruncatedMonodromy.generators
api.statement: Form the finite family indexed by j,k,l and 0≤t≤h−2 from the integral v-divided lower entries.

api.name: TruncatedMonodromy.baseChange
api.statement: For compatible eigenbases, continuous coefficient maps carry the generators to the corresponding generators; this concerns the truncated ideal, not arbitrary base change of the saturated true ideal.

api.name: TruncatedMonodromy.vanishing_iff
api.statement: An R-algebra map kills the ideal exactly when every listed evaluated derivative vanishes.

api.name: TruncatedMonodromy.divisibility
api.statement: Under p>h−2, vanishing is equivalent to (v+p)^(h−1) divisibility of the appropriately v-divided entries.

api.name: TruncatedMonodromy.precision
api.statement: With the explicit genericity/integrality bound, every generator is in I_nabla∞+(p^(m−2h+3)).

tests.name: TruncatedMonodromy.heightOne
tests.statement: At h=1 the generator range is empty and the ideal is zero.

tests.name: TruncatedMonodromy.lowerEntry
tests.statement: For a lower entry P_kl=vF, the t=0 generator is F(−p), not P_kl(−p)=−pF(−p). Thus omitting the v division changes the ideal.

tests.name: TruncatedMonodromy.factorialBoundary
tests.statement: Over F_p, F=(v+p)^p has all ordinary derivatives zero but is not divisible by (v+p)^(p+1); the factorial-unit hypothesis in G10 cannot be omitted.

tests.name: TruncatedMonodromy.precisionZero
tests.statement: When m=2h−3, the stated containment is in I_nabla∞+(1), hence is tautological; it does not assert equality of the two ideals.

items.name: Truncated differential local-model equation
items.statement: If p>h-2, vanishing of the derivatives is equivalent to divisibility by (v+p)^(h-1), and hence to (e'v A'-A Diag(s_or^-1 a'))A^-1 in (v+p)^-1 L^+M. The corresponding local-model parameter is -(s_or^-1 a')/e'.

items.name: Integral precision of the leading monodromy equations
items.statement: For an m-deep lowest-alcove presentation and a height [0,h] module over allowed O-flat complete R with eigenbasis, I_nabla1 is contained in (I_nabla infinity,p^(m-2h+3)). Use m>=2h-3 for an integral ideal statement, as explicitly imposed in the subsequent application. The theorem gives containment, not equality of ideals.

items.name: Emerton–Gee representation stack
items.statement: Import the Noetherian formal algebraic stack X_n of projective rank n étale (phi,Gamma)-modules from [22]. On complete local Noetherian O-algebras with finite residue field it represents the groupoid of continuous rank n GK representations. For a finite étale Z_p-algebra take products over its field factors.

api.name: EmertonGeeStack.import_stack
api.statement: Import the Noetherian formal algebraic stack X_n of rank-n projective etale (phi,Gamma)-modules from Emerton–Gee, with its coefficient field and continuity conventions.

api.name: EmertonGeeStack.local_representation_equivalence
api.statement: On complete local Noetherian O-algebras with finite residue field, identify its groupoid with continuous G_K actions on rank-n projective modules, including equivariant isomorphisms.

api.name: EmertonGeeStack.restriction
api.statement: Use the canonical map X_n→Phi-Mod_et,K whose local representation interpretation is restriction G_K→G_Kinfinity. Do not declare it a monomorphism before the genericity theorem G23.

api.name: EmertonGeeStack.product_fields
api.statement: For a finite etale Z_p-algebra with fraction algebra product_v F_v^+, form the product of the corresponding stacks over Spf O.

api.name: EmertonGeeStack.underlying_reduced

api.name: EmertonGeeStack.supplier_corrections

tests.name: EmertonGeeStack.singleton_product

tests.name: EmertonGeeStack.automorphisms_retained
tests.statement: A rank-one representation over a field has scalar automorphisms. Replacing its groupoid by the set of isomorphism classes loses data and does not define the same stack.

tests.name: EmertonGeeStack.restriction_domain
tests.statement: The local representation equivalence stated here has complete local Noetherian rings with finite residue field as its domain; it must not be invoked on an arbitrary test algebra without the additional comparison theorem.

items.name: Potentially crystalline formal substacks
items.statement: X^{lambda,tau} is the unique O-flat closed formal substack characterized on finite flat O-algebras by potentially crystalline type (lambda,tau). Define X^{[0,h],tau} and X^{<=lambda,tau} as scheme-theoretic unions over the indicated dominant weights, not as reduced unions.

api.name: PotentiallyCrystallineStack.fixed_type
api.statement: For dominant lambda and inertial type tau import the unique O-flat closed formal substack X^(lambda,tau), with the finite-flat coefficient point condition stated by Emerton–Gee.

api.name: PotentiallyCrystallineStack.point_criterion
api.statement: A point over a finite flat O-algebra belongs iff its rational representation is potentially crystalline with Hodge weights lambda and inertial type tau. Nilpotent coefficient algebras remain in the test category.

api.name: PotentiallyCrystallineStack.Hodge_convention
api.statement: Translate LLHLM weights to Emerton–Gee weights by lambda↦-w0(lambda); the LLHLM cyclotomic character has weight +1 and D_pst has the stated covariant type tau.

api.name: PotentiallyCrystallineStack.height_union
api.statement: Form X^([0,h],tau) as the finite scheme-theoretic union over dominant tuples with coordinates in [0,h]. In a chart use the intersection of defining ideals.

api.name: PotentiallyCrystallineStack.dominance_union
api.statement: Form X^(<=lambda,tau) as the finite scheme-theoretic union over dominant lambda_prime<=lambda; retain the fixed central-class requirement.

api.name: PotentiallyCrystallineStack.inclusions
api.statement: Transport inclusions of the finite indexing sets to closed immersions of their unions, preserving their common ambient X_n and the source flat/reduced conclusions.

tests.name: PotentiallyCrystallineStack.cyclotomic_sign
tests.statement: For rank one lambda=1 corresponds to Emerton–Gee weight -1. For GL_2 lambda=(2,0), the translated dominant tuple is (0,-2).

tests.name: PotentiallyCrystallineStack.height_zero
tests.statement: The height interval [0,0] contains only the all-zero dominant tuple in every embedding, so the union is that fixed-Hodge-type locus.

tests.name: PotentiallyCrystallineStack.union_not_reduction
tests.statement: The two flat sections x=0 and x=varpi have integral union x(x-varpi)=0; its special fibre retains x^2=0. Scheme-theoretic union is not the operation of taking a reduced union.

items.name: Analytically unramified formal stack
items.statement: A topologically finite type p-adic formal algebraic stack is analytically unramified when all smooth affine charts have reduced rings, equivalently its finite-type versal rings are reduced. Its associated reduced formal stack pulls back to Spf A_red. Distinguish this from the underlying reduced algebraic stack Spec(A/I)_red.

api.name: AnalyticallyUnramifiedFormalStack.predicate

api.name: AnalyticallyUnramifiedFormalStack.versal_criterion
api.statement: Use the cited formal-stack theorem to identify this property with reduced finite-type versal rings, including the residual Jacobson and Noetherian hypotheses.

api.name: AnalyticallyUnramifiedFormalStack.reduced_formal_substack
api.statement: Construct the maximal analytically unramified closed formal substack Z_prime→Z; on each smooth chart its pullback is Spf(A_red).

api.name: AnalyticallyUnramifiedFormalStack.smooth_pullback
api.statement: Prove this chartwise reduction is compatible with the smooth transition morphisms so that the local closed substacks descend.

api.name: AnalyticallyUnramifiedFormalStack.underlying_algebraic_comparison
api.statement: For an ideal of definition I in A, the underlying reduced algebraic stack has chart Spec((A/I)_red), whereas the associated reduced formal chart is Spf(A_red). Keep both maps into Z.

api.name: AnalyticallyUnramifiedFormalStack.point_detection_hypotheses

tests.statement: For A=O a complete DVR, Spf(A_red)=Spf O but Spec((A/(varpi))_red)=Spec F; these are different objects.

tests.statement: For A=O[epsilon]/epsilon^2 with the p-adic topology, its associated reduced formal scheme is Spf O.

tests.name: AnalyticallyUnramifiedFormalStack.already_reduced
tests.statement: If every smooth chart ring is reduced, the associated reduced formal substack map is an isomorphism.

items.name: Crystalline stacks are flat, topologically finite type and analytically unramified
items.statement: Theorem 7.2.2(1). Let tau be a tame inertial type for K, h >= 0 and lambda in X_*(T^vee)^J dominant, and let ? in {[0,h], <=lambda, lambda}. Then the stack X^{?,tau} is a p-adic formal algebraic stack, flat and topologically of finite type over Spf O. Furthermore, X^{?,tau} is analytically unramified. Here X^{lambda,tau} is the unique closed formal substack of X_n that is O-flat and whose Lambda-points, for finite flat O-algebras Lambda, are the G_K-representations on rank n projective Lambda-modules that become potentially crystalline of Hodge-Tate weight lambda and inertial type tau after inverting p ([22, Thm 4.8.12]). The convention is that the cyclotomic character has weight +1, so this is X^{-w0(lambda),tau} of [22] (Warning 7.2.1). X^{[0,h],tau} is defined in the same way with Hodge-Tate weights in [0,h], and X^{<=lambda,tau} ⊂ X^{[0,h],tau} is the scheme-theoretic union of the X^{lambda',tau} for dominant lambda' <= lambda. Proof: the first half is [22, Thm 4.8.12] (printed [23], E32). The second half (analytic unramifiedness) is proved together with part (2), from part (3) and [49, Thm 3.3.8].
items.note: Route owner: WeightZeroCrystallineLiftingRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Regular generic fibres of smooth charts of crystalline stacks
items.statement: Theorem 7.2.2(2). Let tau be a tame inertial type for K, lambda in X_*(T^vee)^J dominant and ? in {[0,h], <=lambda, lambda}. For any smooth map Spf R -> X^{?,tau} from a topologically finite type affine p-adic formal algebraic space, the ring R[1/p] is regular. Proof: from part (3) and [49, Theorem 3.3.8] (Kisin, Potentially semi-stable deformation rings). The same argument gives the second half of part (1).
items.note: Split from G15. Part (2) of Theorem 7.2.2 is proved together with the second half of part (1), but separately from the first half of (1), from (3) and from (4).

uses.how: An O-flat chart ring R with R[1/p] regular is reduced, which gives analytic unramifiedness of X^{?,tau}.

items.name: Potentially crystalline deformation rings are versal rings of crystalline stacks
items.statement: Theorem 7.2.2(3). Let tau, lambda and ? in {[0,h], <=lambda, lambda} be as in Theorem 7.2.2, and let rhobar in X^{?,tau}(F) correspond to a mod p representation of G_K. Then the potentially crystalline deformation ring R^{?,tau}_rhobar is a versal ring to X^{?,tau} at rhobar. Proof: [22, Proposition 4.8.10] (printed [23], E32).
items.note: Split from G15. Part (3) has its own imported proof.

uses.where: G45 and G15 (Theorem 7.2.2(2) and the second half of (1))

Versal rings of X^{lambda',tau} at semisimple rhobar are identified with the rings R^{lambda',tau}_rhobar, which are domains or zero.
With R^ver = R^square_rhobar, the fibre product Spf R^ver ×_{X_n} X^{lambda+eta,tau} is the framed potentially crystalline deformation ring, which is a versal ring of X^{lambda+eta,tau}.

items.name: Point criterion (1): finite-flat points and an analytically unramified target
items.locator: Lemma 7.2.6(1), PDF144; proof (reduction and first case) PDF144
items.statement: Lemma 7.2.6, case (1). Let f: Y -> Z be a monomorphism of p-adic formal algebraic stacks topologically of finite type over Spf O, and assume that Z is flat over Spf O. Assume that Z is analytically unramified and that, for any finite flat O-algebra Lambda, f: Y(Lambda) -> Z(Lambda) is essentially surjective. Then f is an isomorphism. Proof: the problem is smooth-local on Z, so one may take Z = Spf B with B p-adically complete, topologically of finite type and O-flat; then Y is a formal scheme ([75, Tag 0B89]). B is reduced, Z_p-flat and Nagata. By [2, Lemma 4.1.2], every map B -> A to a local Artinian O-algebra with finite residue field factors through B -> Lambda for a finite flat O-algebra Lambda, so Y(A) -> Z(A) is an equivalence. Lemma 7.2.5 then makes every base change to O/varpi^a an isomorphism.
