items.name: Point criterion (2): closed immersion, points over rings of integers, analytically unramified target
items.statement: Lemma 7.2.6, case (2). Let f: Y -> Z be a monomorphism of p-adic formal algebraic stacks topologically of finite type over Spf O, and assume that Z is flat over Spf O. Assume that Z is analytically unramified, that f is a closed immersion, and that for any finite extension E' of E with ring of integers O', f: Y(O') -> Z(O') is essentially surjective. Then f is an isomorphism. Proof: locally Z = Spf B and Y = Spf B/J. Every map B[1/p] -> E' comes from a map B -> O', so J[1/p] lies in every maximal ideal of B[1/p]. Since B[1/p] is Jacobson and reduced, J[1/p] = 0, and J = 0 because B is O-flat.
items.note: Split from G20. The second of three alternative hypotheses, proved as a separate case.

uses.how: K^{[0,h],tau} -> X^{[0,h],tau} is a closed immersion (Proposition 5.4.3) into an O-flat, analytically unramified stack (G15). The lemma reduces the isomorphism to essential surjectivity on O'-points, which is supplied by Kisin's Breuil-Kisin lattices.

items.name: Point criterion (3): closed immersion and finite-flat points
items.statement: Lemma 7.2.6, case (3). Let f: Y -> Z be a monomorphism of p-adic formal algebraic stacks topologically of finite type over Spf O, and assume that Z is flat over Spf O. Assume that f is a closed immersion and that, for any finite flat O-algebra Lambda, f: Y(Lambda) -> Z(Lambda) is essentially surjective. Then f is an isomorphism. No analytic unramifiedness is assumed. Proof: locally Y = Spf B/J. For each maximal ideal m of B[1/p] and each a >= 1, the map B -> B[1/p]/m^a factors through a finite flat O-algebra Lambda with Lambda[1/p] = B[1/p]/m^a, and the hypothesis forces it to factor through B/J. Hence J[1/p] ⊂ ∩_a m^a, so J[1/p]_m = 0 for every m. Therefore J[1/p] = 0, and J = 0 by O-flatness.
items.note: Split from G20. The third alternative hypothesis, proved as a separate case.

uses.how: Gives Z ≅ Y^{[0,h],tau,nabla_infty}, where Z is the associated reduced formal substack: the map is a closed immersion that is essentially surjective on finite flat points.

items.name: The Kisin-module stack is the crystalline stack for (h+1)-generic types
items.statement: Proposition 7.2.7. Assume that τ is (h+1)-generic. Then the natural map K^{[0,h],τ} → X^{[0,h],τ} is an isomorphism. Here K^{[0,h],τ} = X^{[0,h],τ} ×_{Φ-Mod^{ét,n}_K} Y^{[0,h],τ} is the pullback of ε_τ : Y^{[0,h],τ} → Φ-Mod^{ét,n}_K along X^{[0,h],τ} → X_n → Φ-Mod^{ét,n}_K (the printed "along X^{λ,τ}" is E46). Proof (PDF145): by Proposition 5.4.3 the map is a closed immersion. By Lemma 7.2.6 (second case, G47) it suffices that K^{[0,h],τ}(O′) → X^{[0,h],τ}(O′) is essentially surjective for every finite extension E′/E with ring of integers O′. Let V ∈ X^{[0,h],τ}(O′) be an O′-lattice in a potentially crystalline representation over E′ with Hodge–Tate weights in [0,h], and let 𝓜 ∈ Φ-Mod^{ét,n}_{dd,L′}(O′) be the associated étale φ-module with descent data from L′ to K. By [48, Cor. (1.3.15), Prop. (2.1.5), Lemma (2.1.15)] there is a unique projective φ_𝓜-stable S_{L′,O′}-submodule 𝔐 ⊂ 𝓜 with 𝓜 = 𝔐 ⊗_{S_{L′}} O_{E,L′} and the cokernel of φ_𝓜 on 𝔐 killed by E(u′)^h; projectivity is [2, Remark 2.2.16(2)]. Uniqueness makes 𝔐 stable under the semilinear Δ′-action. Since 𝔐/u′𝔐[1/p] ≅ D_pst(V^∨) ≅ τ^∨ ⊗_O (K′ ⊗_{Z_p} O′) as projective K′ ⊗_{Z_p} O′-modules with the Δ = I(L′/K)-action, 𝔐 ∈ Y^{[0,h],τ}(O′). So V is isomorphic to the image of (V, 𝔐) ∈ K^{[0,h],τ}(O′).
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Breuil–Kisin lattices over finite flat coefficient algebras are projective
items.statement: Remark 7.2.8. Let Λ be a finite flat O-algebra which is not the ring of integers of a finite extension of E, and let V ∈ X^{[0,h],τ}(Λ) with τ (h+1)-generic (printed X^{[0,h]}(Λ); see the S5 source issue). The unique Breuil–Kisin module M associated to V, viewed as an O-lattice in a potentially crystalline representation over E, is a priori only an S_{L′,Λ}-module. However, it follows from Proposition 7.2.7 that in this case it is actually S_{L′,Λ}-projective.
items.note: Split from G21. The paper gives no argument beyond "it follows from the above Proposition". It goes as follows. By Proposition 7.2.7, V lifts to (V, M′) ∈ K^{[0,h],τ}(Λ) with M′ ∈ Y^{[0,h],τ}(Λ), which is projective over S_{L′,Λ} by definition. Since Λ is finite flat over O, S_{L′,Λ} = S_{L′,O} ⊗_O Λ is finite projective over S_{L′,O}. So M′ is also a projective φ-stable S_{L′,O}-lattice in the étale φ-module of V, with cokernel of φ killed by E(u′)^h. The uniqueness from [48] used in the proof of Proposition 7.2.7 then gives M′ = M. The paper does not cite the remark again. It can be folded into G21 (drop.json: "also Remark 7.2.8 (PDF 145)"), but G21 no longer states it, so a folded version must put the claim back into G21.

uses.how: It records what Proposition 7.2.7 (G21) says about Λ-points: V ∈ X^{[0,h],τ}(Λ) comes from a projective S_{L′,Λ}-module in Y^{[0,h],τ}(Λ).

items.name: Cyclotomic-free residual representation
items.statement: A residual representation is cyclotomic free when a prime-to-p unramified extension M/K makes its semisimplification a sum of characters and H^0(G_M,rho_ss tensor epsilon^-1)=0.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Compare invariants, equivariant Hom spaces and stable submodules after restriction to G_Kinfinity.
Deduce generic full faithfulness and integral lattice stability.

api.name: CyclotomicFreeRepresentation.mk
api.statement: A witness consists of an unramified extension M/K of degree prime to p on which rho^ss is a sum of characters, and H^0(G_M,rho^ss tensor epsilon^(-1))=0.

api.name: CyclotomicFreeRepresentation.character_criterion
api.statement: Given the splitting witness, the invariant condition means no character constituent equals the restricted cyclotomic character. This tests rho itself, not automatically all pairwise ratios.

api.name: CyclotomicFreeRepresentation.semisimplification
api.statement: The property depends only on rho^ss by definition; an isomorphism of semisimplifications transports a witness.

api.name: CyclotomicFreeRepresentation.direct_summand
api.statement: A representation whose semisimplification is a direct summand of a finite direct sum of a witnessed rho is cyclotomic free using the same M.

api.name: CyclotomicFreeRepresentation.generic_adjoint
api.statement: Use G23/Lemma7.2.10(2): if rho^ss on inertia is 2-generic, then ad(rho) is cyclotomic free. This is the separate bridge needed to control Hom spaces.

api.name: CyclotomicFreeRepresentation.restriction_Hom
api.statement: Under the source common-semisimplification hypothesis and cyclotomic freeness of its adjoint, restriction identifies the indicated finite-length equivariant Hom groups; apply it to submodule inclusions only through the proved stability lemma.

tests.name: CyclotomicFreeRepresentation.cyclotomic_character_fails
tests.statement: For rho=epsilon modulo p, rho tensor epsilon^(-1) is trivial on every extension, so its H^0 is nonzero and no witness exists.

tests.name: CyclotomicFreeRepresentation.trivial_character_p_odd
tests.statement: For K unramified over Q_p and p>2, the residual cyclotomic character is nontrivial on inertia. The trivial rank-one representation is cyclotomic free with M=K.

tests.name: CyclotomicFreeRepresentation.adjoint_ratios
tests.statement: For a split representation with characters chi_1,chi_2, its adjoint has constituents 1,1,chi_1/chi_2,chi_2/chi_1. The cyclotomic-free test for the adjoint checks these ratios, unlike the test for the original representation.

items.name: Invariants of a cyclotomic-free representation do not grow on restriction to G_{K_infty}
items.statement: Lemma 7.2.10(1). Let rhobar: G_K -> GL_m(Fbar_p) be cyclotomic free (Definition 7.2.9: there is an unramified extension M/K of degree prime to p such that rhobar^ss|_{G_M} is a direct sum of characters and H^0(G_M, rhobar^ss|_{G_M} ⊗ epsilon^{-1}) = 0, where epsilon is the p-adic cyclotomic character). Then the natural inclusion induces an isomorphism H^0(G_K, rhobar) ≅ H^0(G_{K_infty}, rhobar). Proof: from (the proof of) [59, Lemma 3.11].
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Two-generic residual representations have cyclotomic-free adjoint
items.statement: Lemma 7.2.10(2). Let rhobar: G_K -> GL_m(Fbar_p). If rhobar^ss|_{I_K} is 2-generic, then ad(rhobar) is cyclotomic free (Definition 7.2.9). Proof: [59, Proposition 3.9]. That proof is written for n = 3 but works in general, and 2-generic in this paper is stronger than 2-generic in [59] (see [56, Remark 2.2.8]).
items.note: Split from G23. Part (2) is imported separately from [59, Prop 3.9].

uses.how: The residual rhobar is 2-generic by Corollary 5.5.10, so ad(rhobar) is cyclotomic free and Lemma 7.2.10(3) applies.
Makes W/p^N W satisfy the hypothesis of Lemma 7.2.10(4).
'ad(rhobar) is cyclotomic free as rhobar is at least 4n-generic.'

items.name: Restriction to G_{K_infty} is fully faithful for cyclotomic-free finite-length modules
items.statement: Lemma 7.2.10(3). Suppose V and W are two O[G_K]-modules of finite length. Assume there exists a semisimple G_K-representation rhobar such that ad(rhobar) is cyclotomic free and such that V^ss and W^ss are direct summands of a direct sum of finitely many copies of rhobar. Then the natural restriction map induces an isomorphism Hom_{G_K}(V,W) ≅ Hom_{G_{K_infty}}(V,W). Proof: finite direct sums of ad(rhobar) are cyclotomic free, and W^ss ⊗ (V^ss)^vee is a direct summand of one; the result then follows from part (1). See sourceIssues: (1) must be applied to Hom_O(V,W) in its finite-length form.
items.note: Split from G23. Part (3) is deduced from part (1).

uses.how: For local Artinian A with finite residue field, restriction identifies Isom_{G_K}(V_A,W_A) with Isom_{G_{K_infty}}(V_A,W_A).
Makes an inclusion of an irreducible G_{K_infty}-submodule G_K-equivariant.

items.name: G_{K_infty}-submodules are G_K-stable in the cyclotomic-free range
items.statement: Lemma 7.2.10(4). Let W be as in (3): a finite-length O[G_K]-module whose semisimplification is a direct summand of a direct sum of finitely many copies of a semisimple G_K-representation rhobar with ad(rhobar) cyclotomic free. Then any G_{K_infty}-submodule V ⊂ W is G_K-stable. Proof: if V is irreducible, it extends uniquely to a G_K-module, and part (3) makes the G_{K_infty}-equivariant inclusion V ↪ W G_K-equivariant. In general, let V_0 be a nonzero irreducible G_{K_infty}-submodule of V. It is a G_K-submodule of W, and the argument is repeated for V/V_0 ⊂ W/V_0.
items.note: Split from G23. Part (4) is deduced from part (3).

uses.how: Applied to V/p^N W ⊂ W/p^N W to show that the lattice V is G_K-stable.
A G_{K_infty}-stable filtration on rho_x|G_{K_infty} is automatically G_K-stable, which matches the flag from Lemma 7.4.6 (G36) with the flag in (7.15).

items.name: Restriction monomorphism for crystalline families
items.statement: If tau is (h+2)-generic, X^{[0,h],tau}->X_n->étale phi modules is a monomorphism on groupoids over the full coefficient category, proved first on finite Artinian rings and then by represented isomorphism functors.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: True monodromy cuts out the Kisin-crystalline stack (height range [0,h])
items.locator: Proposition 7.2.12, first assertion, PDF147; proof PDF147-148
items.statement: Proposition 7.2.12, first assertion, in the setting of Proposition 7.2.3: h >= 1 and tau an (h+2)-generic tame inertial type. The printed statement omits this hypothesis; see sourceIssues. The natural map K^{[0,h],tau} -> Y^{[0,h],tau} factors through the substack Y^{[0,h],tau,nabla_infty} ⊂ Y^{[0,h],tau}, and the induced map K^{[0,h],tau} -> Y^{[0,h],tau,nabla_infty} is an isomorphism. Here K^{[0,h],tau} = X^{[0,h],tau} ×_{Phi-Mod^{et,n}_K} Y^{[0,h],tau} (E46), and Y^{[0,h],tau,nabla_infty} is the O-flat closed substack on which the ideal I_{M,nabla_infty} of Proposition 7.1.6 vanishes. Proof: take a smooth cover Spf R -> K^{[0,h],tau} ≅ X^{[0,h],tau}. R is O-flat, reduced and topologically of finite type, and I_{M,nabla_infty} vanishes at every O'-point (Proposition 7.1.4), so it lies in the Jacobson radical of R[1/p] and is 0. This gives monomorphisms K ↪ Z ↪ Y^{[0,h],tau,nabla_infty}, where Z is the associated reduced formal substack. Proposition 7.1.4 and Lemma 7.2.13 give essential surjectivity on points over finite flat Lambda. Then K ≅ Z by Lemma 7.2.6(1) and Z ≅ Y^{[0,h],tau,nabla_infty} by Lemma 7.2.6(3).
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Integral lattices of Breuil-Kisin modules with G_K-extendable generic fibre are G_K-stable
items.statement: Lemma 7.2.13. Let tau be (h+2)-generic. Let Lambda be a finite flat O-algebra. Suppose M in Y^{[0,h],tau}(Lambda) and V = T^*_dd(M), a G_{K_infty}-representation on a free Lambda-module of rank n. Suppose V[1/p] extends to a G_K-representation. Then V ⊂ V[1/p] is G_K-stable. Proof: it suffices to treat Lambda local, with residue field F'. The semisimplified reduction V^ss_{F'} extends uniquely to a semisimple G_K-representation rhobar, which is 2-generic by Corollary 5.5.10 (printed 'Lemma 5.5.10'). Choose a Lambda[G_K]-stable O-lattice W in V[1/p] with V ⊂ W; then (W/varpi)^ss is a finite direct sum of copies of rhobar. Take N with p^N W ⊂ V ⊂ W and apply Lemma 7.2.10(4) to V/p^N W ⊂ W/p^N W.
items.note: Split from G25. It is a separately numbered lemma with its own proof.

uses.how: For x in Y^{[0,h],tau,nabla_infty}(Lambda), Proposition 7.1.4 extends V[1/p] to a potentially crystalline G_K-representation. This lemma makes V itself G_K-stable, which gives essential surjectivity of K^{[0,h],tau}(Lambda) -> Y^{[0,h],tau,nabla_infty}(Lambda).

items.name: True monodromy cuts out the Kisin-crystalline stack (Hodge bound <=lambda)
items.locator: Proposition 7.2.12, second assertion, PDF147; proof PDF148-149
items.statement: Proposition 7.2.12, second assertion, in the setting of Proposition 7.2.3: h >= 1 and tau an (h+2)-generic tame inertial type (omitted in print; see sourceIssues). Let lambda = (lambda_j) in X_*(T^vee)^J be dominant with lambda_j in [0,h]^n. The natural map K^{<=lambda,tau} ↪ K^{[0,h],tau} -> Y^{[0,h],tau} factors through Y^{<=lambda,tau,nabla_infty} ⊂ Y^{[0,h],tau}, and the induced map K^{<=lambda,tau} -> Y^{<=lambda,tau,nabla_infty} is an isomorphism. Proof: let V in X^{[0,h],tau}(O') have Breuil-Kisin module M. Then D_dR(V^vee) ≅ (phi^*M / E(u') phi^*M)[1/p] ([22, §4.7]; the dual appears because T^*_dd is contravariant), so V has Hodge-Tate weights <= lambda if and only if M in Y^{<=lambda,tau}(O'). For finite flat Lambda, M in Y^{<=lambda,tau}(Lambda) implies V in X^{<=lambda,tau}(Lambda), because the Hodge filtration is by projective Lambda[1/p]-modules and one may pass to Lambda^red. With these two facts, the argument of G25 runs again.
items.note: Split from G25. The second, unnumbered assertion of Proposition 7.2.12, proved after the first with extra Hodge-filtration input.

uses.how: K^{<=lambda,tau} ↪ Y^{<=lambda,tau} is a closed immersion with image Y^{<=lambda,tau,nabla_infty}, so X^{<=lambda,tau} ≅ Y^{<=lambda,tau,nabla_infty}.
X^{<=lambda,tau} is obtained from Y^{<=lambda,tau} by imposing explicit monodromy equations, which are then compared with local models.

items.name: Presentation-dependent local-model parameter
items.statement: Set a_{tau,j'}=(s_or,j')^-1(a'^(j'))/(1-p^f'). It depends on the chosen lowest-alcove presentation, and reduces to s_j^-1(mu_j+eta_j) modulo varpi for j in J.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Specialize the universal differential equations and the genericity polynomial.
Translate local-model components to the residual representation stack.

api.name: LocalModelTypeParameter.mk
api.statement: From the fixed presentation and K06 data set a_(tau,jprime)=(sor_prime,jprime)^(-1)(a_prime^(jprime))/(1-p^fprime), as a tuple in O^n.

api.name: LocalModelTypeParameter.denominator_unit
api.statement: Since 1-p^fprime reduces to 1 modulo varpi, it is a unit in O; this makes the parameter integral.

api.name: LocalModelTypeParameter.monodromy_sign
api.statement: With eprime=p^fprime-1, identify this parameter with -(sor_prime)^(-1)a_prime/eprime used in G10. This checks the sign in the differential local-model comparison.

api.name: LocalModelTypeParameter.residue
api.statement: For j in J, use Lemma7.3.1 to obtain a_(tau,j) mod varpi=s_j^(-1)(mu_j+eta_j) mod varpi.

api.name: LocalModelTypeParameter.coefficient_extension
api.statement: Base extending the coefficient DVR carries this tuple and its inverse denominator to the tuple for the same presentation over the extension.

api.name: LocalModelTypeParameter.presentation_dependence
api.statement: Store the lowest-alcove presentation with the parameter. Changing presentations requires its explicit transformation law; equality of tame types alone does not assert equality of these integral tuples.

tests.name: LocalModelTypeParameter.one_embedding_identity_orientation
tests.statement: If fprime=1 and s=1, then a_tau=(mu+eta)/(1-p), reducing to mu+eta modulo p.

tests.name: LocalModelTypeParameter.sign_test
tests.statement: For p=5,fprime=1 and oriented a_prime=3, the parameter is -3/4, which is 3 modulo 5; +3/4 would give the wrong residue.

tests.name: LocalModelTypeParameter.central_shift_integral
tests.statement: In the preceding single-embedding setting, shifting the presentation numerator by (p-1)c changes a_tau by -c. Congruent tame character data therefore need not give identical integral parameters.

items.name: Regular-weight unions and framed charts
items.statement: Define M_{J,reg}(<=lambda,nabla a_tau) as the scheme-theoretic union of the flat models for regular dominant lambda'<=lambda. It is the maximal O-flat closed part equidimensional of dimension 1+|J|n(n-1)/2. Define the corresponding affine charts, torus torsors, regular crystalline union X_reg, and formal pullbacks in (7.13).
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Compare the maximal-dimensional flat union to the corresponding regular potentially crystalline formal charts.
Compare underlying reduced components for regular Hodge types.

api.name: RegularHodgeUnion.regular_index
api.statement: Take the finite set of dominant lambda_prime<=lambda that are regular in every embedding, with the common central class and the standing effective bounds.

api.name: RegularHodgeUnion.model_union
api.statement: Form the scheme-theoretic union of M_J(lambda_prime,nabla a_tau) over this set, with ideal intersections in a common bounded ambient model.

api.name: RegularHodgeUnion.maximal_dimension
api.statement: Characterize it as the maximal O-flat closed part of the flat Hodge union that is equidimensional of total dimension 1+|J|n(n-1)/2, using the flag dimensions of the generic strata.

api.name: RegularHodgeUnion.chart_and_torsor
api.statement: Intersect with each affine chart U(z,<=lambda), then pull back to its trivial Tdual^J torsor. The torus lift adds |J|n to the total dimension.

api.name: RegularHodgeUnion.crystalline_union
api.statement: Form X_reg^(<=lambda,tau) as the scheme-theoretic union of X^(lambda_prime,tau) over the same regular index set; define the remaining objects of (7.13) by its specified solid Cartesian squares.

api.name: RegularHodgeUnion.formal_comparison
api.statement: Complete the indicated algebraic charts p-adically before comparing with true-monodromy formal charts. The Elkik-produced dotted map is noncanonical; Warning7.3.3 does not assert commutativity of the full triangle in the ambient chart.

tests.name: RegularHodgeUnion.GL2_regular_selection
tests.statement: For one embedding and lambda=(2,0), the dominant interval consists of (2,0) and (1,1). Only (2,0) is regular, so the regular union omits the central generic point stratum.

tests.name: RegularHodgeUnion.dimension_with_torus
tests.statement: For n=2 and |J|=1, the regular model has total dimension 2 over Spec O, and its torus lift has total dimension 4; their special fibres have dimensions 1 and 3.

tests.name: RegularHodgeUnion.formal_not_algebraic
tests.statement: The infinite true-monodromy equations define a formal chart on complete test rings. A point of an algebraic naive chart does not by itself define an evaluation of those infinite series.

items.name: Approximate equations give a noncanonical closed immersion
items.statement: For regular dominant lambda_j in [0,h]^n and an (h+2)-lowest-alcove presentation of tau, there is N_sing depending only on the set of lambda_j, not p, such that N_sing-depth supplies the diagonal closed immersion from the true-monodromy formal chart to the naive differential formal chart. It lifts the mod-p map using Elkik approximation and is not canonical or required to commute with the ambient triangle.

items.name: Polynomial-generic regular local-model isomorphism
items.locator: Theorem7.3.2(2), first conclusion PDF151–155; stated in the introduction as Theorems 1.2.1 and 1.4.3 (PDF 5, 11)
items.statement: There is a nonzero integral polynomial P depending only on {lambda_j} and the ramification index e of O, not p, such that P-genericity of the presentation makes the vertical map between the framed X_reg chart and the p-completed regular differential chart an isomorphism. All marked solid pullback squares and torus torsors are part of the construction; the isomorphism is not a global canonical gluing over O.

items.name: Domain versal rings at semisimple points
items.locator: Theorem7.3.2(2), second conclusion PDF151–155; also Remark 7.3.4 (PDF 152); stated in the introduction as Theorem 1.5.5 (PDF 17)
items.statement: Under G29, for every regular dominant lambda'<=lambda and every semisimple residual GK representation rho, every corresponding versal ring of X^{lambda',tau} is a domain or zero. No assertion for arbitrary wild residual representations. Products over finitely many unramified local fields retain the theorem by Remark7.3.4.

items.name: Nonempty crystalline shape charts
items.statement: For regular lambda'_j in [0,h']^n and a (4n+h')-generic lowest-alcove presentation, X^{lambda',tau}(z) is nonempty iff z lies in Adm^vee(lambda'). The nonempty direction imports potentially diagonalizable obvious-weight lifts and the detectability criterion, not just existence of a Kisin lattice.

items.name: Serre-labelled Emerton–Gee components
items.statement: Import the irreducible-component labelling of X_n,red from [22, Theorem6.5.1]. The paper defines C_sigma using the dual/det^(n-1) relabelling. For 1-deep sigma=F(kappa), a dense locus consists of maximally nonsplit upper triangular representations with diagonal inertia characters product_j omega_j^((kappa_j+eta_j)_i). Retain the tres-ramifiee boundary rule for nondeep weights.
items.note: Route owner: WeightZeroCrystallineLiftingRings. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Identify sufficiently generic components with the shifted torus quotients of local-model components.
Use component membership for weight and Breuil–Mezard assertions.

api.name: SerreLabelledGaloisComponent.EG_label
api.statement: Import the Emerton–Gee Serre-weight labelling of irreducible components of X_n,red, with the author-errata proof replacement E28.

api.name: SerreLabelledGaloisComponent.relabel
api.statement: Define C_sigma=X_EG,n,red^(sigma_dual tensor det^(n-1)). For multiple local fields use products over the common residue field with the corresponding tuple of labels.

api.name: SerreLabelledGaloisComponent.deep_dense_locus
api.statement: For 1-deep sigma=F(kappa), identify the dense maximally nonsplit upper-triangular locus with unique G_K-stable complete flag and diagonal inertia chi_i=product_j omega_j^((kappa_j+eta_j)_i).

api.name: SerreLabelledGaloisComponent.closure
api.statement: C_sigma is the reduced closure of the prescribed dense locus, using the corrected EG construction; extend assertions on that locus only by an appropriate closedness/density argument.

api.name: SerreLabelledGaloisComponent.boundary_rule
api.statement: Outside the deep range retain the original EG extension-class condition: in the cyclotomic-ratio boundary the p-1 weight difference is tied to the exact cyclotomic character equality and a tres-ramifiee extension, while the other boundary uses difference zero.

api.name: SerreLabelledGaloisComponent.local_model_quotient
api.statement: Under Theorem7.4.2 and a compatible algebraic central lift zeta, identify C_sigma with the quotient of the lifted local-model component C_sigma^zeta by the shifted Tdual^J conjugation action. Do not confuse this with the ordinary left torus torsor used for affine flags.

tests.name: SerreLabelledGaloisComponent.rank_one_relabel
tests.statement: For n=1, det^(n-1)=1, so C_sigma uses the dual-character EG label; the relabelling is not the identity on all characters.

tests.name: SerreLabelledGaloisComponent.GL2_inertia_shift
tests.statement: For one embedding and kappa=(a,b), the deep-locus diagonal inertia exponents are (a+1,b), since eta=(1,0).

tests.name: SerreLabelledGaloisComponent.split_not_dense_locus
tests.statement: A direct sum of two distinct characters has at least two stable complete flags. It fails the maximally nonsplit dense-locus condition, although it may lie in the closure; the dense locus and the component are different sets.

items.name: Special-fiber factorization through the naive local model
items.statement: Under the standing (h+2)-generic setup and the additional (2h-2)-depth bound, the framed X^{<=lambda,tau}_F closed immersion in M_J(<=lambda)_F factors through M_J^naive(<=lambda,nabla a_tau)_F.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Reduced generic crystalline stacks are unions of Serre-labelled components
items.locator: Theorem 7.4.2(1), PDF157; proof PDF161; stated in the introduction as Theorem 1.4.5 (PDF 13)
items.statement: Theorem 7.4.2(1). Setting of §7.4: K/Q_p is finite unramified and zeta in X^*(Z) is an algebraic central character. Let lambda in X_*(T)^J be regular dominant with lambda_j in [0,h]^n for all j in J, and let tau be a tame inertial type with lowest alcove presentation (s,mu), so tau = tau(s, mu+eta), that is (lambda-eta)-compatible with zeta. Assume that mu is max{2(h+1), 4n+h}-deep. Then X^{<=lambda,tau}_{reg,red} = X^{lambda,tau}_red = ∪_sigma C_sigma, where the union runs over all Serre weights sigma in JH(W(lambda-eta) ⊗ sigmabar(tau)). Here X^{<=lambda,tau}_reg is the scheme-theoretic union of the X^{lambda',tau} over regular dominant lambda' <= lambda (§7.3), 'red' denotes the underlying reduced algebraic stack, and C_sigma = X_{EG,n,red}^{sigma^vee ⊗ det^{n-1}} ⊂ X_{n,red}. Proof: from Corollary 7.4.5, since X^{<=lambda,tau}_{reg,red} and X^{lambda,tau}_red are equidimensional of dimension d_J = #J·dim(B\GL_n).
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Top-dimensional components of generic crystalline special fibres
items.statement: Corollary 7.4.5. Setting of §7.4: K/Q_p finite unramified, zeta in X^*(Z), lambda in X_*(T)^J regular dominant with lambda_j in [0,h]^n, and tau = tau(s, mu+eta) with lowest alcove presentation (s,mu). Assume that mu is max{2(h+1), 4n+h}-deep in C_0. Then the d_J-dimensional irreducible components of X^{lambda,tau}_red and X^{<=lambda,tau}_red are exactly the C_sigma with sigma in JH(W(lambda-eta) ⊗ sigmabar(tau)), where d_J = #J·dim_F(B\GL_n)_F. Proof: by Lemma 7.4.4, X^{lambda,tau} has at least #JH(W(lambda-eta) ⊗ sigmabar(tau)) irreducible components of dimension d_J. Proposition 7.4.1 and Theorem 4.6.2 show that X^{<=lambda,tau} has at most that many; here mu being 2(h+1)-deep implies that tau is 2n-generic. Equality must therefore hold at each stage.
items.note: Split from G34. A separately numbered corollary. Its two conclusions (for X^{lambda,tau}_red and X^{<=lambda,tau}_red) come from one counting argument and are kept together.

uses.how: Combined with equidimensionality of X^{<=lambda,tau}_{reg,red} and X^{lambda,tau}_red in dimension d_J.
C_sigma occurs as an irreducible component of X^{<=lambda,tau}_red.

items.name: Full crystalline union is the union of components (conditional on naive-model equidimensionality)
items.statement: Remark 7.4.3(4). Under the hypotheses of Theorem 7.4.2, and using the fact that M^nv_J(<=lambda, nabla_{a_tau})_F is equidimensional (cf. Remark 4.6.3), the first part of the theorem strengthens to X^{<=lambda,tau}_red = ∪_sigma C_sigma, sigma in JH(W(lambda-eta) ⊗ sigmabar(tau)). In particular, X^{<=lambda,tau}_F is equidimensional. The reason given is that Lemma 7.4.4 shows that Xtilde^{<=lambda,tau}_red exhausts all the top-dimensional irreducible components of M^nv_J(<=lambda, nabla_{a_tau})_F, and so has the same underlying reduced scheme. The equidimensionality input is asserted, not proved, in Remark 4.6.3(1); see sourceIssues.
items.note: Split from G34. A separate claim with its own justification; in the source it depends on an unproved input.

uses.how: Strengthens the equality from the regular union X^{<=lambda,tau}_{reg,red} to X^{<=lambda,tau}_red. Remark 7.4.3(4) is not cited later in the paper.

items.name: Product version of the component theorem
items.statement: Remark 7.4.3(5). By taking products over a finite set S_p indexing finite unramified extensions F_v^+ of Q_p, one obtains the evident generalization of Theorem 7.4.2 to X^{F_p^+,lambda,tau}_F. Here F_p^+ = ∏_{v in S_p} F_v^+, X^{F_p^+}_n = ∏_{v in S_p, Spf O} X^{F_v^+}_n, and the irreducible components of X^{F_p^+}_{n,red} = ∏_{v in S_p, F} X^{F_v^+}_{n,red} are indexed by Serre weights sigma of G (§7.4, PDF155). Reading of 'evident generalization': for data (lambda_v, tau_v)_v, each satisfying the hypotheses of Theorem 7.4.2 over F_v^+, parts (1) and (2) hold for the products, with C_sigma = ∏_v C_{sigma_v} and sigma = ⊗_v sigma_v running over ∏_v JH(W(lambda_v-eta) ⊗ sigmabar(tau_v)).
items.note: Split from G34. The source asserts the product version without proof ('evident generalization').

uses.how: 'Theorem 7.4.2(1) implies (after taking products as in Remark 7.4.3(5)) that the irreducible components of Spec R^tau_rhobar are ...' for the product of local deformation rings.

items.name: Local model diagram for each Serre-labelled component
items.locator: Theorem 7.4.2(2) and diagram (7.17), PDF158; proof PDF161
items.statement: Theorem 7.4.2(2), under the hypotheses of Theorem 7.4.2 (G34). For each sigma in JH(W(lambda-eta) ⊗ sigmabar(tau)) there is a local model diagram (7.17). Its top row is Ctilde_sigma ↪ Xtilde^{<=lambda,tau}_F ↪ Mtilde^nv_J(<=lambda, nabla_{a_tau})_F ↪ Mtilde_J(<=lambda)_F ↪ Fltilde^{[0,h]}_{J,wtilde*(tau)}, the last arrow being r_{wtilde*(tau)}. An isomorphism Ctilde_sigma ≅ Ctilde^zeta_sigma is compatible with the closed immersion Ctilde^zeta_sigma ↪ Fltilde^{[0,h]}_{J,wtilde*(tau)}. The bottom row is C_sigma ↪ X^{<=lambda,tau}_F ↪ Y^{<=lambda,tau}_F ↪ [Fltilde^{[0,h]}_{J,wtilde*(tau)} / T^{vee,J}_F-conj] ↪ Phi-Mod^{et,n}_{K,F}. The vertical maps are Ctilde_sigma -> C_sigma, Xtilde^{<=lambda,tau}_F -> X^{<=lambda,tau}_F, pi_{(s,mu)}: Mtilde_J(<=lambda)_F -> Y^{<=lambda,tau}_F, and Fltilde -> [Fltilde/T^{vee,J}_F-conj]. The diagram satisfies three conditions. First, Ctilde_sigma is defined so that all rectangles are Cartesian and all vertical arrows are T^{vee,J}_F-torsors. Second, all hooked arrows are closed immersions. Third, the bottom diagonal map is the canonical composition C_sigma ↪ X_n -> Phi-Mod^{et,n}_{K,F}. Here wtilde*(tau) = s^{-1} t_{mu+eta}, Xtilde^{<=lambda,tau}_F is the pullback of X^{<=lambda,tau}_F along pi_{(s,mu)}, and Ctilde^zeta_sigma is the pullback to Fltilde of C^zeta_sigma (Definition 4.6.1). Proof: C_sigma is a component of X^{<=lambda,tau}_red, so Ctilde_sigma is a top-dimensional component of Mtilde^nv. By Theorem 4.6.2 it therefore equals Ctilde^zeta_{sigma'} wtilde*(tau)^{-1} for some sigma' in JH(W(lambda-eta) ⊗ sigmabar(tau)). Choose a point of Ctilde_sigma of the form (7.15) that lies over U^zeta_{sigma'} (Lemma 7.4.6). By Lemma 7.2.10(2) and (4), its G_{K_infty}-flag is G_K-stable, which gives kappa - kappa' in (p - pi)X^0(T) and hence sigma' = sigma.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Serre-labelled components as quotients of deformed affine Springer components
items.statement: Remark 7.4.3(1). Under Theorem 7.4.2, C_sigma = [Ctilde^zeta_sigma / T^{vee,J}_F-conj] as subfunctors of Phi-Mod^{et,n}_{K,F}, and this depends only on zeta, not on the choice of lambda, s and mu. On the other hand, making the choices lambda, s, mu computes C_sigma as a quotient [T^{vee,J}_F C^zeta_sigma wtilde*(tau)^{-1} /_{(s,mu)} T^{vee,J}]. Here T^{vee,J}_F C^zeta_sigma wtilde*(tau)^{-1} is an irreducible component of a deformed affine Springer fiber in the sense of [32] (Frenkel-Zhu), i.e. of the reduced subvariety of Fltilde^J cut out by the displayed condition, printed (v d/dv g) g^{-1} + Ad(g)(v^{s^{-1}(mu+eta)}) ∈ Lie I (see sourceIssues for the correction). In particular, C_sigma is equisingular to an irreducible component of a deformed affine Springer fiber.
items.note: Split from G35. This consequence of Theorem 7.4.2(2) adds independence of choices and the deformed-affine-Springer description.

uses.where: Introduction, Remark 1.4.6(2) (PDF14) and the strategy in §1.6 (PDF23)
uses.how: Relates C_sigma to deformed affine Springer fibres, so that Boixeda Alvarez's torus-fixed-point count transfers to Theorem 1.6.1.
Identifies C_sigma with the quotient of the lifted local-model component by the shifted T^vee conjugation action.

items.name: The component local-model isomorphism under 2(h+1)-genericity
items.statement: Remark 7.4.3(2). As the proof of Theorem 7.4.2(2) shows, the isomorphism between Ctilde_sigma and Ctilde^zeta_sigma (diagram (7.17)) holds as long as there exists (lambda, tau) such that C_sigma ⊂ X^{<=lambda,tau} and tau is 2(h+1)-generic. In particular, it holds for any irreducible component of the special fiber of X^{eta,tau} where tau is 2n-generic. As long as sigma is (3n-1)-deep this can always be arranged; see the proof of Proposition 7.4.7, where for sigma = F(kappa) the type tau(1,kappa) is 2n-generic and C_sigma ⊂ X^{eta,tau(1,kappa)} by Lemma 6.2.8 and Proposition 2.4.5.
items.note: Split from G35. A weaker-hypothesis form of Theorem 7.4.2(2), justified by rereading its proof.

uses.where: G37, G60, G61 (Proposition 7.4.7 proof, PDF162; printed as 'Remark 7.4.3(3)')
uses.how: Gives the diagram (7.17) with Ctilde_sigma ≅ Ctilde^zeta_sigma for tau = tau(1,kappa).
With Proposition 4.7.5 (unibranch), i*_rhobar(C_sigma) is an irreducible cycle for QP_{4n}-generic rhobar and (3n-1)-deep sigma.
Cited to conclude sigma in JH(sigmabar(tau)) when C_sigma(rhobar) lies in Spec R^{eta,tau}_rhobar/varpi; that content is also the upper bound of Remark 7.4.3(3) (G59).

items.name: Upper bound on components under 2(h+1)-depth
items.statement: Remark 7.4.3(3). In the setting of Theorem 7.4.2, but under the weaker hypothesis that mu is 2(h+1)-deep, one can still show the upper bound on the components X^{lambda,tau}_red ⊂ X^{<=lambda,tau}_{reg,red} ⊂ ∪_sigma C_sigma, sigma in JH(W(lambda-eta) ⊗ sigmabar(tau)). In the proof, the bound 4n+h only appears when invoking weight elimination and modularity of obvious weights from [56].
items.note: Split from G35. The source gives only a one-line justification: in the proof of Theorem 7.4.2, the depth 4n+h is needed only for the lower bound (Lemma 7.4.4).

uses.how: C_{sigma'} ⊂ X^{eta,tau}_F with tau 2n-generic implies sigma' in JH(sigmabar(tau)).
Same deduction: sigma' in JH(sigmabar(tau)).
A component C_sigma of X^{lambda+eta,tau} has sigma in JH(sigmabar(lambda,tau)).

items.name: Dense triangular locus in Springer components
items.statement: For an (n-1)-deep weight with compatible lowest-alcove presentation, the component C_sigma^zeta has an explicitly chosen dense affine open whose associated étale phi modules carry a full flag with diagonal inertia characters determined by kappa+eta. Cyclotomic-free full faithfulness then identifies this flag with the GK flag and fixes the component label.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: An obvious weight puts a generic tame representation on its component
items.statement: Proposition 7.4.7(1). Let sigma be a (3n-1)-deep Serre weight with lowest alcove presentation (wtilde_1, omega), and let rhobar be a tame n-dimensional representation of G_K that is 2n-generic. If sigma in W_obv(rhobar), then rhobar in C_sigma. Proof, whose first steps are shared with parts (2) and (3): let sigma = F(kappa) and tau = tau(1,kappa). Lemma 6.2.8 gives C_sigma ⊂ X^{eta,tau}, and Proposition 2.4.5 makes tau 2n-generic because kappa is (3n-1)-deep. Remark 7.4.3(2), printed as (3), then gives a diagram (7.17) with Ctilde_sigma ≅ Ctilde^zeta_sigma. By Propositions 5.5.2 and 5.5.7, rhobar in C_sigma if and only if rhobar has a lowest alcove presentation with wtilde*(rhobar) in C^zeta_sigma. Part (1) follows from Theorem 4.7.6(1).
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: A predicted weight with polynomial genericity puts rhobar on its component
items.statement: Proposition 7.4.7(2). Let sigma be a (3n-1)-deep Serre weight with lowest alcove presentation (wtilde_1, omega), and let rhobar be a tame n-dimensional representation of G_K that is 2n-generic. For each j in J, let P_{wtilde_{1,j}} in Z[X_1,...,X_n] be as in Proposition 4.7.3. If sigma in W^?(rhobar) and P_{wtilde_{1,j}}(omega_j) ≢ 0 mod p for all j in J, then rhobar in C_sigma. Proof: the reduction in G37, followed by Theorem 4.7.6(3). The proof text says 'corresponding item'; see sourceIssues.
items.note: Split from G37. Part (2) rests on Theorem 4.7.6(3) (M37). The converse without the polynomial condition is part (3) (G61), and Remark 7.4.8 expects the proposition to hold for 2n-deep weights.

uses.how: For Q-generic mu, the compatible presentation of each sigma in W^?(rhobar|I_{Q_p}) satisfies the polynomial hypothesis, so rhobar in C_sigma. This gives W^? ⊂ W^g_gen.

items.name: Membership in a component forces a predicted weight
items.statement: Proposition 7.4.7(3). Let sigma be a (3n-1)-deep Serre weight with lowest alcove presentation (wtilde_1, omega), and let rhobar be a tame n-dimensional representation of G_K that is 2n-generic. If rhobar in C_sigma, then sigma in W^?(rhobar). Proof: the reduction in G37, followed by Theorem 4.7.6(2).
items.note: Split from G37. Part (3) rests on Theorem 4.7.6(2) (M36).

uses.how: W^g_gen(rhobar) ⊂ W^?(rhobar|I_{Q_p}) for 4n-generic rhobar.

items.name: Global top-dimensional stack cycles
items.statement: Define Z[X_n,red] as the free abelian group on Serre-labelled irreducible components C_sigma, with coefficientwise effectivity and order. Define the finite-group representation Grothendieck group and lattice-independent reduction of characteristic-zero representations.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Z_{λ,τ} is a cycle in Z[X_{n,red}].
The geometric Breuil–Mézard conjecture is an identity in Z[X_{n,red}].
Lemma 8.2.2 compares cycles with their versal pullbacks.
The generic cycles Z_σ form a basis of the span of the generic C_σ (Proposition 8.6.2).

api.name: StackCycle.group
api.statement: Z[X_{n,red}] is the free abelian group on the irreducible components C_σ of X_{n,red}, indexed by Serre weights; its elements are cycles, and C_σ is an irreducible cycle.

api.name: StackCycle.le
api.statement: Z₁ ≥ Z₂ iff Z₁ − Z₂ is effective (all coefficients ≥ 0); this is a partial order compatible with addition.

api.name: RepGroth.group
api.statement: K(Rep_F(G)) is the free abelian group on Serre weights, with [W] = Σ_σ [W:σ][σ].

api.name: RepGroth.lattice_indep
api.statement: For a finitely generated E[G]-module V, [V̄°] is independent of the G-stable O-lattice V° (Brauer–Nesbitt); it is written [V̄].

api.name: StackCycle.support
api.statement: The support of a cycle is the set of C_σ with nonzero coefficient.

tests.name: StackCycle.zero
tests.statement: The zero cycle is effective, and 0 ≤ Z for every effective Z.

tests.name: StackCycle.GL1
tests.statement: For n = 1 and residue field of size p^f, the components of X_{1,red} are indexed by the p^f − 1 characters of k^×, so Z[X_{1,red}] ≅ Z^{p^f−1}.

tests.name: StackCycle.partial
tests.statement: ≥ is not total: for σ ≠ σ′, C_σ and C_{σ′} are incomparable.

tests.name: RepGroth.two_lattices
tests.statement: Two lattices in a GL₂(F_p) principal series may have non-isomorphic reductions, but with the same Jordan–Hölder multiset, hence the same class.

items.name: Extremal types and crystalline/semistable cycles
items.statement: A type is (lambda+eta,tau) with lambda dominant and tau a Weil–Deligne inertial type; it is extremal if tau is minimal or maximal for the monodromy order. Its cycle Z_{lambda,tau} records generic-point lengths of X_F^{lambda+eta,tau}. For a set S of types define JH(sigma(S)) as the union of type constituents.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Conjecture 8.1.1 expresses each Z_{λ,τ} in the Z_σ.
Z(M∞(σ̄°(λ,τ))) = Z_{λ,τ}(ρ) for minimal patching functors ([23, Lemma 2.2.10], PDF169).
Theorem 8.4.10(2) proves the geometric equations for generic types.
Corollary 8.4.12 proves them for P_{P,Λ,e}-generic tame types.

api.name: BMType.mk
api.statement: A type is (λ+η, τ) with λ ∈ X*(T^∨) dominant and τ a Weil–Deligne inertial type for K.

api.name: BMType.IsExtremal
api.statement: (λ+η, τ) is extremal iff τ is minimal or maximal for ⪯; X^{λ+η,τ} is then the potentially crystalline, respectively potentially semistable, stack.

api.name: BMType.cycle
api.statement: Z_{λ,τ} := Σ_σ μ_σ(X^{λ+η,τ}_F)·C_σ, with μ_σ the multiplicity of C_σ as an irreducible component of the special fibre ([75, Tag 0DR4]).

api.name: BMType.JH
api.statement: For a set S of extremal types, JH(σ̄(S)) := ⋃_{(λ+η,τ)∈S} JH(σ̄(λ,τ)).

api.name: BMType.cycle_effective
api.statement: Z_{λ,τ} is effective and supported on the components of X^{λ+η,τ}_F.

tests.name: BMType.empty
tests.statement: If X^{λ+η,τ} is empty, Z_{λ,τ} = 0.

tests.name: BMType.not_extremal
tests.statement: For GL₃ with trivial inertia and monodromy of Jordan type (2,1), τ is neither minimal nor maximal, so the type is not extremal.

tests.name: BMType.crystalline
tests.statement: If N_τ = 0, τ is minimal and X^{λ+η,τ} is the potentially crystalline stack of type (λ+η, τ).

tests.name: BMType.semistable
tests.statement: If τ is maximal for ⪯, X^{λ+η,⪯τ} is the potentially semistable stack of the corresponding type.

items.name: Geometric Breuil–Mézard conjectural interface
items.locator: Conjecture8.1.1 PDF163; stated in the introduction as Conjecture 1.5.7 (PDF 18), after [22, Conjecture 8.2.2]
items.statement: For a specified set S of extremal types, conjecture effective cycles Z_sigma with Z_{lambda,tau}=sum_sigma [sigma(lambda,tau):sigma]Z_sigma. This is a conjecture in general, not a theorem of the paper; subsequent results prove restricted generic instances. The extra inequality Z_sigma>=C_sigma is likewise conjectural in Remark8.1.2 outside the proved range.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Conjecture 8.1.1 implies the versal conjecture (Proposition 8.2.1).
Theorem 8.3.5(4) compares the patched cycles with any cycles satisfying the conjecture.
Corollary 8.4.12 proves a generic case.

api.name: GeometricBM.statement
api.statement: Conjectural interface, not a theorem: for a set S of extremal types there are effective Z_σ ∈ Z[X_{n,red}], σ ∈ JH(σ̄(S)), with Z_{λ,τ} = Σ_σ[σ̄(λ,τ):σ]Z_σ for all types in S.

api.name: GeometricBM.unique
api.statement: If S is a Breuil–Mézard system, such cycles are unique if they exist (Remark 8.1.3(2)).

api.name: GeometricBM.provedGeneric
api.statement: Corollary 8.4.12 proves the statement for λ ∈ Λ and tame τ with P_{P,Λ,e}-generic presentation.

api.name: GeometricBM.expected_lower
api.statement: Conjectural: Z_σ ≥ C_σ (Remark 8.1.2). For generic σ the coefficient of C_σ in Z_σ is 1 (Proposition 8.6.1).

api.name: GeometricBM.nonreduced
api.statement: If [σ̄(λ,τ):σ] > 1 and Z_σ ≠ 0, the conjecture forces X^{λ+η,τ}_F to be non-reduced (Remark 8.1.4).

tests.name: GeometricBM.single_irreducible
tests.statement: If S = {(λ+η,τ)} and σ̄(λ,τ) has the single constituent σ with multiplicity one, the conjecture forces Z_σ = Z_{λ,τ}.

tests.name: GeometricBM.not_theorem
tests.statement: The conjecture is not asserted for arbitrary S; only restricted generic instances are proved.

tests.name: GeometricBM.empty
tests.statement: For S = ∅ the conjecture is vacuous.

items.name: Breuil–Mézard system
items.statement: A set S of extremal types is a Breuil–Mézard system if the map from Z[S] to the representation Grothendieck group has finite cokernel. Such a spanning condition gives uniqueness of cycles if they exist; an arbitrary set S does not give uniqueness.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Uniqueness of Breuil–Mézard cycles for a Breuil–Mézard system (Remark 8.1.3(2)).
The relative notion of Definition 8.3.3 weakens this spanning condition.
Theorem 8.3.5(4) assumes a Breuil–Mézard system S̃_elim.

api.name: BMSystem.def
api.statement: S is a Breuil–Mézard system iff Z[S] → K(Rep_F(G)), (λ+η,τ) ↦ [σ̄(λ,τ)], has finite cokernel ([33, §3.3]).

api.name: BMSystem.rational
api.statement: Equivalently, the classes [σ̄(λ,τ)] for types in S span K(Rep_F(G)) ⊗ Q.

api.name: BMSystem.mono
api.statement: If S ⊆ S′ and S is a Breuil–Mézard system, so is S′.

api.name: BMSystem.unique
api.statement: For a Breuil–Mézard system, cycles satisfying Conjecture 8.1.1 are unique if they exist.

tests.name: BMSystem.empty
tests.statement: S = ∅ is never a Breuil–Mézard system, since K(Rep_F(G)) ≠ 0.

tests.name: BMSystem.GL1
tests.statement: For n = 1 each tame type reduces to a single character of k^×, so the set of all tame types is a Breuil–Mézard system with zero cokernel.

tests.name: BMSystem.single_type
tests.statement: A single type is not a Breuil–Mézard system once G has more than one Serre weight.

items.name: Versal cycle pullback
items.statement: Given a versal ring R^ver_rho of X_n, form the crystalline quotient and the effective algebraic versal ring R^alg_rho of X_n,red. The effective map i_rho:Spec R^alg_rho->X_n,red induces pullback of component cycles; formal fibers preserve their multiplicities. Record the dependence on the chosen versal ring.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: The versal conjecture is stated on Spec R_ρ^alg.
Lemma 8.2.2 uses the pullbacks i_x^*.
Theorem 8.3.5(1) uses R∞ = R_ρ ⊗̂ R^p as a versal ring.
Primes p_σ(ρ̄) come from pulled-back components.

api.name: Versal.algRing
api.statement: Spf R_ρ^alg := Spf R_ρ^ver ×_{X_n} X_{n,red}; the versal map is effective, giving i_ρ : Spec R_ρ^alg → X_{n,red} ([24, Definition 2.2.9]).

api.name: Versal.typeRing
api.statement: Spf R_ρ^{ver,λ+η,τ} := Spf R_ρ^ver ×_{X_n} X^{λ+η,τ} is a versal ring of X^{λ+η,τ} at ρ.

api.name: Versal.pullback
api.statement: i_ρ^* : Z[X_{n,red}] → Z[Spec R_ρ^alg]; the components of Spec R_ρ^alg map onto the components of X_{n,red} containing ρ ([75, Tag 0DRB]).

api.name: Versal.pullback_mult
api.statement: Multiplicities are preserved: i_ρ^*(Z_{λ,τ}) = Z(Spec R_{ρ,F}^{ver,λ+η,τ}) ([75, Tag 0DRD]).

api.name: Versal.change
api.statement: Two versal rings have a common formally smooth cover, which identifies components and multiplicities (Remark 8.1.6(1)).

tests.name: Versal.not_on_component
tests.statement: If ρ ∉ C_σ, then i_ρ^*(C_σ) = 0.

tests.name: Versal.detects
tests.statement: i_ρ^*(C_σ) ≠ 0 iff ρ ∈ C_σ.

tests.name: Versal.not_injective
tests.statement: i_ρ^* is not injective on Z[X_{n,red}]: it kills every component not containing ρ.

items.name: Versal Breuil–Mézard conjecture (interface)
items.locator: Conjecture 8.1.5, PDF165; setting PDF164–165; stated in the introduction as Conjecture 1.5.1 (PDF 15)
items.statement: Conjecture 8.1.5 (Versal Breuil–Mézard conjecture). Let S be a set of extremal types. For each σ ∈ JH(σ̄(S)), there exist effective cycles Z_σ(ρ̄) in Spec R^alg_ρ̄ such that for all (λ+η, τ) ∈ S, Z_{λ,τ}(ρ̄) = Σ_σ [σ̄(λ,τ) : σ] Z_σ(ρ̄). Setting (§8.1, PDF164–165): ρ̄ : G_K → GL_n(F) is a continuous Galois representation, also viewed as an F-point of X_n. R^ver_ρ̄ is a fixed versal ring for X_n at ρ̄ (for example R^□_ρ̄), and Spf R^alg_ρ̄ = Spf R^ver_ρ̄ ×_{X_n} X_{n,red}. The effective versal map i_ρ̄ : Spec R^alg_ρ̄ → X_{n,red} induces i^*_ρ̄ : Z[X_{n,red}] → Z[Spec R^alg_ρ̄]. Z_{λ,τ} = Σ_σ μ_σ(X^{λ+η,τ}_F) C_σ, and Z_{λ,τ}(ρ̄) = i^*_ρ̄(Z_{λ,τ}) is the cycle of Spec R^{ver,λ+η,τ}_{ρ̄,F} ([75, Tag 0DRD]). The notation suppresses the dependence on R^ver_ρ̄. The paper does not prove this in general.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: The geometric conjecture implies it (Proposition 8.2.1).
Minimal patching functors prove it with Z_σ(ρ) = Z(M∞(σ)) (Theorem 8.3.5(1)).
Corollary 8.5.2 is a versal statement for generic ρ̄.

api.name: VersalBM.statement
api.statement: Conjectural interface: effective Z_σ(ρ) ∈ Z[Spec R_ρ^alg] with Z_{λ,τ}(ρ) = Σ_σ[σ̄(λ,τ):σ]Z_σ(ρ) for every type in S.

api.name: VersalBM.indep
api.statement: The statement for one versal ring implies it for any other (Remark 8.1.6(1)).

api.name: VersalBM.of_patching
api.statement: A minimal patching functor for ρ and S gives Z_σ(ρ) := Z(M∞(σ)) satisfying it (Theorem 8.3.5(1)).

api.name: VersalBM.recover
api.statement: For S the minimal types and R_ρ^ver = R_ρ, it recovers [23, Conjecture 4.2.1] with effectivity (Remark 8.1.6(2)).

tests.name: VersalBM.from_geometric
tests.statement: Conjecture 8.1.1 for S implies Conjecture 8.1.5 for S at every ρ (Proposition 8.2.1).

tests.name: VersalBM.not_theorem
tests.statement: It is not proved in general; the paper proves it for generic data.

tests.name: VersalBM.far
tests.statement: If ρ lies on no component of any type in S, both sides are 0 and the cycles can be taken to be 0.

items.name: The versal Breuil–Mézard conjecture does not depend on the versal ring
items.statement: Remark 8.1.6(1). As stated, Conjecture 8.1.5 depends on the choice of a versal ring R^ver_ρ̄. However, choose a common formally smooth covering of any two versal rings. A formally smooth covering of an equidimensional scheme induces a bijection between sets of irreducible components and preserves multiplicities of components. Hence Conjecture 8.1.5 for one choice of versal ring implies the same result for any other choice.
items.note: Split from B06 (api VersalBM.indep). Only the quoted sketch is printed. To complete it: completing the fibre product of two versal maps Spf R_1 → X_n and Spf R_2 → X_n at the point over ρ̄ gives a complete local ring that is formally smooth over both, hence a power series ring over each. Minimal primes and their multiplicities correspond under A → A[[x_1,…,x_r]]. Both sides of the equations are pullbacks of the same cycles on X_{n,red}, so effective cycles Z_σ(ρ̄) on R^alg_1 transport to R^alg_2 with the equations intact.

uses.how: Theorem 8.3.5(1) (B15) proves Conjecture 8.1.5 for the versal ring R_∞ = R^□_ρ̄ ⊗̂ R^p of the patching functor (PDF169). This remark moves the statement to any other versal ring, e.g. R^□_ρ̄. Corollary 8.5.2 does not need it, since it goes through global cycles.

items.name: Framed minimal-type case recovers the Emerton–Gee cycle conjecture
items.statement: Remark 8.1.6(2). Taking S to contain all minimal types (τ is minimal) and R^ver_ρ̄ to be the framed deformation ring R^□_ρ̄, Conjecture 8.1.5 recovers [23, Conjecture 4.2.1] with the added assertion that Z_σ(ρ̄) is effective.
items.note: Split from B06 (api VersalBM.recover). No proof is printed; the remark compares two conjecture statements. [23] is Emerton–Gee, A geometric perspective on the Breuil–Mézard conjecture, J. Inst. Math. Jussieu 13 (2014). The introduction's Conjecture 1.5.1 (PDF15) is the related [23]-style statement over R^□_ρ̄/ϖ, for all types, with virtual r(τ) and no effectivity. The paper does not cite the remark again; it is a candidate to fold into B06.

uses.how: It places Conjecture 8.1.5 (B06) relative to the literature, and the introduction's Conjecture 1.5.1 is written in this framed form.

items.name: Cycle of a finite module
items.statement: For a finite module on a type's special-fiber versal ring, its top-dimensional cycle sums each irreducible component with coefficient equal to the length of the module localized at its generic prime.
items.note: Route owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Z_σ(ρ) = Z(M∞(σ)) is a module cycle.
The recursion manipulates Z(M∞(σ)) and Z(M∞(σ̄(τ))).

api.name: ModuleCycle.def
api.statement: For finite M over R_{ρ,F}^{ver,λ+η,τ}, Z(M) := Σ_C length(M_{p_C})·C over the irreducible components C, with p_C the generic prime of C.

api.name: ModuleCycle.additive
api.statement: Z is additive in short exact sequences ([23, Lemma 2.2.7]).

api.name: ModuleCycle.effective
api.statement: Z(M) is effective, and zero iff Supp M has smaller than top dimension.

api.name: ModuleCycle.ring
api.statement: Z(R_{ρ,F}^{ver,λ+η,τ}) = Z_{λ,τ}(ρ).

tests.name: ModuleCycle.two_lines
tests.statement: For R = F[[x,y]]/(xy) and M = R/(x), Z(M) = C_{x=0}: M has length 1 at (x) and is 0 at (y).

tests.name: ModuleCycle.closed_point
tests.statement: A module supported at the closed point has Z(M) = 0, though M ≠ 0.

items.name: Geometric equations imply versal equations
items.statement: Geometric Breuil–Mézard for S implies the versal form at every residual point, by pullback preserving multiplicities.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Component-meeting testing set
items.statement: For P contained in residual stack points, define i_P^* as the product of versal pullbacks. P meets all components of S if every component supporting some type in S contains a point of P.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Lemma 8.2.2: injectivity and effectivity detection.
Proposition 8.2.3: uniqueness of descended cycles.
P_ss meets all components of S_{Λ,t} (Lemma 8.4.9).

api.name: TestSet.pullback
api.statement: i_P^* := ∏_{x∈P} i_x^* : Z[X_{n,red}] → ∏_{x∈P} Z[Spec R_x^alg].

api.name: TestSet.MeetsAll
api.statement: P meets all components of S iff every C ∈ C(S), the components in the support of some X^{λ+η,τ} with type in S, contains a point of P.

api.name: TestSet.injective
api.statement: If P meets all components of S, i_P^* is injective on Z[C(S)], and Z ∈ Z[C(S)] is effective iff every i_x^*(Z) is (Lemma 8.2.2).

api.name: TestSet.mono
api.statement: If P ⊆ P′ and P meets all components of S, so does P′.

tests.name: TestSet.Pss
tests.statement: P_ss meets all components of S_{Λ,t} (Lemma 8.4.9).

tests.name: TestSet.missing_component
tests.statement: If some C ∈ C(S) contains no point of P, then i_P^*(C) = 0, so i_P^* is not injective on Z[C(S)].

tests.name: TestSet.empty_S
tests.statement: Every P, including ∅, meets all components of S = ∅.

items.name: Cycle detection by versal pullbacks
items.statement: If P meets all components of S, i_P^* is injective on their integral span and detects effectivity. This does not by itself construct global cycles from arbitrary locally chosen cycles.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Uniqueness, effectivity and the geometric equations for descended cycles
items.statement: Proposition 8.2.3. Let S be a set of extremal types and P ⊂ X_n(F) a subset. Assume (1) P meets all components of S; and (2) Conjecture 8.1.5 holds for S and all x ∈ P, with cycles Z_σ(x) for each σ ∈ JH(σ̄(S)) and x ∈ P. Then for each σ ∈ JH(σ̄(S)) there is at most one cycle Z_σ in Z[X_{n,red}] such that the support of Z_σ is contained in the support of Z_{λ,τ} for some (λ+η,τ) ∈ S and, for each x ∈ P, i^*_x(Z_σ) = Z_σ(x). If all such cycles exist, then they satisfy the conclusion of Conjecture 8.1.1. Here P meets all components of S if every irreducible component of X_{n,red} in the support of some X^{λ+η,τ}, (λ+η,τ) ∈ S, meets P. Proof (PDF166): uniqueness is Lemma 8.2.2 (B10). For effectivity, suppose an irreducible C has a negative coefficient in Z_σ. Some x ∈ P lies on C, and then i^*_x(Z_σ) is not effective ([75, Tag 0DRD]), which contradicts the effectivity of Z_σ(x). The equality Z_{λ,τ} = Σ_σ [σ̄(λ,τ):σ] Z_σ follows again from Lemma 8.2.2.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Strong converse of Proposition 8.2.1 via smooth points
items.statement: Remark 8.2.4 (recalling [22, §8.3]). Let S be a set of extremal types. The set P = {x_C}_C, where C ranges over irreducible components of ∪_{(λ+η,τ)∈S} X^{λ+η,τ}_F and x_C ∈ C is a smooth point of X_{n,red}, meets all components of S. Moreover, one can define Z_σ as in [22, §8.3] so that this collection satisfies the hypothesis of Proposition 8.2.3. In fact, i^*_P induces an isomorphism on (top-dimensional) cycles. Hence the following strong form of the converse of Proposition 8.2.1 holds: if Conjecture 8.1.5 holds at all points in P, then Conjecture 8.1.1 holds.
items.note: Split from B11. Imported from [22, §8.3] (Emerton–Gee, Moduli stacks of étale (φ,Γ)-modules); no proof is printed. At a smooth point x_C of X_{n,red}, the ring R^alg_{x_C} is a power series ring over F, hence a domain, and x_C lies on C only. So i^*_{x_C} reads off the coefficient of C, and i^*_P is an isomorphism from Z[C(S)] onto ∏_C Z. Defining Z_σ coefficientwise from the Z_σ(x_C) gives the existence that Proposition 8.2.3 needs. Smooth points exist on each C because X_{n,red} is a reduced algebraic stack of finite type over F. The remark goes on to ask whether the converse holds for every P meeting all components; §8.3–8.4 answer this for semisimple P using patching.

uses.how: "In fact, the converse of this statement is true (see Remark 8.2.4)". This is a forward reference only; no proof uses the remark.

items.name: Irrelevant weights
items.statement: A weight is (rho,S_elim)-irrelevant if it occurs in a type whose ordered semistable deformation ring is zero; it is (P,S_elim)-irrelevant if this holds for each rho in P. Weak patching vanishes on such weights. If versal BM holds, their cycles vanish as well.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: (P, S̃_elim)-Breuil–Mézard systems span modulo irrelevant weights.
Weights outside W?(x|_I) are irrelevant (Lemma 8.4.2).
The proof of Theorem 8.3.5(2) uses M∞(σ) = 0 on irrelevant weights (Remark 8.3.2).

api.name: Irrelevant.def
api.statement: σ is (ρ, S_elim)-irrelevant iff some (λ+η,τ) ∈ S_elim has σ ∈ JH(σ̄(λ,τ)) and R_ρ^{λ+η,⪯τ} = 0; (P, S_elim)-irrelevant iff this holds for every ρ ∈ P.

api.name: Irrelevant.patching_zero
api.statement: For any weak patching functor for ρ, M∞(σ) = 0 on ρ-irrelevant σ (Remark 8.3.2).

api.name: Irrelevant.cycle_zero
api.statement: If the versal conjecture holds for S_elim, then Z_σ(ρ) = 0 for (ρ, S_elim)-irrelevant σ.

api.name: Irrelevant.of_not_predicted
api.statement: For (6n−2)-generic tame ρ|_I, σ ∉ W?(ρ|_I) is (ρ, S̃_{Λ,t,elim})-irrelevant (Lemma 8.4.2).

tests.name: Irrelevant.empty_elim
tests.statement: With S_elim = ∅ no weight is irrelevant.

tests.name: Irrelevant.one_witness
tests.statement: Irrelevance needs only one type in S_elim containing σ with vanishing ring; other types containing σ may have nonzero rings.

tests.name: Irrelevant.empty_P
tests.statement: For P = ∅ every weight is vacuously (P, S_elim)-irrelevant.

items.name: Covering, disjointness and relative genericity for type sets
items.statement: For S, sigma S-covers kappa when every type in S containing sigma has C_kappa in its special-fiber support. Define S-disjointness from S' by excluding every such component from all S' supports. For S contained in S_tilde, relative genericity means S_tilde-disjointness from S_tilde minus S.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: S_P is defined through (S, S̃)-generic weights.
tr_{σ,S} keeps the components σ S̃-covers.
For (3n−1)-deep σ, S̃_{Λ,t}-covering implies covering (Lemma 8.4.5).
Generic weights are (S_{Λ,t}, S̃_{Λ,t})-generic (Lemma 8.4.8).

api.name: TypeSet.Covers
api.statement: σ S-covers σ′ iff for every (λ+η,τ) ∈ S with σ ∈ JH(σ̄(λ,τ)), C_{σ′} lies in X^{λ+η,τ}_F.

api.name: TypeSet.Disjoint
api.statement: σ is S-disjoint from S′ iff no κ S-covered by σ has C_κ in X^{λ+η,τ}_F for any (λ+η,τ) ∈ S′.

api.name: TypeSet.RelGeneric
api.statement: For S ⊆ S̃, σ is (S, S̃)-generic iff σ is S̃-disjoint from S̃ ∖ S.

api.name: TypeSet.covers_anti
api.statement: If S ⊆ S′ and σ S′-covers σ′, then σ S-covers σ′, since there are fewer types to check.

api.name: TypeSet.covers_to_covers
api.statement: For (3n−1)-deep σ, S̃_{Λ,t}-covering implies covering in the sense of Definition 2.3.10 (Lemma 8.4.5).

tests.name: TypeSet.vacuous
tests.statement: If σ lies in no type of S, σ S-covers every σ′.

tests.name: TypeSet.not_reflexive
tests.statement: σ need not S-cover itself: C_σ ≤ Z_{λ,τ} is not known a priori (Remark 8.3.4).

tests.name: TypeSet.relGeneric_self
tests.statement: Every σ is (S, S)-generic, since S ∖ S = ∅.

items.name: Relative Breuil–Mézard system and good subsystem
items.statement: S_tilde is a (P,S_elim)-BM system if every Serre class has a nonzero integer multiple that is an integral combination of its type classes modulo irrelevant weights. Define S_P by requiring all constituents to be relatively generic. This quotient-spanning definition differs from B04.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Theorem 8.3.5(2) assumes S̃ is a P-Breuil–Mézard system containing S.
S̃_{Λ,t} is a (P_ss, S̃_{Λ,t,elim})-Breuil–Mézard system (Lemma 8.4.4).
Theorem 8.4.10 applies Theorem 8.3.5 with these systems.

api.name: RelBMSystem.def
api.statement: S̃ is a (P, S̃_elim)-Breuil–Mézard system iff for every σ there are d_σ ≠ 0 and n^σ_{λ,τ} ∈ Z with d_σ[σ] − Σ_{(λ+η,τ)∈S̃} n^σ_{λ,τ}[σ̄(λ,τ)] supported on (P, S̃_elim)-irrelevant weights.

api.name: RelBMSystem.of_BM
api.statement: A Breuil–Mézard system is a (P, S_elim)-Breuil–Mézard system for every P and S_elim.

api.name: GoodSubsystem.def
api.statement: For S ⊆ S̃ with S̃ a P-Breuil–Mézard system, S_P ⊆ S consists of the types all of whose constituents are (S, S̃)-generic.

api.name: GoodSubsystem.proved
api.statement: Under Theorem 8.3.5(2), Conjecture 8.1.1 holds for S_P.

tests.name: RelBMSystem.from_BM
tests.statement: If S̃ has finite cokernel, take d_σ to be an exponent of the cokernel and no irrelevant part.

tests.name: RelBMSystem.weaker
tests.statement: A P-Breuil–Mézard system need not be a Breuil–Mézard system, since spanning holds only modulo irrelevant weights.

tests.name: GoodSubsystem.empty
tests.statement: If S = ∅, then S_P = ∅.

items.name: Minimal patching gives versal cycles
items.statement: If every x in P has a minimal patching functor for S, then the versal equations hold with Z_sigma(x)=Z(M_infty^x(sigma)). The rank-one generic support condition is used for equality with the ring cycle.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Truncated inversion gives effective geometric cycles
items.statement: In addition to B15, assume P meets every S component and S_tilde containing S is a relative P-BM system. Every relatively generic sigma has a unique effective global cycle with the required support and local pullbacks, giving geometric BM for S_P. Construction first inverts the type matrix rationally and then truncates components; versal detection proves integrality and effectivity.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Patched cycles are independent of the patching functors
items.statement: Let P ⊂ X_n(F) and let S be a set of extremal types (λ+η, τ). Suppose that for each x ∈ P there is a minimal patching functor M^x_∞ for x and S, that P meets all components of S, and that Ŝ is a P-Breuil–Mézard system containing S, and let Z_σ ∈ Z[X_{n,red}], for (S, Ŝ)-generic σ, be the cycles of Theorem 8.3.5(2). Then for each (S, Ŝ)-generic σ, the cycle Z_σ does not depend on the choice of the patching functors M^x_∞ for x ∈ P. In particular, the cycle Z(M^x_∞(σ)) in R^alg_x depends only on the versal ring R^x_∞ of X_n at x (and not on other data in M^x_∞).
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Patched cycles agree with conjectural Breuil–Mézard cycles
items.statement: Let P ⊂ X_n(F) and let S be a set of extremal types. Suppose that for each x ∈ P there is a minimal patching functor M^x_∞ for x and S, that P meets all components of S, and that Ŝ is a P-Breuil–Mézard system containing S, and let Z_σ, for (S, Ŝ)-generic σ, be the cycles of Theorem 8.3.5(2). If furthermore there is a Breuil–Mézard system Ŝ_elim containing Ŝ such that Ŝ is a (P, Ŝ_elim)-Breuil–Mézard system and Conjecture 8.1.1 holds for Ŝ_elim, then the above cycles Z_σ coincide with those in Conjecture 8.1.1: Z_σ = Z^BM_σ for every (S, Ŝ)-generic σ, where (Z^BM_κ)_κ are cycles satisfying Conjecture 8.1.1 for Ŝ_elim.
items.note: Split from B17. The proof on PDF 170–171 sets σ_irr := [σ] − d_σ^{-1}Σ n^σ_{λ,τ}[σ̄(λ,τ)], which is supported at (P, Ŝ_elim)-irrelevant weights, and Z^BM_{σ_irr} := Z^BM_σ − d_σ^{-1}Σ n^σ_{λ,τ}Z_{λ,τ}, a rational combination of the Z^BM_κ for irrelevant κ. It shows tr_{σ,S}(Z^BM_σ) = Z^BM_σ, by the argument of Lemma 8.3.7. It also shows tr_{σ,S}(Z^BM_{σ_irr}) = 0: each irrelevant κ has Z^BM_κ ≤ Z_{λ_x,τ_x} with x outside that support, so the support contains no point of P, while P meets every component of S. The two displays on PDF 170 print these sums over S where Ŝ is needed (see sourceIssues). The 'def' step on PDF 171 already sums over Ŝ. Since Ŝ_elim is a Breuil–Mézard system, cycles satisfying Conjecture 8.1.1 for it are unique if they exist (Remark 8.1.3(2)), so 'those in Conjecture 8.1.1' is unambiguous.

uses.how: Theorem 8.4.10(4) is deduced from Theorem 8.3.5(4) with P = P_ss, S = S_{Λ,t}, Ŝ = Ŝ_{Λ,t} (proof, PDF 174).

items.name: Component truncation idempotents; truncation kills excluded types
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 8.3.5 (definitions of tr_{σ,S} and tr_{σ,S}(x)); Lemma 8.3.6, PDF 169
items.statement: Let P ⊂ X_n(F) and let S ⊂ Ŝ be sets of extremal types with Ŝ a P-Breuil–Mézard system, and let σ be (S, Ŝ)-generic. Let tr_{σ,S} denote the idempotent endomorphism of Z[X_{n,red}] which maps C_{σ′} to itself if σ Ŝ-covers σ′ and to 0 otherwise. For x ∈ P, let tr_{σ,S}(x) be the idempotent endomorphism of Z[Spec R^alg_x] such that i_x^* ∘ tr_{σ,S} = tr_{σ,S}(x) ∘ i_x^*, which exists and is unique by [75, Tag 0DRB, Tag 0DRD]. Lemma 8.3.6: if (λ+η, τ) ∈ Ŝ ∖ S, then tr_{σ,S}(Z_{λ,τ}) = 0.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: The proof of Theorem 8.3.5(2) defines Z_σ with tr_{σ,S}.
The proof of Theorem 8.3.5(4) compares truncated cycles.

api.name: Trunc.def
api.statement: tr_{σ,S} : Z[X_{n,red}] → Z[X_{n,red}] sends C_{σ′} to C_{σ′} if σ S̃-covers σ′, and to 0 otherwise.

api.name: Trunc.idem
api.statement: tr_{σ,S} is an idempotent linear projection preserving effectivity.

api.name: Trunc.versal
api.statement: There is a unique tr_{σ,S}(x) on Z[Spec R_x^alg] with i_x^*∘tr_{σ,S} = tr_{σ,S}(x)∘i_x^* ([75, Tags 0DRB, 0DRD]).

api.name: Trunc.kills_excluded
api.statement: tr_{σ,S}(Z_{λ,τ}) = 0 for (λ+η,τ) ∈ S̃ ∖ S, when σ is (S, S̃)-generic (Lemma 8.3.6).

api.name: Trunc.fixes_patched
api.statement: tr_{σ,S}(x)(Z_σ(x)) = Z_σ(x) (Lemma 8.3.7).

api.name: Trunc.defZ
api.statement: Z_σ := tr_{σ,S}((1/d_σ)·Σ n^σ_{λ,τ} Z_{λ,τ}), a priori with rational coefficients; integrality follows from i_x^*(Z_σ) = Z_σ(x).

tests.name: Trunc.nothing_covered
tests.statement: If σ S̃-covers no weight, tr_{σ,S} = 0.

tests.name: Trunc.idempotent
tests.statement: tr_{σ,S} ∘ tr_{σ,S} = tr_{σ,S}.

tests.name: Trunc.needed
tests.statement: Before truncation, (1/d_σ)Σ n^σ_{λ,τ} Z_{λ,τ} can have non-integral coefficients and components that σ does not cover; truncation removes the latter.

items.name: Truncation fixes the patched cycle
items.statement: Let P ⊂ X_n(F) and let S be a set of extremal types. Suppose that for each x ∈ P there is a minimal patching functor M^x_∞ for x and S, and that Ŝ ⊇ S is a P-Breuil–Mézard system. Let σ be (S, Ŝ)-generic, set Z_σ(x) := Z(M^x_∞(σ)), and let tr_{σ,S}(x) be as in B18. Then tr_{σ,S}(x)(Z_σ(x)) = Z_σ(x).
items.note: Split from B18, and it relies on B18's tr_{σ,S}(x). Proof (PDF 169): suppose C_{σ′}(x) is an irreducible cycle in the support of Z_σ(x) and also in the support of i_x^*(C_{σ′}). Then for any (λ+η, τ) ∈ Ŝ with σ ∈ JH(σ̄(λ,τ)), C_{σ′}(x) ≤ Z_σ(x) ≤ Z_{λ,τ}(x). Hence C_{σ′} ≤ Z_{λ,τ}, i.e. σ Ŝ-covers σ′. The paper attributes the middle inequality to '(by (1))', which covers only types in S; see sourceIssues for types in Ŝ ∖ S.

uses.how: The third equality in the proof of Theorem 8.3.5(2) (PDF 170) inserts tr_{σ,S}(x) by Lemma 8.3.7.
In the proof of Theorem 8.3.5(4) (PDF 171), tr_{σ,S}(Z^BM_σ) = Z^BM_σ 'follows from the proof of Lemma 8.3.7'.

items.name: Generic crystalline type systems
items.statement: For a finite dominant-weight set Lambda containing zero, define S_{Lambda,t} using subordinate dominant weights and tame types with both P_{lambda+eta,e}-genericity and (6n-2+h_{lambda+eta})-depth. Define P_ss, S_tilde by adjoining 2n-generic weight-zero types, and S_tilde_elim by adjoining all extremal tame-inertia weight-zero types. Keep these three type systems distinct.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Lemma 8.4.2 is stated for these systems.
Lemma 8.4.4 is stated for these systems.
Lemma 8.4.9: P_ss meets all components of S_{Λ,t}.
Theorem 8.4.10 is stated for S_{Λ,t} and P_ss.
Lemma 8.4.11 places P_{P,Λ,e}-generic types in S_{P,Λ,t}.

api.name: TypeSystem.S
api.statement: S_{Λ,t} is the set of extremal types (λ+η, τ) with λ dominant, λ ≤ λ′ for some λ′ ∈ Λ, and τ a P_{λ+η,e}-generic and (6n−2+h_{λ+η})-generic tame inertial type.

api.name: TypeSystem.Pss
api.statement: P_ss := {x ∈ X_n(F) : x|_{I_K} is a (6n−2)-generic tame inertial F-type}.

api.name: TypeSystem.Stilde
api.statement: S̃_{Λ,t} := S_{Λ,t} ∪ {(η,τ) : τ 2n-generic tame}, and S̃_{Λ,t,elim} := S_{Λ,t} ∪ {(η,τ) extremal with ρ_τ tame}.

api.name: TypeSystem.chain
api.statement: S_{Λ,t} ⊆ S̃_{Λ,t} ⊆ S̃_{Λ,t,elim}.

api.name: TypeSystem.BM
api.statement: S̃_{Λ,t} is a (P_ss, S̃_{Λ,t,elim})-Breuil–Mézard system (Lemma 8.4.4).

tests.name: TypeSystem.chain_test
tests.statement: S_{Λ,t} ⊆ S̃_{Λ,t} ⊆ S̃_{Λ,t,elim}.

tests.name: TypeSystem.Lambda0
tests.statement: For Λ = {0}, S_{{0},t} consists of the (η,τ) with τ P_{η,e}-generic and (6n−2+h_η)-generic.

tests.name: TypeSystem.distinct
tests.statement: A 2n-generic tame τ that is not (6n−2+h_η)-generic gives (η,τ) ∈ S̃_{{0},t} ∖ S_{{0},t}, so the systems differ.

items.name: Weights outside W? are irrelevant at generic tame points
items.statement: Let Λ ⊂ X_*(T^∨) be a finite set of dominant weights containing 0, and let Ŝ_{Λ,t,elim} be as in §8.4. Suppose that ρ̄ ∈ X_n(F) is such that ρ̄|_{I_K} is a (6n−2)-generic tame inertial F-type for K. If σ ∉ W^?(ρ̄|_{I_K}), then σ is (ρ̄, Ŝ_{Λ,t,elim})-irrelevant.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: The enlarged tame system is a relative Breuil–Mézard system
items.statement: Let Λ ⊂ X_*(T^∨) be a finite set of dominant weights containing 0, and let P_ss, Ŝ_{Λ,t} and Ŝ_{Λ,t,elim} be as in §8.4. The set Ŝ_{Λ,t} is a (P_ss, Ŝ_{Λ,t,elim})-Breuil–Mézard system.
items.note: Split from B20. Proof (PDF 172). Write [σ] = Σ_R n^σ_R[R̄] over irreducible E-representations R ([72, Theorem 33]). Take d_σ = 1, n^σ_{0,τ} := n^σ_{σ(τ)} for 2n-generic tame τ, and n^σ_{λ,τ} := 0 for all other types in Ŝ_{Λ,t}. A weight left over in [σ] − Σ n^σ_{σ(τ)}[σ̄(τ)] lies in JH(R̄) for some Deligne–Lusztig R that is not 2n-generic ([19, Corollary 7.7]). So it is not (4n−2)-deep (Lemma 2.3.4) and lies outside W^?(x|_{I_K}) for every x ∈ P_ss (Proposition 2.6.2). The final step, that it is therefore (P_ss, Ŝ_{Λ,t,elim})-irrelevant, is Lemma 8.4.2 (B20), which the proof uses without citing it. The displayed sum is indexed over all of Ŝ_{Λ,t} (see sourceIssues). Remark 8.4.3 (PDF 172) notes that Theorem 8.3.5 only needs patching functors to vanish on P_ss-irrelevant weights, which Proposition 6.2.3 gives.

uses.how: Theorem 8.4.10(2) applies Theorem 8.3.5(2), whose hypothesis that Ŝ is a P-Breuil–Mézard system is this lemma with P = P_ss, Ŝ = Ŝ_{Λ,t} (proof, PDF 174).

For Theorem 8.4.10(4), Ŝ_{Λ,t} must be a (P_ss, S′)-Breuil–Mézard system for the given Breuil–Mézard system S′ ⊇ Ŝ_{Λ,t,elim}. This follows from this lemma, because (P, S_elim)-irrelevance only grows with S_elim (Definition 8.3.1).

items.name: Abstract covering reduces to combinatorial covering
items.statement: If sigma is (3n-1)-deep and S_tilde-covers kappa, then sigma covers kappa in the finite-group sense of Definition2.3.10. This requires component upper bounds and the genericity comparison, not an identification of the two definitions in all ranges.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Generic Serre weights for BM
items.statement: A weight is generic when it occurs in S_{0,t} and covers no constituent of any type in S_tilde_{0,t} outside S_{0,t}. It is consequently (6n-2)-deep, and every weight it covers is again generic.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Theorem 8.4.10(2) constructs Z_σ for generic σ.
Generic Z_σ form a basis (Proposition 8.6.2).
W_gen(r̄) uses this genericity (Definition 9.1.1).

api.name: SerreWeight.IsBMGeneric
api.statement: σ is generic iff σ ∈ JH(σ̄(τ)) for some (η,τ) ∈ S_{{0},t}, and σ covers no weight of JH(σ̄(τ′)) for any (η,τ′) ∈ S̃_{{0},t} ∖ S_{{0},t}.

api.name: SerreWeight.IsBMGeneric.deep
api.statement: A generic weight is (6n−2)-deep (Remark 8.4.7(1)).

api.name: SerreWeight.IsBMGeneric.covers
api.statement: If σ is generic and covers σ′, then σ′ is generic (Remark 8.4.7(2)).

api.name: SerreWeight.IsBMGeneric.relGeneric
api.statement: A generic σ is (S_{Λ,t}, S̃_{Λ,t})-generic for every Λ (Lemma 8.4.8).

tests.name: SerreWeight.BMGeneric_absent
tests.statement: A weight that lies in σ̄(τ) for no (η,τ) ∈ S_{{0},t} is not generic.

tests.name: SerreWeight.BMGeneric_depth_insufficient
tests.statement: Depth is not enough: a (6n−2)-deep weight covering a constituent of some 2n-generic type outside S_{{0},t} is not generic.

tests.name: SerreWeight.BMGeneric_GL2
tests.statement: For GL₂, covering between 3-deep weights is equality (N45), so σ is generic iff it occurs in some σ̄(τ) with (η,τ) ∈ S_{{0},t} and in no σ̄(τ′) with (η,τ′) ∈ S̃_{{0},t} ∖ S_{{0},t}.

items.name: Generic weights are relatively generic
items.statement: Let Λ ⊂ X_*(T^∨) be a finite set of dominant weights containing 0, and let S_{Λ,t} ⊂ Ŝ_{Λ,t} be as in §8.4. If σ is generic (Definition 8.4.6), then σ is (S_{Λ,t}, Ŝ_{Λ,t})-generic (for any set Λ as above).
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Semisimple generic points meet every component of the tame system
items.statement: Let Λ ⊂ X_*(T^∨) be a finite set of dominant weights containing 0, and let S_{Λ,t} and P_ss be as in §8.4. The set P_ss meets all components of S_{Λ,t}: every irreducible component C_σ of X^{λ+η,τ}_F, for any (λ+η, τ) ∈ S_{Λ,t}, contains a point of P_ss.
items.note: Split from B23. Printed with S_{Λ,τ} for S_{Λ,t} (E41). Proof (PDF 173). By Remark 7.4.3(3), σ ∈ JH(σ̄(λ,τ)). Fix a (6n−2+h_{λ+η})-generic lowest alcove presentation of τ; Proposition 2.3.7 then gives a λ-compatible presentation (w̃, w̃(τ)w̃_2^{-1}(0)) of σ with w̃ ↑ t_λ w̃_h^{-1} w̃_2. Take a semisimple ρ̄ with w̃(ρ̄|_{I_K}) = w̃(τ)w̃_2^{-1}ww̃ for some w ∈ W. This presentation is (6n−2)-generic, so ρ̄ ∈ P_ss. Moreover σ ∈ W_obv(ρ̄|_{I_K}), so ρ̄ ∈ C_σ by Proposition 7.4.7(1). This is an explicit construction of one obvious semisimple point on each component.

uses.how: The hypothesis 'P meets all components of S' of Theorem 8.3.5(2), with P = P_ss and S = S_{Λ,t}, used to prove Theorem 8.4.10(2) (PDF 174).
