The proof of Corollary 8.5.2 (PDF 176) uses Lemma 8.2.2 at P_ss to deduce Z_σ = 0 from i_x^*(Z_σ) = 0 for all x ∈ P_ss. That step needs P_ss to meet the relevant components.

items.name: Tame points of generic crystalline stacks are generic
items.statement: Let Λ ⊂ X_*(T^∨) be a finite set of dominant weights containing 0, and let S_{Λ,t} be as in §8.4. Any tame ρ̄ ∈ X^{λ+η,τ}(F) where (λ+η, τ) ∈ S_{Λ,t} is (6n−2)-generic.
items.note: Split from B23. Printed as 'Any tame ρ̄ ∈ X^{λ,τ}(F) where (λ,τ) ∈ S_{Λ,τ}', corrected as in E41. It is a separate assertion from B40, and the printed proof addresses only B40. See sourceIssues for a proof from Proposition 7.2.3 and Corollary 5.5.10. In this paper 'tame' means ρ̄ = ρ̄^ss (§5.5, PDF 122), and ρ̄ is m-generic when ρ̄^ss|_{I_K} is (Definition 5.5.1(1)). So the assertion puts every tame point of these stacks in P_ss.

uses.how: Remark 8.6.4 (PDF 179) takes any tame ρ̄ on C_σ′, for σ′ covered by a generic σ. Such C_σ′ lies in X^{η,τ}_F with (η,τ) ∈ S_{{0},t} ⊆ S_{Λ,t} (Remark 8.4.7(2), Theorem 7.4.2). This sentence then puts ρ̄ in P_ss, where Theorem 8.4.10(2) gives i_ρ̄^*(Z_κ) = Z(M^ρ̄_∞(κ)). The use is implicit: the text layer has no citation of Lemma 8.4.9.

items.name: Minimal patching for tame generic residual representations
items.statement: For semisimple (6n-2)-generic rho there exists a minimal patching functor for S_{Lambda,t}, and its module cycles satisfy the versal BM equations. The domain theorem and detectability upgrade generic rank at most one to rank exactly one.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Generic geometric BM cycles and support
items.statement: For each generic sigma there is a unique cycle with support among C_kappa covered by sigma and pullbacks equal to all chosen minimal patching cycles at P_ss. These cycles are effective by the preceding abstract theorem.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Generic BM cycles are independent of the patching functors
items.locator: Theorem 8.4.10(3), PDF 173; proof PDF 174; alternative proof §8.6.1, PDF 177–179
items.statement: Let Λ ⊂ X_*(T^∨) be a finite set of dominant weights containing 0, with S_{Λ,t} and P_ss as in §8.4. For each x ∈ P_ss choose a minimal patching functor M^x_∞ for x and S_{Λ,t} (these exist by Theorem 8.4.10(1)), and for generic σ let Z_σ be the cycle of Theorem 8.4.10(2). For generic σ, the cycle Z_σ does not depend on the choice of the patching functors M^x_∞ for x ∈ P_ss. For generic σ and semisimple (6n−2)-generic ρ̄ with minimal patching functor M^ρ̄_∞ for ρ̄ and S_{Λ,t}, Z(M^ρ̄_∞(σ)) depends only on the versal ring R_∞ (i.e., it is the pullback to R_∞ of a cycle that is independent of M^ρ̄_∞).
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Generic BM cycles agree with any conjectural BM cycles
items.statement: Let Λ ⊂ X_*(T^∨) be a finite set of dominant weights containing 0, let S_{Λ,t}, P_ss and Ŝ_{Λ,t,elim} be as in §8.4, and for generic σ let Z_σ be the cycle of Theorem 8.4.10(2) (built from minimal patching functors M^x_∞ for x ∈ P_ss and S_{Λ,t}). Assume Conjecture 8.1.1 holds for a Breuil–Mézard system containing Ŝ_{Λ,t,elim}. Then the above cycles Z_σ (for generic σ) coincide with those from Conjecture 8.1.1.
items.note: Split from B26. The proof is 'Items (2), (3), and (4) follow from Theorem 8.3.5 (and the previous lemmas in this section)'. For (4) this means Theorem 8.3.5(4) (B38) with P = P_ss, S = S_{Λ,t}, Ŝ = Ŝ_{Λ,t} and Ŝ_elim the given Breuil–Mézard system S′. The hypotheses come from: Theorem 8.4.10(1) (B24) for the minimal patching functors; Lemma 8.4.9 (B40) for P_ss meeting all components; Lemma 8.4.4 (B39) plus monotonicity of irrelevance in S_elim (Definition 8.3.1, used without comment) for (P_ss, S′)-Breuil–Mézard; and S′ ⊇ Ŝ_{Λ,t,elim} ⊇ Ŝ_{Λ,t}. Lemma 8.4.8 (B23) makes each generic σ (S_{Λ,t}, Ŝ_{Λ,t})-generic.

uses.how: The introduction claims, citing Theorem 8.4.10, that cycles from any extension of Theorem 1.5.9 to a spanning set must agree with the constructed Z_σ for sufficiently generic σ.

items.name: Shifted polynomial genericity
items.statement: For an integral polynomial f and dominant omega, define f^omega as the finite product over lattice points nu in Conv(omega) of f(X-nu). Build P_{P,Lambda,e} from the shifted product of P_{eta,e}P_{7n-3}; distinguish this polynomial from the original local-model P_{lambda,e}.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Lemma 8.4.11 uses P_{P,Λ,e}.
Corollary 8.4.12 uses P_{P,Λ,e}.
Lemma 8.5.1 transports P_{P,Λ,e}-genericity along admissibility.
Theorem 9.1.6's polynomial includes P^η_{η,e₀} from (8.1).

api.name: ShiftPoly.def
api.statement: For f ∈ Z[t₁,…,t_n] and dominant ω, f^ω(t) := ∏_{ν∈Conv(ω)∩Z^n} f(t − ν) (8.1).

api.name: ShiftPoly.generic_iff
api.statement: a is f^ω-generic iff a − ν is f-generic for every lattice point ν of Conv(ω), since a product is a unit iff each factor is.

api.name: ShiftPoly.used
api.statement: If μ is P_{P,Λ,e}-generic, then (λ+η, τ) ∈ S_{P,Λ,t} for every λ ∈ Λ (Lemma 8.4.11).

tests.name: ShiftPoly.zero
tests.statement: For ω = 0, Conv(0) = {0} and f^0 = f.

tests.name: ShiftPoly.GL2
tests.statement: For n = 2 and ω = (1,0), the lattice points of Conv(ω) are (1,0) and (0,1), so f^ω(t₁,t₂) = f(t₁−1, t₂)·f(t₁, t₂−1).

tests.name: ShiftPoly.not_Plambda
tests.statement: P_{P,Λ,e} is not the local-model polynomial P_{λ,e}; the shift over Conv(λ+η−w₀(η)) is essential for Lemma 8.4.11.

items.name: Polynomial genericity places types in the good subsystem
items.statement: Let Λ ⊂ X_*(T^∨) be a finite set of dominant weights containing 0, and let P_{P,Λ,e} := ∏_{λ∈Λ} ∏_{j∈J} P̃_{η,e}^{(λ+η−w_0(η))_j}, where P̃_{η,e} = P_{η,e}·P_{7n−3} and f^ω is the shifted product (8.1). Let τ be a tame inertial type for K with a lowest alcove presentation (s, μ−η) such that μ is P_{P,Λ,e}-generic. Then (λ+η, τ) ∈ S_{P,Λ,t} for any λ ∈ Λ. Here S_{P,Λ,t} ⊂ S_{Λ,t} is the set of types (λ+η, τ) such that JH(σ̄(λ,τ)) consists only of generic Serre weights (PDF 173).
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Polynomial-generic geometric Breuil–Mézard
items.locator: Corollary 8.4.12, PDF 175; stated in the introduction as Theorem 1.5.9 (PDF 18)
items.statement: Let Λ ⊂ X_*(T^∨) be a finite set of dominant weights containing 0. Then there exist effective cycles Z_σ ∈ Z[X_{n,red}] for each Serre weight σ such that Z_{λ,τ} = Σ_σ [σ̄(λ,τ):σ] Z_σ for any λ ∈ Λ and tame inertial type τ with a lowest alcove presentation (s, μ−η) with μ P_{P,Λ,e}-generic.
items.note: Split from B28. Proof: 'This follows from Lemma 8.4.11 and Theorem 8.4.10.' Lemma 8.4.11 (B28) puts every such (λ+η, τ) in S_{P,Λ,t}. The equations and effectivity come from Theorem 8.3.5(2) ('Conjecture 8.1.1 holds for S_P', with S_{P,Λ,t} ⊆ S_P by Lemma 8.4.8) through the proof of Theorem 8.4.10; the printed statement of Theorem 8.4.10(2) does not contain them (see sourceIssues). Remark 8.4.13 (PDF 175): a non-generic σ lies in no JH(σ̄(λ,τ)) with (λ+η,τ) ∈ S_{P,Λ,t}, so only generic σ occur, and the remaining Z_σ may be any effective cycles, e.g. 0. No uniqueness is claimed (Remark 1.5.10(1)); Proposition 8.6.5 (B37) is the uniqueness statement for very generic weights. The introduction states the result as Theorem 1.5.9 (PDF 18–19), for regular dominant weights and 'sufficiently generic' τ. The hypothesis inherits the problems with P_{P,Λ,e} recorded against Lemma 8.4.11.

uses.how: It is the proved generic instance of Conjecture 8.1.1 (API entry GeometricBM.provedGeneric).
Proposition 8.6.5 takes two effective solutions of exactly these equations and proves they agree at very generic σ₀.
The introduction's statement of this corollary.

items.name: Product compatibility of BM cycles
items.statement: For a finite product of unramified local fields, completed tensor products of patching functors and uniqueness give the corresponding product structure of the generic cycles.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Admissibility transports polynomial genericity
items.statement: For finite dominant Lambda and residual inertia with shifted P_{P,Lambda,e}^eta-generic parameter, any tame tau with relative shape in Adm(lambda+eta) for some lambda in Lambda belongs to the good type subsystem.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Generic small-weight versal BM for all tame WD types
items.locator: Corollary8.5.2 PDF176; stated in the introduction as Theorems 1.2.3 and 1.5.3 (PDF 6, 16)
items.statement: For finite dominant Lambda containing zero, let h=max_{lambda in Lambda,alpha} <lambda,alpha^vee> and m=max{2h+2h_eta,6n-2}. If rho_ss inertia has parameters generic for P_{P,Lambda,e}^eta P_m, cycles on the chosen algebraic versal ring satisfy Z(R^{lambda+eta,tau}_{rho,F})=sum_sigma [r(tau) tensor V(lambda):sigma]Z_sigma(rho) for every lambda in Lambda and every tame Weil–Deligne type. The virtual type r(tau) may have signed coefficients. Genuine noncrystalline semistable types have zero relevant rings in this range; this is not a geometric domain theorem for wild rho.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Unit leading coefficient of a generic BM cycle
items.statement: For generic sigma, the coefficient of C_sigma in Z_sigma is one. The argument uses a specially chosen obvious semisimple point where the crystalline deformation ring is formally smooth and a detectable minimal patching functor is nonzero.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Generic BM cycles form an integral basis
items.statement: The generic Z_sigma form a basis of the integral span of the generic C_sigma, via the covering partial order and a unipotent triangular transition matrix.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Defect of a predicted weight
items.statement: For 2n-generic tame residual inertia, the pair (w,w1) indexing sigma in W? defines delta_rho(sigma)=length(t_eta)-length((w_h w)^-1 w0 w1). It is independent of the lowest-alcove presentation, nonnegative, and zero exactly on obvious weights.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Proposition 8.6.3: the unique defect-maximizing weight.
The recursion runs by induction on defect.
Lemma 9.1.10 uses strictly defect-lowering types.

api.name: Defect.def
api.statement: For 2n-generic tame ρ and σ ∈ W?(ρ) corresponding to (w̃, w̃₁) under (2.14), δ_ρ(σ) := ℓ(t_η) − ℓ((w̃_h w̃)⁻¹ w₀ w̃₁).

api.name: Defect.indep
api.statement: δ_ρ(σ) is independent of the lowest-alcove presentation, since changing it conjugates by Ω, which preserves length.

api.name: Defect.nonneg
api.statement: δ_ρ(σ) ≥ 0, with equality iff σ ∈ W_obv(ρ), by Wang's theorem.

api.name: Defect.max
api.statement: If w̃(ρ,τ) ∈ Adm^reg(η), then W?(ρ) ∩ JH(σ̄(τ)) has a unique weight of maximal defect (Proposition 8.6.3).

tests.name: Defect.GL2
tests.statement: For GL₂ every Herzig weight is obvious (N65), so δ_ρ ≡ 0.

tests.name: Defect.GL3_bound
tests.statement: For GL₃, ℓ(t_η) = 1 + 1 + 2 = 4; the 6 obvious weights have defect 0 and the 3 shadow weights have positive defect.

tests.name: Defect.domain
tests.statement: δ_ρ is defined only on W?(ρ) for 2n-generic ρ.

tests.name: Defect.not_length
tests.statement: δ_ρ(σ) is not ℓ(w̃); it measures the gap to ℓ(t_η).

items.name: Unique maximal defect in a type intersection
items.statement: For compatible 2n-generic tame rho,tau with relative shape in Adm_reg(eta), the factorization w2^-1 w0 w1 determines a unique constituent in W?(rho) intersect JH(barsigma(tau)) maximizing defect.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Recursive BM coefficient computation
items.statement: Choose a type for each predicted sigma so that every other constituent in its predicted intersection has smaller defect. Compute the sigma cycle from the type cycle by subtracting the lower-defect terms and dividing by its positive multiplicity. The displayed (8.3) must exclude kappa=sigma from the sum; the image verifies the omission, recorded in E21. Component-meeting semisimple test points recover global coefficients.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: The alternative proof of Theorem 8.4.10(3).
Proposition 8.6.5 repeats the recursion for very generic weights.
Lemma 9.1.10 uses the same defect-lowering choice of τ.

api.name: BMRecursion.choose
api.statement: For σ ∈ W?(ρ) corresponding to (w̃, w̃₁), choose τ with w̃(τ) = w̃(ρ)(w̃_h w̃)⁻¹w₀w̃₁; then W?(ρ) ∩ JH(σ̄(τ)) consists of σ and weights of strictly smaller defect.

api.name: BMRecursion.step
api.statement: [σ̄(τ):σ]·Z_σ(ρ)^gen = Z_τ(ρ)^gen − Σ_{κ∈W?(ρ)∩JH(σ̄(τ)), κ≠σ} [σ̄(τ):κ]·Z_κ(ρ)^gen, which is (8.3) with the exclusion κ ≠ σ of E21.

api.name: BMRecursion.base
api.statement: If δ_ρ(σ) = 0, then W?(ρ) ∩ JH(σ̄(τ)) = {σ} (Corollary 2.6.5), so [σ̄(τ):σ]·Z_σ(ρ)^gen = Z_τ(ρ)^gen.

api.name: BMRecursion.global
api.statement: Choosing ρ on C_{σ′} for each σ′ covered by σ recovers the coefficient of C_{σ′} in Z_σ (Remark 8.6.4, via Proposition 8.2.3).

tests.name: BMRecursion.obvious
tests.statement: If σ is obvious (δ = 0), no subtraction occurs.

tests.name: BMRecursion.E21
tests.statement: Including κ = σ in the subtracted sum, as (8.3) is printed, would subtract Z_σ(ρ)^gen from both sides and give a false identity (E21).

tests.name: BMRecursion.GL2
tests.statement: For GL₂ all Herzig weights are obvious, so each Z_σ(ρ)^gen is read off one type: [σ̄(τ):σ]·Z_σ(ρ)^gen = Z_τ(ρ)^gen with τ from Corollary 2.6.5.

items.name: Very generic Breuil–Mézard cycles are determined by the polynomial-generic equations
items.statement: Proposition 8.6.5. Let Λ ⊂ X_*(T^∨) be a finite set of dominant weights containing 0. Suppose there are two collections of effective cycles Z_σ, Z′_σ ∈ Z[X_{n,red}], one for each Serre weight σ, such that Z_{λ,τ} = Σ_σ [σ̄(λ,τ):σ] Z_σ and Z_{λ,τ} = Σ_σ [σ̄(λ,τ):σ] Z′_σ for any λ ∈ Λ and any tame inertial type τ which is P_{P,Λ,e}-generic. Let σ_0 be a Serre weight with the following property: for any pair of tame types τ_1, τ_2 such that JH(σ̄(τ_1)) ∩ JH(σ̄(τ_2)) ≠ ∅ and κ ∈ JH(σ̄(τ_1)) for some κ covered by σ_0, τ_2 is P_{P,Λ,e}-generic. Then for each semisimple ρ̄ ∈ X_n(F), Z_{σ_0}(ρ̄) = Z′_{σ_0}(ρ̄). In particular, Z_{σ_0} = Z′_{σ_0}. Here P_{P,Λ,e} = ∏_{λ∈Λ} ∏_{j∈J} P̃^{(λ+η−w_0(η))_j}_{η,e} (§8.4.1, PDF174). A tame type is P-generic when it has a lowest alcove presentation (s, μ−η) with μ P-generic, as in Corollary 8.4.12. Z_σ(ρ̄) = i^*_ρ̄(Z_σ).
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Polynomial genericity gives the very generic hypothesis
items.statement: Remark 8.6.6. The condition on the Serre weight σ_0 in Proposition 8.6.5 is guaranteed by Q-genericity, for an appropriate polynomial Q built out of P_{P,Λ,e} (cf. Proposition 2.3.7 and the proof of Lemma 8.4.11).
items.note: Split from B37. The paper prints no proof and no explicit Q. The intended argument is the shift argument of Lemma 8.4.11 (B28). If σ_0 covers κ ∈ JH(σ̄(τ_1)) and JH(σ̄(τ_1)) ∩ JH(σ̄(τ_2)) ≠ ∅, then compatible lowest alcove presentations of τ_1 and τ_2 differ from one of σ_0 by elements of bounded convex hulls. The Jordan–Hölder constituents of Deligne–Lusztig representations are controlled by Proposition 2.3.7. So Q can be a finite product of shifts f^ω of P_{P,Λ,e} as in (8.1). A blueprint must fix those ω and prove the bound, which the remark does not do.

uses.how: "…they do determine a subset of Z_σ for which σ is sufficiently generic, cf. Proposition 8.6.5 and Remark 8.6.6."

items.name: Definite unitary global setting
items.statement: Fix a CM extension F/F+ with F+ totally real and not Q, all p-adic places split in F, and a form of GL_n over F+ split over F and definite at infinity. Choose its integral model away from N prime to p, a place above each split place, and identifications with GL_n locally. Assume F is unramified at p, as stated in §1.6 PDF20; the body §9.1 uses that standing local hypothesis.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Algebraic automorphic forms on G (9.2).
Hecke algebras at split places outside S.
Theorem 9.1.6 is stated in this setting.
Polarized global deformation data for G_{F+} (§A.3.2).

api.name: DefiniteUnitary.setup
api.statement: F/F⁺ CM with F⁺ ≠ Q totally real, all places above p split in F, and G/F⁺ an outer form of GL_n split over F and definite at every archimedean place; a reductive model over O_{F⁺}[1/N] with p ∤ N and ι : G/O_F[1/N] ≅ GL_n/O_F[1/N] (9.1).

api.name: DefiniteUnitary.iota_split
api.statement: For split w | v, ι_w : G(O_{F⁺_v}) ≅ GL_n(O_{F_w}); choosing ṽ | v gives ι_v.

api.name: DefiniteUnitary.compact
api.statement: G(F⁺⊗R) is compact, so G(F⁺)\G(A^∞_{F⁺})/U is finite for compact open U.

tests.name: DefiniteUnitary.U1
tests.statement: For n = 1, G is the norm-one torus U(1)_{F/F⁺}, compact at infinity.

tests.name: DefiniteUnitary.not_Q
tests.statement: F⁺ = Q is excluded by the standing hypotheses of §9.1.

tests.name: DefiniteUnitary.conj_choice
tests.statement: Replacing ṽ by its conjugate changes ι_v by the outer automorphism g ↦ ᵗg⁻¹, which the paper suppresses.

tests.name: DefiniteUnitary.finite_quotient
tests.statement: For every compact open U, the double coset space G(F⁺)\G(A^∞)/U is finite.

items.name: Algebraic automorphic forms with coefficients
items.statement: For compact open U=U_p U^p and finite O-module W with continuous U_p-action, S(U,W) consists of functions on G(F+)\G(A_f) satisfying f(gu)=u_p^-1 f(g). A sufficiently small level has stabilizer orders prime to p; then S(U,-) is exact and finite over O.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Hecke operators act on S(U,W).
Modular weights are defined by nonvanishing of localized S(U, σ^∨∘ι_p).
Auxiliary parahoric levels (§A.4).
Finite patching modules (§A.5).

api.name: AlgAutForm.mk
api.statement: S(U,W) := {f : G(F⁺)\G(A^∞_{F⁺}) → W | f(gu) = u_p⁻¹f(g) for all g, u ∈ U}, for U = U_pU^{∞,p} compact open and W a finite O-module with continuous U_p-action.

api.name: AlgAutForm.finite
api.statement: S(U,W) is a finite O-module.

api.name: AlgAutForm.exact
api.statement: If U is sufficiently small (all t⁻¹G(F⁺)t ∩ U have order prime to p), W ↦ S(U,W) is exact.

api.name: AlgAutForm.levelChange
api.statement: For U′ ⊆ U there are the restriction S(U,W) → S(U′,W) and the trace S(U′,W) → S(U,W), Hecke-equivariant away from the level.

tests.name: AlgAutForm.trivial_coeff
tests.statement: If U is sufficiently small and W = O with trivial action, S(U,O) ≅ O^h with h = #G(F⁺)\G(A^∞)/U.

tests.name: AlgAutForm.not_small
tests.statement: Without sufficient smallness exactness can fail: for a stabilizer of order p, W ↦ W^{Z/p} is not exact.

tests.name: AlgAutForm.reduction
tests.statement: For U sufficiently small and W O-flat, S(U, W⊗F) = S(U,W)⊗F.

items.name: Hecke algebra and attached polarized Galois representation
items.statement: Define the universal unramified Hecke algebra using split places outside S, its image on S(U,W), and localization at a residual eigensystem. Import the associated G_n-valued Galois representation with characteristic polynomial coefficients (-1)^j Norm(w)^(j(j-1)/2) T_w^(j). Define automorphic residual representations by nonzero localized forms.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Automorphy of level U and weight σ is nonvanishing at the maximal ideal of r̄.
Theorem 9.1.6 assumes r̄ automorphic.
r_m is the source of the global deformation data (§A.3).
The patched ring acts through Hecke algebras (§A.5).

api.name: HeckeAlgebra.universal
api.statement: T^P := O[T_w^{(i)} : w ∈ P, 0 ≤ i ≤ n] for P ⊆ P_S of finite complement, closed under complex conjugation.

api.name: HeckeAlgebra.image
api.statement: T^P(U,W) := image of T^P in End_O(S(U,W)), a semilocal ring; T^Q(U,W) for Q the places removed from P_S.

api.name: HeckeAlgebra.galoisRep
api.statement: For m in the support there is r_m : G_{F⁺,S} → G_n(T^Q(U,W)_m) with det(1 − r_m|_{G_F}(Frob_w)X) = Σ_j (−1)^j N_{F/Q}(w)^{j(j−1)/2} α(T_w^{(j)}) X^j for w ∈ P (imported).

api.name: Automorphic.def
api.statement: r̄ is automorphic of level U and coefficients W iff S(U,W)_m ≠ 0 for the corresponding maximal ideal m ⊂ T^P.

api.name: Automorphic.modF
api.statement: S(U,W)_m ≠ 0 iff S(U, W⊗F)_m ≠ 0.

tests.name: HeckeAlgebra.GL2_charpoly
tests.statement: For n = 2, det(1 − r_m(Frob_w)X) = 1 − α(T_w^{(1)})X + N(w)α(T_w^{(2)})X².

tests.name: HeckeAlgebra.n1
tests.statement: For n = 1 the polynomial is 1 − α(T_w^{(1)})X.

tests.name: HeckeAlgebra.not_in_support
tests.statement: If S(U,W)_m = 0, no Galois representation is attached to m at this level.

items.name: Modular Serre weight and generic modular weights
items.statement: A weight sigma is modular for residual r at hyperspecial p-level U when S(U,sigma^vee composed with iota_p) localized at r is nonzero. Define W(r) by varying the away-from-p level and W_gen(r) by the generic-weight condition. An automorphic r has at least one such weight by exactness and pro-p invariants.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Conjecture 9.1.4 predicts W(r̄) = W?(r̄_p|_I).
Theorem 9.1.6 proves W(r̄) = W^g_gen(r̄_p) = W?(r̄_p|_I) under P-genericity.
The arbitrary-level patching functor realizes modular weights (Lemma A.1.1(1)).

api.name: ModularWeight.def
api.statement: For U = G(O_p)U^{S_p} sufficiently small, σ is modular for r̄ at level U iff r̄ is automorphic of level U and coefficients σ^∨∘ι_p; σ is modular iff this holds for some such U.

api.name: ModularWeight.sets
api.statement: W(r̄) is the set of modular weights, and W_gen(r̄) ⊆ W(r̄) the generic ones (Definition 8.4.6).

api.name: ModularWeight.nonempty
api.statement: If r̄ is automorphic then W(r̄) ≠ ∅, by exactness of S(U,−)_m and pro-p invariants.

api.name: ModularWeight.dual
api.statement: The coefficients are the F-dual σ^∨ transported by ι_p, not σ itself.

tests.name: ModularWeight.not_automorphic
tests.statement: If r̄ is not automorphic, W(r̄) = ∅.

tests.name: ModularWeight.dual_matters
tests.statement: Using σ instead of σ^∨ gives the dual set in general; for GL₂ over F_p the dual of Sym^r⊗det^a is Sym^r⊗det^{−r−a}.

tests.name: ModularWeight.gen_subset
tests.statement: W_gen(r̄) ⊆ W(r̄), with equality when every modular weight is generic, as Remark 9.1.7(2) arranges.

items.name: Geometric and BM Serre weights
items.statement: A geometric weight sigma is one for which the tuple of local residual representations lies on C_sigma. W_gen^g retains (3n-1)-deep weights. W_gen^BM consists of generic weights for which the tuple lies in the support of Z_sigma. It has product structure over p-adic places, and generic geometric weights are BM weights by the unit leading coefficient.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Theorem 9.1.6 identifies W(r̄) with W^g_gen and W_gen with W^BM_gen.
W^g_gen(ρ̄) = W?(ρ̄|_I) for P-generic ρ̄ (Lemma 9.1.9).
Generic weights with M∞(σ) ≠ 0 are W^BM_gen(ρ̄) (Lemma 9.1.10).

api.name: GeometricWeight.def
api.statement: σ = ⊗_vσ_v is a geometric weight of ρ̄ iff (ρ̄_v) lies on C_σ, equivalently ρ̄_v lies on C_{σ_v} for all v ∈ S_p; W^g_gen(ρ̄) keeps the (3n−1)-deep ones.

api.name: BMWeight.def
api.statement: W^BM_gen(ρ̄) is the set of generic weights σ with ρ̄ in the support of Z_σ (Theorem 8.4.10(2)).

api.name: BMWeight.pi
api.statement: W^BM_gen(ρ̄) = {⊗_vσ_v : σ_v ∈ W^BM_gen(ρ̄_v)} (Remark 8.4.14).

api.name: GeometricWeight.subset_BM
api.statement: Every generic weight in W^g_gen(ρ̄) lies in W^BM_gen(ρ̄), by the unit leading coefficient (Remark 9.1.3, Proposition 8.6.1).

tests.name: GeometricWeight.single_place
tests.statement: For |S_p| = 1 the product description of W^BM_gen is tautological.

tests.name: GeometricWeight.depth_cut
tests.statement: A geometric weight that is not (3n−1)-deep is excluded from W^g_gen(ρ̄), although ρ̄ lies on its component.

tests.name: GeometricWeight.product
tests.statement: σ = ⊗σ_v is geometric for (ρ̄_v) iff each σ_v is geometric for ρ̄_v.

items.name: Herzig-type weight conjecture for definite unitary groups
items.statement: Conjecture 9.1.4 (based on [39, Conjecture 6.9] and [33, §2 and 9.2]). Suppose that r̄ : G_{F+} → G_n(F) is automorphic and that the inertial L-homomorphism r̄_p|_{I_{Q_p}} over F is tame and 2n-generic. Then W(r̄) = W^?(r̄_p|_{I_{Q_p}}). Here W(r̄) is the set of modular Serre weights of r̄ (Definition 9.1.1). r̄_p : W_{Q_p} → ^L G(F), with G = GL_n, is the L-homomorphism given by the restrictions (r̄|_{G_{F+_v}})_{v∈S_p}, in the §9.1 setting: F^+ ≠ Q totally real, F/F^+ CM, all places above p split, G definite unitary. This is a conjecture. Theorem 9.1.6 (V07) proves it under P-genericity and adequacy.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Theorem 9.1.6 proves both conjectures for P-generic, adequate r̄.
Remark 9.1.7 describes the polynomial that makes the conjectures unconditional.

api.name: Conjecture914
api.statement: Interface, not a theorem: if r̄ is automorphic and r̄_p|_{I_{Q_p}} is tame and 2n-generic, then W(r̄) = W?(r̄_p|_{I_{Q_p}}).

api.name: Conjecture914.provedGeneric
api.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 9.1.6 (V07): p ∤ 2n, r̄|_{G_F}(G_{F(ζ_p)}) adequate, and r̄_p|_{I_{Q_p}} tame with a lowest alcove presentation (s, μ−η), μ P-generic. Then W(r̄) = W^g_gen(r̄_p) = W?(r̄_p|_{I_{Q_p}}), which is the conclusion of the conjecture.

api.name: Conjecture914.companion
api.statement: Conjecture 9.1.5 (V14) is the companion equality W_gen(r̄) = W^BM_gen(r̄_p), with no genericity hypothesis on r̄_p. Theorem 9.1.6 proves both under P-genericity.

tests.name: Conjecture914.from_V07
tests.statement: Theorem 9.1.6 gives W(r̄) = W^g_gen(r̄_p) = W?(r̄_p|_{I_{Q_p}}), which is Conjecture 9.1.4 for every r̄ satisfying its hypotheses. P_{6n−2} | P makes μ (6n−2)-deep, hence 2n-generic.

tests.name: Conjecture914.not_general
tests.statement: Nothing is asserted when r̄_p|_{I_{Q_p}} is wildly ramified or not 2n-generic, and W? is defined only for tame inertial parameters. The conjecture is not used as an axiom anywhere.

tests.name: Conjecture914.GL2
tests.statement: For n = 2 and generic tame r̄_p, Herzig's W?(r̄_p|_I) agrees with the Buzzard–Diamond–Jarvis weight set, so Conjecture 9.1.4 specializes to the generic weight part of Serre's conjecture for U(2).

items.name: Generic Breuil–Mézard weight conjecture for definite unitary groups
items.locator: Conjecture 9.1.5, PDF183; stated in the introduction as Conjecture 1.6.2 (PDF 22)
items.statement: Conjecture 9.1.5 (an unconditional version of [33, Conjecture 3.2.7], made possible by Theorem 8.4.10(2)). Suppose that r̄ : G_{F+} → G_n(F) is automorphic. Then W_gen(r̄) = W^BM_gen(r̄_p). Here W_gen(r̄) is the set of generic Serre weights (Definition 8.4.6) in W(r̄). W^BM_gen(ρ̄) is the set of generic Serre weights σ such that ρ̄ lies in the support of the cycle Z_σ of Theorem 8.4.10(2) (Definition 9.1.2, with Remark 8.4.14 for the product over v ∈ S_p).
items.note: Split from V06. This is a conjecture and is not proved in general. It imposes no genericity hypothesis on r̄_p: "generic" restricts only the Serre weights, and W^BM_gen is defined through the cycles Z_σ that Theorem 8.4.10(2) builds for generic σ without conditions.

uses.how: Theorem 9.1.6 proves W_gen(r̄) = W^BM_gen(r̄_p) for P-generic tame r̄_p with adequate image.
Lemma 9.1.10's second equality, {σ generic | M_∞(σ) ≠ 0} = W^BM_gen(ρ̄), is the patched local form.
Conjecture 1.6.2 restates it, and the text notes that Theorem 1.5.3 implies it for tame r̄ with sufficiently generic r̄_v.

api.name: Conjecture915
api.statement: Interface, not a theorem: if r̄ : G_{F+} → G_n(F) is automorphic, then W_gen(r̄) = W^BM_gen(r̄_p).

api.name: Conjecture915.provedGeneric
api.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 9.1.6 (V07), W_gen(r̄) = W^BM_gen(r̄_p).

api.name: Conjecture915.patching
api.statement: Take tame r̄_p with a lowest alcove presentation (s, μ−η), μ P-generic. Lemma 9.1.10 (V11) gives {σ generic | M_∞(σ) ≠ 0} = W^BM_gen(r̄_p) for every weak detectable patching functor. The functor of Lemma A.1.1 has M_∞(σ) ≠ 0 exactly when σ ∈ W(r̄), which turns this into the conjecture.

api.name: Conjecture915.geometricInclusion
api.statement: Remark 9.1.3: every generic Serre weight in W^g_gen(r̄_p) lies in W^BM_gen(r̄_p) (Proposition 8.6.1).

tests.name: Conjecture915.from_V07
tests.statement: The second equality of Theorem 9.1.6, W_gen(r̄) = W^BM_gen(r̄_p), is Conjecture 9.1.5 when r̄_p is P-generic and tame, r̄|_{G_F}(G_{F(ζ_p)}) is adequate and p ∤ 2n.

tests.name: Conjecture915.noGenericWeights
tests.statement: If no Serre weight is generic, both sides are empty and the conjecture holds trivially. For n ≥ 2 this happens for all small p, because a generic weight is (6n−2)-deep (Remark 8.4.7(1)).

tests.name: Conjecture915.notHerzig
tests.statement: The conjecture does not identify W_gen(r̄) with the generic part of W?(r̄_p|_{I_{Q_p}}). For sufficiently generic wildly ramified ρ̄ the introduction states W^BM(ρ̄) ⊊ W?(ρ̄^ss) (Remark 1.6.3(2), PDF22), so the two predictions differ there.

items.name: Polynomial-generic weight part of Serre's conjecture for U(n)
items.locator: Theorem9.1.6 PDF183–184; stated in the introduction as Theorems 1.2.5 and 1.6.1 (PDF 6, 21)
items.statement: In the standing definite-unitary unramified local setting, with p not dividing 2n, residual r automorphic, r restricted to G_{F(zeta_p)} adequate, and tame local inertia whose chosen lowest-alcove parameters mu are generic for a nonzero integral polynomial P independent of p, W(r)=W_gen^g(r_p)=W?(r_p inertia) and W_gen(r)=W_gen^BM(r_p). Preserve all global hypotheses and do not impose an additional mild-level condition away from p.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.
proofSteps: The printed proof is two lines and defers entirely: 'The result follows from Lemmas 9.1.10 and A.1.1.' A blueprint must therefore carry both lemmas as owned obligations, not as citations.

Lemma A.1.1 supplies the object: for automorphic r-bar with adequate restriction to G_{F(zeta_p)} it produces a weak patching functor whose nonvanishing set is exactly W(r-bar), and, under the extra P_{6n-2}P_{2 eta, e}-genericity, a detectable one.
Lemma 9.1.10 computes that nonvanishing set for a detectable functor: it equals W?(r-bar_p restricted to inertia), and among generic weights equals W^BM_gen(r-bar_p).

Chaining the two identifies W(r-bar) with W?(r-bar_p|I), and Lemma 9.1.9 identifies the latter with W^g_gen(r-bar_p), giving the three-way equality in the statement; the generic clause is the second half of 9.1.10.

Record the genericity polynomial explicitly, as Remark 9.1.7(1) does: P may be taken to be the product of P_{6n-2}, P_{2 eta, e}, P_{eta_0 eta, e} and the Q of Lemma 9.1.9. The theorem is only as effective as that product, which is not made explicit in rank n.

items.name: Explicit genericity polynomial for Theorem 9.1.6
items.statement: Remark 9.1.7(1). The polynomial P in Theorem 9.1.6 can be taken to be the product of the polynomials P_{6n−2}, P_{2η,e}, P^{η_0}_{η,e} and Q appearing, respectively, in Remark 2.1.11, Theorem 7.3.2(2), equation (8.1) and the proof of Lemma 9.1.9. Here P_{6n−2} = ∏_{i=1}^n ∏_{j=1}^{6n−2} (X_i − X_{i+1} − j) with X_{n+1} = X_1. P_{λ,e} is the polynomial of Theorem 7.3.2(2) for Hodge type λ, which depends only on λ and the ramification index e of O. P^{η_0}_{η,e} is the shift (8.1) of P_{η,e} by η_0, where f^ω = ∏_{ν∈Conv(ω)} f(t_1−ν_1, …, t_n−ν_n). Q = ∏_{w̃∈R} ∏_{w̃_2↑w̃, w̃_2∈W̃^+} ∏_{w∈W} P_{w̃}(X + w w̃_2^{−1}(0)), with P_{w̃} from Proposition 4.7.3 and R a set of representatives of W̃_1^+/X^0(T).
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Theorem 9.1.6 requires μ to be P-generic. Remark 9.1.7(1) says this P works.
The proof of Lemma 9.1.10 uses P = P^{η_0}_{η,e}·P_{6n−2}·Q, which divides this P.
P_{6n−2}·P_{2η,e} divides P, which is the genericity needed for a detectable patching functor.

api.name: GenericityPoly.mk
api.statement: P := P_{6n−2}·P_{2η,e}·P^{η_0}_{η,e}·Q, with P_{6n−2} from Remark 2.1.11 and P_{2η,e} = P_{λ,e} of Theorem 7.3.2(2) for λ = 2η. P^{η_0}_{η,e} is the shift (8.1) of P_{η,e} by η_0, and Q comes from the proof of Lemma 9.1.9 (Remark 9.1.7(1)).

api.name: GenericityPoly.mul
api.statement: If μ is PQ′-generic it is P-generic, so enlarging P keeps every conclusion of Theorem 9.1.6.

api.name: GenericityPoly.dvd
api.statement: P^{η_0}_{η,e}·P_{6n−2}·Q divides P, and this is the polynomial of the proof of Lemma 9.1.10 (V11). P_{6n−2}·P_{2η,e} divides P, and this is the genericity that Lemma A.1.1(2) needs for a detectable patching functor.

api.name: GenericityPoly.allGeneric
api.statement: Remark 9.1.7(2) (V15): P can be enlarged so that W?(r̄_p) contains only generic Serre weights.

tests.name: GenericityPoly.Pm_n1
tests.statement: For n = 1, P_m = ∏_{j=1}^m (−j) = (−1)^m m!, so P_m-genericity only asks that p > m.

tests.name: GenericityPoly.indep_p
tests.statement: The four factors depend on n, η, e and the finite data of the proof of Lemma 9.1.9, not on p. This matches "independent of p" in Theorem 9.1.6.

tests.name: GenericityPoly.small_p
tests.statement: For n ≥ 2 and p | 2n, no tame inertial L-parameter is n-generic (Remark 6.2.5; E88 notes the exception n = 1). Since P_{6n−2} | P, a P-generic μ is (6n−2)-deep. So no input is P-generic and Theorem 9.1.6 is vacuous.

items.name: Enlarging P makes every predicted weight generic
items.statement: Remark 9.1.7(2). There exists P such that the P-genericity hypothesis of Theorem 9.1.6 implies that W?(r̄_p) contains only generic Serre weights. So W_gen(r̄) in Theorem 9.1.6 could be replaced by W(r̄), giving W(r̄) = W^BM_gen(r̄_p).
items.note: Split from V08 (api GenericityPoly.allGeneric). No proof is printed. By Definition 8.4.6, σ is generic if σ ∈ JH(σ̄(τ)) for some (η,τ) ∈ S_{0,t} and σ covers no weight of JH(σ̄(τ′)) for (η,τ′) ∈ Ŝ_{0,t} \ S_{0,t}. Every σ ∈ W?(r̄_p|_I) has a lowest alcove presentation at bounded distance from that of r̄_p (Proposition 2.6.2), and so do the types τ, τ′ involved. A finite product of shifted polynomials f^ω as in (8.1) therefore puts those types in S_{0,t}, as in Lemma 8.4.11 and Remark 8.4.13 (B51). The second sentence then follows from Theorem 9.1.6: W(r̄) = W?(r̄_p|_I) consists of generic weights, so W_gen(r̄) = W(r̄). The paper does not cite the remark again; it is a candidate to fold into V08 or V07.

uses.how: Not cited in any proof. It strengthens the conclusion of Theorem 9.1.6 to W(r̄) = W^BM_gen(r̄_p) for suitable P.

items.name: Global realization of generic semisimple local representations
items.statement: Remark 9.1.8. Suppose that p ∤ 2n, K/Q_p is a finite unramified extension, and ρ̄ : G_K → GL_n(F) is a semisimple continuous Galois representation such that ρ̄|_{I_K} has a lowest alcove presentation (s, μ−η) with μ P-generic, with P as in Theorem 9.1.6. Then by [14, Corollary A.7] there exist a CM extension F/F^+ with F^+ ≠ Q and a (potentially diagonalizably) automorphic representation r̄ : G_{F+} → G_n(F) which is isomorphic to ρ̄ at all p-adic places and whose restriction r̄|_{G_F}(G_{F(ζ_p)}) is adequate. Then Theorem 9.1.6 applies to r̄.
items.note: Split from V08 (api Globalization.exists). The globalization is imported from [14] (Caraiani–Emerton–Gee–Geraghty–Paškūnas–Shin, Patching and the p-adic local Langlands correspondence, Camb. J. Math. 4 (2016)), Corollary A.7, and is not checked here. "Isomorphic to ρ̄ at all p-adic places" needs F^+_v ≅ K for every v | p. Applying Theorem 9.1.6 needs r̄ to lie in the §9.1 setting (all places above p split in F; PDF180–181). The remark asserts both through [14]. The paper does not cite it again.

uses.how: It shows that the hypotheses of Theorem 9.1.6 (V07) are met by a large supply of global r̄.

items.name: Geometric weights equal predicted weights generically
items.statement: A nonzero integral polynomial Q built from finitely many shifted fixed-point polynomials P_w, together with the 4n-depth polynomial, makes W_gen^g(rho)=W?(rho inertia) for tame residual L-parameters. The product is finite modulo central translations.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.
proofSteps: One inclusion is quoted: W^g_gen(rho) is contained in W?(rho restricted to I) by Proposition 7.4.7(3), for 4n-generic rho. Only the reverse inclusion needs the polynomial.

Build the polynomial. Fix a set R of representatives for the finite quotient W-tilde^+_1 / X_0(T) and set Q(X_1, ..., X_n) to be the product, over w-tilde in R, over w-tilde_2 with w-tilde_2 up-arrow w-tilde and w-tilde_2 in W-tilde^+, and over w in W, of P_{w-tilde}(X + w w-tilde_2^{-1}(0)), where P_{w-tilde} is the fixed-point polynomial of Proposition 4.7.3 and w w-tilde_2^{-1}(0) is read in Z^n under X^*(T) = Z^n. The product is finite because the quotient is.

Reverse inclusion. If rho restricted to I_K has a Q-generic lowest alcove presentation (s, mu - eta), then for sigma in W?(rho|I_K) the compatible presentation supplied by Proposition 2.6.2 satisfies the hypothesis of Proposition 7.4.7(2), whence rho lies in C_sigma, i.e. sigma lies in W^g_gen(rho).
Take P = Q P_{4n}, the second factor securing the 4n-genericity that the first inclusion needed. Note that P depends on n but not on p, which is what makes the statement uniform in p.

items.name: Primes of pulled-back Serre components
items.statement: For sufficiently generic tame rho and (3n-1)-deep sigma, the pullback of C_sigma to the product framed deformation ring is irreducible or zero; define its prime p_sigma(rho), using the unit ideal for an absent component. This requires analytic irreducibility, not merely an irreducible stack component.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: The proof of Lemma 9.1.10 compares Ann M∞(σ) with p_σ(ρ̄) and uses (9.4).
Theorem 7.4.2(1) identifies the components of Spec R_ρ̄^τ.

api.name: ComponentPrime.mk
api.statement: For QP_{4n}-generic tame ρ̄ and (3n−1)-deep σ, i_ρ̄^*(C_σ) is irreducible or zero, and p_σ(ρ̄) ⊂ R_ρ̄ is its prime; the unit ideal is used when it is zero.

api.name: ComponentPrime.irreducible
api.statement: The irreducibility of the pullback uses Proposition 4.7.5 and Remark 7.4.3(2) (analytic irreducibility), not merely irreducibility of C_σ.

api.name: ComponentPrime.components_type
api.statement: The irreducible components of Spec R_ρ̄^τ are the C_{σ′}(ρ̄) with σ′ ∈ W?(ρ̄|_I) ∩ JH(σ̄(τ)) (9.4).

tests.name: ComponentPrime.absent
tests.statement: If ρ̄ does not lie on C_σ, then p_σ(ρ̄) is the unit ideal.

tests.name: ComponentPrime.minimal
tests.statement: For a suitably generic τ with σ ∈ W?(ρ̄) ∩ JH(σ̄(τ)), p_σ(ρ̄) is a minimal prime of R_ρ̄^τ, by (9.4).

tests.name: ComponentPrime.needs_generic
tests.statement: Without the genericity hypothesis, the pullback of an irreducible stack component to a versal ring may have several analytic branches.

items.name: Support of any weak detectable patching functor
items.statement: For a suitable polynomial-generic tame rho, a weak detectable patching functor has nonzero weight evaluations exactly on W?(rho inertia), and among generic weights exactly on W_gen^BM(rho). The argument uses defect-lowering types, domains, maximal Cohen–Macaulay support and component primes. No minimal rank-one hypothesis is imposed on this functor.
items.note: Route owner: GenericGL3SerreWeightsAndLattices. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.
proofSteps: Fix the polynomial first: P is the product of P_{eta_0 eta, e}, P_{6n-2} and the Q of Lemma 9.1.9. Every genericity appeal below names which factor it consumes.
Easy inclusion. {sigma : M_infinity(sigma) nonzero} is contained in W?(rho|I) by Proposition 6.2.3, using that P_{6n-2} divides P.

Defect-lowering claim, which carries the argument. If sigma is in W?(rho) and Ann_{R_rho} M_infinity(sigma) is contained in p_{sigma'}(rho) for some sigma' in W^g_gen(rho), then delta(sigma') <= delta(sigma) for the defect function of section 8.6.1. It is proved by choosing a 2n-generic tame tau with w-tilde(tau) = w-tilde(rho|I)(w-tilde_h w-tilde)^{-1} w_0 w-tilde_1, so that W?(rho|I) intersect JH(sigma-bar(tau)) contains sigma together with weights of strictly smaller defect, and reading off the components of Spec R^tau_rho from Theorem 7.4.2(1).

Hard inclusion. For sigma in W?(rho|I) choose tau as above. Since (w-tilde_h w-tilde)^{-1} w_0 w-tilde_1 lies in Adm(eta) by Proposition 2.1.6 and P_{eta_0 eta, e} divides P, the pair (eta, tau) lies in S_{0,t}. Combining four inputs - M_infinity(sigma^circ(tau)) maximal Cohen-Macaulay over R_infinity(tau); R^tau_rho a domain by Theorem 7.3.2(2); M_infinity(sigma^circ(tau)) nonzero by Proposition 6.2.7; and Theorem 7.4.2(1) - gives Ann M_infinity(sigma^circ(tau)) contained in p_sigma(rho). Applying the defect claim with the roles of sigma and sigma' exchanged, and strict defect lowering, forces sigma = sigma', so M_infinity(sigma) is nonzero.

Generic clause. For generic sigma, membership of W?(rho) and of W^BM_gen(rho) agree: forwards by Lemma 9.1.9 with Remark 9.1.3; backwards because for a minimal patching functor for S_{0,t} Theorem 8.4.10(2) gives nonvanishing, hence membership of W? by Proposition 6.2.3, with an alternative route through Remark 4.7.4(2).
Scope caution: this lemma assumes only weak and detectable, with no minimality and no rank-one hypothesis on M_infinity; the minimal functor appears only inside the last step as an auxiliary object.

items.name: Modularity lifting from polynomial-generic local domains
items.statement: For a CM extension in the applicable local unramified setting, a continuous r:G_F->GL_n(E) with finite ramification, potentially crystalline regular type (lambda+eta,tau) at p, polynomial-generic tame tau, polarization r^c=r^vee epsilon^(1-n), semisimple residual restrictions at p, adequate residual image on G_{F(zeta_p)} and zeta_p not in F^{ker ad rbar}, and a residual RACSDC automorphic lift with matching weight and K-types, is automorphic with that weight and type. The residual bars were checked in the published PDF image; residual automorphy is the hypothesis, not prior automorphy of r.
items.note: Route owner: PolarizedAutomorphyLifting. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.
proofSteps: The printed proof is one sentence: the theorem 'follows from Theorem 7.3.2 from standard base change and Taylor-Wiles patching arguments', with a reference to the proof of a cited automorphy lifting paper. Treat this as an outstanding obligation, not as a proof.

What Theorem 7.3.2 supplies is the local input: for a P_{lambda+eta,e}-generic tame tau, the potentially crystalline deformation ring R^{lambda+eta,tau}_rho is a domain (and normal, Cohen-Macaulay). That is the hypothesis a Taylor-Wiles patching argument needs in order to conclude that the patched module is supported on the whole of the local deformation space.

The blueprint obligation is therefore the standard chain, stated in full and not deferred: solvable base change to a setting where the relevant level is mild and r-bar remains adequate; construction of the patched module for the definite unitary group of section 9.1; the support argument using the domain property; and the descent back to automorphy of r with the stated weight and K-type.

Carry all the hypotheses of the statement without weakening: the polarization r^c = r^vee epsilon^{1-n}, semisimplicity of r-bar locally above p, adequacy of r-bar on G_{F(zeta_p)} with zeta_p not in F^{ker ad r-bar}, and the residual RACSDC automorphic lift of matching weight and type. Remark 9.2.2(2) itself records that the inexplicit P_{lambda+eta,e} makes the theorem impractical to apply, which a blueprint should not hide.

items.name: Change-of-weight relaxation of modularity lifting
items.statement: After strengthening the genericity polynomial, the residual automorphic lift in V12 need not initially have matching weight/type: the weight theorem supplies the change of weight. The polynomial is not made effective in arbitrary rank.
items.note: Route owner: PolarizedAutomorphyLifting. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.
proofSteps: The remark asserts two things, and only the first is a mathematical claim: after possibly enlarging the polynomial P_{lambda+eta,e}, the last hypothesis of Theorem 9.2.1 can be relaxed to r-bar being isomorphic to r-bar_iota(pi) for some RACSDC pi with no matching of weight or type.

The mechanism is the weight theorem: Theorem 9.1.6 identifies W(r-bar) with W?(r-bar_p|I) under polynomial genericity, so an automorphic lift of any weight can be moved to one whose weight and K-type match (lambda, sigma(tau)), which is exactly a change of weight.

The enlargement of the polynomial is what pays for this, and it is not made explicit; the blueprint should record which factors are added (those of Theorem 9.1.6, i.e. P_{6n-2}, P_{2 eta, e}, P_{eta_0 eta, e} and Q) rather than leave 'possibly changing' unquantified.

The second assertion of the remark is not a theorem but a caveat, that the inexplicit polynomial makes the result impractical; keep it as a recorded limitation of the whole section rather than dropping it.

items.name: Arbitrary-level patching functor realizing modular weights
items.statement: For p not dividing 2n, automorphic residual r in the standing definite-unitary setting with adequate restriction to G_{F(zeta_p)}, there exists a weak patching functor M_infty such that M_infty(sigma) is nonzero iff sigma belongs to W(r). The construction allows arbitrary away-from-p level after choosing one sufficiently small level realizing all weights.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.
proofSteps: Work in the standing definite-unitary setting of §9.1 with p not dividing 2n, and take r automorphic with r|_{G_{F(zeta_p)}} adequate.

Build the patched module M_infty by the Taylor-Wiles construction of A.4-A.5, then define the functor M_infty(-) = Hom^cont_{O[[G_0(Z_p)]]}(M_infty, (-)^dual)^dual from finite O[G_0(Z_p)]-modules to finitely generated R_infty-modules; it is exact and covariant (PDF 200).

Shrink U^{S_p} so that W = O and so that if r is modular of weight sigma then it is modular of weight sigma AT level G(O_p)U^{S_p}. This is a genuine normalisation, not cosmetic: it is what makes the nonvanishing computation below compute S(U,F)^dual_m.
Check the weak-patching axioms of Definition 6.2.1. Equidimensionality of R_infty comes from R_infty = R_{r_p} tensor-hat_O R^p with R^p = (tensor-hat_{v in S minus S_p} R_v^{xi_v})[[x_1,...,x_g]].

Nonvanishing: the chain of identifications on PDF 200 gives M_infty(Ind^{G_0(Z_p)}_{U^{S_p}} F)/a_infty = Hom^cont(lim_r S(K_pU^{S_p},O/pi^r)^dual, (Ind F)^dual)^dual = S(U,F)^dual_m, which is non-zero.

For the 'if and only if' read the support: M_infty(sigma) is non-zero exactly when sigma is in W(r-bar), which is the statement of part (1). Do not conflate this with detectability, which is part (2) and needs the extra genericity of A02.

items.name: Detectability of the global patching functor
items.statement: If additionally local inertia is tame with parameters generic for P_{6n-2}P_{2eta,e}, the functor in A01 can be taken detectable. This uses upper-alcove obvious-weight nonvanishing followed by the external weight-propagation theorem [56, Theorem4.3.8].
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.
proofSteps: Add the hypotheses of part (2): r_p|_{I_{Q_p}} tame with a lowest alcove presentation (s, mu - eta) in which mu is both P_{6n-2}-generic and P_{2eta,e}-generic.

Take the functor of A01 and strengthen it to a detectable one. The two inputs are the upper-alcove obvious-weight nonvanishing of A04 and the external weight-propagation theorem cited in the appendix.

Genericity is what licenses each: P_{2eta,e}-genericity is the hypothesis of A04, and the P_{6n-2} bound is what the propagation step consumes. Record both separately rather than as one 'generic enough' condition.

Keep the scope of the conclusion exact: detectability is a property of the constructed functor, so the statement is that M_infty CAN be taken detectable, not that every weak patching functor for r_p is.

items.name: Annihilator containment forces covering
items.statement: For a weak patching functor, a (3n-1)-deep sigma0 whose annihilator lies in the component prime p_sigma must cover sigma in the finite-group sense. Type annihilators and the component upper bound establish the implication.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.
proofSteps: Assume sigma_0 is (3n-1)-deep and Ann_{R_rho} M_infty(sigma_0) is contained in p_sigma(rho).
Choose a 2n-generic tame inertial L-parameter tau with sigma_0 in JH(sigma-bar(tau)); the depth hypothesis on sigma_0 is what makes such a tau available.

Apply Definition 6.2.1 to get the chain p_sigma(rho) contains Ann M_infty(sigma_0) contains Ann M_infty(sigma^circ(tau)) contains p_tau(rho) + (pi). The middle containment is the patching axiom; the outer one is the hypothesis.
Feed that chain into Remark 7.4.3(2), which yields sigma in JH(sigma-bar(tau)).

Conclude that sigma_0 covers sigma in the finite-group sense. Note what is used and what is not: the argument needs the type annihilators and the component upper bound, and it does not need rho to be generic.

items.name: Upper-alcove obvious weights occur for weak patching
items.statement: For P_{2eta,e}-generic tame rho and any weak patching functor for rho, every obvious weight in the highest p-restricted alcove has nonzero evaluation. Use a Hodge-2eta domain, maximal Cohen–Macaulay support and the covering criterion; this does not assert all obvious weights for an arbitrary weak functor without the propagation input.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.
proofSteps: Let rho be tame with a lowest alcove presentation (s, mu - eta) where mu is P_{2eta,e}-generic, and let M_infty be any weak patching functor for rho.
Choose tau tame with a lowest alcove presentation eta-compatible with that of rho and w-tilde(tau) = w-tilde(rho) t^{-eta - w_0 eta}.
Proposition 6.2.3 with Lemma 2.6.7 give M_infty(sigma^circ(eta,tau)) non-zero for any lattice sigma^circ(eta,tau) inside sigma-bar(eta,tau).

Compute the annihilator. tau has a lowest alcove presentation (s, mu - 2eta - w_0 eta) in which mu - eta - w_0 eta is P_{2eta,e}-generic up to X^0(T), so Ann_{R_rho} M_infty(sigma^circ(eta,tau)) = p_{eta,tau}(rho): here R_rho^{2eta,tau} is a domain by Theorem 7.3.2 and M_infty(sigma^circ(eta,tau)) is maximally Cohen-Macaulay over it by Definition 6.2.1(1).

Both M_infty(sigma^circ(eta,tau)) and R_rho^{2eta,tau} are O-flat, so the annihilator is p_{eta,tau}(rho) + (pi); by Theorem 7.4.2 it is contained in p_sigma(rho) for every sigma in JH(sigma-bar(eta,tau)), and hence for each such sigma some Serre weight sigma' has Ann M_infty(sigma') inside p_sigma(rho).

Now specialise to sigma in W_obv(rho) in the highest p-restricted alcove. Proposition 7.4.7(1) puts rho in C_sigma; A03 gives M_infty(sigma') non-zero for some sigma' covering sigma; Proposition 2.3.12(2) forces sigma' = sigma. That is the claim.
The alcove restriction is essential and should not be dropped: the last step uses that sigma sits in the highest p-restricted alcove.

items.name: Liftings, strict equivalence and abelianized determinant
items.statement: For a continuous residual representation into a split possibly disconnected reductive group, define A-valued liftings over complete Noetherian local O-algebras with residue F, strict conjugacy by the reduction kernel, deformation classes and composition to the abelianized group. These are prerequisites imported once from the deformation owner.
items.note: Route owner: GlobalGaloisDeformations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Local deformation problems are subfunctors of liftings, stable under strict equivalence.
Global deformations are strict-equivalence classes of liftings of type S.
Fixed-determinant problems use det r_A : Γ → G^ab(A).

api.name: Lifting.def
api.statement: For r̄ : Γ → G(F) and A ∈ C_O, an A-valued lifting is a continuous r_A : Γ → G(A) with r_A ≡ r̄ mod m_A.

api.name: Lifting.strictEquiv
api.statement: ker(G(A) → G(F)) acts on A-valued liftings by conjugation; deformations are the orbits.

api.name: Lifting.det
api.statement: det r_A : Γ → G^ab(A) is the composite with G → G^ab; it depends only on the deformation class.

api.name: Lifting.map
api.statement: A morphism A → B in C_O maps liftings to liftings and deformations to deformations, compatibly with det.

tests.name: Lifting.residue
tests.statement: For A = F the only lifting is r̄ itself.

tests.name: Lifting.GL1_dual_numbers
tests.statement: For G = GL₁ and A = F[ε], the liftings of χ̄ are χ̄·(1 + εc) with c ∈ Hom_cont(Γ, F), and strict equivalence is trivial because G is abelian.

tests.name: Lifting.strict_only
tests.statement: Equivalence uses only ker(G(A) → G(F)): conjugating by an element with nontrivial image in G(F) can give a lifting of a different residual representation, which is not a strict equivalence.

tests.name: Lifting.det_invariant
tests.statement: det(βr_Aβ⁻¹) = det r_A for β ∈ ker(G(A) → G(F)).

items.name: Polarized group G_n and multiplier
items.statement: G_n=(GL_n times GL_1) semidirect {1,j}, with j(g,a)j=(a transpose(g)^-1,a), multiplier nu(g,a)=a and nu(j)=-1. Import the abelianization description and the adjoint action used by the global deformation complex.
items.note: Actual representation carrier supplied by ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7; GlobalGaloisDeformations G7 imports it. The LLHLM abelianization claim is retained as a separate supplier obligation, not inferred from the semidirect-product formulas.

uses.how: Encodes pairings as actual G_n representations.
Defines the polarized adjoint action.
Fixes the value of the multiplier at complex conjugation.

api.name: PolarizedGroup.inl_mul
api.statement: The identity-component inclusion sends ((g,a),(h,b)) to (gh,ab).

api.name: PolarizedGroup.j_conj
api.statement: j(g,a)j⁻¹=(a g⁻ᵗ,a), and j²=1.

api.name: PolarizedGroup.multiplier_j
api.statement: ν(j)=−1 and ν(g,a)=a.

api.name: PolarizedGroup.scalar_conj_outside
api.statement: Conjugation of (A,b)j by (cI,1) gives (c²A,b)j.

api.name: PolarizedGroup.ad_j
api.statement: On gl_n, Ad(j)(X)=−Xᵗ; the GL_n action is ordinary conjugation.

tests.name: PolarizedGroup.rankOneInvolution
tests.statement: For n=1, j(g,a)j=(a/g,a); applying twice returns(g,a).

tests.name: PolarizedGroup.multiplierOutside
tests.statement: ν((A,b)j)=−b, including over F5.

tests.name: PolarizedGroup.scalarSquare
tests.statement: Over F7, conjugating(I,1)j by(2I,1) yields(4I,1)j, not(2I,1)j.

tests.name: PolarizedGroup.characteristicTwo
tests.statement: Over F2, ν(j)=1 although j is in the nonidentity component; ν alone does not detect the component.

tests.name: PolarizedGroup.adjoint_j
tests.statement: On Lie G_n = gl_n × gl_1, Ad(j)(X, b) = (bI − ᵗX, b), so the coordinate projection (X, b) ↦ X is not j-equivariant; ad r̄ lives on ker(dν) = gl_n × 0, where j acts by X ↦ −ᵗX (E42).

items.name: Local deformation problem
items.statement: A nonempty strict-conjugacy-invariant subfunctor of framed local liftings is a local deformation problem when it preserves the specified Artinian fiber products, inverse limits and descent along injective coefficient maps. It is represented by a quotient of the framed deformation ring.
items.note: Route owner: GlobalGaloisDeformations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Global data carry a local deformation problem at each place of S.
Taylor–Wiles conditions are local deformation problems ([78, Lemma 4.2]).
Theorem A.4.1 uses the local problems D_v^{λ_v,τ_v} at p.

api.name: LocalDefProblem.def
api.statement: A local deformation problem for ρ̄ is a nontrivial subfunctor D ⊆ D_ρ̄^□ such that D(R₁ ×_{R₀} R₂) is the equalizer of D(R₁) × D(R₂) ⇉ D(R₀) for surjections R₁, R₂ ↠ R₀, which is invariant under ker(G(A) → G(F))-conjugation, commutes with inverse limits, and satisfies r_A ∈ D(A) iff i_*(r_A) ∈ D(B) for injections i : A → B.

api.name: LocalDefProblem.represent
api.statement: Every local deformation problem is represented by a quotient R_ρ̄^D of R_ρ̄^□.

api.name: LocalDefProblem.locRing
api.statement: For local deformation problems D_v, v ∈ T, the completed tensor product R^loc_{S,T} := ⊗̂_{v∈T,O} R_v of their representing rings is the local base of the partially framed global ring (A10).

tests.name: LocalDefProblem.all
tests.statement: D_ρ̄^□ itself is a local deformation problem, represented by R_ρ̄^□.

tests.name: LocalDefProblem.unramified
tests.statement: For v ∤ p and unramified ρ̄, the unramified lifts form a local deformation problem.

tests.name: LocalDefProblem.not_invariant
tests.statement: The subfunctor of lifts taking a prescribed non-scalar value at a fixed Frobenius lift is not invariant under ker(G(A) → G(F))-conjugation, so it is not a local deformation problem.

tests.name: LocalDefProblem.quotient
tests.statement: R_ρ̄^□ → R_ρ̄^D is surjective, and D(A) = Hom(R_ρ̄^D, A).

items.name: Fixed-determinant local deformation quotients
items.statement: Fix a lift xi of the abelianized determinant. Define its framed quotient and then the maximal O-flat quotient. If the residual image lies in the identity component, projection to GL_n identifies the intended fixed-multiplier lifting problem with the GL_n problem; verify the paper's distinction between flat and unrestricted quotients before treating this as a literal ring identity.
items.note: Route owner: GlobalGaloisDeformations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Global data fix ξ and use the local problems D^{ξ_v}_{r̄_v}.
Theorem A.4.1 uses D_v^{ξ_v} away from p.
R^loc_{S,S} is built from these rings in §A.5.

api.name: FixedDet.def
api.statement: For a lift ξ : G_L → G_n^ab(O) of det ρ̄, D_ρ̄^{ξ,□}(A) := {ρ_A : det ρ_A = ξ}, represented by R_ρ̄^{ξ,□}; R_ρ̄^ξ is its maximal O-flat quotient.

api.name: FixedDet.GL_iso
api.statement: If ρ̄(G_L) ⊆ G_n⁰(F), then ρ_A ↦ ρ_A| (projection to GL_n) identifies the fixed-multiplier lifting problem with the GL_n lifting problem.

api.name: FixedDet.flat
api.statement: R_ρ̄^ξ := R_ρ̄^{ξ,□}/(ϖ^∞-torsion) is the maximal O-flat quotient; D_ρ̄^ξ is the local deformation problem it represents, kept distinct from D_ρ̄^{ξ,□}.

tests.name: FixedDet.condition
tests.statement: A lift has fixed determinant exactly when its composite with G_n → G_n^ab equals ξ.

tests.name: FixedDet.flat_quotient
tests.statement: R_ρ̄^{ξ,□} ↠ R_ρ̄^ξ is an isomorphism exactly when R_ρ̄^{ξ,□} has no ϖ-power torsion.

tests.name: FixedDet.split_place
tests.statement: At a place of F⁺ split in F, ρ̄ lands in G_n⁰ and the fixed-multiplier ring is the GL_n framed lifting ring of ρ̄|.

items.name: Polarized global deformation data
items.statement: A datum consists of F/F+, finite ramification set S, O, residual G_n-valued r inducing the quadratic component character, a fixed determinant lift xi and local deformation problems. Absolute irreducibility on G_F gives representability of global deformation classes and their local-condition quotient.
items.note: Route owner: GlobalGaloisDeformations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Partially framed rings are defined for a datum S.
Taylor–Wiles primes are chosen for a datum S (Proposition A.3.3).
Theorem A.4.1 produces representations of type S, S and S_Q.

api.name: GlobalDatum.def
api.statement: S = (F/F⁺, S, O, r̄, ξ, {D_v}_{v∈S}), with r̄ : G_{F⁺,S} → G_n(F) inducing G_{F⁺}/G_F ≅ G_n/G_n⁰, ξ a lift of det r̄, and D_v local deformation problems for r̄_v inside D^{ξ_v}_{r̄_v}.

api.name: GlobalDatum.type
api.statement: A lifting r_A is of type S iff det r_A = ξ and r_A|_{G_{F⁺_v}} ∈ D_v(A) for all v ∈ S; a deformation is of type S iff some (equivalently every) lifting in it is.

api.name: GlobalDatum.represent
api.statement: If r̄|_{G_F} is absolutely irreducible, deformations of type S are represented by R_S, and liftings of type S by R_S^□.

tests.name: GlobalDatum.any_lift
tests.statement: Being of type S is independent of the lifting chosen in a strict-equivalence class.

tests.name: GlobalDatum.irreducible_needed
tests.statement: Without absolute irreducibility of r̄|_{G_F}, the deformation functor of type S need not be representable.

tests.name: GlobalDatum.unrestricted
tests.statement: With D_v = D^{ξ_v,□}_{r̄_v} for every v ∈ S, R_S^□ = R_r̄^{□,ξ}: only the determinant condition remains.

items.name: Partially framed global deformation rings
items.statement: For T contained in S, introduce frames alpha_v reducing to identity and simultaneous strict equivalence. Construct the representing ring R_S^{square T}, its map from the completed tensor of local rings at T, and the power-series frame comparison after choosing a universal lifting. For a nonempty framing set and p>2 the polarized centralizer is trivial; avoid treating an unframed torsor as canonically trivial.
items.note: Route owner: GlobalGaloisDeformations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: The relative tangent space of R_S^T (Proposition A.3.2).
Generator bounds over R^loc_{S,T} (Proposition A.3.3).
R∞ maps onto R^S_{S_{Q_m}} (§A.5).

api.name: PartialFramed.def
api.statement: For T ⊆ S, a T-framed lifting is (r_A, (α_v)_{v∈T}) with α_v ∈ ker(GL_n(A) → GL_n(F)); equivalence is simultaneous conjugation β·(r_A, α_v) = (βr_Aβ⁻¹, βα_v); R_S^T represents T-framed deformations.

api.name: PartialFramed.localMap
api.statement: [(r_A, α_v)] ↦ (Ad(α_v⁻¹) r_A|_{G_{F⁺_v}})_v gives R^loc_{S,T} := ⊗̂_{v∈T,O} R_v → R_S^T.

api.name: PartialFramed.frameIso
api.statement: After choosing a universal lifting, R_S^T ≅ R_S ⊗̂_O O_T with O_T = O[[z_{v,i,j}]]_{v∈T, 1≤i,j≤n}; this uses p > 2 and absolute irreducibility, which make the centralizer of r̄ in ker(GL_n(A) → GL_n(F)) trivial.

api.name: PartialFramed.liftRing
api.statement: T-framed liftings are represented by R_{S,T} ≅ R_S^□ ⊗̂_O O_T.

tests.name: PartialFramed.empty
tests.statement: For T = ∅, R_S^∅ = R_S.

tests.name: PartialFramed.count
tests.statement: O_T is a power series ring in n²·#T variables.

tests.name: PartialFramed.noncanonical
tests.statement: The isomorphism R_S^T ≅ R_S ⊗̂_O O_T depends on the chosen universal lifting; it is not canonical.

items.name: Relative tangent and Selmer complexes
items.statement: Use the relative tangent m/(m^2+varpi A) for maps to F[epsilon]/epsilon^2. Form the global cochain cone with local subcomplexes C^0 and permitted local cocycles L_v at unframed places. The source's displayed tangent identification omits the relative base term and writes all 1-cochains where liftings give 1-cocycles; these are recorded in E22–E23 after image verification. The full Lie algebra of G_n has an additional multiplier summand; identify it with gl_n only for the fixed-multiplier problem.
items.note: Route owner: GlobalGaloisDeformations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Proposition A.3.2 identifies the relative tangent space with H¹_{S,T}.
Selmer and dual Selmer dimensions control the Taylor–Wiles count.
Trace evaluation kills the auxiliary dual Selmer group.

api.name: RelTangent.def
api.statement: For (A, m_A) ∈ C_O, the relative tangent space is Hom_F(m_A/(m_A² + ϖA), F), identified with Hom_{C_O}(A, F[ε]/ε²) (E22).

api.name: SelmerComplex.def
api.statement: C^i_{S,T}(G_{F⁺,S}, ad r̄) := C^i(G_{F⁺,S}, ad r̄) ⊕ ⊕_{v∈S} C^{i−1}(G_{F⁺_v}, ad r̄)/M_v^{i−1}, with M_v⁰ = C⁰ and M_v¹ = L_v for v ∈ S ∖ T and 0 otherwise; ∂(φ, (ψ_v)) = (∂φ, (φ|_{G_{F⁺_v}} − ∂ψ_v)).

api.name: SelmerComplex.H1
api.statement: H¹_{S,T}(G_{F⁺,S}, ad r̄) ≅ Hom_F(m_{R_S^T}/(m²_{R_S^T} + m_{R^loc_{S,T}}), F) (Proposition A.3.2).

api.name: LocalTangent.cocycles
api.statement: The tangent space of the framed local lifting ring is Z¹(G_{F⁺_v}, ad ρ̄), the 1-cocycles, not all 1-cochains (E23).

tests.name: RelTangent.E22
tests.statement: Hom_F(m_A/m_A², F) is not the relative tangent space when ϖ ∉ m_A²: the ϖA term must be quotiented.

tests.name: LocalTangent.E23
tests.statement: C¹(G, ad ρ̄) is too large: framed first-order liftings are exactly the 1-cocycles.

tests.name: SelmerComplex.T_eq_S
tests.statement: If T = S, no local conditions M_v are imposed and C_{S,S} is the cone of the restriction to all v ∈ S.

items.name: Relative framed tangent comparison
items.statement: The relative tangent space of R_S^{square T} over the tensor of local rings is naturally H^1 of the specified Selmer cone. Its displayed quotient includes the local base maximal ideal; keep this relative statement distinct from the incorrect preceding absolute-looking formula.
items.note: Route owner: GlobalGaloisDeformations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.
proofSteps: Fix the setup of A.3.1 and recall from A.3.3 that for (A, m_A) in C_O the reduced tangent space of A is Hom_O(m_A/m_A^2, F), identified with the morphisms A -> F[eps]/eps^2 in C_O.
For the framed local ring this gives the reduced tangent space of R_rho^square identified with BOTH D_rho^square(F[eps]/eps^2) and C^1(G_{F_v^+}, ad rho).
Globally, fix the G_n-deformation datum S = (F/F^+, S, O, r-bar, xi, {D_v}) and let L_v inside C^1(G_{F_v^+}, ad r-bar) be the subspace corresponding to D_v(F[eps]/eps^2).

For T a subset of S, define H^i_{S,T}(G_{F^+}, ad r-bar) as the cohomology of C^i_{S,T} = C^i(G_{F^+,S}, ad r-bar) + sum over v in S of C^{i-1}(G_{F_v^+}, ad r-bar)/M_v^{i-1}, with M_v^i = 0 unless v is in S minus T, and the stated exceptions at i = 0 and i = 1.
Identify the relative tangent space of R_S^{square T} over the tensor product of the local rings with H^1 of that Selmer complex.

Keep the statement RELATIVE. The displayed quotient includes the local base maximal ideal, so this is not the absolute tangent space of R_S^{square T}, and the two must not be substituted for one another downstream.

items.name: Taylor–Wiles local deformation condition
items.statement: At a split auxiliary place with norm 1 modulo p, choose a nonzero generalized Frobenius eigenspace on which Frobenius acts semisimply and its stable complement. Lift the complement unramified and require inertia on the selected summand to be scalar. This defines the auxiliary local deformation problem.
items.note: Route owner: GlobalGaloisDeformations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Taylor–Wiles data consist of such places and eigenspaces (Proposition A.3.3).
Scalar inertia characters on ψ_v give O[Δ_Q] → R_{S_Q}.
The diamond-level representation has type S_Q.

api.name: TWCondition.def
api.statement: For v split with Nv ≡ 1 mod p and ψ_v a nonzero generalized eigenspace of r̄(Frob_v) on which it acts semisimply, D_v(A) consists of liftings preserving a decomposition s_v ⊕ ψ_v lifting the residual one, with s_v unramified and inertia acting on ψ_v by scalars.

api.name: TWCondition.problem
api.statement: D_v is a local deformation problem ([78, Lemma 4.2]).

api.name: TWCondition.scalar_char
api.statement: The scalar inertia action on ψ_v gives a character k_v^× → R_{S_Q}^× factoring through k_v^×(p).

tests.name: TWCondition.whole_space
tests.statement: If ψ_v is the whole space (d_v = n), the condition says inertia acts by scalars.

tests.name: TWCondition.nonzero
tests.statement: ψ_v must be nonzero; the empty summand is excluded.

tests.name: TWCondition.semisimple
tests.statement: A generalized eigenspace on which r̄(Frob_v) is not semisimple cannot be chosen as ψ_v.

items.name: Adequate Taylor–Wiles prime supply
items.statement: Let p>2 and S=(F/F+,S,O,rbar,ξ,{D_v}) be the polarized global datum of Appendix A, with rbar|G_F absolutely irreducible. Require the G_n-version of adequacy for rbar(G_{F+(ζ_p)}) and ξ(c_v)=−1 at every infinite place. Let T⊂S and assume every v∈S\T splits in F. For every v∈S\T impose dim_F L_v−dim_F H^0(G_{F_v+},ad rbar)=[F_v+:Q_p]n(n−1)/2 if v|p, and 0 otherwise. Let q=max(dim_F H^1_{L^perp,T}(G_{F+,S},ad rbar(1)),q0), with q0≥0. For every N≥0 choose exactly q split primes Q disjoint from S, with Nv≡1 mod p^N and Nv≡1 mod p, and nonzero full generalized Frobenius eigenspaces ψ_v on which Frobenius acts semisimply, such that the augmented dual Selmer group is zero. For N=0 use the N=1 construction. The generator conclusion is A25.
items.note: Route owner: GlobalGaloisDeformations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.
items.proofOutline: Thorne Proposition 4.4 supplies primes at positive level; its Lemma 4.3 imposes the displayed local dimension formula only for v∈S\T. The odd multiplier kills the archimedean correction. Read the G_n adequacy definition, rather than substituting GL_n adequacy or enormous image. Distinct primes can be chosen by Chebotarev while successively killing trace evaluations on dual Selmer. If q exceeds the original dual Selmer dimension, add further eligible primes.

items.name: Diamond group and augmentation descent
items.statement: Define Delta_Q as the product of maximal p-quotients of residue-field units at Q. Scalar inertia characters give O[Delta_Q]->R_{S_Q}; quotient by its augmentation ideal recovers the original deformation ring, including the partially framed variant.
items.note: Route owner: GlobalGaloisDeformations. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Diamond modules are free over O[Δ_Q] (§A.4).
O_∞ maps onto O[Δ_{Q_m}] in the patching construction.
Diamond freeness and augmentation descent (Thorne Lemmas 6.3–6.4).

api.name: Diamond.group
api.statement: Δ_Q := ∏_{v∈Q} k_v^×(p), with k_v^×(p) the maximal p-quotient of k_v^×.

api.name: Diamond.map
api.statement: The scalar inertia characters give O[Δ_Q] → R_{S_Q}, and O[Δ_Q] → R_{S_Q}^T.

api.name: Diamond.descent
api.statement: R_{S_Q}/a_Q ≅ R_S and R_{S_Q}^T/a_Q ≅ R_S^T, with a_Q the augmentation ideal of O[Δ_Q].

tests.name: Diamond.empty
tests.statement: For Q = ∅, Δ_Q = 1 and R_{S_Q} = R_S.

tests.name: Diamond.cyclic
tests.statement: If Nv − 1 = p^N·u with p ∤ u, then k_v^×(p) ≅ Z/p^N.

tests.name: Diamond.augmentation
tests.statement: The descent is by the augmentation ideal a_Q, not by the ideal generated by p.

items.name: Auxiliary parahoric levels
items.statement: From the selected eigenspace dimensions form the block parahoric levels U_0(Q), their determinant-kernel levels U_1(Q), and the quotient U_0(Q)/U_1(Q)=Delta_Q. Preserve the chosen split-place identifications and original arbitrary away-from-p level.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Theorem A.4.1 is stated at levels U, U_0(Q) and U_1(Q).
Taylor–Wiles projectors act on S(U_i(Q), W).
Finite patching modules use level K_pU_1(Q_m)^{S_p}.

api.name: AuxLevel.parahoric
api.statement: For v ∈ Q with d_v = dim ψ_v, p_v ⊆ GL_n(O_{F⁺_v}) is the block upper-triangular parahoric of type (n − d_v) + d_v, and p_{v,1} := ker(p_v → GL_{d_v}(k_v) →det k_v^× → k_v^×(p)).

api.name: AuxLevel.U
api.statement: U_0(Q) := (∏_{v∈Q} ι_v⁻¹(p_v))·U^Q and U_1(Q) := (∏_{v∈Q} ι_v⁻¹(p_{v,1}))·U^Q, keeping the original level away from Q.

tests.name: AuxLevel.full
tests.statement: If d_v = n, then p_v = GL_n(O_{F⁺_v}) and p_{v,1} is the kernel of det onto k_v^×(p).

tests.name: AuxLevel.GL2
tests.statement: For n = 2 and d_v = 1, p_v is the Iwahori subgroup (upper triangular mod v), and p_v/p_{v,1} ≅ k_v^×(p) via the lower-right diagonal entry.

tests.name: AuxLevel.delta
tests.statement: The quotient U_0(Q)/U_1(Q) is identified with the diamond group Δ_Q of §A.3.4.

items.name: Local-global compatibility at original level
items.statement: Assume the Appendix A.4 setting: p>2, F/F+ CM with F+≠Q, all p-adic places split, a unitary group definite at infinity with the chosen integral model away from N, a sufficiently small compact open U, and S containing the p-adic places, primes dividing N and all non-hyperspecial places of U. Fix a dominant algebraic weight λ, WD inertial types τ_v, a stable O-lattice W in ⊗_{v|p}σ(λ_v,τ_v)^*◦ι_v, and the nonzero localized residual Hecke eigensystem with absolutely irreducible rbar|G_F from the Appendix A setup. Fix a Taylor–Wiles datum Q disjoint from S and the associated ideal m_Q away from S∪Q. Put ξ=ε^(1−n)δ_(F/F+)^n. At p use Hodge weights λ_v+η and WD monodromy dominated by τ_v, as required by E33–E34. At original level there is a polarized representation r(U,W)_mQ:G_{F+,S}→G_n(T_Q(U,W)_mQ), characterized up to strict equivalence by the Hecke polynomials. For each allowed split w away from S∪Q, det(1−r|G_F(Frob_w)X)=Σ_{j=0}^n(−1)^j(Nw)^(j(j−1)/2)α_level(T_w^(j))X^j. It has multiplier ξ, the corrected p-adic local conditions above and the O-flat fixed-multiplier conditions at S\S_p. In particular it is unramified at Q.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.
proofSteps: Assume the full A.4 setting: p > 2, F/F^+ CM with F^+ not Q, every p-adic place split, a unitary group definite at infinity with the chosen integral model away from N, U sufficiently small, and S containing the p-adic places, the places dividing N and every place where U is not unramified.

Fix xi = epsilon^{1-n} delta_{F/F^+}^n and a dominant weight lambda, and for each v in S_p an n-dimensional Weil-Deligne inertial type tau_v; let W be the U-lattice in the tensor over v in S_p of sigma(lambda_v, tau_v)^* with sigma(tau_v) as in Theorem 2.5.4, and take D_v = D_{r-bar_v}^{lambda_v, tau_v}.
Produce the maximal ideal m_Q in T^{P_{S minus Q}} and the map alpha: T^{P_{S minus Q}} -> T^Q(U,W)_{m_Q}.

Construct r(U,W): G_{F^+,S} -> G_n(T^Q(U,W)_{m_Q}) and pin it down by the characteristic-polynomial identity det(1 - r(U,W)|_{G_F}(Frob_w) X) = sum_j (-1)^j N_{F/Q}(w)^{2j} alpha(T_w^{(j)}) X^j for all w in P_{S minus Q}. Uniqueness is part of the statement and comes from that identity holding for all such w.
Record the type: S = (F/F^+, S, O, r-bar, xi, {D_v}_{v in S_p} union {D_v^{xi_v}}_{v in S minus S_p}). This is the ORIGINAL level, so the type's place set is S and carries no local problem at Q.
Do not merge this with A28 and A29. The three conclusions differ precisely in level and in the type's place set, and the diamond case A29 enlarges S to S union Q.

items.name: Taylor–Wiles projectors and free diamond modules
items.statement: At the Taylor–Wiles levels of A16, put H_i=pr(S(U_i(Q),W)_mQ) with the commuting spectral selection operators of A31–A32 and let T_i^pr be the Hecke image on H_i. Then H_1 is finite free over O[Δ_Q], H_0 identifies with H_1[a_Q] by inclusion, and trace identifies H_1/a_QH_1 with H_0. The map pr from original-level forms to H_0 is an isomorphism. The universal scalar-inertia deformation ring acts through T_1^pr. The polynomial operator pr need not be an idempotent or act as identity on the natural inclusion of original-level vectors.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Forms finite diamond-level patching modules with the correct Galois action.
Names the image Hecke algebras on which auxiliary local conditions hold.
Supplies finite free modules and augmentation comparison for patching.

api.name: AuxiliaryProjector.image
api.statement: Define H_i and the Hecke image T_i^pr; export the commuting diamond and Hecke actions.

api.name: AuxiliaryProjector.originalEquiv
api.statement: The operator pr, composed with level inclusion, is the isomorphism from original-level localized forms onto H_0.

api.name: AuxiliaryProjector.spectralSummand
api.statement: Show the image is the Hensel-selected generalized eigensummand, with the polynomial operator invertible there. Normalize to an idempotent only by a proved construction.

api.name: AuxiliaryProjector.diamondFree
api.statement: H_1 is finite free over O[Δ_Q]; distinguish the invariant inclusion from the trace map on coinvariants.

api.name: AuxiliaryProjector.localGalois
api.statement: The Galois action over T_1^pr has the selected scalar inertia character, identified with the diamond operator.

tests.name: AuxiliaryProjector.emptyPrimes
tests.statement: For Q empty, the product operator is identity, Δ_Q is trivial and all levels coincide.

tests.name: AuxiliaryProjector.nonIdempotent
