tests.statement: On Z_5^2 let T=diag(3,2), select the eigenvalue2 and take Q(X)=X−3. Then Q(T)=diag(0,−1), whose image is the selected eigenspace although its square differs from itself.

tests.name: AuxiliaryProjector.inclusionDifferent
tests.statement: If a spherical vector decomposes into several parahoric Hecke eigenlines, applying pr selects its component; its raw included line need not equal the selected eigenspace.

tests.name: AuxiliaryProjector.traceCoinvariants
tests.statement: For O[Δ] the invariant module is O times Σδ, and trace sends the coinvariant class of1 to Σδ. This is an isomorphism even when p divides |Δ|.

tests.name: AuxiliaryProjector.fixedRingBoundary
tests.statement: A Q-local scalar inertia character may be nontrivial on H_1; it becomes trivial after augmentation. It must not be forced trivial before passing to that quotient.

items.name: Finite patching modules and coefficient power series
items.statement: Define the projected Pontryagin-dual finite modules M_{m,K_p,r}, then adjoin S-frames and quotient augmentation powers to obtain M^square. Choose generators of each auxiliary Delta and maps O[[y_1,...,y_q]] to its group ring. S_infty combines these diamond variables with the frame variables, with fixed augmentation quotient.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: The ultraproduct patches these finite modules.
R∞ acts through the finite-level rings.
The patching functor is defined on M∞.

api.name: PatchModule.finite
api.statement: M_{m,K_p,r} := pr(S(K_pU_1(Q_m)^{S_p}, W/ϖ^r)_{m_{Q_m}})^∨ / a^r_{Q_m}, with (−)^∨ the Pontryagin dual.

api.name: PatchModule.framed
api.statement: M^□_{m,K_p,r} := M_{m,K_p,r} ⊗_{R_{S_{Q_m}}} R^S_{S_{Q_m}}/a_S^r, with a_S the augmentation ideal of the frame ring O_S.

api.name: PatchModule.Sinf
api.statement: O_∞ := O[[y_1, …, y_q]] maps onto O[Δ_{Q_m}] by y_i ↦ [g_i] − 1 for chosen generators g_i; S_∞ := O_∞ ⊗̂_O O_S with augmentation ideal a_∞.

tests.name: PatchModule.q0
tests.statement: If q = 0 (Q_m = ∅), then O_∞ = O and Δ_{Q_m} = 1.

tests.name: PatchModule.surj
tests.statement: O_∞ → O[Δ_{Q_m}] is surjective, because each factor k_v^×(p) is cyclic and generated by g_i.

tests.name: PatchModule.projected
tests.statement: The module uses the projected space pr(S(…)), not the full auxiliary space; the projector restriction is essential (E38, A30).

items.name: Ultrafilter patched module
items.statement: Choose a nonprincipal ultrafilter on the auxiliary levels. The localized product of O modulo varpi^r has completion O; use this to form the inverse limit of the tensor of products of finite patching modules. Its augmentation quotient is completed localized automorphic forms. This choice-dependent construction must precede any later independence theorem.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Projectivity and regular sequences of M∞.
R∞ acts on M∞ through the ultraproduct of finite-level rings.
M∞(−) is defined from M∞.

api.name: Ultrapatch.ring
api.statement: For a non-principal ultrafilter F on N, R := ∏_{m∈N} O, and S_F ⊂ R the multiplicative set of idempotents e_I with I ∈ F, the diagonal gives O ≅ lim_r S_F⁻¹R/(ϖ^r).

api.name: Ultrapatch.aug
api.statement: M∞/a∞ ≅ lim_{K_p,r} S(K_pU^{S_p}, W/ϖ^r)^∨_m (A.4).

api.name: Ultrapatch.choice
api.statement: The construction depends on the ultrafilter and on the chosen data at each level; independence statements come later.

tests.name: Ultrapatch.principal
tests.statement: A principal ultrafilter would select a single level m and patch nothing.

tests.name: Ultrapatch.O
tests.statement: O ⊗_R ∏_m O/ϖ^r ≅ O/ϖ^r for every r, via the ultrafilter.

tests.name: Ultrapatch.completed_forms
tests.statement: Modulo a∞, M∞ recovers the dual of the completed localized automorphic forms (A.4).

items.name: Projectivity and regular sequence of the patched module
items.statement: The diamond and frame variables form an M_infty-regular sequence. The augmentation quotient is projective over O[[G_0(Z_p)]], giving maximal Cohen–Macaulayness and, by [82, Theorem6.2], finite projectivity over S_infty[[G_0(Z_p)]]. No generic rank-one conclusion follows here.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.
proofSteps: Show first that (y_1,...,y_q, z_1,...,z_{n^2 #S}) is an M_infty-regular sequence, where (z_1,...,z_{n^2 #S}) is any O-regular sequence. These are the diamond and framing variables.

Use that G(O_S)U_S^p is sufficiently small to get that lim over K_p inside U_p and r of S(K_p U_S^p, W/pi^r)^dual is a FINITE FREE O[[G(Z_p)]]-module. Sufficient smallness is doing real work here and should be carried as a hypothesis.
By (A.4) the quotient M_infty/a_infty is then a finitely generated projective, hence finitely generated maximal Cohen-Macaulay, O[[G_0(Z_p)]]-module.

Lift that along the regular sequence: M_infty is a finitely generated maximal Cohen-Macaulay S_infty[[G_0(Z_p)]]-module, and by [82, Theorem 6.2] a finitely generated PROJECTIVE S_infty[[G_0(Z_p)]]-module.

For the framing, set R_infty = R_{S,S}^{loc}[[x_1,...,x_g]] with g = q - [F:Q]n(n-1)/2, choose for each m a surjection R_infty ->> R_{S_{Q_m}}^{square S} by Proposition A.3.3, and assemble the surjective map R_infty -> product_m R_{S_{Q_m}}^{square S} ->> O tensor-hat product_m R_{S_{Q_m}}^{square S}.

Record that the S_infty-action on M_infty factors through that quotient as in A.4, and that the lift of S_infty into the product exists by formal smoothness of S_infty. Both are used and neither is automatic.

items.name: Patched deformation ring and its actions
items.statement: Form R_infty=R_loc[[x_1,...,x_g]] with g given by the Taylor–Wiles generator bound, choose maps to finite-level framed rings, and obtain its action on M_infty. Formal smoothness lifts the S_infty-action. The printed g uses [F:Q] where PropositionA.3.3 gives [F+:Q]; use the corrected degree [F+:Q] as recorded in E24.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: M∞(−) takes values in R∞-modules.
Support and maximal Cohen–Macaulay properties over R∞(λ,τ).
R∞ has the shape R_ρ ⊗̂ R^p of §6.2.

api.name: PatchedDefRing.def
api.statement: R∞ := R^loc_{S,S}[[x_1, …, x_g]] with g = q − [F⁺:Q]·n(n−1)/2 (E24; the paper prints [F:Q]).

api.name: PatchedDefRing.surj
api.statement: Proposition A.3.3 gives surjections R∞ ↠ R^S_{S_{Q_m}} for each m, hence R∞ → O ⊗_R ∏_m R^S_{S_{Q_m}} acting on M∞.

api.name: PatchedDefRing.Sinf_lift
api.statement: S∞ is formally smooth over O, so its action lifts to a map S∞ → R∞ compatible with the action on M∞.

api.name: PatchedDefRing.shape
api.statement: R∞ ≅ R_{r̄_p} ⊗̂_O R^p with R^p := (⊗̂_{v∈S∖S_p,O} R_v^{ξ_v})[[x_1, …, x_g]], equidimensional ([5, Theorem 3.3.3], [12, Theorem 1]).

tests.name: PatchedDefRing.GL2
tests.statement: For n = 2 and [F⁺:Q] = d, g = q − d.

tests.name: PatchedDefRing.E24
tests.statement: Using the printed [F:Q] = 2[F⁺:Q] would give g = q − [F:Q]n(n−1)/2, which does not match the generator bound of Proposition A.3.3 for T = S.

tests.name: PatchedDefRing.no_vars
tests.statement: If q = [F⁺:Q]·n(n−1)/2, then R∞ = R^loc_{S,S}.

items.name: Exact covariant patching functor
items.statement: Set M_infty(W)=Hom_cont,O[[G_0(Z_p)]](M_infty,W^vee)^vee. Projectivity makes it exact and covariant on finite coefficient modules, with finite R_infty- and S_infty-values. For a Serre weight its augmentation quotient identifies with the dual localized automorphic space of dual coefficients.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Lemma A.1.1(1): M∞(σ) ≠ 0 iff σ ∈ W(r̄).
M∞(σ°(λ,τ)) is maximal Cohen–Macaulay over R∞(λ,⪯τ).
It is the weak patching functor of Definition 6.2.1.

api.name: PatchFunctor.def
api.statement: M∞(W) := Hom^cont_{O[[G_0(Z_p)]]}(M∞, W^∨)^∨ for finite O[G_0(Z_p)]-modules W.

api.name: PatchFunctor.exact
api.statement: M∞ is projective over S∞[[G_0(Z_p)]] ([82, Theorem 6.2]), so M∞(−) is exact and covariant, with values finitely generated over S∞ and R∞.

api.name: PatchFunctor.aug
api.statement: M∞(σ)/a∞ ≅ S(G(O_p)U^{S_p}, σ^∨)^∨_m for a Serre weight σ.

api.name: PatchFunctor.nonzero_iff
api.statement: By Nakayama, M∞(σ) ≠ 0 iff σ ∈ W(r̄) (Lemma A.1.1(1)).

tests.name: PatchFunctor.modular
tests.statement: For a Serre weight σ, M∞(σ) ≠ 0 exactly when σ is a modular weight of r̄.

tests.name: PatchFunctor.induced
tests.statement: M∞(Ind_{U_{S_p}}^{G_0(Z_p)} F)/a∞ ≅ S(U, F)^∨_m ≠ 0, so the functor is nonzero.

items.name: Support and maximal Cohen–Macaulay properties
items.statement: Local-global compatibility forces type evaluations to factor through the appropriate ordered semistable quotient. Dimension equality gives maximal Cohen–Macaulayness there and, for weight constituents, on its special fiber. Nakayama identifies nonzero patched weight values with modular weights. The away-from-p tensor is equidimensional by [5]/[12], and is not asserted formally smooth for arbitrary level.
items.note: Route owner: CompletedCohomologyAndLocalGlobalCompatibilityPartIIPatchedGLdDensity. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.
proofSteps: Start from local-global compatibility (A17, A28, A29) and conclude that type evaluations of M_infty factor through the appropriate ordered semistable quotient of the framed deformation ring.
Compare dimensions: equality of the dimension of that quotient with the dimension of the support gives maximal Cohen-Macaulayness of the evaluation over it.
Repeat the dimension comparison for the weight constituents on the special fibre, which is where the Serre-weight statements are read off.
Apply Nakayama to descend the conclusion from the special fibre to the module itself, using the finite generation supplied by A21.
Keep the two Cohen-Macaulay claims apart: one is over the semistable quotient in mixed characteristic, the other on its special fibre, and they are established by separate dimension counts.

items.name: Explicit rank-three monodromy chart
items.statement: For n=3, singleton J, lambda=(3,1,0), z=(23)t_(2,1,1), write the universal determinant-bounded chart matrix and impose det(A)=-(v-t)^4, minor divisibility and reduced closure. Central translation reduces the monodromy parameter to (a,b,0).
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Eliminate six matrix coefficients over the explicit genericity locus and compute special-fibre primes and the Jacobian ideal.
Base change at t=-p and compare with the explicit partial normalization.

api.name: RankThreeMonodromyChart.determinant_bound
api.statement: Impose equality det(A)=-(v-t)^4 as a polynomial identity, hence coefficient equations, in the determinant-bounded chart.

api.name: RankThreeMonodromyChart.Schubert_bound
api.statement: Impose the lambda minor-divisibility conditions in v-t and then take the underlying reduced subscheme as in the source Schubert construction. Keep this reduction separate from the later scheme-theoretic special fibre.

api.name: RankThreeMonodromyChart.central_parameter
api.statement: Use the central-shift invariance of the differential condition to write the parameter tuple as (a,b,0); this normalization applies to the monodromy parameter, not to an arbitrary change of Hodge type.

api.name: RankThreeMonodromyChart.monodromy_closure
api.statement: Define the flat monodromy chart by intersecting the universal flat model with this open chart, over the coefficient locus V when using PropositionB.0.1.

api.name: RankThreeMonodromyChart.elimination_interface
api.statement: Identify the chart over V with the three-equation algebra recorded in sourceData.appendixB.chartEquations through the source elimination of c11,d11,c21,c23,c31,c33. Preserve its required t-torsion-freeness and the invertibility of P.

tests.name: RankThreeMonodromyChart.distinguished_special_point
tests.statement: At t=0 and all twelve variable coefficients zero, A has rows (v^2,0,0),(0,0,v),(0,v,0); its determinant is -v^4 and it is the chosen monomial point z.

tests.name: RankThreeMonodromyChart.determinant_sign
tests.statement: The permutation (23) has sign -1. Imposing +(v-t)^4 rejects the distinguished special point in characteristic different from 2.

tests.name: RankThreeMonodromyChart.zero_coefficients_not_generic_section
tests.statement: With all twelve coefficients zero at general t, det(A)=-v(v-t)^3, not -(v-t)^4. The special-fibre fixed point does not define the constant-coefficient generic section.

items.name: Explicit open genericity locus
items.statement: Use V=Spec Z[a,b,1/P] with P=7! b(b-1)(a-1)(a-2)(a-b)(a-b-1)(a-b-2). Invert all these factors before eliminating variables or asserting normality; the coefficient prime therefore exceeds 7.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Make the elimination denominators and the normalization leading coefficient units before specializing.

api.name: ExplicitGenericityOpen.polynomial
api.statement: Set P=7!*b*(b-1)*(a-1)*(a-2)*(a-b)*(a-b-1)*(a-b-2) in Z[a,b], with every factor and its multiplicity as printed.

api.name: ExplicitGenericityOpen.localization
api.statement: Define V=Spec Z[a,b,1/P] and its open immersion into A^2_Z by the localization universal property.

api.name: ExplicitGenericityOpen.points
api.statement: A ring map Z[a,b,1/P]→R is a pair (a_R,b_R) for which P(a_R,b_R) is a unit. Over a general ring nonzero is insufficient.

api.name: ExplicitGenericityOpen.factor_units
api.statement: Invertibility of P is equivalent to invertibility of every displayed factor, including 7!, in the commutative target ring.

api.name: ExplicitGenericityOpen.DVR_specialization
api.statement: For a coefficient DVR, the pair lies in V exactly when P has nonzero residue. In mixed characteristic this requires residue characteristic p>7 and avoidance of each displayed hyperplane modulo p.

api.name: ExplicitGenericityOpen.base_change
api.statement: Every coefficient map preserving the chosen pair transports its unit witnesses, giving the canonical base change of all chart algebras over V.

tests.name: ExplicitGenericityOpen.F11_point
tests.statement: Over F_11, (a,b)=(5,2) belongs to V: 7!,2,1,4,3,3,2,1 are all nonzero.

tests.name: ExplicitGenericityOpen.small_prime_excluded
tests.statement: There are no F_7-points of V because 7!=0; checking only the linear factors misses this exclusion.

tests.name: ExplicitGenericityOpen.nonzero_not_unit
tests.statement: At integer values (a,b)=(5,2), P is nonzero in Z but not a unit. This pair does not define a Z-point of V.

items.name: Three equations for the explicit chart
items.statement: On V the rank-three chart is presented by the three displayed polynomials in t,a,b,c12,c13,d21,c22,d31,d33, eliminating the other six chart coefficients using monodromy and t-torsion-freeness. The exact three equations are in sourceData.appendixB.chartEquations. Rational-function-field consistency checks are recorded in validation; a uniform localized-integer certificate is a remaining blueprint proof obligation.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.
proofSteps: Start from the universal determinant-bounded matrix A of Proposition 3.2.8 and the presentation of U(z~)^{det,<=0} as Z[t,c11,d11,c12,c13,c21,d21,c22,c23,d31,c31,c33,d33] modulo det A = -(v-t)^4.
Work over V = Spec Z[a,b][1/P] with the simplified monodromy condition of Remark 3.3.2, the third monodromy coordinate being 0.

The monodromy equations solve the six coefficients c11, d11, c21, c23, c31, c33 in terms of t, c12, c13, d21, c22, d31, d33. Both stated hypotheses are used and neither is decorative: t-torsion-freeness of the ring of functions, and invertibility of P(a,b).

Conclude only that U(z~,lambda,grad) x V is a CLOSED subscheme of Spec R, and that after inverting t it is all of Spec R[1/t]. Equality on the nose is not available here; it comes from the density argument in Q05.

Blueprint obligation: the source states the elimination without displaying the six solved expressions. Supply them together with a uniform localized-integer certificate over Z[a,b][1/P]. A consistency check in the rational function field is not a substitute, since it cannot see the denominator locus.

items.name: Seven special-fiber components
items.statement: On t=0 the chart has the seven component ideals listed in sourceData.appendixB.specialFiberMinimalPrimes. Keep scheme multiplicities distinct from the list of minimal primes; this is not a claim that the original special fiber is reduced.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.
proofSteps: Take the seven ideals recorded in sourceData.appendixB.specialFiberMinimalPrimes and verify each is prime in R/t.
Verify that they are exactly the minimal primes of Spec R/t, so that no component is missing from the list.
Record the consequence that is actually consumed downstream: each fibre of Spec R/t over Spec Z[t,a,b][1/P] has codimension three. Q05 uses this number, not the individual ideals.

Do not upgrade this to a statement about the special fibre as a scheme. These are minimal primes only: no multiplicity is computed and no reducedness is claimed. Reducedness appears later and only after normalization, in Q08.

items.name: Complete intersection and flatness of the explicit chart
items.statement: On V the presented chart is an irreducible complete intersection flat over X times V. Fiber codimension three and the regular domain generic fiber identify the presentation with the flat closure.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.
proofSteps: Match the codimension-three count of Q04 against the three equations of Q03; by Stacks Tag 00R4 this makes R a complete intersection.
Obtain that Spec R[1/t] is a regular domain, using the corresponding fact for U(z~,lambda,grad) x_{X x A^2} X^0 x V from Proposition 3.3.4.
Use that t is a regular element of R, which the complete-intersection property supplies, to conclude that Spec R[1/t] is dense in Spec R.

Combine density with the closed immersion of Q03: a closed subscheme containing a dense open subscheme of a reduced ambient scheme is everything, so U(z~,lambda,grad) x V = Spec R, and flatness over V follows.
Keep the scope straight: irreducibility is asserted for the chart over V, not for its special fibre, whose seven components are Q04.

items.name: Effective Elkik Jacobian bound
items.statement: The ideal of 3-by-3 minors of the relative Jacobian of the three-equation presentation contains t^3. The source cites a Macaulay2 computation without a displayed certificate; this needs an independently reproducible polynomial certificate or explicit outstanding proof leaf, not a claimed verified computation.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.
proofSteps: Fix H as the ideal of 3x3 minors of the Jacobian of the three-equation presentation of Q03, taken relative to Z[t,a,b][1/P].
Record the source's justification verbatim and without softening it: Proposition B.0.1(4) is proved by 'a computation in Macaulay 2', and no certificate is displayed in the paper.

Blueprint obligation, and this is the substance of the item: exhibit 3x3 minors m_i of that Jacobian and polynomials h_i over Z[t,a,b][1/P] with t^3 = sum h_i m_i, uniformly in (a,b), and name the exceptional denominator locus on which the certificate degenerates.

Do not treat the machine claim as discharged. The exponent r = 3 is consumed by Proposition 3.3.9 and by Q11's depth bound, so an unsupported exponent propagates into the depth-ten hypothesis rather than staying local to this item.

items.name: Partial normalization by an explicit fraction
items.statement: Adjoin W=-t d21/c22 in the fraction field of the chart. The seven displayed relations define the proposed finite birational partial normalization. All statements here are after base change to V, as required by the proposition. The exact seven relations are in sourceData.appendixB.partialNormalizationEquations.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

uses.how: Obtain the normalization after t=-p specialization and compute component splitting in Table1.

api.name: ExplicitPartialNormalization.fraction_subalgebra
api.statement: Over V and the integral chart algebra R of Q03, let W=-t*d21/c22 in Frac(R), and form the R-subalgebra generated by W. Require the proved domain and nonzero-denominator hypotheses.

api.name: ExplicitPartialNormalization.presentation
api.statement: Compare this subalgebra with the seven-equation quotient recorded in sourceData.appendixB.partialNormalizationEquations. Proving equality includes ruling out extra c22-torsion in the presented algebra; the rational substitution alone proves only one direction.

api.name: ExplicitPartialNormalization.integrality
api.statement: The sixth displayed equation is quadratic in W with leading coefficient (a-1)(b-1)(a-b), a unit on V. Divide by that unit to obtain a monic relation and deduce finiteness of the generated subalgebra over R.

api.name: ExplicitPartialNormalization.birational
api.statement: After inverting c22, the first relation uniquely gives W=-t*d21/c22 and the map is an isomorphism. Together with the subalgebra realization this identifies fraction fields.

api.name: ExplicitPartialNormalization.normalization_after_specialization
api.statement: Use PropositionB.0.2 for O-points (t,a,b)=(-p,a,b) in X×V to conclude O-flatness and normality of the specialized algebra. Do not extend this normality claim to coefficient points outside V.

api.name: ExplicitPartialNormalization.special_fiber_components
api.statement: Use the complete Table1 primary/component data already transcribed to describe preimages of the seven special-fibre components, retaining all splitting branches and their equations.

tests.name: ExplicitPartialNormalization.denominator_open
tests.statement: On c22 invertible, the first relation eliminates W and the inverse map is the rational formula -t*d21/c22.

tests.name: ExplicitPartialNormalization.origin_fiber_nonreduced
tests.statement: Over F_11 at (a,b)=(5,2), set t=c12=c13=d21=c22=d31=d33=0. The seven relations reduce to W^2=0 up to a unit, so the fibre of the finite map is F_11[W]/(W^2), not a single reduced point.

tests.name: ExplicitPartialNormalization.boundary_not_fraction_evaluation
tests.statement: At c22=0 the subalgebra morphism still has a fibre, but evaluating the rational expression by division is undefined. The finite-algebra presentation is required there.

items.name: O-flatness of the specialized explicit chart
items.statement: Proposition B.0.2(1). Suppose we are given s : Spec O → X × V ⊂ X × A^2, corresponding to (−p, a, b) ∈ O^3. Then the base change U(z̃, λ, ∇_{(a,b,0)}) = U(z̃, λ, ∇) ×_{X×A^2,s} Spec O is O-flat. Here V = Spec Z[a,b][1/P(a,b)] ⊂ A^2 with P(a,b) = 7! b(b−1)(a−1)(a−2)(a−b)(a−b−1)(a−b−2), and U(z̃, λ, ∇) = (U(z̃) × A^2) ∩ M_X(λ, ∇) is the open affine of the simplified universal local model of Appendix B (PDF202). Proof (PDF204): immediate from Proposition B.0.1(3) (Q05).
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.
proofSteps: Part (1) is immediate from Q05 (Proposition B.0.1(3): U(z̃,λ,∇) ×_{A^2} V → X × V is flat) by base change along s : Spec O → X × V, the point (−p,a,b). No new input is needed.

items.name: Normality of the specialized partial normalization
items.statement: Proposition B.0.2(2). Suppose we are given s : Spec O → X × V ⊂ X × A^2, corresponding to (−p, a, b) ∈ O^3. Then the base change U(z̃, λ, ∇_{(a,b,0)})^nm = U(z̃, λ, ∇)^nm ×_{X×A^2,s} Spec O is O-flat and normal. In particular, the base changed map U(z̃, λ, ∇_{(a,b,0)})^nm → U(z̃, λ, ∇_{(a,b,0)}) is the normalization map. Here U(z̃, λ, ∇)^nm is the spectrum of the quotient of Z[t,a,b,W,c12,c13,d21,c22,d31,d33] (over V) by the ideal Ĩ generated by the seven polynomials on PDF204. It is finite and birational over U(z̃, λ, ∇), with W = −t d21/c22 (Q07).
items.note: Split from Q08. Proof as printed. (i) Let I be the image of Ĩ in F[W,c12,c13,d21,c22,d31,d33]. Since 7! b(b−1)(a−1)(a−2)(a−b)(a−b−1)(a−b−2) ∈ F^×, Buchberger's algorithm for W > c12 > c13 > d21 > c22 > d31 > d33 gives the printed Gröbner basis; the exception for the 8th generator is misprinted (E25). (ii) Macaulay2 shows that the leading-term monomial scheme is Cohen–Macaulay, so by flat Gröbner degeneration the special fibre U(z̃,λ,∇_{(a,b,0)})^nm_F is Cohen–Macaulay. (iii) Its seven listed components show by inspection that it is generically reduced; with S1 it is reduced. (iv) The proof asserts that U^nm is topologically flat over O, without argument (S5 source issue). A ϖ-power-torsion global function not divisible by ϖ would then be nilpotent and reduce to a nonzero nilpotent on the reduced special fibre, so U^nm is O-flat. (v) O-flat with reduced special fibre gives normality by [69, Proposition 8.2] (Pappas–Zhu); that criterion also needs a normal generic fibre (same source issue). Blueprint obligation, carried over from Q08: the Gröbner basis is computed with (a,b) specialized into a field, so it certifies one fibre, not the family. Supply a parametric Gröbner system over Z[a,b][1/P] with its exceptional locus explicit, or check Serre's R1 and S2 directly. apply.py copies neither proofSteps nor prerequisites for new items, so copy the two fields given here by hand.

uses.how: Corollary B.0.4 proof, PDF208: "π is the normalization map by Proposition B.0.2(2)".
Remark B.0.6, PDF209: taking products preserves reducedness of the special fibres, so the product of the U^nm is the normalization of the product.

proofSteps: For part (2), take the image I of the base-changed ideal in F[W,c12,c13,d21,c22,d31,d33], using that P(a,b) is a unit in F.
Run Buchberger's algorithm for the monomial order W > c12 > c13 > d21 > c22 > d31 > d33; the Groebner basis printed at PDF 205 is what the rest of the argument consumes.

Read Cohen-Macaulayness off the leading ideal, list the special-fibre components of the normalization, and observe by inspection that the special fibre is generically reduced. Generically reduced together with S1, which Cohen-Macaulayness supplies, gives reduced.

For O-flatness argue by contradiction from topological flatness: a global function not divisible by pi but with pi-power torsion would be nilpotent, and reducing mod pi would produce a non-zero nilpotent on the reduced special fibre.
Conclude normality from O-flat with reduced special fibre, which is what makes the finite birational map of Q07 the normalization map and is the input Q10 needs.

Blueprint obligation: the Groebner basis is computed with (a,b) specialized into a field, so it certifies one fibre and not the family. Supply a comprehensive (parametric) Groebner system over Z[a,b][1/P] with its exceptional denominator locus made explicit, or replace this step by a direct verification of Serre's R1 and S2.

items.name: Normalization fibers of all seven components
items.statement: Table1 gives the decomposition of the inverse image of each original component, distinguishing the unique maximal-dimensional component from lower-dimensional extras. All seven rows were read in the rotated PDF image and transcribed in sourceData.appendixB.normalizationFiberComponents. The ideals are in the normalization quotient: row four retains its inherited quadratic W equation.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.
proofSteps: Treat Table 1 as data with its own locator: it is read from a rotated image at PDF 207 and transcribed in sourceData.appendixB.normalizationFiberComponents.
Record that the source calls this decomposition 'a direct computation in Macaulay 2', so it carries the same evidential status as Q06 and the Gröbner computation in Q13.

For each of the seven components of the special fibre, pull back along the normalization map and decompose the preimage, separating the unique maximal-dimensional component from the lower-dimensional extras.
Blueprint obligation: re-derive each row from the Groebner data of Q08 rather than transcribing it, and keep the table only as a cross-check.
Note the blast radius: Q10 consumes one row of this table set-theoretically, so an error in a single row is confined to that component's unibranch analysis and does not invalidate the others.

items.name: Unibranch fixed point and a dense branching locus
items.statement: For p>7 and all seven parameter factors units, the chart is unibranch at z because its normalization fiber is a singleton. On the component (c22,c13,c12), a generically étale degree-two normalization cover gives a Zariski-dense locus that is not geometrically unibranch. This disproves a blanket all-point unibranch conclusion; distinguish ordinary from geometric unibranchness at nonclosed points.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.
proofSteps: Use Q13 (Proposition B.0.2(2)) to know that pi: U(z~,lambda,grad)^{nm}_{(a,b,0)} -> U(z~,lambda,grad)_{(a,b,0)} is the normalization map, not merely a finite birational one.
For the first claim, show pi^{-1}(z~) is set-theoretically a singleton; unibranchness at z~ is then immediate.

For the second claim, let C be the component cut out by (c22,c13,c12). By the corresponding row of Table 1, at the set-theoretic level pi^{-1}(C) -> C is identified with Z -> A^3_F, (d21,d31,d33,W) |-> (d21,d31,d33), where Z is the subscheme of A^4_F cut out by the displayed quadratic relation in W.

That quadric is irreducible, so the map is a double cover of A^3_F, hence generically finite etale of degree two. Every point off the branch locus has two preimages and so is not geometrically unibranch, and those points are Zariski dense in C.
The hypotheses p > 7 and invertibility of the seven factors of P are used, not incidental: they keep P a unit and 2 invertible, without which the degree-two cover argument does not run.
State the conclusion precisely. This refutes a blanket unibranch expectation on the special fibre; it says nothing against the first claim, and z~ itself remains unibranch.

items.name: Explicit depth-ten local comparison in one chart
items.statement: For n=3,K=Q_p,lambda=(3,1,0),z=(23)t_(2,1,1), a 5-generic presentation with mu 10-deep gives the local comparison conclusions in this chart, using Jacobian exponent 3 and m-6+3>6. Use the explicit 10-depth hypothesis: the printed raw polynomial product_{m=0}^{10}(X-Y-m)(Y-Z-m)(Z-X-m) does not imply it, as E26 shows. Alternatively evaluate a signed wall polynomial at mu+eta. Interpret the local isomorphism on the completed framed chart in Theorem7.3.2, retaining its torus torsors.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.
proofSteps: Fix the numerical setting: n = 3, K = Q_p, lambda = (3,1,0), z~ = (23)t^{(2,1,1)}, with (s,mu) a 5-generic lowest alcove presentation of a tame inertial type.
To run the Elkik approximation of Propositions 3.3.9 and 7.1.10 the depth must satisfy the source's inequality m - 6 + 3 > 6, where the Jacobian exponent r = 3 comes from Q06 and h = 3.

Solve it: m >= 10, which is what forces the printed choice P(X,Y,Z) = prod_{m=0}^{10} (X-Y-m)(Y-Z-m)(Z-X-m). Use the depth hypothesis itself rather than the printed raw product, which is a presentation of that hypothesis and not an independent condition.
Note that the second conclusion of Theorem 7.3.2 needs no extra work here: the unibranch property it requires is already supplied by Q10's first claim for this z~.
Obtain the final comparison X^{lambda,tau}(z~) = U(z~,lambda,grad) from the fact that z~ is not lambda'-admissible for any lambda' < lambda.
Carry the caveat forward explicitly: the depth 10 is only as good as r = 3, which rests on the uncertified Macaulay 2 claim in Q06. If that exponent changes, this depth changes with it.

items.name: Product extension of the numerical example
items.statement: Products preserve the reduced special-fiber and normalization facts in this example, giving the analogous chart statement for general unramified K/Q_p and corresponding product data. This is not an arbitrary-product preservation theorem for unibranchness without the stated geometric hypotheses.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.
proofSteps: Recall that Q10 is stated for J a singleton, which is the only case the explicit chart covers.
Extend to general J by taking products of the corresponding charts and of their normalizations.

The step that makes this work is that taking products preserves reducedness of the special fibres, so the product of the normalizations is still the normalization of the product; the per-factor reducedness is exactly what Q13 established.
Conclude the generalization of Q11 to K a general unramified extension of Q_p.

Do not read this as a general preservation theorem for unibranchness under products. It rests on the reducedness supplied by Q13 and on normality of a product of O-flat normal schemes with reduced special fibres, and outside those hypotheses the argument gives nothing.

items.name: Type A equivalued affine Springer fixed points
items.locator: Cited input [1], Boixeda Alvarez arXiv:1910.04780v3 Theorem3.1, PDF5; definitions PDF1–4; used in LLHLM23 Proposition4.7.3.
items.statement: Over C, for the simply connected Type A group with chosen Borel/Iwahori and diagonal regular semisimple s, put gamma=t*s. For w in the fundamental box F of dominant restricted alcoves, let Y_w be the closure of G(C[[t]])wB/B intersect Fl_gamma. Then its T-fixed points are exactly the affine Weyl elements y with y<=w0*w. The GLn central-translation and left/right quotient adapters must be supplied when importing this into LLHLM23; the theorem itself is a characteristic-zero result, and LLHLM23 spreads nonempty intersections to obtain polynomial conditions in characteristic p.
items.note: Route owner: LocalGaloisDeformationRingsPartIIMonodromyModels. This is a source extraction and planning claim; no Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Explicit affine Springer component matrix and inverse
items.locator: Cited input [1], Boixeda Alvarez arXiv:1910.04780v3 AppendixB.2–B.5, PDF8–17; corrected E29–E31.
items.statement: For w in the Type A fundamental box, set a^w_ji to the least k for which w^-1(e_i-e_j)+k*delta is a positive affine root. Construct the lower unitriangular matrix whose ji entry is the sum over increasing paths i=i1<...<ik=j of product_l ((s_il-s_i(l+1))/(s_il-s_ik))*t^(sum_l a^w_i(l+1),il)*product_l A_i(l+1),il. Distinct s_i make all denominators units. The inverse has path coefficient (-1)^(k-1)*product_l (s_il-s_i(l+1))/(s_i1-s_i(l+1)). This gives an affine open in the component and satisfies M^-1*t*s*M in w Lie(B). The fixed-point witness reduces to nonsingular determinant minors; the source degree-maximization algorithm and Vandermonde reductions are explicit further proof leaves, with transversality intersection zero.

uses.where: LLHLM23 LLHLM23 Section4.3, using Boixeda Alvarez AppendixB.2–B.5
uses.how: Provide explicit affine opens and the nonvanishing minors used to place Weyl fixed points in component closures.

api.name: AffineSpringerPathMatrix.exponents
api.statement: For w in the Type A fundamental box and i<j, choose a^w_ji as the least integer k for which w^(-1)(e_i-e_j)+k*delta is a positive affine root; retain the source positivity convention.

api.name: AffineSpringerPathMatrix.path_matrix
api.statement: Use diagonal entries 1 and, for j>i, sum over increasing paths i=i1<...<ik=j of the product over l of (s_il-s_i(l+1))/(s_il-s_ik), times t^(sum_l a^w_i(l+1),il) times the corresponding A variables. Distinct eigenvalues over the field make denominators units.

api.name: AffineSpringerPathMatrix.inverse
api.statement: Use path coefficients (-1)^(k-1) product_l (s_il-s_i(l+1))/(s_i1-s_i(l+1)) for the inverse. Verify both products are identity by the unitriangular recursion, retaining the E30 correction of s_1 to the path-start eigenvalue.

api.name: AffineSpringerPathMatrix.conjugated_entries
api.statement: Prove the strict lower entry of M^(-1)*t*s*M is t^(a^w_ji+1) A_ji (s_j-s_i); higher-path contributions cancel. The diagonal entries are t*s_i.

api.name: AffineSpringerPathMatrix.affine_open
api.statement: Use the exponent condition and conjugated-entry formula for affine Springer membership; then prove the parameter map identifies an affine open of the selected component. The matrix identity alone does not establish openness or the component dimension.

api.name: AffineSpringerPathMatrix.fixed_point_minors
api.statement: Translate intersection with the attracting chart into nonsingularity of the source finite minors, using zero lattice intersection (E29). Keep the degree-maximization and Vandermonde argument as further proof obligations; when expanding its final matrix use the last-column cofactor (E31).

tests.name: AffineSpringerPathMatrix.two_by_two
tests.statement: For n=2 the only strict lower entry is x=t^a A21, so M=I+xE21 and M^(-1)=I-xE21; the conjugated lower entry is t*x*(s2-s1).

tests.name: AffineSpringerPathMatrix.path_start_not_one
tests.statement: For the path 2<3, the inverse coefficient must be -1. The printed expression -(s2-s3)/(s1-s3) generally fails, while the corrected denominator s2-s3 gives -1.

tests.name: AffineSpringerPathMatrix.three_step_inverse
tests.statement: For the path 1<2<3, put r=(s1-s2)/(s1-s3), so M31 contains r*x32*x21. The inverse coefficient on x32*x21 is 1-r=(s2-s3)/(s1-s3), agreeing with the corrected path formula.

tests.name: AffineSpringerPathMatrix.regular_semisimple_boundary
tests.statement: If s1=s3, the length-three path coefficient has a zero denominator and the constructor is outside its domain; no limiting matrix is supplied by this formula.

items.name: Elkik's presentation-dependent Jacobian ideal
items.statement: For B=A[X_1,…,X_N]/J with fixed generators f_1,…,f_q, for each subset α of the generators let F_α be their ideal, Δ_α the ideal of |α|×|α| minors of their Jacobian (zero if |α|>N), and K_α=(F_α:J). Put H=Σ_α K_αΔ_α, with the usual empty-minor convention. Elkik permits a chosen H_B⊂H. The vanishing locus of the image of H in B is the nonsmooth locus.
items.locator: Elkik (1973), §0.2, printed p. 555/PDF4; LLHLM23 Proposition3.3.9 proof PDF69
items.note: Continuation by Codex — codex-hjdg0j. Owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations. Planning only.
proofSteps: The definition of the full H has no smoothness hypothesis. Z40–Z43 now supply its fixed-presentation smooth-locus theorem, including the empty-row summand and the non-Noetherian finite-presentation extension; the theorem consumes this definition, not conversely.

Z44 produces a finite universal power identity; Z39 transports admissibility under coefficient maps. Z07 evaluates it and removes a strictly higher-order error by a principal unit. A smaller chosen H_B need not define the full smooth locus.

unitTests.name: ElkikPresentation.zeroIdeal
unitTests.statement: For the presentation A[X_1,…,X_N]/(0), the empty-row contribution is (1), so H=(1), including N=0.

unitTests.name: ElkikPresentation.hypersurface
unitTests.statement: For J=(f), H=Ann(f)+(∂_1 f,…,∂_N f). Over a domain with nonzero f this is the gradient ideal; the annihilator contribution is retained over general rings.

unitTests.name: ElkikPresentation.duplicateEquation
unitTests.statement: Over Z[X], the presentation (X,X) has H=(1): either singleton row has derivative 1 and conductor (1). The two-row minor ideal is zero, so using only the full-row Jacobian gives a wrong result.

unitTests.name: ElkikPresentation.baseChangeStrict
unitTests.statement: For J=(2) in Z[X], H=(0); after base change to F_2, the new H=(1), while the image of the old H remains zero. Only base-change inclusion is asserted.

unitTests.name: ElkikPresentation.productRule
unitTests.statement: Jacobian entries are evaluations of Mathlib MvPolynomial.pderiv; the entry for f=X_1 X_2 is (X_2,X_1), and coefficient base change commutes with each entry.

unitTests.name: ElkikPresentation.smallerWitness
unitTests.statement: In Z_p[X] with J=(X), the full H=(1) but the permitted H_B=(p) is not the full smooth-locus ideal. At a=0, p∈H_B(a) whereas 1∉H_B(a).

unitTests.name: ElkikPresentation.conductorDenominator
unitTests.statement: For k[X] with generators (X(X−1),X²), J=(X); at Q=(X) the first equation generates J only locally. The conductor element k=X−1 satisfies k X²=X·X(X−1), and k·(2X−1) is nonzero at Q. Do not replace local generation by global equality.

unitTests.name: ElkikPresentation.inseparable
unitTests.statement: For F_p[X]/(X^p), all partial derivatives vanish and H=0. Its differential module is free of rank one, but the algebra is nowhere smooth. The conormal injection, not only freeness of differentials, is required.

unitTests.name: ElkikPresentation.strictPowerThreshold
unitTests.statement: For S=Z[1/2,t], J=(X²−t²), the full H=(2X) and t²=(X/2)(2X)−(X²−t²). After t↦3 in A=Z/81Z at a=0, J(a)⊂(3²), but 3²∉H(a)=0: m=r=2 does not suffice. Z07's m>r is essential even for the full ideal.

uses.how: A power of the base parameter in H+J gives a uniform lifting precision independently of the test ring.
Select finite conductor identities and minors to produce a linear correction without assuming the full Jacobian is square.
Transport the evaluated power witness through tuple changes and coefficient base changes; only the latter operation changes the coefficient ring.

api.statement: Form H from the chosen finite polynomial presentation and its conductor-weighted minors.

api.name: ElkikPresentation.baseChange_le

api.statement: Export a concrete finite identity v^r=h+j with h∈H and j∈J for use after all base changes. Z44 requires generic smoothness of the full universal presentation; no uniform bound across unrelated presentations.

api.name: ElkikPresentation.emptyMinor
api.statement: The empty-row summand is Ann(J), so H=(1) when J=0.

api.name: ElkikPresentation.finiteWitness
api.statement: Membership t^r∈H_B(a) with H_B⊂H gives a finite A-linear combination of evaluated conductor-weighted minors; no finite generation of the individual conductor ideals is required.

api.name: ElkikPresentation.witnessPerturbation
api.statement: In a complete separated (t)-adic ring, a change modulo t^s with s>r preserves t^r∈H_B(a); exported as Z35.

items.name: Newton correction with an Elkik minor witness
items.statement: Let A be a t-torsionfree ring with a finite polynomial presentation J=(f_i), an admissible H_B, and a tuple a with t^r∈H_B(a) and J(a)⊂t^m A, m>2r. There exists y∈(t^(m−r)A)^N such that J(a−y)⊂t^(2m−2r)A.
items.locator: Elkik Lemma1 proof, printed pp. 556–558/PDF5–7, specialized to I=A and no t-torsion
items.note: Continuation by Codex — codex-hjdg0j. Owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations. Planning only.
proofSteps: Use Z33 to obtain y∈t^(m−r) with f(a)−D(a)y∈t^(2m−r).
Apply Z30 with L=(t^(m−r)). Its remainder lies in t^(2m−2r). Since 2m−r≥2m−2r, the linear residual lies in the same ideal, so f(a−y)∈t^(2m−2r).
The step itself only needs m≥r for these bounds. The stated m>2r gives strict improvement and permits witness persistence in the iteration.

unitTests.name: Z04.test_1
unitTests.statement: For f(X)=t^r X−t^m and a=0 the exact correction has valuation m−r.
unitTests.status: mathematical acceptance test; no Lean compilation

unitTests.name: Z04.test_2
unitTests.statement: The inequality m>2r gives 2m−2r>m; equality at m=2r does not provide strict improvement.
unitTests.status: mathematical acceptance test; no Lean compilation

acceptance: For Z_3 and f=X²−18 at a=3, r=1 and m=2=2r satisfy the residual and Jacobian conditions, but f has no root in Z_3: any root divided by 3 would square to 2 modulo 3. Thus the strict threshold in the exact-lifting theorem cannot in general be weakened to m≥2r.

items.name: Elkik approximation with bounded torsion
items.statement: Let A be Noetherian and t-adically complete, I an ideal, T the t-power torsion ideal, and k satisfy T∩t^k A=0. If t^h∈H_B(a), J(a)⊂t^n I and n>max(2h,h+k), there is a^0 with J(a^0)=0 and a^0−a∈(t^(n−h)I)^N.
items.note: Continuation by Codex — codex-hjdg0j. Owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations. Planning only.
proofSteps: The source's standing Noetherian hypothesis supplies the torsion cutoff and closedness of the relevant ideals.
Use the conductor-weighted adjugate correction, controlling the torsion during division by t^h, then iterate with improved precision and pass to the limit.
Do not export this arbitrary-I statement to arbitrary non-Noetherian rings merely by citing the source.

items.name: Torsionfree complete approximation without a Noetherian test ring
items.statement: For a t-adically complete and separated t-torsionfree ring A, a finite polynomial presentation and admissible H_B, if t^r∈H_B(a), J(a)⊂t^m A and m>2r, there is an exact zero a^0 with a^0−a∈(t^(m−r)A)^N.
items.locator: Proof extracted from Elkik Lemma1 with I=A; used in LLHLM23 Proposition3.3.9
items.note: Continuation by Codex — codex-hjdg0j. Owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations. Planning only.
proofSteps: Use L32 to express complete separated t-adic topology as IsAdicComplete (t) A. Z36 supplies a Newton sequence with e_j=m_j−r=r+2^j(m_0−2r).
Apply Z37 coordinatewise to obtain a^0 with a^0−a_j∈t^e_j for every j. At j=0 this is the promised agreement modulo t^(m_0−r).
Apply Z38 to the residual orders m_j≥e_j to conclude J(a^0)=0.

No Noetherian condition or arbitrary-ideal closure assertion is used. Z05 retains the separate original theorem for general I; this argument concerns only its torsionfree I=A specialization. Uniqueness of a^0 is not asserted.

unitTests.name: Z06.test_1
unitTests.statement: N=2r+1 is a valid integral threshold for this witness r.
unitTests.status: mathematical acceptance test; no Lean compilation

unitTests.name: Z06.test_2
unitTests.statement: Agreement modulo t^m is false in general: t^r X=t^m with r>0 has the unique solution t^(m−r).
unitTests.status: mathematical acceptance test; no Lean compilation

items.name: A fixed smooth generic presentation gives a uniform exponent
items.statement: For the fixed finitely presented universal chart over the Noetherian base S in U24, smoothness after inverting v implies v^r∈H+J for some r≥0. Choose H_B after base change to be the image of this full universal H, which is admissible by Z03. After any base map S→A with v↦t, an approximate zero modulo t^m with m>r satisfies t^r∈H_B(a) if A is t-adically complete.
items.note: Continuation by Codex — codex-hjdg0j. Owner: SchemeAndStackFoundations. Planning only.
proofSteps: U23 supplies generic smoothness for the fixed universal chart. Apply Z44 to the full H, using Z43 for the fixed-presentation smooth locus and L40/L41 for radical membership, and choose a finite identity v^r=h+Σ b_i f_i before base change.

Z39 makes the coefficient image H_B admissible. Evaluating the fixed identity at a gives t^r=h(a)+t^m b with h(a)∈H_B(a). Because m>r, rewrite h(a)=t^r(1−t^(m−r)b). L29 and L30 make the parenthesis a unit. Multiply by its inverse to obtain t^r∈H_B(a); this uses no cancellation, no Noetherianity and no t-torsionfree hypothesis on A.
Combining with Z06 permits N=2r+1. Both r and N are chosen from the universal presentation, not separately for each test ring.

items.name: Geometric connectedness in the affinoid finite-extension sense
items.statement: For a nonzero strict affinoid algebra A over a complete nontrivially valued nonarchimedean field K, call A geometrically connected in the finite-extension sense if Spec(A⊗_K L) is connected for every finite field extension L/K. Z53 identifies each such tensor with the completed tensor. Comparison with the scheme predicate testing arbitrary extensions is a separate interface.
items.note: Continuation by Codex — codex-hjdg0j. Owner: AdicSpacesPartII. Planning only.
proofSteps: Record the finite-extension convention used in the product proof; do not conflate an ordinary tensor product of affinoids with their completed tensor product.

unitTests.name: Z08.test_1
unitTests.statement: K itself satisfies the condition.
unitTests.status: mathematical acceptance test; no Lean compilation

unitTests.name: Z08.test_2
unitTests.statement: A nontrivial finite separable field extension of K is connected but not geometrically connected after a splitting extension.
unitTests.status: mathematical acceptance test; no Lean compilation

uses.where: U43/Z13 and LLHLM23 Theorem3.7.1 final paragraph
uses.how: The product's connectedness, together with its independently supplied regularity, proves it is a domain.

api.name: AffinoidGeometricallyConnected.baseChange

api.name: AffinoidGeometricallyConnected.cofinal
api.statement: It suffices to test a cofinal collection of finite field extensions; connectedness descends along further field extension.

api.name: AffinoidGeometricallyConnected.noIdempotents

api.name: AffinoidGeometricallyConnected.completedTensor
api.statement: The completed tensor product preserves this condition once the affinoid fiber comparison is established.

tests.statement: K satisfies the predicate since K⊗_K L=L for every finite field extension.

items.name: BLGGT geometric connectedness of an affinoid product
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_l and A_1,A_2 geometrically connected affinoid K-algebras in the finite-extension sense. Then A_1 completed-tensor_K A_2 is geometrically connected.
items.locator: BLGGT LemmaA.1.1, printed p. 596/PDF96; standing field convention p. 595
items.note: Continuation by Codex — codex-hjdg0j. Owner: AdicSpacesPartII. Planning only.
proofSteps: Assume a disconnected finite scalar extension; each open-and-closed part has a maximal ideal. Make both residue fields rational over a common finite extension.
Project one selected point to the first factor and the other to the second. Fibers over the projections are connected copies of the opposite factor, hence lie in the two different parts.
Their simultaneous fiber is the field, giving a common point in disjoint parts, a contradiction. Track which of the two chosen points supplies each projection.

items.name: A connected affinoid with a rational point is geometrically connected
items.statement: For a complete nontrivially valued nonarchimedean field K, a connected strict affinoid K-algebra A admitting a K-algebra retraction A→K is geometrically connected in the finite-extension sense. Normality and regularity are unnecessary for this conclusion.
items.locator: Implicit input before BLGGT LemmaA.1.1 is applied in LLHLM23 Theorem3.7.1, PDF79–80
items.note: AdicSpacesPartII:R0 affinoid adapter of the general algebraic result Z47. This strengthens the earlier correct normal-connected statement; it is not a new source erratum.
proofSteps: Apply Z47 to the underlying K-algebra, then Z53 to identify each finite scalar extension with its completed extension.
The former normality/component proof is replaced by the explicit invariant-idempotent product and inseparable Frobenius proof. No finite étale normality theorem is needed.

unitTests.name: Z10.test_2

items.name: Khare–Wintenberger completed tensor theorem in its original scope
items.statement: Let O be the integers of a finite extension E/Q_p and R_i a finite family of complete Noetherian local O-algebras with residue field O/m_O. Suppose each R_i is a domain with an O-algebra retraction R_i→O and R_i[1/p] is regular. Their completed tensor product, completed for the sum of maximal ideals, is a domain, has an O-point, and has regular generic fiber.
items.locator: Khare–Wintenberger II Proposition2.2(ii), author PDF9; conventions PDF4–6
items.note: Continuation by Codex — codex-hjdg0j. Owner: DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra. Planning only.
proofSteps: At the chosen rational generic points, the completed local rings are power series rings over E.
Use the cofinality of the saturated point-ideal filtration (Chevalley) to embed the completed tensor in the product-point formal power series ring, hence obtain a domain.

The source separately proves generic regularity by considering all closed generic points after finite coefficient extension. This last step is not needed merely to deduce the domain conclusion and must not be generalized to imperfect fields without its own hypotheses.

items.name: Domain part over an arbitrary complete DVR
items.statement: Let O be a complete DVR with fraction field K, and R_i complete Noetherian local O-domains with the same residue field as O and O-algebra retractions ξ_i. Assume the local rings of R_i[1/π] at ker(ξ_i)[1/π] are regular. Then the completed tensor over O, for the sum of maximal ideals, is a domain and has an O-point.
items.locator: LLHLM23 Theorem3.7.1, PDF79, general-DVR adaptation of KWII Proposition2.2
items.note: Continuation by Codex — codex-hjdg0j. Owner: DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra. Planning only.
proofSteps: Construct C and its O-retraction by Z24. For a nonempty family, Z22 embeds C in the generic jet limit; Z21 identifies that limit with a power-series domain over K. C is nonzero by its O-retraction, hence a domain. For the empty family C=O.

Z15–Z22 expose the saturated-jet, finite-free, cofinality, exact-quotient and generic-completion comparisons used in this argument. They do not import the finite-Q_p theorem Z11 as if it already applied to arbitrary DVRs.

The detailed source argument is now explicit; regular completion dimension/cotangent and power-series dimension atoms still need exact baseline/supplier closure. No general-field generic-regularity conclusion for arbitrary factors is asserted.

unitTests.statement: The theorem applies with O=k[[π]] for arbitrary k, including infinite or imperfect fields, provided the stated rational-point local rings are regular.
