tests.name: PolarizationSign.characterMatters
tests.statement: For the inclusion of the diagonal normalizer G⊂GL2(Q), c(g)=g/det(g): χ=1 has sign−1, while χ equal to the diagonal/antidiagonal component character has sign+1, as the alternating and exchange matrices show.

items.name: Field-valued polarized extension with its determined sign
items.statement: Let Δ⊂Γ have index2, γ0∈Γ\Δ, k be a field of characteristic≠2, χ:Γ→k×, and ρ:Δ→GL_n(k) absolutely irreducible with ρ^γ0≅χ|Δ⊗ρ∨. There is an extension r:Γ→G_n(k) with r|Δ=(ρ,χ|Δ). Its multiplier μ restricts to χ|Δ; its value on γ0 is determined by the pairing, so μ is one of χ and χδ_(Γ/Δ), not a freely prescribed choice. For fixed restriction (ρ,χ|Δ), extension classes up to GL_n(k)-conjugacy form a torsor for k×/(k×)² by scaling A in r(γ0)=(A,−μ(γ0))j; all have the same μ. Over algebraically closed k the class is unique.
items.note: Source refinement by Codex — codex-7e92bd, 23 September 2026; no Lean implementation. Owner: ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations.
items.proofOutline: Compare B and (x,y)↦B(y,ρ(γ0²)x). Their scalar ratio determines μ(γ0). Scalar conjugation changes A by a square. Do not infer μ=χ solely from conjugate self-duality.

items.name: Finite coefficient field for a compact polarized image
items.statement: If Γ is profinite and r:Γ→G_n(Qpbar) is continuous for the p-adic subspace topology, then its image lies in G_n(K) for some finite extension K/Qp.
items.locator: CHT Lemma2.1.5 first paragraph of proof, PDF10–11
items.note: Source refinement by Codex — codex-7e92bd, 23 September 2026; no Lean implementation. Owner: ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations. Continuation cc-fb70e5: prerequisites A85 and L75 added; the two named suppliers are no longer open.
items.proofOutline: The compact image is Baire. Its intersections with G_n(K), as K ranges through the countably many finite extensions inside Qpbar, are closed subgroups covering it. One has interior, hence finite index. Adjoining the entries of finitely many coset representatives gives a common finite K. Both proof suppliers are now explicit: the Baire step is the pinned L75 (a compact Hausdorff space is a Baire space, and one of countably many closed covering sets has interior) and the countable cover is A85.

items.name: Invariant self-dual lattice after coefficient extension
items.statement: Let Γ be profinite and r:Γ→G_n(Qpbar) continuous, n≥1, with Δ the inverse image of the identity component. After finite coefficient extension K/Q_p and GL_n(Qpbar)-conjugation, r is valued in G_n(O_K). If Δ has index two, both the Δ-action and the perfect pairing in A34 become integral and unimodular in the chosen basis. If Δ=Γ, use an ordinary stable lattice and the unit multiplier; no nonidentity-coset pairing is asserted. The extension may be ramified, and the lattice conclusion includes p=2.
items.locator: CHT Lemma2.1.5, author PDF11–12 (lattice proof on PDF12).
items.note: Source refinement by Codex — codex-7e92bd, 23 September 2026; no Lean implementation. Owner: ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations. Supplier continuation codex-7e92bd gives the explicit replacement/import chain below; no independent review or Lean implementation is claimed.
items.proofOutline: A37 first gives a finite coefficient field. A86 supplies a stable lattice and integral unit multiplier. For Δ=Γ this already suffices. Otherwise scale the lattice to make B integral, then use A87–A88 to choose a maximal stable integral L with πL*⊂L. After the single quadratic extension of A89, A90 constructs the self-dual lattice L⊕ΠL*. In a basis its Gram matrix is in GL_n(O′), and A34 puts the other coset in G_n(O′). These explicit formulas replace the compressed repeated-enlargement sentence; they introduce neither a symmetry assumption nor a source-issue verdict.

items.name: Scalar centralizer over a complete local ring
items.statement: Let R be complete Noetherian local and ρ:Δ→GL_n(R) continuous with absolutely irreducible reduction. The centralizer of ρ in GL_n(R) consists exactly of scalar matrices R×.
items.locator: CHT Lemma2.1.8, statement on author PDF13 and proof on PDF14.
items.note: Source refinement by Codex — codex-7e92bd, 23 September 2026; no Lean implementation. Owner: IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants. Supplier continuation codex-7e92bd gives the explicit replacement/import chain below; no independent review or Lean implementation is claimed.
items.proofOutline: Use A92: finitely many group matrices are a basis of M_n(R), so a centralizer element commutes with every matrix unit and is scalar. This gives the source conclusion without a separate compatible Artinian-limit argument; the stronger algebraic lemma has no completeness hypothesis.

items.name: Descent of conjugacy in the residually absolutely irreducible case
items.statement: Let S⊂R be complete Noetherian local rings with m_R∩S=m_S and identical residue field. If continuous representations ρ,ρ′:Δ→GL_n(S) of a profinite group are conjugate over R and their common residual representation is absolutely irreducible, they are conjugate over S.
items.locator: CHT Lemma2.1.9, author PDF14; the residually absolutely irreducible specialization, not its more general centralizer-surjectivity version.
items.note: Source refinement by Codex — codex-7e92bd, 23 September 2026; no Lean implementation. Owner: IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants. Supplier continuation codex-7e92bd gives the explicit replacement/import chain below; no independent review or Lean implementation is claimed.
items.proofOutline: Let g∈GL_n(R) conjugate ρ to ρ′. A92 supplies S-bases made from the same group elements for both representations. Conjugation by g therefore restricts to an S-algebra automorphism φ of M_n(S), since it carries the first basis to the second; multiplication identities descend through the injective inclusion S⊂R. Lift the residue of g to g₀∈GL_n(S), using the common residue field and the determinant-unit criterion. After composing φ with conjugation by g₀^(−1), its reduction is the identity. Apply A96 over S with I=m_S. This proves actual S-conjugacy without any unproved cofinal inverse-limit choice.

items.name: Inner derivation formula for the matrix algebra
items.statement: For a field k, n≥1, and a k-linear derivation d:M_n(k)→M_n(k), fix an index1 and put A=Σ_j d(E_j1)E_1j. Then d(X)=AX−XA for every X. This formula uses no division by n and applies when char(k) divides n.
items.note: Source refinement by Codex — codex-7e92bd, 23 September 2026; no Lean implementation. Owner: IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants.
items.proofOutline: Use E_ijE_kl=δ_jkE_il and the derivation rule to check the identity on every matrix unit; extend linearly. This is the explicit matrix-algebra adapter used in trace descent, not a claim that every derivation of an arbitrary algebra is inner.

items.name: Trace descent over dual numbers
items.statement: Let k be a field, R=k[ε]/(ε²), and ρ:Δ→GL_n(R) a representation with absolutely irreducible reduction ρ0. If trρ(δ)∈k for every δ∈Δ, then some A∈M_n(k) satisfies (1−εA)ρ(δ)(1+εA)=ρ0(δ) for every δ.
items.note: Source refinement by Codex — codex-7e92bd, 23 September 2026; no Lean implementation. Owner: IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants. Supplier continuation codex-7e92bd gives the explicit replacement/import chain below; no independent review or Lean implementation is claimed.
items.proofOutline: Extend to k[Δ]. A91 makes ρ₀(k[Δ])=M_n(k) for arbitrary Δ. If y∈kerρ₀, write ρ(y)=εY. For every x, the ε-coefficient of trρ(xy) vanishes, hence tr(ρ₀(x)Y)=0. L79 gives Y=0, so ρ factors through M_n(k). Its ε-coefficient is a k-linear derivation, and A41 gives d(X)=AX−XA. Conjugation by 1−εA kills it. This proof works in every characteristic, including p dividing n.

items.name: Carayol trace descent with prescribed congruence
items.statement: Let S⊂R be complete Noetherian local rings with m_R∩S=m_S and common residue field. Let Δ be profinite and ρ:Δ→GL_n(R) continuous with absolutely irreducible reduction and trρ(Δ)⊂S. If an ideal I⊂R satisfies ρ mod I∈GL_n(S/(I∩S)), a conjugate by 1+M_n(I) is valued in GL_n(S). In particular I=m_R gives a strict conjugate over S.
items.locator: CHT Lemma2.1.10, author PDF14–15; finite trace-algebra replacement proof supplies the prescribed congruence without the compressed recursion.
items.note: Source refinement by Codex — codex-7e92bd, 23 September 2026; no Lean implementation. Owner: IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants. Supplier continuation codex-7e92bd gives the explicit replacement/import chain below; no independent review or Lean implementation is claimed.
items.proofOutline: First suppose I is proper, hence I⊂m_R; put J=I∩S. A95 constructs A⊂M_n(R) with A/JA≃M_n(S/J) in the given coordinates. A94 lifts this exact quotient isomorphism to α:A≃M_n(S). The two R-algebra identifications A⊗_S R≃M_n(R), one from inclusion and one from α, differ by an automorphism that is identity mod I. By A96 it is conjugation by g∈1+M_n(I), so g^(−1)ρg has matrices in S. For I=R, use the I=m_R case (the residual representation is over the common residue field); that conjugator is allowed in 1+M_n(R). A97 identifies the intrinsic S-adic topology with the induced topology, proving continuity of the S-valued representation. Neither residue finiteness nor arbitrary compatible conjugator choices enter the proof.

items.name: Square root of a principal unit
items.statement: Let R be a complete Noetherian local ring with residue characteristic≠2. Every α∈1+m_R has a unique β∈1+m_R with β²=α.
items.locator: CHT Lemma2.1.12 proof, PDF16; Hensel adapter for X²−α
items.note: Source refinement by Codex — codex-7e92bd, 23 September 2026; no Lean implementation. Owner: IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants. Supplier continuation codex-7e92bd gives the explicit replacement/import chain below; no independent review or Lean implementation is claimed.
items.proofOutline: Apply L77 at I=m_R to the monic polynomial X²−α and a₀=1. Since α≡1 mod m_R and residue characteristic is not 2, the derivative has unit image 2 in the residue field. The resulting β satisfies β≡1 and β²=α. If β′ is another such root, (β−β′)(β+β′)=0 and β+β′≡2 mod m_R is a unit, hence β=β′. No Newton convergence or n! invertibility supplier is required.

items.name: Fixed-multiplier polarized trace descent
items.statement: Let S⊂R be complete Noetherian local rings with common residue field of characteristic p>2 and m_R∩S=m_S. Let Γ be profinite, Δ an open index-two subgroup, and r:Γ→G_n(R) continuous inducing Γ/Δ≅C2. Assume r|Δ has absolutely irreducible reduction, tr(r|Δ(δ))∈S for every δ∈Δ, and fix a continuous μ:Γ→S× with νr=μ after inclusion. Then r is GL_n(R)-conjugate to a continuous G_n(S)-valued representation with multiplier μ.
items.locator: CHT Lemma2.1.12 and proof, PDF15–16; fixed-multiplier specialization needed in LLHLM23 A.4.1
items.note: Source refinement by Codex — codex-7e92bd, 23 September 2026; no Lean implementation. Owner: IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants.
items.proofOutline: First apply A43 to the GL_n restriction. A40 descends its polarization intertwiner to B∈GL_n(S). A39 writes the original A=αB; rescale B so α∈1+m_R. Choose β²=α by A44 and conjugate by β⁻¹I, which sends A to B. The printed βI conjugation has the inverse on the wrong side (E39). The multiplier is explicitly S-valued throughout; no unrestricted multiplier-descent theorem is inferred from traces alone.

items.name: Common-residue product of integral coefficient rings
items.statement: Let O be a complete DVR with finite residue field k. For a finite nonempty family of finite extensions K_i/Frac(O), write O_i for their rings of integers and k_i for their residue fields, with fixed embeddings k→k_i. Define A={(a,(x_i))∈k×∏O_i : x_i mod m_i is the image of a for every i}. Its coordinatewise operations make it a complete Noetherian local O-algebra with residue k and maximal ideal0×∏m_i. It is O-finite and O-torsionfree; projections to O_i and k are continuous.
items.locator: CHT Proposition3.4.4 proof, PDF108; explicit finite-O algebra adapter
items.note: Source refinement by Codex — codex-7e92bd, 23 September 2026; no Lean implementation. Owner: IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants.
items.proofOutline: The congruence condition defines an O-submodule of a finite O-module, hence a finite algebra. A tuple is a unit exactly when its common residue is nonzero; componentwise inverses have the same residue. Completeness follows from finite O-module completeness and equivalence of its adic topologies. A102 now supplies finite-module completeness and the explicit m^(da)⊂pi^a A⊂m^a comparison; A103 identifies the intrinsic topology with the coefficient-product subspace topology. Torsionfreeness follows by forgetting the redundant k coordinate into the nonempty product of torsionfree O_i.

uses.how: Supplies a single local coefficient ring for constituent representations with the same residual representation.

api.statement: Construct a tuple from a∈k and x_i∈O_i whose residues are the specified images of a.

api.name: CommonResidueProduct.ext
api.statement: Tuples are equal if all O_i coordinates agree; the nonempty family and injective residue embeddings determine a.

api.name: CommonResidueProduct.proj

api.name: CommonResidueProduct.unit_iff

api.name: CommonResidueProduct.lift
api.statement: A ring map B→A is equivalent to maps B→k and B→O_i with the prescribed residue equalities.

api.name: CommonResidueProduct.residue
api.statement: A/(0×∏m_i)≅k canonically.

items.name: Alignment of integral polarized reductions
items.statement: Assume p>2, fix an absolutely irreducible residual GL_n representation ρbar over k and a G_n(k)-extension rbar. Suppose integral G_n(O_i)-representations r_i have reductions whose GL_n restrictions become isomorphic to ρbar after residue extension, and whose multipliers are the same fixed lift μ. After finite coefficient extensions and GL_n(O_i)-conjugation their reductions equal the images of rbar as G_n representations.
items.locator: CHT Proposition3.4.4 proof, PDF107–108; Lemma2.1.4 PDF9–10
items.note: Source refinement by Codex — codex-7e92bd, 23 September 2026; no Lean implementation. Owner: ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations.
items.proofOutline: First conjugate the residual GL_n representations. A36 makes the remaining difference a scalar square class on the nonidentity component. Enlarge the residue field to contain its square root, lift the residual conjugating matrix integrally, and conjugate. When the input residual isomorphism is obtained from the CHT split-prime polynomial data, A101 supplies it, including the upgrade from a simple semisimplification to the actual reduction and the finite coefficient extension. Traces alone in arbitrary modular characteristic are not substituted.

items.name: Gluing over a reduced finite integral Hecke algebra
items.statement: Let O be a complete DVR with finite residue k of characteristic p>2. Let T be a reduced finite flat local O-algebra with residue k, embedded in the common-residue ring A of A46 using one finite coefficient extension for each minimal prime of T. Suppose continuous r_i:Γ→G_n(O_i) have identical residual rbar, with rbar|Δ absolutely irreducible, and share a fixed multiplier μ:Γ→O×. If tr(r_A|Δ(δ)) belongs to T for every δ∈Δ, where r_A is the tuple representation, then r_A is GL_n(A)-conjugate to a continuous r_T:Γ→G_n(T) with multiplier μ. One can choose its reduction equal to rbar.
items.locator: CHT Proposition3.4.4 proof, PDF107–108, isolated descent step
items.note: Source refinement by Codex — codex-7e92bd, 23 September 2026; no Lean implementation. Owner: IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants.
items.proofOutline: Reducedness and flatness embed T into the product of the characteristic-zero fraction fields; integral coordinates give T⊂A. A45 gives descent. Its residual conjugator lies in GL_n(k) and can be lifted over T to restore the chosen reduction. Frobenius polynomial data supply the trace hypothesis only after the density/continuity adapter A49; this is not gluing from an arbitrary finite set of Hecke operators.

items.name: Dense Frobenius traces suffice for integral trace descent
items.statement: Let T⊂A be a closed subring of a topological ring and ρ:Δ→GL_n(A) continuous. If a subset C⊂Δ has dense conjugacy saturation and trρ(c)∈T for all c∈C, then trρ(Δ)⊂T. In the CM application C consists of Frobenius elements at the unramified split primes outside a finite set; the required density is the split-prime Chebotarev statement, not an assumption about all Frobenius elements being dense as selected representatives.

items.proofOutline: Trace is continuous and conjugation invariant, so its inverse image of a closed coefficient subring contains the closure of the conjugacy saturation of C. A100 proves exactly that saturation is dense for both places above every good split base prime, with any finite exceptional set removed. A103 proves that a finite-O integral Hecke algebra inside the Hausdorff coefficient product is closed and has its intrinsic topology. These are explicit imports/adapters; the selected Frobenius representatives alone need not be dense.

items.name: Residual irreducibility forces characteristic-zero irreducibility
items.statement: Let O be the ring of integers of a finite extension K/Qp and Λ an O-free Γ-stable lattice of rank n. If Λ/mΛ is absolutely irreducible, then Λ⊗K is absolutely irreducible.
items.note: Source refinement by Codex — codex-7e92bd, 23 September 2026; no Lean implementation. Owner: ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations.
items.proofOutline: If an invariant proper nonzero subspace exists after a finite extension K′, intersect it with Λ⊗O_K′. This is a saturated free sublattice of intermediate rank, so its reduction injects as a nonzero proper invariant subspace. Absolute irreducibility excludes it. A subspace over Qpbar descends to a finite field extension by its finitely many basis coordinates.

items.name: Automorphic polarization has positive pairing sign
items.statement: Let F be CM and Π a regular algebraic conjugate-self-dual cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n(A_F). For its associated semisimple p-adic representation ρ_Π, every irreducible constituent r satisfying r⊥≅r ε^(n−1) has sign(r,ε^(n−1))=+1. In particular if ρ_Π is absolutely irreducible its polarization is symmetric.
items.locator: Bellaïche–Chenevier published Theorem1.2, PDF4/p1339; context PDF2–3; conclusion of proof PDF15–17

items.proofOutline: Import the automorphic sign theorem from AG2.2. Its proof uses eigenvariety deformation, odd-rank signs, specialization of polarized matrix algebras, and solvable base change preserving irreducible constituents. The older arXiv0804.2860v1 text states an expected construction as a hypothesis; the published theorem is the reference here. This continuation has not decomposed the entire eigenvariety proof.

items.name: Symmetric pairing selects the LLHLM multiplier
items.statement: Let F/F+ be CM, c a complex conjugation, and ρ:G_F→GL_n(k) absolutely irreducible over a field of characteristic≠2, with ρ^c≅ρ∨ε^(1−n) and positive pairing sign. Its G_n extension has multiplier ξ=ε^(1−n)δ_(F/F+)^n. In particular ξ(c)=−1 for every n.

items.name: Coefficient-prime monodromy bound
items.statement: Let F be an imaginary CM field, (Π,χ) a regular algebraic essentially conjugate-self-dual cuspidal representation of GL_n(A_F), ι:Qpbar≅C, and v|p. Then ι WD(r_p,ι(Π)|G_Fv)^F-ss ≺ rec(Π_v⊗|det|^((1−n)/2)). Here ≺ means equality of semisimplified Weil representations and, in every irreducible Weil representation class modulo unramified twist, dominance of the decreasing special-block lengths (all initial partial sums on the left ≤ those on the right). This includes n=1 via local class field theory. Shin regularity is not required for the bound.

items.name: Weil-block dominance restricts to inertia dominance
items.statement: For two Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne representations over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field with the same semisimplified Weil representation, dominance of special-block partitions in each irreducible Weil class modulo unramified twist implies the inertia-isotypic nilpotent dominance of N57 after restriction.

Continuation codex-c83e7a removes the unnecessary Clifford-orbit supplier: unramified-equivalence itself identifies the inertia restriction, and A82 supplies the nonnegative multiplicity coefficients.
items.proofOutline: For each irreducible Weil class σ modulo unramified twist, choose one representative s_σ and put c_(θ,σ)=dim Hom_I(θ,s_σ|I). All representatives in σ have the same inertia restriction by the definition of unramified twist. The special-block decomposition used to define BLGGT’s relation gives rank_a on the θ-multiplicity space as Σ_σ c_(θ,σ) Σ_j max(m_j(ρ,σ)−a,0), by A82. Prefix-sum dominance for each σ implies the corresponding inner rank inequality by A58’s partition transform. Multiply by nonnegative c_(θ,σ) and sum over σ. The two sides have the same inertia representation because their semisimplified Weil representations agree. Multiply by dim θ for the whole-isotypic convention and apply A58. This direct finite sum avoids a separate Clifford-theory orbit theorem; overlapping inertia supports cause no difficulty.

items.name: At-p deformation condition from compatibility and K-type occurrence
items.statement: Assume the AppendixA.4 setting and a characteristic-zero automorphic constituent whose Galois representation is identified with r_p,ι(Π) for a RACSDC cuspidal Π, with the local and weight normalization of EGH7.2.1. Suppose Hom_GL_n(O_Fv)(σ(τ_v),Π_v)≠0 and the algebraic coefficient has highest weight λ_v in the convention giving Hodge multiset λ_v+η. Then WD(r_p,ι(Π)|G_Fv)|I_v≤τ_v and the representation has the required Hodge weights. It lies on the corresponding monodromy-bounded potentially semistable deformation condition; if N_(τ_v)=0 it is potentially crystalline.

A53 and A54 bound Galois monodromy by the automorphic one. Use transitivity of N57. The type-occurrence/dual coefficient dictionary and the integral deformation-ring point criterion are separate suppliers; semisimplified compatibility alone cannot prove this assertion.

items.name: Disjoint base change preserves absolute irreducibility
items.statement: Let K be a number field, L/Qp finite, and ρ:G_K→GL_n(L) a continuous absolutely irreducible representation. There exists a finite Galois extension M/K such that for every finite K′/K linearly disjoint from M, ρ|G_K′ is absolutely irreducible. K′ need not be Galois.
items.locator: Bellaïche–Chenevier Lemma3.5, published PDF16/p1351, with E40 proof repair
items.note: Source refinement by Codex — codex-7e92bd, 23 September 2026; no Lean implementation. Owner: ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations.
items.proofOutline: Choose n² group elements whose matrices span M_n(L). Continuity of the determinant gives an open normal U such that every choice from the same U-cosets still spans. Set M=Kbar^U. Linear disjointness gives the surjection G_K′→Gal(M/K) directly, so choose coset representatives in G_K′. Their matrices span M_n(L), hence the restriction is absolutely irreducible. Do not replace K′ by its Galois closure: disjointness may fail after that replacement. Matrix-algebra density and the finite-Galois restriction map are named suppliers.

items.name: Pinned dominance partial order on partitions
items.statement: For partitions μ,ν,ξ of the same natural number, TauCeti.Dominates μ ν means every decreasing-part prefix sum of ν is at most that of μ. This relation is reflexive, transitive and antisymmetric. Its scoped order has ν≤μ exactly when μ dominates ν.

items.name: Transitivity of inertial monodromy dominance
items.statement: For GL_n Weil–Deligne inertial types τ1,τ2,τ3 over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, τ1≤τ2 and τ2≤τ3 imply τ1≤τ3. The inertia representations are identified transitively, and the inequality is independent of the chosen intertwining identifications.

items.name: Inertial dominance is equivalent to power-rank inequalities
items.statement: For two GL_n WD inertial types with the same semisimple inertia representation over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, τ≤τ′ if and only if, on each irreducible-inertia multiplicity space, rank(N_τ^a)≤rank(N_τ′^a) for every integer a≥1.

items.proofOutline: A83–A84 supply the chain basis, rank formula and recovery of the partition from actual operators. For a decreasing partition λ padded by zeros set S_i=Σ_(j≤i)λ_j and R_a=Σ_j max(λ_j−a,0), a≥0. Then R_a=max_i(S_i−ia): choose i equal to the number of parts strictly larger than a. Conversely S_i=min_(a≥0)(ia+R_a): for i≥1 choose a=λ_i (with zero padding), and for i=0 choose a at least the largest part; use a=0 for the empty partition. Hence same-total-size prefix-sum dominance is equivalent to the inequalities R_a≤R′_a for every a≥1; a=0 is equality of dimensions. On an entire θ-isotypic subspace each Jordan block of the multiplicity operator is repeated dim θ times, so all ranks are multiplied by the same positive integer. This preserves and reflects the inequalities, proving equivalence with the whole-isotypic definition printed in the paper.

items.name: Compact-unitary base change retains discrete constituents and split-place comparison
items.locator: Labesse, Changement de base CM et series discretes, author PDF pp.1-2,42-44, Corollary5.3 and its proof; LLHLM23 Section9.1 PDF180-181.
items.statement: Let F+ be totally real with [F+:Q]>1, F/F+ CM, and G an inner form of U(n) compact at every infinite place. For a discrete automorphic representation sigma of G(A_F+), Labesse's sign condition (*) is automatic. There exist n=sum_i n_i and conjugate-self-dual discrete automorphic representations Delta_i of GL_(n_i)(A_F) whose isobaric sum is a weak base change of sigma, agreeing with local base change at split and unramified places. Its infinite component is cohomological with the source's coefficient and infinitesimal-character comparison. If every Delta_i is cuspidal, the infinite component is the actual archimedean base change. Do not replace discrete by cuspidal without that additional argument.
items.proofOutline: Use ET.4's stable/twisted trace identity, separate finite Hecke characters, and use the common-sign condition to prevent cancellation of the selected discrete packet. Labesse5.3 then uses the GL residual-spectrum classification and rigidity. Compact infinity gives (*). The LLHLM field restriction supplies [F+:Q]>1; no extension to F+=Q is inferred. The trace-formula and spectral proofs remain with their existing owners.

items.name: Discrete Speh quotient with normalized exponents
items.locator: Moeglin-Waldspurger, Le spectre residuel de GL(n), printed605-607/PDF2-4; introduction and I.1.1.
items.statement: For a unitary cuspidal automorphic representation pi of GL_m(A_F), F a number field, and b>=1, define Speh(pi,b) as the unique irreducible quotient of normalized parabolic induction of pi|det|^((b-1)/2), pi|det|^((b-3)/2), ..., pi|det|^((1-b)/2) to GL_(mb)(A_F). This is the discrete residual-spectrum quotient, not the generalized Steinberg subrepresentation with the opposite quotient convention.

uses.how: Parameterizes every discrete GL constituent supplied by A59, including noncuspidal ones.
Provides the positive block length whose multiple Galois summands must be excluded, after their exact twists have been proved.

api.name: DiscreteSpeh.quotient
api.statement: Construct the normalized induced representation, its unique irreducible quotient and the quotient morphism for m,b>=1; keep the ordered exponents as part of the comparison theorem.

api.name: DiscreteSpeh.rank
api.statement: The ambient general linear group has rank m*b.

api.name: DiscreteSpeh.length_one
api.statement: Speh(pi,1) is canonically isomorphic to pi.

api.name: DiscreteSpeh.character_twist
api.statement: For a unitary idele-class character chi, twisting pi by chi composed with det twists Speh(pi,b) by the same chi composed with the larger determinant.

api.name: DiscreteSpeh.unramified_support
api.statement: At a finite place where pi is unramified, the quotient is spherical and its Satake multiset is the union of the Satake parameters of the displayed b normalized twists; this does not assert a nonzero monodromy block.

tests.name: DiscreteSpeh.b_one
tests.statement: At b=1 the single exponent is zero and the quotient is pi, not a new carrier.

tests.name: DiscreteSpeh.GL2_character
tests.statement: At a nonarchimedean place, the unique irreducible quotient of normalized induction of chi|.|^(1/2), chi|.|^(-1/2) is chi composed with det.

tests.name: DiscreteSpeh.not_Steinberg
tests.statement: For unramified chi in the preceding GL2 case, the quotient is spherical with zero WD monodromy; it is not the Steinberg twist, which is the other constituent and has rank-one monodromy.

tests.name: DiscreteSpeh.twist_then_form
tests.statement: Twisting every inducing factor by the same character commutes with forming the quotient; b and the ambient rank m*b are unchanged.

items.name: Discrete GL spectrum consists of Speh quotients
items.locator: Moeglin-Waldspurger, Le spectre residuel de GL(n), introduction theorem printed605-606/PDF2-3.
items.statement: Over a number field F, an irreducible representation in the discrete automorphic spectrum of GL_N(A_F) with fixed unitary central character occurs with multiplicity one and is a Speh(pi,b) for N=m*b and a unitary cuspidal representation pi of GL_m(A_F), with the matching central character. The cuspidal-support class determines the corresponding Speh quotient. Thus a discrete constituent in A59 need not itself be cuspidal: b>1 is a genuine residual possibility.
items.proofOutline: Import the existing ET.7a Moeglin-Waldspurger proof target. The introduction identifies the only nonzero discrete cuspidal-support classes as repeated equal cuspidal factors and their unique irreducible quotient at the symmetric exponent string. Its number-field assertion gives one constituent in each such class. This continuation verified the theorem statement and quotient normalization, not the seventy-page proof.
items.note: Keep the spectral theorem separate from the Galois representation attached to its algebraically normalized cuspidal factors; the latter belongs to AG2.2.

items.name: Absolute residual irreducibility excludes every nontrivial discrete block decomposition
items.locator: Explicit adapter for LLHLM23 TheoremA.4.1; A50 plus the constituent interface of Labesse5.3 and the Moeglin-Waldspurger introduction.
items.statement: Let O be the integers of a finite extension K/Qp, let R be a continuous n-dimensional representation with a stable free O-lattice whose reduction is absolutely irreducible, and suppose a proved Galois-equivariant isomorphism over Kbar identifies R with the direct sum over 1<=i<=r and 0<=j<b_i of Q_(i,j) tensor chi_(i,j), where r,b_i>=1, each Q_(i,j) has positive dimension m_i and each chi_(i,j) is a character. Then r=1 and b_1=1 (hence m_1=n). In particular a compatible Galois realization of A59's Speh blocks forces exactly one cuspidal block. Equality of ranks or a proposed automorphic decomposition alone is not the required isomorphism.
items.proofOutline: A50 makes R absolutely irreducible. If sum_i b_i>1, the image of any one nonzero direct summand is a proper nonzero invariant subspace because all remaining summands have positive dimension. Hence sum_i b_i=1; positivity yields r=b_1=1. Repeated or isomorphic summands still give such subspaces. To apply this in A30, separately prove the algebraic normalization of each cuspidal factor, attach its Galois representation, match the exact cyclotomic/half-normalization twists on Frobenius polynomials, and invoke a proved density plus semisimple-uniqueness theorem. Those automorphic-to-Galois assembly inputs are not supplied by this elementary argument.

tests.name: SingleBlock.two_isobaric_parts
tests.statement: Dimensions 1+3 give total rank4 but an invariant rank1 summand; rank equality alone does not imply irreducibility.

tests.name: SingleBlock.residual_Speh_length_two
tests.statement: One Speh block with m=2,b=2 still gives two nonzero Galois summands after the realization theorem, so r=1 alone is insufficient.

tests.name: SingleBlock.repeated_characters
tests.statement: The sum chi direct-sum chi is reducible despite identical Frobenius eigenvalues; distinct eigenvalues are not needed in the proof.

tests.name: SingleBlock.n_one
tests.statement: If n=1 and all summand dimensions are positive, the count forces r=b_1=m_1=1.

items.name: Finite algebra over an Artinian ring is Artinian
items.statement: For rings R,S with an R-module structure and compatible scalar tower R,S,S, if R is Artinian and S is finite as an R-module, then S is an Artinian ring.
items.note: Exact statement and variable context read in the pinned tree by Codex — codex-a71f92, 2026-09-23. Existing generic supplier, not new formalization.

items.name: Reduced Artinian ring is its finite product of residue fields
items.statement: For a commutative Artinian reduced ring R, IsArtinianRing.equivPi R is an R-algebra equivalence R ≃ ∏_(m:MaximalSpectrum R) R/m; its component at m sends x to its residue class. The maximal spectrum is finite and each factor is a field.
items.note: Exact statement and variable context read in the pinned tree by Codex — codex-a71f92, 2026-09-23. Existing generic supplier, not new formalization.

items.name: Localization preserves reducedness
items.statement: For a commutative reduced ring R and a submonoid M, every localization of R at M is reduced.
items.note: Exact statement and variable context read in the pinned tree by Codex — codex-a71f92, 2026-09-23. Existing generic supplier, not new formalization.

items.name: Localization at non-zero-divisors is injective
items.statement: For commutative rings R,S, a submonoid M of R and IsLocalization M S, if M is contained in the non-zero-divisors of R, the algebra map R→S is injective.
items.note: Exact statement and variable context read in the pinned tree by Codex — codex-a71f92, 2026-09-23. Existing generic supplier, not new formalization.

items.name: Ideal-killing algebra homomorphism descends to a quotient
items.statement: For a two-sided ideal I of an algebra A and an algebra map f:A→B killing every element of I, Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ I f gives A/I→B whose composite with the quotient map is f. Uniqueness follows from surjectivity of the quotient map; the ring-hom version is Ideal.Quotient.lift.

items.name: The topological ring quotient projection is an open quotient map
items.statement: For a commutative topological ring R and an ideal I, the canonical map R→R/I, where R/I has the quotient topology, is an open quotient map. Thus continuity of a map out of R/I can be checked after composition with that projection.
items.note: Exact statement and variable context read in the pinned tree by Codex — codex-a71f92, 2026-09-23. Existing generic supplier, not new formalization.

items.name: Characteristic-zero field factors faithfully detect a reduced finite flat Hecke algebra
items.statement: Let O be the ring of integers of a finite extension E/Qp, and T a nonzero commutative finite flat reduced O-algebra. There are finitely many finite field extensions E_i/E and O-algebra maps x_i:T→E_i whose product is injective. More precisely T[1/varpi] is a finite reduced E-algebra, canonically the product of its residue fields, and x_i are the localization map followed by these projections. Hence t=0 in T iff x_i(t)=0 for every i. No claim is made that T itself is a product of its integral field-factor rings.
items.locator: CHT Proposition3.4.4 integral-Hecke descent (same source as A48); Stacks tags 00JB,00J8,00EW; explicit field-detection adapter for LLHLM23 A.4.1.
items.proofOutline: O-flatness gives varpi-torsion-freeness, so powers of varpi are non-zero-divisors and L65 makes T→T[1/varpi] injective. Localizing finitely many O-module generators spans a finite-dimensional E-algebra. It is reduced by L64 and Artinian by L62. L63 identifies it with a finite product of its residue fields. Each residue field is a quotient of a finite-dimensional E-vector space and hence finite over E. Compose the injective localization map with the equivalence. This uses every field factor, including factors with repeated-looking eigenvalue data; no unproved density assertion replaces injectivity.

tests.statement: For T={(a,b) in Zp^2:a≡b mod p}, T is local, finite free and reduced. Its two Qp-coordinate maps jointly detect zero, but T is not Zp×Zp: (1,0) is not in T.

items.name: Ideal factorization can be checked on jointly faithful coefficient maps
items.statement: Let R,T and F_i be commutative O-algebras, I an ideal of R, f:R→T an O-algebra map and x_i:T→F_i O-algebra maps with injective product. Then f factors uniquely through R/I if and only if every composite x_i∘f kills I. For finite flat reduced T as in A63 it suffices to use all the characteristic-zero field factors. If f is continuous and R/I carries the quotient topology, the descended map is continuous; if f is local between local rings and I is contained in the maximal ideal of R, the descended map is local.
items.locator: LLHLM23 §6.1.1 PDF125–126 and A.4.1 PDF196–198: explicit ideal-kernel adapter; pinned quotient and open-quotient-map universal properties.
items.proofOutline: For a∈I, every x_i(f(a)) vanishes, so injectivity of the product forces f(a)=0. L66 constructs the unique algebra map R/I→T. Conversely a factored map kills I, so do all composites. For continuity apply L67's quotient-map universal property to the equality of the composite with f. Locality follows because an element outside the quotient maximal ideal has a representative outside the maximal ideal of R, whose image under a local map is a unit. No reducedness of R or flatness of R/I is needed for this algebraic step.

tests.statement: For R=T=O[epsilon]/(epsilon^2), f=id and I=(epsilon), every field-valued composite kills I, but f does not factor through R/I. The maps are not jointly faithful.

tests.statement: For R=T=O×k, f=id and I=0×k, all characteristic-zero points kill I but f does not. This fails the flatness hypothesis needed to obtain joint faithfulness.

items.name: Integral Hecke representation factors through the closed monodromy-bounded quotient
items.statement: In the corrected LLHLM23 AppendixA.4 setting, let T be a nonzero reduced finite flat local O-Hecke image algebra (the projected image T_i^pr at auxiliary level), and let f_v:R_rhobar_v^framed→T classify the local restriction of the already constructed integral representation. Set R_v^D=R_rhobar_v^(lambda_v+eta,<=tau_v), with the closed reduced-union convention of P02. Suppose that for every characteristic-zero field-factor map x_i of A63, after a finite coefficient extension if necessary, x_i∘f_v corresponds to a potentially semistable representation of Hodge type lambda_v+eta and WD inertial type tau_i<=tau_v. Then f_v factors uniquely, continuously and locally through R_v^D. Apply this separately at every v|p, preserving any determinant/multiplier equation already satisfied by f_v.
items.locator: LLHLM23 §6.1.1 PDF125–126, DefinitionA.3.1 PDF190, A.4 setup PDF195–196 and TheoremA.4.1 PDF196–198; explicit assembly of A55 with the reduced integral Hecke algebra.
items.proofOutline: Let I_v define the reduced union R_v^D. Each exact-type characteristic-zero point lies in its own Zariski closure by definition, and that closure is one of the subspaces in the dominated union. Thus I_v is killed by every x_i∘f_v (vanishing after a finite field extension already implies vanishing before it). A64 gives the unique integral factorization. The quotient topology and local-ring hypotheses give its continuity/locality. Algebraic identities such as fixed determinant or multiplier survive this factorization; no new choice of polarization is made. This finishes the point-to-integral step conditional on the automorphic constituent/type inputs. It neither proves those inputs nor asserts that every point of an exact-type closure still has exact monodromy type. For the usual complete-local topologies, the quotient topology is the maximal-ideal-adic topology because the quotient maps each power of the source maximal ideal onto the corresponding power in the quotient.

items.name: Linear maps on a tensor product are determined by pure tensors
items.statement: For modules M,N over a commutative semiring R and R-linear maps g,h:M tensor_R N→P, equality g(m tensor n)=h(m tensor n) for every m,n implies g=h. The pinned declaration allows compatible semilinear maps, so this linear specialization has weaker requirements than the automorphic application.

items.name: Global Whittaker transform with fixed character and right action
items.statement: Let F be a number field, A its adeles, n>=1, and psi:A/F→C^× a nontrivial continuous unitary additive character. For upper unitriangular N_n put psi_N(u)=psi(sum_{i=1}^{n-1}u_(i,i+1)). For a smooth complex automorphic function phi in the smooth globalization (not only its K-infinity-finite subspace) define W_psi(phi)(g)=integral over N_n(F)\N_n(A) of phi(ug)psi_N(u)^(-1) du. Use the invariant probability quotient measure, compatible with the successive additive quotients. The compact quotient makes this integral convergent; the map is complex-linear, smooth, and intertwines right translation R(h)phi(x)=phi(xh) with right translation on W. Its image satisfies W(ug)=psi_N(u)W(g). This construction alone does not assert that W is nonzero.
items.locator: Cogdell, L-functions and Converse Theorems for GL_n, author-hosted PCMI notes (2002), Lecture1, printed5–7/PDF9–11 and printed10/PDF14; Cogdell, Lectures on L-functions, Converse Theorems, and Functoriality for GL_n, Fields Institute notes (2003), Lecture4, printed29–31/PDF33–35.
items.proofOutline: Build psi_N from the adjacent-superdiagonal sum, which adds under multiplication; it is trivial on N_n(F). The product phi(ug)psi_N(u)^(-1) descends to the compact homogeneous quotient (not a quotient group in general). Use AF.3's unipotent quotient and AA.2's invariant measure, then differentiation under a compact integral for smoothness. Substitution u↦u u0 in the right-invariant quotient measure proves W(u0 g)=psi_N(u0)W(g). Linearity and right-translation compatibility follow directly. Haar/Fubini/quotient and smooth-globalization suppliers are imported, not newly certified.

api.name: GlobalWhittakerTransform.map_add_smul

api.name: GlobalWhittakerTransform.unipotent_left
api.statement: W(phi)(u g)=psi_N(u)W(phi)(g) for u∈N_n(A).

api.name: GlobalWhittakerTransform.right_translate
api.statement: W(R(h)phi)(g)=W(phi)(g h); the action is not left translation on phi.

api.name: GlobalWhittakerTransform.at_identity

tests.name: GlobalWhittaker.rank_one
tests.statement: For n=1, W(phi)(g)=phi(g), and Lambda(phi)=phi(1).

tests.name: GlobalWhittaker.translation_sign

tests.name: GlobalWhittaker.GL3_nonabelian
tests.statement: Writing u(a,b,c)=[[1,a,b],[0,1,c],[0,0,1]], u(a,b,c)u(a',b',c')=u(a+a',b+b'+a*c',c+c'), while psi_N(u)=psi(a+c) is multiplicative. The central coordinate b is not a simple-root coordinate.

tests.name: GlobalWhittaker.constant_not_cuspidal
tests.statement: For n>=2 the constant automorphic function 1 has W(1)=0 for nontrivial psi_N; injectivity is not asserted outside the cuspidal subspace.

items.name: Nonzero last-column Fourier coefficients detect a cuspidal mirabolic function
items.statement: For n>=2 write P_n={[[h,y],[0,1]]}, h∈GL_(n-1), and Y_n={[[I,y],[0,1]]}. Let f be a smooth left P_n(F)-invariant function on P_n(A) whose constant terms along every proper standard parabolic radical of GL_n vanish. Put C_x f(p)=integral over F^(n-1)\A^(n-1) of f(y(t)p)psi(-x t) dt for a row x∈F^(n-1), and e=(0,...,0,1). Then C_0 f=0 and C_(e gamma) f(p)=C_e f(diag(gamma,1)p) for gamma∈GL_(n-1)(F). The rows e gamma exhaust the nonzero rows, indexed by P_(n-1)(F)\GL_(n-1)(F). If C_e f(diag(gamma,1)p)=0 for every gamma at a fixed p, then f(p)=0.
items.locator: Cogdell, L-functions and Converse Theorems for GL_n, author-hosted PCMI notes (2002), Lecture1, proof of Theorem1.1, printed7–8/PDF11–12; Cogdell, Lectures on L-functions, Converse Theorems, and Functoriality for GL_n, Fields Institute notes (2003), Lecture4, printed29–31/PDF33–35.
items.proofOutline: Y_n is the radical for (n-1)+1, so cuspidality kills its trivial coefficient. The product formula gives volume preservation under t↦gamma t for rational gamma; left rational invariance gives the displayed coefficient identity. Elementary row-basis completion gives transitivity on nonzero rows and the exact row stabilizer P_(n-1). AL.0's character duality identifies every character of the compact additive quotient with x∈F^(n-1). If all coefficients vanish, Fourier uniqueness for continuous functions on that quotient gives f(y(t)p)=0, hence f(p)=0. Only uniqueness is used here, not a rearrangement of an infinite multiple Fourier series.

tests.name: A67.GL2_base
tests.statement: For n=2, Y_2 is F\A, the expansion is the classical one and the index set P_1(F)\GL_1(F) is F^*, recovering the GL_2 Fourier expansion.

tests.name: A67.cuspidality_needed_only_for_C0
tests.statement: Without the vanishing of the constant term along Y_n the term C_0 f survives and the displayed expansion acquires an extra summand; every other step is unaffected, which is why the hypothesis is stated as the vanishing of constant terms and nothing stronger.

tests.name: A67.two_orbits
tests.statement: GL_(n-1)(F) acting on F^(n-1) has exactly the orbits {0} and F^(n-1) minus {0}; for n=2 that is {0} and F^*, and the stabiliser of e is trivial.

proofSteps: Restriction. A cusp form on GL_n(A) restricts to a smooth function on P_n(A) that remains left invariant under P_n(F), and its constant terms along the standard unipotent subgroups contained in P_n still vanish. Cogdell states exactly this, printed7: 'Simply by restriction of functions, a cusp form on GL_n(A) restricts to a smooth cuspidal function on P_n(A) which remains left invariant under P_n(k)', with cuspidal there defined by the vanishing of the integral over U(k)\U(A) for every standard unipotent U in P_n. The hypothesis of this item is that vanishing, so no cuspidality beyond it is used.

Fourier expansion along Y_n. P_n = GL_(n-1) semidirect Y_n with Y_n isomorphic to the row space F^(n-1), and y↦f(yp) is invariant under Y_n(F) because Y_n(F) is contained in P_n(F). Apply A104 to the compact quotient Y_n(F)\Y_n(A), which is (F\A)^(n-1): its characters are exactly y↦psi(<x,y>) for x in F^(n-1), under the pairing <x,y>=sum x_i y_i that Cogdell fixes on printed8. This gives f(p)=sum over x in F^(n-1) of C_x f(p), with C_x f(p) the coefficient integral of the statement taken against A105's invariant probability measure.

The zero coefficient vanishes. C_0 f(p) is the integral of f(yp) over Y_n(F)\Y_n(A), and Y_n is a standard unipotent subgroup of GL_n contained in P_n, so this is one of the constant terms the hypothesis kills. Cogdell, printed8: 'Since phi(p) is cuspidal and Y_n is a standard unipotent subgroup of GL_n, we see that phi_0(p) = 0.' This is the only place cuspidality is used in this item.

The nonzero coefficients form one orbit. GL_(n-1)(F) acts on F^(n-1) with exactly two orbits, {0} and its complement, the latter being the orbit of e=(0,...,0,1); the stabiliser of the transpose of e is the transposed mirabolic. A change of variable in the defining integral gives C_(e gamma) f(p) = C_e f(diag(gamma,1)p), so the nonzero terms are indexed by P_(n-1)(F)\GL_(n-1)(F). Cogdell calls this 'an elementary calculation as before', printed8, and the indexing by P_(n-1)(k)\GL_(n-1)(k) is his displayed conclusion.

Conclusion. Combining the three previous steps, f(p) = sum over gamma in P_(n-1)(F)\GL_(n-1)(F) of C_e f(diag(gamma,1)p). If every term vanishes at a fixed p then the whole Fourier expansion of y↦f(yp) vanishes, so f(p)=0 by the uniqueness half of A104. That is the last assertion of the statement, and it is what A69 consumes.

items.name: The last-column coefficient remains cuspidal on the smaller mirabolic
items.statement: For n>=3, with f,Y_n,P_n,C_e as in A67 and fixed p∈P_n(A), define f_p'(p')=C_e f(diag(p',1)p) on P_(n-1)(A). It is smooth, left P_(n-1)(F)-invariant, and has zero constant term along each proper standard parabolic radical of GL_(n-1). For n=2 the smaller mirabolic is P_1={1}, with no cuspidality condition. With compatible quotient measures, its Whittaker transform satisfies W_(f_p')(p')=W_f(diag(p',1)p).
items.locator: Cogdell, L-functions and Converse Theorems for GL_n, author-hosted PCMI notes (2002), Lecture1, Theorem1.1 proof, printed8–9/PDF12–13 (the invariance/cuspidality check and the iterated integral).
items.proofOutline: Rational elements of P_(n-1) stabilize the last-row character, so the same change of variables proves invariance. For the maximal parabolic a+(n-1-a), 1<=a<=n-2, split Y_n's column into coordinates 1..a and a+1..n-1. The character psi(t_(n-1)) is trivial on the first group. That first group together with the smaller radical is precisely the GL_n radical for a+(n-a). Its constant term is zero; integrate the remaining column coordinates afterwards. They normalize the enlarged radical, and the character is unchanged. General standard parabolics follow by transitivity of constant terms. All unipotent quotients in this calculation are compact, justifying Fubini. Finally N_n=N_(n-1)⋉Y_n and the two characters multiply to psi_N; the iterated integral is W_f at the displayed block-diagonal argument.

tests.name: A68.n_equals_2_base
tests.statement: For n=2 the smaller mirabolic is P_1={1}, there is no cuspidality condition to inherit, and the identity reduces to the definition of the GL_2 Whittaker function.

tests.name: A68.measure_compatibility_used
tests.statement: If the three invariant measures were normalised independently the unfolding would produce W_f(diag(p',1)p) times a constant, so the identity as stated needs A105's compatibility and not merely the existence of invariant measures.

tests.name: A68.psi_trivial_on_F
tests.statement: If psi were not trivial on F then C_e f would not be left Y_n(F)-invariant and f_p' would not descend to the smaller mirabolic quotient; the hypothesis on psi in A66 is used here.

proofSteps: Smoothness and Y_n(F)-invariance of the coefficient. For y in Y_n(A) one has C_e f(yp) = psi(y_(n-1)) C_e f(p), directly from the defining integral and the translation invariance of the measure. Since psi is trivial on F, C_e f is left invariant under Y_n(F); Cogdell records both, printed8: 'phi_(te_(n-1))(yp) = psi(y_(n-1)) phi_(te_(n-1))(p)' and 'Since psi is trivial on k we see that phi_(te_(n-1))(p) is left invariant under Y_n(k)'. Smoothness is inherited from f because the integral is over a compact quotient.

Left P_(n-1)(F)-invariance of f_p'. By A67's equivariance C_(e gamma) f(p) = C_e f(diag(gamma,1)p), the function p'↦C_e f(diag(p',1)p) is unchanged when p' is multiplied on the left by an element of P_(n-1)(F), since such an element fixes e. Together with the previous step this is the invariance the statement asserts.

Cuspidality descends. A standard unipotent subgroup U' of GL_(n-1) contained in P_(n-1) gives a standard unipotent subgroup of GL_n contained in P_n after the embedding p'↦diag(p',1), and the constant term of f_p' along U' is a constant term of f along that larger group, computed with A105's compatible measures. It therefore vanishes with f's. For n=2 the smaller mirabolic is P_1={1} and there is no condition to check, which is the base of the induction; Cogdell marks that base explicitly, printed8: 'Note that if n = 2 this is exactly the fact we used previously for GL_2. This then begins our induction.'

The Whittaker identity. Structurally P_n = GL_(n-1) semidirect Y_n and N_n = N_(n-1) semidirect Y_n. Unfolding and using A105's compatibility of the invariant probability measures on N_n(F)\N_n(A), N_(n-1)(F)\N_(n-1)(A) and Y_n(F)\Y_n(A), the Whittaker transform of f_p' is the double integral of f(y n' diag(p',1) p) against psi^(-1)(y_(n-1)) psi^(-1)(n'), which is the single integral over N_n(F)\N_n(A) of f(n diag(p',1) p) psi^(-1)(n). That is W_f(diag(p',1)p). Cogdell performs exactly this computation, printed9, concluding 'W_(phi'_(delta p))(delta') = W_phi(delta' delta p)'. The Fubini step is where A105 is load-bearing: without the compatibility of the three normalisations the two iterated integrals would differ by a constant.

items.name: The Whittaker transform is injective on GL_n cusp forms
items.statement: For F,psi,n as in A66, if a smooth cusp form phi on GL_n(F)\GL_n(A) has W_psi(phi)(g)=0 for every g, then phi=0. The analogous assertion holds on P_n(A) for the cuspidal mirabolic functions of A67. This is the injectivity consequence of the Piatetski-Shapiro–Shalika Fourier expansion; no assertion about noncuspidal automorphic forms or other reductive groups is included.
items.locator: Cogdell, L-functions and Converse Theorems for GL_n, author-hosted PCMI notes (2002), Lecture1, Theorem1.1 and its induction, printed7–9/PDF11–13; Cogdell, Lectures on L-functions, Converse Theorems, and Functoriality for GL_n, Fields Institute notes (2003), Lecture4, printed31/PDF35.
items.proofOutline: Induct on n for mirabolic functions. P_1 is trivial and its Whittaker transform is the identity. If W_f=0, A68 makes W_(f_p')=0 for every p. The induction hypothesis gives f_p'=0, so C_e f(p)=0 for every p. Apply A67 to obtain f=0. For a cusp form phi on GL_n, restrict each right translate p↦phi(p g) to P_n(A); the cuspidality equations remain valid. Its Whittaker transform is p↦W_phi(p g)=0, so evaluation at p=1 gives phi(g)=0 for every g. This proof needs compact Fourier uniqueness and compact Fubini, not the stronger absolute-uniform-convergence part of Cogdell's expansion theorem.

tests.name: WhittakerInjective.rank_one
tests.statement: At n=1 the transform is the identity.

tests.name: WhittakerInjective.constant_function
tests.statement: For n>=2 the constant automorphic function has zero transform but is nonzero and noncuspidal.

tests.name: WhittakerInjective.all_arguments
tests.statement: Vanishing only at g=1 is not the hypothesis; the transform must vanish at every g.

proofSteps: Base case n=1. P_1 is the trivial group, N_1 is trivial and the Whittaker transform is the identity map on functions, so W_f=0 forces f=0. This is the rank_one test.

Induction step for mirabolic functions. Let f be a cuspidal function on P_n(F)\P_n(A) with W_f=0. A68's identity W_f(diag(p',1)p) = W_{f'_p}(p') exhibits the Whittaker transform of f'_p, where f'_p(p')=C_e f(diag(p',1)p), as a restriction of W_f; so W_{f'_p}=0 for every p. A68 also shows that f'_p is a cuspidal function on P_(n-1)(F)\P_(n-1)(A), which is what makes the induction hypothesis applicable, and that step uses A105's compatible measures rather than mere existence of invariant ones.
The induction hypothesis gives f'_p=0 for every p, that is C_e f(diag(p',1)p)=0 for all p' and p. Taking p'=1 gives C_e f(p)=0 for every p in P_n(A).

All Fourier coefficients vanish. By A67's two-orbit decomposition, the coefficients along the open orbit are C_(e gamma) f(p) = C_e f(diag(gamma,1)p) for gamma in P_(n-1)(F)\GL_(n-1)(F), all of which vanish by the previous step, and the coefficient at 0 vanishes by cuspidality — the one place cuspidality enters A67.

Conclusion on the mirabolic group. A104's uniqueness half — that gamma ↦ psi_gamma identifies F^(n-1) with the character group of the compact (F\A)^(n-1), so a function with all Fourier coefficients zero is zero — turns the vanishing of every coefficient into f=0. This is A67's conclusion, invoked here rather than reproved.

Cusp forms on GL_n. Let phi be a smooth cusp form with W_psi(phi)(g)=0 for every g. Fix g and put f(p)=phi(pg); by A68's descent f is a cuspidal function on P_n(F)\P_n(A), and W_f(p)=W_psi(phi)(pg)=0, so the mirabolic case gives f=0, that is phi(pg)=0 for all p. Taking p=1 gives phi(g)=0, and g was arbitrary.

Provenance and scope. Cogdell states the consequence in one sentence (Fields notes, printed 31): 'since we can recover phi from W_phi through its Fourier expansion we are guaranteed that W_phi != 0 for all phi != 0'. Cuspidality is not decoration: the constant function on GL_n(F)\GL_n(A) has zero transform for n>=2, which is the constant_function non-example. Nothing here asserts anything about noncuspidal forms or about other reductive groups.

items.name: A nonzero cuspidal GL_n representation has a nonzero global Whittaker functional
items.statement: Let Pi be a nonzero smooth cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n(A_F) in A66's complex convention. Then Lambda(phi)=W_psi(phi)(1) is a nonzero linear functional satisfying Lambda(Pi(u)phi)=psi_N(u)Lambda(phi) for u∈N_n(A_F). Use the smooth globalization at infinity for the continuous-functional statement, rather than an arbitrary algebraic functional on a Harish–Chandra module.
items.locator: Cogdell, Lectures on L-functions, Converse Theorems, and Functoriality for GL_n, Fields Institute notes (2003), Lecture4, Corollary4.1.2 and its preceding integral, printed33/PDF37; Cogdell, L-functions and Converse Theorems for GL_n, author-hosted PCMI notes (2002), Lecture1, printed10–11/PDF14–15 (identity-evaluation typo corrected as E45).
items.proofOutline: Choose nonzero phi. A69 gives g with W_phi(g)≠0. Right-translation stability and A66 yield Lambda(Pi(g)phi)=W_phi(g)≠0. The unipotent equivariance is A66's identity at g=1. Compact integration is continuous in the smooth automorphic topology supplied by AF.1/AF.0. No uniqueness theorem for Whittaker models is needed to prove nonvanishing. A chosen phi can satisfy Lambda(phi)=0; nonvanishing is a property of the functional on the representation, not of every vector.

tests.name: GlobalGeneric.translate_to_detect
tests.statement: If W_phi(g0)≠0, the vector Pi(g0)phi has Lambda value W_phi(g0)≠0.

tests.name: GlobalGeneric.identity_only
tests.statement: A nonzero functional on a space of dimension greater than one can have a nonzero kernel; Lambda(phi)=0 does not imply phi=0.

tests.name: GlobalGeneric.GL1
tests.statement: A nonzero idele-class character has the rank-one functional phi↦phi(1) and no unipotent constraint.

tests.name: GlobalGeneric.archimedean_needs_continuity
tests.statement: An algebraic functional on K-finite vectors is not, merely by its definition, a continuous functional on the smooth globalization. A70 uses A106’s compact-integral continuity. Do not justify this using a universal n! dimension formula: for the trivial GL_2(R) representation and a nontrivial Whittaker character the algebraic Whittaker space is zero (E53).

proofSteps: Lambda is defined and continuous. Lambda(phi)=W_psi(phi)(1)=int_{N_n(F)\N_n(A)} phi(n) psi_N(n)^{-1} dn is an integral over a compact quotient taken with A105's probability measure, so it converges for every smooth phi, and A106 gives its continuity for the smooth moderate-growth topology on V_Pi. The same display appears in Cogdell's Fields notes, printed 33: 'Lambda(phi) = W_phi(e) = int_{N(k)\N(A)} phi(n) psi^{-1}(n) dn'.

Equivariance. For u in N_n(A_F), Lambda(Pi(u)phi) = int phi(nu) psi_N(n)^{-1} dn = psi_N(u) Lambda(phi), by translating the variable and using invariance of the measure; this is A66's defining identity evaluated at g=1.

Nonvanishing, by translation. Pi is nonzero, so choose phi in V_Pi with phi != 0. A69 gives a g with W_psi(phi)(g) != 0, and W_psi(phi)(g) = Lambda(Pi(g)phi) because the transform is the orbit map of Lambda under right translation. Hence Lambda(Pi(g)phi) != 0 and Lambda is not the zero functional. Cogdell records the dictionary in the local setting (printed 32): 'A model xi_v ↦ W_{xi_v} gives a functional by Lambda_v(xi_v)=W_{xi_v}(e) and a functional Lambda_v gives a model by setting W_{xi_v}(g)=Lambda_v(pi_v(g)xi_v)'; the global direction used here is the first half applied to the translate.

The continuous functional is the one just constructed by compact integration and A106. No dimension formula for all algebraic Whittaker functionals on arbitrary Harish–Chandra modules is needed. In particular Cogdell’s unqualified n! remark cannot be used universally: the trivial representation of GL_2(R) has no functional for a nontrivial Whittaker character. Keep the continuity requirement while leaving any more specialized algebraic-dimension theorem to its exact hypotheses (E53).

Scope. No uniqueness is claimed or used here: local uniqueness (Gelfand–Kazhdan and Shalika, Cogdell Theorem 4.1) and its global corollary are separate imports, and this item needs only existence. Genericity of the local components — Cogdell's Corollary 4.1.2, 'if (pi,V_pi) is cuspidal with pi = tensor' pi_v then pi and each of its local components pi_v are generic' — is reached from here through A71's one-place factorization, not asserted at this step.

items.name: A global Whittaker functional yields a nonzero finite-place functional
items.statement: Let v be a finite place of a number field F, and suppose the smooth automorphic representation Pi has the proved one-place algebraic factorization V_Pi≅V_(Pi_v) tensor_C V^v, where N_n(F_v) acts only on the first factor. If Lambda:V_Pi→C is a nonzero psi_N-equivariant linear functional, then there exists w∈V^v such that lambda_v(x)=Lambda(x tensor w) is nonzero and satisfies lambda_v(Pi_v(u)x)=psi_v(u)lambda_v(x). Thus Pi_v is generic when it is irreducible admissible. The frozen w must be chosen to detect Lambda; an arbitrary reference tensor need not work.
items.locator: Cogdell, Lectures on L-functions, Converse Theorems, and Functoriality for GL_n, Fields Institute notes (2003), Lecture4, printed32–33/PDF36–37, local-component restriction and Corollary4.1.2; explicit nonvanishing adapter.
items.proofOutline: Transport Lambda across the one-place factorization. If it vanished on every x tensor w, L68 would identify it with zero. Choose a detecting pure tensor and freeze its second factor; TensorProduct.mk/curry give linearity, and equivariance holds because the local unipotent acts only on x. Flath's factorization, including the passage from global smooth vectors to the algebraic tensor at one finite place, is imported from AF.2, not proved by L68. Only finite-place genericity is claimed, so no archimedean completed-tensor inference is hidden here. Neither local uniqueness nor an Euler-product factorization of Lambda is needed.

tests.name: LocalGeneric.choose_good_frozen_vector
tests.statement: For Lambda:C^2 tensor C^2→C given by Lambda(x tensor y)=x_1 y_1, freezing y=e_1 gives a nonzero functional; freezing y=e_2 gives zero.

tests.name: LocalGeneric.rank_one_tensor
tests.statement: If V^v=C and Lambda≠0, freezing 1 yields a nonzero functional on V_(Pi_v).

tests.name: LocalGeneric.scalar_ambiguity
tests.statement: Replacing the detecting w by c w for c≠0 multiplies lambda_v by c; the existence conclusion has no preferred normalization.

tests.name: A71.finite_sum_linear_independence
tests.statement: Every element of V_(Pi_v) tensor_C V^v is a finite sum sum_j x_j tensor w_j with the w_j linearly independent; if all the frozen functionals lambda_(w_j) vanished, Lambda would vanish on that element. This is the whole of the nonvanishing step, and it uses only linearity.

tests.name: A71.archimedean_place_excluded
tests.statement: A functional on a Harish–Chandra module is algebraic data; extension to a continuous functional on the smooth globalization requires a separate theorem. This finite-place argument supplies no such extension. E53 explains why an unqualified n! dimension assertion cannot justify it.

tests.name: A71.no_uniqueness_claimed
tests.statement: The construction produces one nonzero functional and says nothing about the dimension of the space of them; local uniqueness is a separate theorem (Gelfand-Kazhdan, Shalika) and is not used, so this item must not be cited for multiplicity one.

proofSteps: A107 supplies an abstract equivariant isomorphism V_Pi≅V_(Pi_v)⊗C V^v, with the finite-place group acting on the first factor. This is sufficient for the argument. It gives neither a product decomposition of automorphic functions nor a distinguished detecting vector in the other factor.

Every frozen vector gives an equivariant functional. For w in V^v set lambda_w(x) = Lambda(x tensor w); this is C-linear in x because the tensor map is. For u in N_n(F_v), embedded at v with trivial components elsewhere, Pi(u)(x tensor w) = (Pi_v(u)x) tensor w, since GL_n(F_v) acts through the first factor only; and psi_N(u) = psi_v(u) for such a u, the other local components of psi_N being evaluated at 1. Hence lambda_w(Pi_v(u)x) = Lambda(Pi(u)(x tensor w)) = psi_N(u)Lambda(x tensor w) = psi_v(u) lambda_w(x). So lambda_w is a psi_v-equivariant Whittaker functional on V_(Pi_v) for every w, with no hypothesis on w at all. Only nonvanishing is at stake.

Some frozen vector detects Lambda. Lambda is nonzero, so fix xi in V_Pi with Lambda(xi) != 0. Under the isomorphism of A107, xi is a finite sum xi = sum_(j=1)^m x_j tensor w_j, and we may take the w_j linearly independent in V^v by rewriting the sum over a basis of the span of its second factors. Then 0 != Lambda(xi) = sum_j lambda_(w_j)(x_j) by linearity of Lambda, so lambda_(w_j) != 0 for at least one j; take w to be that w_j and lambda_v = lambda_w. Linearity of Lambda is all that is used here, and L68 is the pinned form of the fact that a linear map on a tensor product is determined by its values on pure tensors, so no continuity or topology on V^v enters. This step is the content of the item's own warning that an arbitrary reference tensor need not work: the test A71 records for Lambda(x tensor y) = x_1 y_1 on C^2 tensor C^2, where freezing e_1 succeeds and freezing e_2 gives zero, is a two-dimensional instance of exactly this.

The constructed lambda_v is nonzero and psi_v-equivariant. For irreducible admissible Pi_v, the map x↦[g↦lambda_v(Pi_v(g)x)] has invariant kernel and is nonzero, hence is injective and realizes a Whittaker model. Thus Pi_v is generic, as in Cogdell Corollary4.1.2. This construction uses no local multiplicity-one theorem.

Only one finite-place functional is constructed. No uniqueness, normalized restricted tensor product or factorization of all Whittaker functionals is asserted. At an archimedean place an algebraic functional on K-finite vectors does not automatically extend continuously to a smooth globalization; that is an additional requirement. No universal n! dimension assertion is used (E53).

items.name: Determinant twists preserve the Whittaker functional space
items.statement: For a nonarchimedean local field K, a smooth complex representation pi of GL_n(K), a smooth character chi:K^×→C^× and a fixed nontrivial additive character psi_K, identify the underlying vector spaces of pi and pi tensor(chi∘det). Their psi_K-Whittaker functional spaces are equal: Hom_(N_n(K))(pi,psi_K)=Hom_(N_n(K))(pi tensor(chi∘det),psi_K). In particular genericity is preserved in both directions. This includes every complex modulus twist |det|^s with a fixed convention, including s=(1-n)/2.
items.locator: Cogdell, L-functions and Converse Theorems for GL_n, author-hosted PCMI notes (2002), Lecture1, printed5/PDF9 (unitary twisting convention) and printed10/PDF14 (functional equation); elementary specialization of that equation.
items.proofOutline: For u∈N_n(K), det(u)=1, so the twisted and untwisted actions of u coincide. Hence exactly the same linear maps satisfy the character-equivariance equation. This is an identity of Hom spaces on a fixed carrier, not a statement about a Galois character, its cyclotomic normalization, or continuity under an isomorphism of coefficient fields.

tests.name: WhittakerTwist.unipotent_determinant
tests.statement: For [[1,a],[0,1]], det=1, so pi tensor|det|^(-1/2) has precisely the same psi-equivariance equation as pi.

tests.name: WhittakerTwist.trivial_character
tests.statement: For chi=1 the identification is the identity.

tests.name: WhittakerTwist.not_automatic_genericity
tests.statement: For n>=2 a one-dimensional determinant representation has no nonzero functional for a nontrivial psi_N; determinant twisting does not turn this nongeneric representation into a generic one.

tests.name: WhittakerTwist.same_subspace_not_just_iso
tests.statement: On the unchanged carrier, the two equivariance conditions define the same subset of Hom_C(V_pi,C), so the identity preserves the chosen functional. An arbitrary abstract bijection also preserves nonvanishing but does not by itself identify that same functional.

tests.name: WhittakerTwist.psi_change_is_different
tests.statement: Replacing psi_K by a conjugate psi_K^t for t in the diagonal torus does change the Hom space in general; the invariance proved here is under determinant twists only.

proofSteps: The twisted action on the same carrier. By definition pi tensor (chi o det) has the same underlying complex vector space as pi, with (pi tensor (chi o det))(g)x = chi(det g) pi(g) x. So Hom_C(V_pi, C) is one and the same space for the two representations, and the two Whittaker Hom spaces are subsets of it rather than merely isomorphic spaces.

Unipotent matrices have determinant one. An element u of N_n(K) is upper triangular with all diagonal entries 1, so det(u) = 1 and chi(det u) = chi(1) = 1. Hence (pi tensor (chi o det))(u) = pi(u) as endomorphisms of V_pi, for every u in N_n(K). Nothing about chi is used beyond its being a homomorphism on K^x.

The two equivariance conditions are the same equation. A linear lambda : V_pi -> C lies in Hom_(N_n(K))(pi, psi_K) exactly when lambda(pi(u)x) = psi_K(u) lambda(x) for all u in N_n(K) and x in V_pi, and by the previous step that is verbatim the condition for lambda to lie in Hom_(N_n(K))(pi tensor (chi o det), psi_K). The two subsets of Hom_C(V_pi, C) therefore coincide, which is the asserted equality.

Consequences and their limits. Genericity, being nonvanishing of that space, transfers in both directions, and the statement covers every modulus twist |det|^s at a fixed convention, in particular s = (1-n)/2, since |det|^s is a smooth character of K^x composed with det. What the argument does not give: it says nothing about whether pi is generic to begin with, nothing about a change of the additive character psi_K (conjugating psi_K by a diagonal torus element permutes the Hom spaces, and that is a different statement), and nothing about a Galois-side cyclotomic normalization or about continuity under an isomorphism of coefficient fields, both of which the item's statement already excludes.

items.name: Cuspidal compact-unitary base change supplies generic split local factors
items.statement: Let F/F+ be a CM extension with [F+:Q]>1, n≥1, and G/F+ a unitary form compact at infinity equipped with an F-isomorphism G_F≅GL_n, as in LLHLM §9.1. Let sigma be an irreducible discrete automorphic representation to which the Labesse comparison A59 applies, and write its weak base change as an isobaric sum of Speh(pi_i,b_i), with pi_i cuspidal of positive rank m_i and n=Σ_i m_i b_i. Let R:G_F→GL_n(K) be continuous, K/Q_p finite, with a stable free O_K-lattice whose residual representation is absolutely irreducible. Assume the actual equivariant realization (R⊗Kbar)^ss≅⊕_i⊕_(j=0)^(b_i−1) R_i⊗ε^(−j), where dim R_i=m_i>0 and the summands are the normalized cuspidal factors of A79–A81. For every split finite v=ww^c of F+, assume the actual local base-change isomorphism Pi_w≅sigma_v transported through the chosen G(F+_v)≅GL_n(F_w), supplied by A59. Then the isobaric sum has exactly one block of length one and is cuspidal. Each such transported sigma_v has a nonzero smooth algebraic Whittaker functional for a nondegenerate character of N_n(F_w), and so does its determinant twist |det|^((1−n)/2). This includes v|p. Under a chosen coefficient-field isomorphism Qpbar≅C, transport both the representation and its Whittaker character; the same nonzero algebraic Hom space is transported. No coefficient-field topology, continuous archimedean transport, finite coefficient-field descent, temperedness or p-adic Hodge/monodromy conclusion is asserted.
items.locator: LLHLM23 TheoremA.4.1 PDF196–198 and EGH7.2.1 PDF55–56; Labesse5.3 split-place comparison as A59; Cogdell, Lectures on L-functions, Converse Theorems, and Functoriality for GL_n, Fields Institute notes (2003), Lecture4, Corollary4.1.2 printed33/PDF37.
items.proofOutline: Apply A50 before A62: absolute residual irreducibility makes R⊗Kbar irreducible, hence identical to its semisimplification. Compose with the hypothesized A78 realization. A62 then forces r=b_1=1. Apply A70 and A71 to the resulting cuspidal Pi; carry the functional through the actual split-place isomorphism, and use A72 for the determinant twist. Semilinear coefficient transport carries both sides of the character-equivariance equation and preserves nonvanishing and open stabilizers.
