tests.name: SplitGeneric.not_residual_genericity
tests.statement: The conclusion is Whittaker genericity of a characteristic-zero smooth representation. It implies neither adequacy of a residual Galois representation nor the noncyclotomic Frobenius-ratio condition.

tests.name: SplitGeneric.Speh_rank_two
tests.statement: The GL_2 Speh quotient from a character with length2 is a determinant character and nongeneric. A single discrete block is insufficient until its length is proved to be1.

tests.name: SplitGeneric.no_type_dictionary
tests.statement: Whittaker nonvanishing alone does not imply Hom_K(sigma(tau),pi)≠0 for a prescribed tau, nor a specified Hodge type.

tests.name: SplitGeneric.semisimplification_bridge
tests.statement: A78 initially gives an isomorphism only for R^ss. A50 first identifies an absolutely irreducible R with R^ss; without that step the input is not literally A62’s actual decomposition.

tests.name: SplitGeneric.split_model_required
tests.statement: For a general inner form at a split place, do not replace its local transfer by a GL_n intertwining isomorphism without a split-model hypothesis. LLHLM supplies G_F≅GL_n.

tests.name: SplitGeneric.transport_character_too
tests.statement: Under complex conjugation, the C4-character sending a generator to i becomes the character sending it to −i. The transported one-dimensional functional is equivariant for the transported character; keeping the original i-character would make the equation fail.

tests.name: SplitGeneric.rank_one
tests.statement: At n=1 there is one length-one rank-one block, the determinant exponent is zero and the unipotent group is trivial; a nonzero linear functional suffices.

items.previousStatement: In A59's compact-unitary setting with [F+:Q]>1, assume the exact Galois realization of all discrete Speh constituents needed by A62 has been proved and the stable residual lattice is absolutely irreducible. Then A62 gives one cuspidal GL_n(A_F) base-change constituent Pi. At every finite split place v=ww^c of F+, the representation sigma_v transported by G(F_v+)≅GL_n(F_w) is generic; so is its twist by |det|^((1-n)/2). This includes places above the coefficient prime. If coefficients are transported along a chosen abstract field isomorphism Qpbar≅C, the same nonzero algebraic smooth Whittaker Hom is transported; no topological isomorphism or descent to a finite coefficient field is asserted.

hypotheses.statement: F/F+ is CM, [F+:Q]>1, G is compact at infinity and an explicit F-isomorphism G_F≅GL_n is fixed. At a chosen split place, use the resulting group isomorphism, not a Jacquet–Langlands transfer from a nonsplit inner form.
A59–A61 supply the same weak base-change representation Pi=boxplus_i Speh(pi_i,b_i), with r,b_i,m_i≥1 and n=Σm_i b_i; at the finite split place its component is isomorphic to the transported sigma_v.
R is a continuous representation over a finite extension K/Q_p with a free stable O_K-lattice of rank n and absolutely irreducible reduction.

A proved equivariant isomorphism identifies (R⊗Kbar)^ss with the direct sum of the positive-rank normalized factors R_i⊗ε^(−j), not merely a rank identity or a proposed automorphic parameter. A78 produces this isomorphism from its separate realization, polynomial and density inputs.

Use the actual global functional from A70 and finite-place tensor comparison from A71/A107. These consume their Fourier, measure and globalization suppliers; neither global uniqueness nor a normalized product of all local functionals is required.

proofSteps: Local carrier. Fix a split finite v and one w|v. The projection F⊗F+ F+_v→F_w and the stipulated F-splitting of G give iota_w:G(F+_v)≅GL_n(F_w). The LLHLM §9.1 source explicitly supplies this splitting. The argument is only for this carrier; being a unitary inner form compact at infinity alone would not assert a GL_n identification at every split place.

Remove the semisimplification ambiguity. By A50, a stable lattice with absolutely irreducible residual representation makes R absolutely irreducible. Hence R⊗Kbar is simple and its semisimplification is isomorphic to it. Compose that isomorphism with the realized-semisimplification hypothesis. This is the actual isomorphism required by A62; a Hecke polynomial identity without A78 is insufficient.

Exclude all residual blocks. If Σ_i b_i>1, the image of one positive-dimensional direct summand is a nonzero proper invariant subspace of R⊗Kbar. This contradicts irreducibility. Since r and every b_i are positive, Σ_i b_i=1 forces r=1 and b_1=1; the dimension identity then gives m_1=n. Repeated or isomorphic summands still give proper subspaces, so no eigenvalue-distinctness condition is used.

Identify the cuspidal representation. Speh(pi_1,1)=pi_1 by A60, and pi_1 is cuspidal by construction. Thus the same Pi delivered by base change is a cuspidal GL_n automorphic representation. Its algebraic normalization exponent from A79 is (m_1+b_1−n−1)/2=0. There is no remaining half-cyclotomic character or change of the automorphic carrier.

Produce a global detecting functional. A70 gives nonzero Lambda on Pi, equivariant for psi_N. Its proof chooses a translate detected by the injective Whittaker transform and obtains continuity at infinity from A106. The present conclusion uses existence, not local/global uniqueness or an Euler-product factorization.

Pass to one finite place. Under A71/A107, write V_Pi≅V_(Pi_w) tensor V^w. Since pure tensors span and Lambda is nonzero, choose x0,w0 with Lambda(x0 tensor w0)≠0. Then lambda_w(x)=Lambda(x tensor w0) is nonzero and satisfies lambda_w(Pi_w(u)x)=psi_w(u)lambda_w(x). The nontrivial local character and local action conventions are those of the imported Whittaker carrier.

Transport through local base change. For an intertwining isomorphism T:V_(sigma_v transported)→V_(Pi_w), put lambda_sigma=lambda_w∘T. Surjectivity of T preserves nonvanishing, and its intertwining property proves the same N-equivariance. The split-place comparison holds at ramified as well as unramified split places. No step used residue characteristic different from the coefficient prime, so this finite-place argument includes v|p.

Normalize the determinant twist. For u∈N_n(F_w), det(u)=1. The actions before and after |det|^((1−n)/2) therefore coincide on N, so exactly the same functional works by A72. This is a characteristic-zero field statement and does not invoke an integral co-Whittaker theorem in residue characteristic p.

Transport coefficients algebraically. Write iota:k→C for the chosen field isomorphism and V^iota for the transported vector space. If T is the iota-semilinear identification, define lambda_k=iota^(-1)∘lambda_C∘T and psi_k=iota^(-1)∘psi_C. Additivity, scalar linearity and lambda_k(rho_k(u)x)=psi_k(u)lambda_k(x) follow by applying iota^(-1) to the equation over C; nonzero values remain nonzero. The inverse construction gives the Hom-space identification. The group stabilizers of vectors and kernel of psi are unchanged, so smoothness at the finite place survives. This makes no continuity claim for iota or for an archimedean globalization.

Boundary of the conclusion. The result is characteristic-zero local Whittaker genericity. It neither implies residual adequacy/noncyclotomic Frobenius ratios nor supplies a prescribed K-type occurrence or Hodge/monodromy type. Those remain the separate A74–A76 and A55/A65 consumers.

items.name: Algebraic automorphic forms with coefficient sigma(lambda,tau)^* decompose by K-type occurrence at p
items.statement: In the AppendixA.4 setting let U=G(O_p)U^p be sufficiently small with U_p=prod_{v in S_p}G(O_{F_v^+}), and let W be a G(O_p)-stable O-lattice in tensor_{v in S_p} sigma(lambda_v,tau_v)^* o iota_v, where sigma(lambda_v,tau_v)=V(lambda_v) tensor sigma(tau_v) as in LLHLM23 §6.2 and sigma(tau_v) is as in N58. Fix iota:Qpbar≅C. Keeping the smooth factor sigma(tau)^* at p and moving the algebraic factor tensor V(lambda_v)^* to the infinite places through iota gives an isomorphism, equivariant for the Hecke algebra away from S, S(U,W) tensor_(O,iota) C ≅ Hom_(U×G(F+_infinity))(V(lambda)_(iota,infinity) tensor sigma(tau)_C, A) ≅ direct sum over automorphic pi of G(A_F+) with pi_infinity≅V(lambda)_(iota,infinity) of m(pi) (pi^(infinity,p))^(U^p) tensor Hom_(G(O_p))(tensor_v sigma(tau_v) o iota_v tensor_iota C, pi_p). Here A is the space of automorphic forms and V(lambda)_(iota,infinity) is the irreducible algebraic representation of the compact group G(F+_infinity) attached to tensor V(lambda_v) through iota. In particular S(U,W)[1/p] tensor Qpbar is a semisimple Hecke module, and a Hecke eigensystem occurs in it iff it is the eigensystem of such a pi with (pi^(infinity,p))^(U^p)≠0 and Hom_(G(O_p))(sigma(tau),pi_p)≠0. The Hodge normalization of the attached Galois representation is not asserted here; it is the one of A55 and E33.
items.locator: LLHLM23 (A.2) PDF194 and TheoremA.4.1 PDF196 (coefficient lattice in tensor sigma(lambda_v,tau_v)^*); CHT Lemma3.3.1 PDF99, Proposition3.3.2 and its proof PDF100–102, Corollary3.3.3 PDF102; EGH §7.1.2 PDF53 and Lemma7.1.6 PDF55.
items.proofOutline: For U sufficiently small, f↦(f(t_j))_j identifies S(U,W) with a finite free O-module (CHT Lemma3.3.1), and S(U,W) tensor_O C=S(U,W tensor_(O,iota) C). CHT's map i(f)(alpha)(g)=alpha(xi_(a,iota)(g_infinity)^(-1)(xi_a(g_l)f(g^infinity))) in the proof of Proposition3.3.2 moves only the algebraic factor of the coefficient to infinity and keeps the smooth factor (there rho_v at S(B)) at its finite places; applied with the smooth factor sigma(tau)^* at p it gives the first isomorphism. Since G(F+_infinity) is compact, A is a semisimple admissible G(A^infinity)-module (CHT Corollary3.3.3), so Hom over U×G(F+_infinity) splits over the isotypic decomposition, and Schur's lemma for the compact group forces pi_infinity≅V(lambda)_(iota,infinity). For U=U^pG(O_p) the pi-summand is (pi^(infinity,p))^(U^p) tensor Hom_(G(O_p))(sigma(tau),pi_p). Hecke operators away from S act through the unramified pi_v, hence semisimply. EGH Lemma7.1.6 is the case with no smooth factor.

items.name: The projected auxiliary Hecke image is a reduced finite free local O-algebra
items.statement: In the setting of A18, for i=0,1 let H_i=pr(S(U_i(Q),W)_mQ) and let T_i^pr be the image of the away-from-S∪Q Hecke algebra in End_O(H_i). If H_i≠0 then T_i^pr is a nonzero commutative local O-algebra, finite and free as an O-module, and reduced. The same holds for the unprojected image T(U,W)_m at original level. These are exactly the hypotheses on T in A63–A65.
items.locator: CHT §3.4, remark after the definition of TT(X), PDF104, with Corollary3.3.3 PDF102; LLHLM23 PDF197–198 (pr commutes with the Hecke algebra); Thorne Proposition5.9, arXiv1107.5989v1 PDF25.
items.proofOutline: S(U_i(Q),W) is finite free over O because U_i(Q) is sufficiently small (A33, CHT Lemma3.3.1). Its localization at m_Q is a direct summand, hence O-free. pr is a polynomial in commuting operators and commutes with the Hecke algebra (LLHLM23 PDF197–198), so H_i is a Hecke-stable O-submodule, torsion free and hence free, and X=H_i tensor K is Hecke-stable in S(U_i(Q),W tensor K). T_i^pr embeds in End_K(X), so it is finite and torsion free, hence free, over O; this is CHT's 'TT(X) is finite and free as an O-module'. By A74, X is a Hecke-stable subspace of a semisimple Hecke module on which the commutative Hecke algebra acts through characters, so T_i^pr tensor K is a product of fields and T_i^pr is reduced (CHT: 'by Corollary3.3.3 it is reduced'). It is a quotient of the local ring T_mQ, hence local when nonzero.

items.name: Characteristic-zero points of the projected Hecke image are sigma(tau)-typed automorphic eigensystems
items.statement: In the setting of A18 and A74 (so U_i(Q) has level G(O_p) at p), every O-algebra map x:T_i^pr→Qpbar is the Hecke eigensystem of an automorphic representation pi of G(A_F+) with pi_infinity≅V(lambda)_(iota,infinity), (pi^(infinity,p))^(U_i(Q)^p)≠0 and Hom_(G(O_p))(tensor_v sigma(tau_v) o iota_v,pi_p)≠0, whose eigensystem occurs in H_i tensor Qpbar. Consequently, once A59, A62 and A73 supply the RACSDC cuspidal Pi and the identification of the Galois representation required by A55, every characteristic-zero field factor x_j of A63 satisfies A55's hypothesis, and x_j∘f_v lies on R_rhobar_v^(lambda_v+eta,<=tau_v). This discharges A65's point hypothesis conditionally on those automorphic inputs.
items.locator: LLHLM23 TheoremA.4.1 PDF196–198 and its use at level G(O_p)U_1(Q_m)^(S_p) in §A.6 PDF201; CHT Proposition3.3.2 proof PDF100–102; EGH Theorem7.2.1 PDF55.
items.proofOutline: T_i^pr tensor Qpbar is a finite reduced Qpbar-algebra (A75), so its Qpbar-points are the simultaneous eigenvalue systems of the commuting Hecke operators on H_i tensor Qpbar, each with a nonzero eigenvector. H_i tensor Qpbar sits Hecke-equivariantly in S(U_i(Q),W tensor Qpbar), so the eigenvector lies in the isotypic part of an automorphic pi described by A74. Transporting through iota and applying A55 (with A59, A62 and A73 for the base change and the Galois realization) gives the local condition at every v|p. The factorization of f_v through R^D is then A64/A65.

items.name: Frobenius characteristic polynomials on a conjugacy-dense set determine a semisimple representation
items.statement: Let Delta be a topological group, C a subset of Delta whose conjugacy saturation is dense (the hypothesis of A49), and L an algebraically closed Hausdorff topological field of characteristic zero. Let rho_1,rho_2:Delta→GL_n(L) be continuous semisimple representations with det(1−rho_1(c)X)=det(1−rho_2(c)X) in L[X] for every c in C. Then rho_1 is isomorphic to rho_2. Equal characteristic polynomials give equal traces on C, hence on its conjugacy saturation, hence on Delta by continuity and density; in characteristic zero the trace of a semisimple representation determines it up to isomorphism, by linear independence of the irreducible characters. Both hypotheses are needed: without semisimplicity only the semisimplifications agree, and no modular (Brauer–Nesbitt) statement in characteristic p is claimed here — the residual polynomial-recognition statement is A101, whereas A50 concerns lifting irreducibility to characteristic zero.
items.locator: LLHLM23 TheoremA.4.1 PDF196–197, where each of r(U,W), r(U_0(Q),W) and r(U_1(Q),W) is 'uniquely determined by' the displayed Frobenius characteristic-polynomial equations over the Hecke algebra; the density input is A49 (CHT Proposition3.4.4 proof, PDF107–108).
items.proofOutline: Equal characteristic polynomials give equal traces. The traces are continuous conjugation-invariant functions into a Hausdorff field, so their equality set is closed and contains the dense conjugacy saturation of C. For the algebraic step, take the finite-dimensional image algebra of L[Delta] in End(V_1⊕V_2). Both V_i are semisimple modules over it; pass to its semisimple quotient and decompose into matrix blocks over algebraically closed L. On a diagonal matrix unit in each simple block the trace is the multiplicity of its simple module. Equal traces therefore give equal multiplicities because characteristic zero embeds the integers injectively. This is valid for arbitrary Delta and does not assume a finite group or finite Galois image. A98 now isolates the arbitrary-group character-independence step with pinned L84/L85, so no finite-group character-pairing theorem is imported here.
items.implementationStatus: Not implemented. Stated as the uniqueness half of the Hecke-algebra-valued construction; the determinant/Cayley–Hamilton machinery of IHG.1 is the intended carrier.

items.name: Galois realization of the base-changed discrete spectrum is a twisted sum of the cuspidal blocks
items.statement: In A59–A61, form the normalized regular algebraic cuspidal factors Pi_i and their semisimple Galois representations R_i from A79–A80. Let r:G_F→GL_n(Qpbar) be a continuous representation satisfying the good-prime equations of LLHLM TheoremA.4.1 for the rank-n unitary automorphic representation. Then r^ss≅⊕_i ⊕_(j=0)^(b_i−1) R_i⊗ε^(−j). Indeed at every unramified split place w outside the fixed finite bad set the characteristic polynomial is prod_i prod_j det(1−q_w^j R_i(Frob_w)X), with geometric Frob_w and ε(Frob_w)=q_w^(−1). The dense split-Frobenius set from A49 and Hausdorff characteristic-zero uniqueness A77 give the isomorphism. Every summand has positive dimension m_i, so A62 applies once the residual absolute irreducibility hypothesis is imposed.
items.locator: LLHLM23 TheoremA.4.1 PDF196–197 (the characteristic-polynomial equations) and §9.1 PDF180–181; A59 (Labesse, Changement de base CM et series discretes, Corollary5.3), A60 and A61 (Moeglin–Waldspurger, Le spectre residuel de GL(n), printed605–607).
items.proofOutline: A79 proves the algebraicity and polarization of the correct normalized factors. A80 imports their Galois realization from the existing AG2.2 theorem. A81 identifies the exact rank-normalized polynomials with the integral twists ε^(−j). Apply A49 and A77 to r^ss and this semisimple direct sum. Since the representations have finite dimension, semisimplification preserves good-prime characteristic polynomials and continuity. This supplies A62’s assumed Galois-equivariant decomposition without asserting the existence of a half-power of ε.
items.implementationStatus: Not implemented. The normalized-factor realization is an explicit planned import from AG2.2; the consumer’s exponent and polynomial conversion are missing source adapters in that same owner.
items.note: Continuation codex-c83e7a replaces the earlier half-twist formula. Both old residual hypotheses are discharged at the source-interface level: the factors to which the existence theorem applies are Pi_i, and every Galois twist in the decomposition is ε^(−j). The remaining global-descent supplier audit is not thereby declared closed.

items.name: Algebraic normalization and polarization of cuspidal Speh factors
items.statement: In A59–A61 let the regular algebraic rank-n weak base change be the isobaric sum of Delta_i=Speh(pi_i,b_i), where pi_i is unitary cuspidal of rank m_i and n=Σm_i b_i. Then each pi_i is conjugate self-dual, by uniqueness of the unitary cuspidal Speh support. Put t_i=(m_i+b_i−n−1)/2 and Pi_i=pi_i⊗|det|_F^(t_i), where the global adelic norm has its positive real half-powers. Then Pi_i is regular algebraic cuspidal. With d_i=2t_i∈Z and chi_i=|.|_(F+)^(d_i) δ_(F/F+)^(m_i), the pair (Pi_i,chi_i) is polarized in BLGGT §2.1: Pi_i^c≅Pi_i^∨⊗(chi_i∘Norm_(F/F+)∘det), and chi_i,v(−1)=(−1)^(m_i) at every real place. The half-integral t_i is used only for an automorphic norm twist; no p-adic cyclotomic half-character is asserted.
items.locator: LLHLM23 §9.1 PDF180–181 and Theorem A.4.1 PDF196–197; Labesse Corollary5.3 PDF43–44; Mœglin–Waldspurger introduction printed605–607; BLGGT (2014) §2.1 printed536–538
items.proofOutline: The total rank-n infinitesimal-character coordinates lie in Z+(n−1)/2 and are distinct, since the total parameter is cohomological with algebraic coefficients. The Speh segment shifts the coordinates a_(i,k) of pi_i by (b_i−1)/2−j. Taking j=0 shows a_(i,k) lies in Z+(n−b_i)/2; adding t_i puts it in Z+(m_i−1)/2. Distinctness of the total coordinates implies distinctness within this subset. After ordering, subtracting the rank-m_i half-sum of positive roots gives an integral dominant highest weight; hence Pi_i is regular algebraic. Norm twists preserve cuspidality. Conjugate self-duality of Delta_i and uniqueness of its unitary Speh support give pi_i^c≅pi_i^∨. Twisting yields the stated norm character with exponent 2t_i. The quadratic character δ is trivial after pullback by Norm and has value −1 at each real −1, supplying the required parity without changing the conjugate-duality equation.

tests.statement: For one block b=1,m=n, t=0: Pi=pi and chi=δ^n.

tests.statement: For n=2,m=1,b=2, t=0 even though the raw Speh induction uses half-integer exponents.

items.note: A precise source refinement of AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII:AG2.2, which already owns discrete constituents with algebraic twists. Regularity is an infinitesimal-character statement; actual archimedean base change is not needed before the cuspidality argument. This corrects an extraction gap, not a source error in LLHLM.

items.name: Galois representation of each algebraically normalized cuspidal factor
items.statement: For each regular algebraic cuspidal polarized pair (Pi_i,chi_i) from A79, fix iota:Qpbar≅C. The existing polarized automorphic-system theorem supplies a continuous semisimple R_i=r_(p,iota)(Pi_i):G_F→GL_(m_i)(Qpbar). At each finite w∤p, iota WD(R_i|G_Fw)^(F−ss)≅rec_w(Pi_(i,w)⊗|det|_w^((1−m_i)/2)); in particular this identifies the good-prime characteristic polynomials. Its polarization is R_i^c≅R_i^∨ ε^(b_i−n). The existence theorem applies to the normalized Pi_i, which may be nonunitary, and not to an unproved algebraicity claim for the original pi_i.
items.locator: BLGGT (2014), Theorem2.1.1(1)–(2), printed538/PDF38; consumed through LLHLM23 TheoremA.4.1 and EGH Theorem7.2.1
items.proofOutline: Apply the existing regular algebraic cuspidal polarized realization theorem to A79. The norm character |.|^d_i has p-adic avatar ε^d_i under geometric Artin reciprocity; δ restricts trivially to G_F. Thus the multiplier restricted to G_F is ε^(1−m_i+d_i)=ε^(b_i−n). Only the good-prime characteristic-polynomial consequence is needed for the block comparison; no extra p-adic monodromy assertion is inferred here.
items.note: Imported planned theorem, not a new construction or a pinned implementation. The exact normalization is source-read in BLGGT2.1.1. Preserve the geometry/local-comparison producers AG2.1a→ET.6→AG2.1b rather than assuming a circular geometric construction.

items.name: Rank-normalized Speh polynomials use integral cyclotomic twists
items.statement: Use geometric Frobenius Frob_w, q_w=Norm(w), ε(Frob_w)=q_w^(-1), and the local Langlands convention rec_w(π_w⊗|det|^((1−rankπ)/2)). With t_i,Pi_i,R_i as in A79–A80, the good-prime polynomial for the rank-n isobaric Speh sum is prod_i prod_(j=0)^(b_i−1) det(1−q_w^j R_i(Frob_w)X). Equivalently the corresponding semisimple local parameter is the direct sum of R_i|W_Fw⊗ε^(−j). The exponent identity is (b_i−1)/2−j+(1−n)/2=t_i+(1−m_i)/2−j. All cyclotomic exponents are integers.
items.locator: LLHLM23 §1.8.3 PDF28, TheoremA.4.1 PDF196–197; EGH Theorem7.2.1(iii) PDF55; BLGGT Theorem2.1.1(2) PDF38; Mœglin–Waldspurger normalized induction printed605–607
items.proofOutline: The rank-n normalization adds (1−n)/2 to each Speh exponent (b_i−1)/2−j. The normalized rank-m_i factor Pi_i adds t_i+(1−m_i)/2=(b_i−n)/2. The difference is −j. An unramified twist |.|^(−j) contributes q_w^j at geometric Frobenius, exactly ε^(−j). Normalized parabolic induction unions the unramified Satake parameters, so determinant polynomials multiply. The A.4.1 Hecke polynomial has the same rank-n normalization: for elementary symmetric Satake coordinate e_k, T_w^(k) has eigenvalue q_w^(k(n−k)/2)e_k and the displayed factor q_w^(k(k−1)/2) gives q_w^(k(n−1)/2)e_k.

tests.statement: For pi=1 on GL1, b=2,n=2, the normalized polynomial is (1−X)(1−q_w X), realized by 1⊕ε^(−1); it is not a polynomial with q_w^(±1/2) eigenvalues.

items.name: Finite prime-power torsion module decomposition over a PID
items.statement: Let R be a commutative principal ideal ring, p∈R irreducible, and M a finite R-module whose every element is killed by some power of p. Then for some d and k:Fin d→N there is an R-linear equivalence M≃⊕_(i:Fin d) R/(p^(k_i)). Exponent zero is allowed and gives a zero summand; remove such summands when forming a positive-parts partition.

items.name: Special-block restriction to an inertia multiplicity space
items.statement: Let Ω be algebraically closed of characteristic zero and r a finite-dimensional irreducible Weil representation with open kernel. Choose a finite quotient I of inertia through which r restricts, and put s=r|I. For an irreducible I-representation θ put c_θ=dim Hom_I(θ,s). On restriction to I, the special Weil–Deligne block Sp_d(r) has nilpotent operator id_s⊗J_d: its θ-multiplicity space has c_θ copies of J_d, so the a-th power rank is c_θ max(d−a,0). On the whole θ-isotypic subspace multiply that rank by dim θ. Unramified Weil twists leave c_θ unchanged.
items.locator: BLGGT Local-global compatibility for l=p II, PDF3 and5 special-block definition/decomposition; LLHLM23 PDF49–50; explicit restriction adapter
items.proofOutline: Choose a finite common inertia quotient through which the representation factors. L72–L74 give a finite direct sum of copies of irreducible inertia modules. By L73, evaluation identifies the θ-copy coefficient space with Hom_I(θ,s), giving s≅⊕_θ θ⊗Hom_I(θ,s). Tensor with the d-dimensional chain space; N commutes with I and acts as identity on θ and Hom_I(θ,s), and as J_d on the chain. Each multiplicity basis vector therefore supplies one chain of length d. Restricting a Weil twist trivial on I changes neither s|I nor c_θ. No Clifford orbit classification, multiplicity-one restriction or disjointness between different Weil classes is needed.

items.name: Nilpotent Jordan chains from the existing PID decomposition
items.statement: For any field k, finite-dimensional k-vector space V and nilpotent N∈End_k(V), there are finitely many positive integers d_i and a basis e_(i,j), 0≤j<d_i, with N e_(i,j)=e_(i,j+1) for j+1<d_i and N e_(i,d_i−1)=0. Empty V has an empty family. Algebraic closedness is not required for nilpotent normal form.
items.locator: Jordan normal form recalled immediately before LLHLM Definition2.5.3, PDF49; explicit reduction to pinned polynomial-module/PID suppliers L69–L71
items.proofOutline: Use the existing polynomial module AEval′ N. A power X^D kills it because N^D=0, and it is finite over k[X] since it is finite over k. The polynomial X is irreducible and k[X] is a PID. Apply L69 to obtain a finite direct sum of k[X]/(X^d_i), discard the zero d_i summands, and restrict scalars. L71 gives the monomial basis in each quotient; multiplication by X gives precisely the asserted chain equations. This is an adapter from existing general suppliers, not a second PID structure theorem.

items.name: Power ranks recover every nilpotent block multiplicity
items.statement: For N with Jordan block sizes d_i, set r_a=rank(N^a) for all a≥0. Then r_a=Σ_i max(d_i−a,0). The number of blocks of size at least a+1 is r_a−r_(a+1), and the number of blocks of size exactly d≥1 is r_(d−1)−2r_d+r_(d+1). Thus the full power-rank sequence determines the Jordan partition and the nilpotent conjugacy class.
items.locator: LLHLM23 PDF49 nilpotent conjugacy classification and Definition2.5.3; linear-algebra supplier of A58
items.proofOutline: A length-d chain maps under N^a onto its last max(d−a,0) basis vectors; disjoint chains have independent images, so their ranks add. Taking the first and second finite differences counts blocks at least and exactly the stated size. The recovered positive block multiplicities determine a common chain basis, hence conjugacy. Conversely conjugacy preserves all ranks. These are natural-number dimensions, so the computation is valid in every characteristic.

tests.name: NilpotentRanks.partition_3_1
tests.statement: For partition(3,1), ranks are4,2,1,0; second differences recover one block of size1 and one of size3.

tests.name: NilpotentRanks.single_rank_insufficient
tests.statement: Partitions(3,1) and(2,2) both have dimension4 and rank2, but their square ranks are1 and0. Rank(N) alone does not classify.

tests.name: NilpotentRanks.terminal_zero
tests.statement: For the empty partition every r_a is zero, including r_0.

items.name: Existing Maschke semisimplicity for finite group algebras
items.statement: For a field k, finite group G with (Nat.card G:k) nonzero, and any k[G]-module V, every submodule has a complementary submodule; hence V is semisimple. In characteristic zero the cardinality hypothesis holds. No finite-dimensionality hypothesis is required for this library theorem.

items.name: Existing Schur dimension formula for finite-dimensional representations
items.statement: Over an algebraically closed field k, the k-dimension of the intertwining space between two simple finite-dimensional representations V and W is one when they are isomorphic and zero otherwise. An irreducible finite-dimensional representation has only scalar equivariant endomorphisms.

items.name: Existing independent exhaustive isotypic components
items.statement: For a ring R and an R-module M, the family of its nonzero isotypic components is independent. When M is semisimple their supremum is top. If M is Noetherian this family is finite. Together these give the finite internal isotypic decomposition used for finite-dimensional semisimple inertia representations.

items.name: Existing Baire category theorem in the form: one of countably many closed covering sets has interior
items.statement: In a nonempty Baire space X, if (f i) is a countable family of closed sets whose union is the whole space, then some f i has nonempty interior. A compact Hausdorff space is a Baire space, being locally compact and T2, so this applies to the compact image of a profinite group.

items.name: Existing Krasner's lemma for complete nonarchimedean fields
items.statement: Let L be a normed field over K with IsKrasner K L. If x, y in L are such that the minimal polynomial of x over K is separable and splits in L, y is integral over K, and ‖x − y‖ < ‖x − x'‖ for every conjugate root x' ≠ x of x, then x lies in K(y). The hypothesis IsKrasner K L holds whenever K is a complete nontrivially normed ultrametric field and L is an algebraic normed K-algebra.

items.name: Countably many finite extensions of Q_p inside a fixed algebraic closure
items.statement: Fix an algebraic closure Qpbar of Q_p. The set of subfields K ⊂ Qpbar that are finite over Q_p is countable. Indeed, for each n ≥ 1 the degree-n subfields are countably many, and the union over n of countable sets is countable. Nothing stronger is claimed here: the finiteness of the number of extensions of a given degree is true but is not needed by A37, which needs only a countable cover.
items.locator: LLHLM23 A37's named supplier ('countability of finite p-adic extensions'); CHT Lemma 2.1.5 first paragraph of proof, PDF10–11.
items.proofOutline: Q_p has characteristic 0, so every finite K ⊂ Qpbar is separable and, by the primitive element theorem, K = Q_p(x) for some x whose minimal polynomial f over Q_p has degree n = [K:Q_p]. Since Q is dense in Q_p, choose a monic g in Q[X] of degree n whose coefficients are close enough to those of f. Root continuity makes some root y of g close to x, closer than the distance from x to any other conjugate root of x; Krasner's lemma (L76, applied with the complete field Q_p and the algebraic normed algebra Qpbar, which supplies IsKrasner) then gives x ∈ Q_p(y), and comparing degrees gives K = Q_p(y). So K is generated by a root of a polynomial over Q, and the set of such roots inside Qpbar is countable, being a countable union of finite sets. Hence the degree-n subfields are countably many, and so are all finite subfields.

items.name: Existing Hensel lifting for an adically complete ring
items.statement: For a commutative ring R and ideal I, IsAdicComplete I R supplies HenselianRing R I. If f∈R[X] is monic, f(a₀)∈I and the image of f′(a₀) is a unit in R/I, there is a∈R with f(a)=0 and a−a₀∈I. The general class also requires I⊂Jac(R). This is existence with prescribed residue, not uniqueness of every polynomial root.

items.name: Existing Burnside density for arbitrary monoids over an algebraically closed field
items.statement: For a field k, any monoid G, a finite-dimensional k-vector space V, [IsAlgClosed k], and an irreducible representation ρ:Representation k G V, the algebra map ρ.asAlgebraHom:k[G]→End_k(V) is surjective. There is no Finite G assumption.

items.name: Existing full-matrix trace pairing separates matrices in every characteristic
items.statement: For finite index types m,n and a nonassociative semiring R, matrices A,B:m×n satisfy A=B iff tr(A X)=tr(B X) for every X:n×m. Applied to B=0 over a commutative ring, the full matrix trace pairing has zero left kernel, including when the characteristic divides n. This does not assert nondegeneracy on the trace-zero subspace.

items.name: Existing bilinear dual submodule and basis duality
items.statement: Let R be a commutative ring, K a field with an R-algebra structure, V a compatible R- and K-module and B a K-bilinear form. The existing B.dualSubmodule(L) is {x:∀y∈L, B(x,y)∈image(R→K)}. If B is nondegenerate and b is a finite K-basis, the dual of span_R(b) is span_R(B.dualBasis b). Applying the opposite form gives B-dual(B.flip-dual(L))=L and B.flip-dual(B-dual(L))=L for such a basis lattice. Same-form double duality without a flip requires extra symmetry/asymmetry information.

items.name: Compact linear images preserve an integral lattice
items.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q_p, O its integer ring, Γ a compact group and ρ:Γ→GL_K(V) continuous on a finite-dimensional K-vector space. There is a full finite free O-lattice L with ρ(γ)L=L for all γ. A continuous character Γ→K× has image in O×. This imports the existing invariant-lattice target at R01.1; it is not a second proposed target.
items.locator: CHT Lemma2.1.5, author PDF11–12; ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.1 explicitly plans stable lattices by compactness.

items.proofOutline: Fix a basis lattice L₀. Compactness of finitely many matrix-coordinate images bounds every ρ(γ)L₀ inside π^(−a)L₀. The O-span of the orbit contains L₀ and is a submodule of the finite Noetherian module π^(−a)L₀, so is finite, full and stable; inverse group elements give equality. A compact subgroup of the discrete group Z is finite, hence zero, so the valuation of the character vanishes. A sufficiently large π-power of L makes any fixed bilinear form integral.

items.name: Equivariant opposite-form duality for a polarized lattice
items.statement: Let O be a DVR with fraction field K, V finite-dimensional, Δ a group, ρ:Δ→GL_K(V), σ an automorphism of Δ, χ:Δ→O×, and B a perfect K-bilinear form satisfying B(ρ(δ)x,ρ(σδ)y)=χ(δ)B(x,y). Suppose T∈ρ(Δ), c∈O× and B(x,T y)=cB(y,x). For a Δ-stable full O-lattice L, P=B.dualSubmodule(L) is a Δ-stable full lattice, equals B.flip.dualSubmodule(L), and B.dualSubmodule(P)=L. Thus both B(P,L) and B(L,P) are integral. If L is integral then L⊂P. This is valid without assuming B symmetric or alternating.

Since T L=L and c is a unit, B(x,L)⊂O iff B(L,x)⊂O. Apply the same argument to stable P and L80 opposite-form double duality to get P*=L. In CHT use σδ=γ₀δγ₀^(−1), T=ρ(γ₀²), c=−μ(γ₀).

items.name: Maximal integral stable lattices have uniformizer-killed dual defect
items.statement: In A87, start with any integral Δ-stable full lattice L₀. There is a maximal integral Δ-stable L between L₀ and L₀*. For every such maximal L, writing P=L*, one has πP⊂L⊂P, where π is a uniformizer. No semisimplicity hypothesis on P/L is used.

items.proofOutline: The quotient L₀*/L₀ has finite O-length: each is a finite full lattice and a power of π bounds the quotient; its successive π-quotients are finite-dimensional residue spaces. Hence integral stable enlargements have a maximal element. Choose the least m≥0 with π^mP⊂L. If m≥2, N=L+π^(m−1)P is strictly larger, stable, and inside P⊂L₀*. Cross terms pair integrally. Moreover π^mB(P,P)⊂O because π^mP⊂L, and 2m−2≥m, so B(N,N)⊂O. This contradicts maximality. Thus m≤1 and πP⊂L. This replaces the compressed semisimplicity step in the source without alleging that step false.

items.name: Quadratic Eisenstein coefficient extension and its integral basis
items.statement: Let K/Q_p be finite, O its integer ring and π a uniformizer. For K′=K(Π) with Π²=π, X²−π is Eisenstein, [K′:K]=2, K′/K is totally ramified, Π is a uniformizer and O′=O⊕ΠO. For a,b∈K, v_(K′)(a+Πb)=min(2v_K(a),1+2v_K(b)), with v(0)=∞. In particular a+Πb∈O′ iff a,b∈O. This includes p=2 and uses no tameness hypothesis.

items.name: Explicit self-dual lattice after one ramified quadratic extension
items.statement: In A87–A89, let L be integral and stable and P=L* satisfy πP⊂L. In V′=K′⊗_K V=V⊕ΠV, with B′ the scalar extension of B, define M=L⊕ΠP={a+Πb:a∈L,b∈P}. Equivalently M=O′L+ΠO′P. Then M is a full finite free Δ-stable O′-lattice and M*=M for B′. This is an actual construction with the same rank as V; no extra hyperbolic summand is added.

items.proofOutline: Multiplication by Π sends a+Πb to πb+Πa, which remains in M because πP⊂L⊂P. Finite generation, spanning and torsionfreeness give a full free lattice over the DVR O′. All four pairing terms are integral by B(L,L), B(L,P), B(P,L), πB(P,P)⊂O. For x=a+Πb∈M*, testing L and using A89 gives a,b∈P; testing ΠP gives a∈P*=L and πb∈P*=L. The latter condition follows from b∈P. Thus M*⊂M, and integrality gives the reverse inclusion. Group stability holds componentwise.

items.name: Absolute Burnside density descends from an algebraic closure
items.statement: Let k be any field, G any group (also valid for a monoid), V finite-dimensional, and ρ a representation that becomes irreducible after extension to an algebraic closure kbar. Then span_k{ρ(g):g∈G}=End_k(V). In coordinates one can choose n² group elements whose matrices form a basis. No cardinality restriction on G or invertibility of n is required.
items.locator: CHT author version Lemmas2.1.8–2.1.10, PDF13–15; explicit supplier/replacement proof, not an additional theorem attributed to the source.
items.implementationStatus: No new Lean implementation; extraction and proof plan only.

items.proofOutline: In a basis, let W be the span of the matrices over k. Its kbar-span is the image algebra of the extended representation, hence all M_n(kbar) by L78. The rank of a matrix with entries in k does not change over kbar: a maximal nonzero minor remains nonzero, and all larger minors remain zero. Choose a finite basis subset of the original spanning set to conclude dim_k W=n². This finite matrix-rank argument avoids the [Finite G] hypothesis on the pinned finrank_intertwiningMap_baseChange theorem.

items.name: Residual Burnside bases lift over a local coefficient ring
items.statement: Let R be a commutative local ring with residue k and ρ:G→GL_n(R), n≥1, with absolutely irreducible residual representation. Choose g₁,…,g_(n²) whose residual matrices form a k-basis by A91. Then (ρ(g_i)) is an R-basis of M_n(R). Consequently the commutant of ρ(G) in M_n(R) consists of scalar matrices, and its invertible commutant is R×. Completeness, continuity and finiteness of the residue field are unnecessary for this algebraic statement.
items.locator: CHT author version Lemmas2.1.8–2.1.10, PDF13–15; explicit supplier/replacement proof, not an additional theorem attributed to the source.
items.implementationStatus: No new Lean implementation; extraction and proof plan only.
items.note: Continuation Codex — codex-7e92bd, 23 September 2026. Owner: IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants.
items.proofOutline: Flatten the n² matrices into the columns of an n²×n² matrix. Its determinant is nonzero modulo the maximal ideal, hence a unit in R, so its inverse gives the basis coordinates. A matrix commuting with all group matrices commutes with this basis and hence every E_ij. Commutation with E_ii kills off-diagonal entries; commutation with E_ij equates diagonal entries. This proves the scalar statement even when char(k) divides n.

items.name: Congruence-preserving idempotent lifting in a finite free complete algebra
items.statement: Let S be a complete Noetherian commutative local ring, A a possibly noncommutative S-algebra finite free as an S-module, and J⊂m_S. Every idempotent ebar∈A/JA lifts to an idempotent e∈A. No assumption that 2 is invertible is needed, and uniqueness of a noncentral idempotent lift is not asserted.
items.locator: CHT author version Lemmas2.1.8–2.1.10, PDF13–15; explicit supplier/replacement proof, not an additional theorem attributed to the source.
items.implementationStatus: No new Lean implementation; extraction and proof plan only.
items.note: Continuation Codex — codex-7e92bd, 23 September 2026. Owner: IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants.
items.proofOutline: Lift ebar to a₀ and recursively set a_(r+1)=3a_r²−2a_r³. These are polynomials in a₀, so commute even when A is noncommutative. For q=a²−a, the change is −(2a−1)q and the next error is q²(4a²−4a−3). Thus a_r²−a_r∈J^(2^r)A and consecutive differences have that precision. In a finite S-basis the sequence is m_S-adically Cauchy, so L27 coordinatewise supplies a limit. Multiplication is continuous in these coordinates. L03 applied to A/JA shows JA is closed, and applied to A shows separation; hence e≡a₀ mod JA and e²=e. The same argument applies to J=0 (the initial lift is already idempotent). This supplies an explicit compatible sequence, not arbitrary lifts in each quotient.

items.name: Matrix coordinates from a lifted rank-one idempotent
items.statement: Let S be complete Noetherian local, A an associative unital S-algebra free of rank n², n≥1, and J⊂m_S. Given an S/J-algebra isomorphism θ:A/JA≃M_n(S/J), there is an S-algebra isomorphism α:A≃M_n(S) reducing exactly to θ. Construct it from an idempotent lifting θ^(−1)(E₁₁), not from a choice of incompatible finite-level algebra isomorphisms.
items.locator: CHT author version Lemmas2.1.8–2.1.10, PDF13–15; explicit supplier/replacement proof, not an additional theorem attributed to the source.
items.implementationStatus: No new Lean implementation; extraction and proof plan only.
items.note: Continuation Codex — codex-7e92bd, 23 September 2026. Owner: IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants.
items.proofOutline: Lift e by A93. P=Ae is the image of the S-linear idempotent x↦xe, so is a finite projective direct summand of A and is free by L81. Modulo m_S its dimension is n. Modulo J, θ identifies P/JP with the standard column module M_n(S/J)E₁₁. Lift its standard n columns to P; they form an S-basis by L81. Left multiplication A→End_S(P), expressed in this basis, reduces modulo J to θ; modulo m_S it is a bijection of n²-dimensional spaces. Its determinant is therefore a unit, giving the required algebra isomorphism α.

items.name: Finite free trace-span algebra with relative quotient coordinates
items.statement: Let S⊂R be commutative local rings inducing an isomorphism of residue fields, n≥1, and ρ:G→GL_n(R) residually absolutely irreducible with trρ(g)∈S for every g. Choose a residual Burnside family g_i and let A=Σ_i Sρ(g_i)⊂M_n(R). Then A is a unital S-subalgebra free of rank n², contains ρ(G), and A⊗_S R≃M_n(R). If I⊂m_R and each ρ(g) mod I lies in GL_n(S/J), J=I∩S, then A∩M_n(I)=JA and entrywise reduction induces A/JA≃M_n(S/J).
items.locator: CHT author version Lemmas2.1.8–2.1.10, PDF13–15; explicit supplier/replacement proof, not an additional theorem attributed to the source.

items.proofOutline: A92 makes the chosen matrices an R-basis. The Gram matrix H_ij=tr(ρ(g_i)ρ(g_j)) has entries in S and is invertible modulo m_S by L79, hence H^(−1) has entries in S. For g∈G, the traces tr(ρ(g)ρ(g_j))=trρ(gg_j) lie in S, so H^(−1) computes its coordinates in S. This proves containment, identity and multiplication closure. R-linear independence gives S-freeness and the scalar-extension isomorphism. For the relative claim, reduction of the chosen matrices is a basis of M_n(S/J) because its determinant is a unit modulo m_S/J. If a∈A has entries in I, the trace vector lies in I∩S=J, so its coordinates lie in J. Conversely JA has entries in I. This identifies the kernel and quotient without flatness of S→R.

items.name: A local matrix automorphism trivial modulo an ideal is strictly inner
items.statement: Let R be a commutative local ring, I⊂m_R, n≥1, and φ an R-algebra automorphism of M_n(R) inducing the identity modulo I. There is g∈1+M_n(I) with φ(X)=gXg^(−1) for every X. This holds without completeness, Noetherianity, a finite residue field or division by n.

Matrix-unit relations give f_ij v_l=δ_jl v_i, hence f_ij=gE_ijg^(−1), and linearity proves the assertion for every matrix. All formulas are polynomial before inversion of the unit determinant.

items.name: Cofinality for a local embedding of complete Noetherian rings
items.statement: Let S⊂R be an injective local homomorphism of complete Noetherian local rings. Their residue fields need not be finite or identical. For every b≥1 there is a≥1 with S∩m_R^a⊂m_S^b. Consequently the intrinsic m_S-adic topology is exactly the topology induced from the m_R-adic topology; a continuous map into R whose image is in S is continuous into S. More generally, any descending sequence of ideals J_a⊂S with intersection zero is cofinal with the powers of m_S.
items.locator: Explicit proof of the topology assertion S=lim S/(S∩I) in CHT Lemma2.1.9, author PDF14; general complete-local algebra supplied to its representation consumers.
items.implementationStatus: No new Lean implementation; extraction and proof plan only.
items.note: Continuation Codex — codex-7e92bd, 23 September 2026. Owner: DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra.
items.proofOutline: For each b, the images of J_a in the finite-length module S/m_S^b form a descending chain, hence stabilize to E_b. The maps E_(b+1)→E_b are surjective: choose a beyond both stabilization indices and use the image of J_a. If some E_b contains a nonzero x_b, recursively lift along these surjections to compatible x_c for c≥b (and project below b). Completeness L27 gives x∈S with these residues. For each fixed a, all its residues lie in the image of J_a; L03 on the finite S-module S/J_a gives x∈J_a. Thus x∈∩J_a=0, contradicting its nonzero residue. Hence E_b=0 and some J_a⊂m_S^b. For the local embedding take J_a=S∩m_R^a; separation of R by L03 makes their intersection zero, and locality gives the reverse-continuity inclusion m_S^a⊂S∩m_R^a. This finite-length stabilization argument works over infinite residue fields and constructs compatible residues explicitly.

items.name: Compactness of finite modules and finitely generated submodules
items.statement: Let R be a compact commutative semiring and M a topological R-module with continuous addition and scalar multiplication. Every finitely generated R-submodule N⊂M is compact. In particular a module-finite M is compact. If M is Hausdorff, such N is closed. These statements do not require M to be free or torsionfree.

items.name: Compactness criterion for a rank-one valuation ring
items.statement: For a field K with a rank-one valuation, its valuation ring O is compact if and only if O is complete, is a discrete valuation ring, and has finite residue field. Use the valuation topology, not an arbitrary topology on the underlying ring.

items.name: Finite-dimensional split semisimple algebras are products of matrices
items.statement: A finite-dimensional semisimple algebra B over an algebraically closed field k is k-algebra isomorphic to a finite product of matrix algebras M_(d_i)(k), with every d_i nonzero. No characteristic-zero or group-order invertibility hypothesis is present.

items.name: Radical annihilation and Artinian semisimplicity
items.statement: The Jacobson radical of an arbitrary ring B annihilates every semisimple B-module. For an Artinian ring B, B is semisimple if and only if its Jacobson radical is zero. Thus the finite-dimensional image algebra acting faithfully on a semisimple module is semisimple.

items.name: Compact-to-Hausdorff embeddings and quotient maps
items.statement: A continuous injective map from a compact space to a Hausdorff space is a closed embedding. A continuous surjective map between such spaces is a quotient map. These results retain the given topologies.
items.implementationStatus: Pinned statements read; no new Lean implementation.

items.name: Independence of simple characters for an arbitrary group
items.statement: Let k be algebraically closed, G any group, and S_1,…,S_r pairwise nonisomorphic nonzero finite-dimensional simple k[G]-modules. Their k-valued trace characters on G are k-linearly independent, in every characteristic. G need not be finite.
items.locator: Wiese, Galois Representations (13 February 2012), Theorem2.4.4 and Remark2.4.2(i), printed/PDF34–35; explicit arbitrary-group image-algebra specialization.
proofSteps: Let V be the direct sum of the S_i and B the image of k[G] in End_k(V). This is finite-dimensional, acts faithfully, and V is semisimple over B because B-invariant and G-invariant subspaces agree. L85 makes B semisimple.

Apply L84. The simple B-modules are the column modules of its matrix blocks. Distinct S_i occupy different blocks. For a chosen i, take a matrix unit E_11 in its block and zero in all other blocks, and lift this element to k[G]. Its trace on S_i is 1 and on every other S_j is 0.

A linear relation among characters on G extends linearly to k[G], since group elements span that algebra. Evaluating at these lifted matrix units kills each coefficient. This uses trace 1 on E_11, not trace dim(S_i) on the central idempotent, which may vanish in characteristic p.

tests.name: A98.modular_dimension
tests.statement: In characteristic p, the identity of M_p(k) has trace0 while E_11 has trace1; central idempotents alone cannot perform this separation.

tests.name: A98.infinite_group
tests.statement: The argument applies to the infinite cyclic group with distinct one-dimensional characters; no finite-group orthogonality or division by |G| is used.

tests.name: A98.repeated_simple
tests.statement: Two copies of the same simple module have the same character; pairwise nonisomorphism is required.

items.name: Brauer–Nesbitt by cancellation and division of multiplicities
items.statement: Let k be algebraically closed, G any group, and V,W finite-dimensional k[G]-modules. If det(T−g|V)=det(T−g|W) for every g∈G, then V and W have isomorphic semisimplifications. If both are semisimple they are isomorphic. This holds in every characteristic and imposes no bound on dimension.
items.locator: Wiese Theorem2.4.6, printed/PDF36, cancellation and p-divisibility proof, and Remark2.4.7(iii), PDF37; algebraically closed group version. Do not use the generator-only assertion in Remark2.4.7(iv); E52.
proofSteps: Pass to composition factors: a basis adapted to a composition series makes every operator block upper triangular, so its characteristic polynomial is the product of the factor polynomials. Cancel common simple summands using that k[T] is an integral domain. The remaining semisimple modules have disjoint simple supports and equal characteristic polynomials at every g.

Equal characteristic polynomials give equal traces. A98 shows that the multiplicity of each remaining simple factor is zero as an element of k. In characteristic zero the multiplicities are zero integers, finishing the proof.

In characteristic p>0 every remaining multiplicity is divisible by p. Write V=V_1^(⊕p), W=W_1^(⊕p). Their characteristic polynomials satisfy P_(V_1,g)^p=P_(W_1,g)^p for every g. In k[T], (P−Q)^p=0 implies P=Q, so the smaller modules again satisfy the same hypothesis.

Use strong induction on the common dimension after cancellation: division by p strictly decreases every positive dimension. Hence the disjoint remainders are zero. At no point is equality of characteristic polynomials extended by linearity from G to its group algebra; only equality of traces is extended. Only semisimplification is recovered.

tests.name: A99.trace_loss
tests.statement: For G=C2 in characteristic3, 1^(⊕3) and sign^(⊕3) both have identically zero trace, but at the nontrivial element their polynomials are T^3−1 and T^3+1. Trace equality is insufficient.

tests.name: A99.extension_loss
tests.statement: For G=C_p in characteristic p, a nontrivial two-dimensional unipotent Jordan block and the two-dimensional trivial action have identical characteristic polynomials at every element; their semisimplifications agree but the representations need not.

tests.name: A99.zero_rank
tests.statement: The zero-dimensional representation has polynomial1 at the identity. Equality forces the other dimension to be zero.

tests.name: A99.generators_do_not_span
tests.statement: E52 gives two irreducible representations of C2*C2 with identical polynomials for all powers of each chosen generator but different trace on their product. All group elements, or a spanning subset of the image of the group algebra, are required.

items.name: Frobenius classes above split primes are conjugacy-dense
items.statement: Let F/F+ be a quadratic extension of number fields, S a finite set of finite places of F+, and G_F⊂G_(F+) the absolute Galois groups in a common closure. Let C contain Frobenius lifts for both places w of F above every v∉S that splits in F, with each lift taken using a decomposition group. The G_F-conjugacy saturation of C is dense in G_F. In a quotient unramified outside S one may use Frobenius classes directly. Both arithmetic and geometric conventions work after simultaneous inversion.
items.locator: CHT Proposition3.4.4 proof, author PDF107–108, split-prime polynomial input; explicit application of existing Chebotarev Layer10 and the residue-degree-one tower law.
proofSteps: To hit a basic open coset gU in G_F, shrink the open normal subgroup U of G_F to U∩cUc^(−1), for a lift c of the nontrivial quadratic automorphism. It is normal in G_(F+): c² lies in G_F. Let L be its fixed field. Then L/F+ is finite Galois and contains F.

Apply the existing Chebotarev infinitude theorem to the conjugacy class of the image of g in Gal(L/F+), excluding S and the finitely many primes ramified in L. Its restriction to F is trivial, so the resulting base prime v splits in F.

Choose a prime of L above v whose Frobenius is exactly the selected image of g, using conjugation of primes above v. Its contraction w to F is one of the two split places. Because f(w/v)=1, the Frobenius in L/F equals the Frobenius in L/F+, with no additional power. A representative from C for this w is G_F-conjugate to it modulo U; every Frobenius lift has the same image because L is unramified at v.

Thus the G_F-conjugacy saturation meets gU. This does not assert that arbitrarily selected individual representatives themselves form a dense set. Inversion carries the arithmetic statement to the geometric one, and exclusion of any further finite set is built into Chebotarev infinitude.

tests.name: A100.two_split_places
tests.statement: In the finite quotient S3 with index-two subgroup A3, the S3 class of a 3-cycle contains g and g^(−1), but these are different A3 classes. One arbitrarily chosen place over every split base prime can select only one class; retaining both places avoids the loss.

tests.name: A100.inert_places
tests.statement: Frobenius of a base prime inert in F restricts nontrivially to Gal(F/F+); it cannot replace the kernel-class argument.

tests.name: A100.orientation
tests.statement: In A3 the two nonidentity classes are interchanged by inversion. Geometric Frobenius requires inverting the class as well as the cyclotomic convention.

items.name: Residual recognition gives an actual isomorphism when one side is absolutely irreducible
items.statement: Let F/F+ and S be as in A100. Let rho_1,rho_2:G_F→GL_n(kbar) be continuous with kbar an algebraic closure of a finite field carrying the discrete topology, unramified above every split v∉S. If their characteristic polynomials agree at both w above each such v, their semisimplifications over kbar are isomorphic. If rho_1 is absolutely irreducible, rho_2 itself is isomorphic to rho_1. If both are originally over finite coefficient fields, the conjugating matrix is defined over a common finite extension; no descent to a smaller field is asserted.
items.locator: CHT Proposition3.4.4, author PDF107–108, implicit residual recognition before Lemma2.1.4; Wiese Corollary2.4.8 PDF37 and the explicit absolutely irreducible upgrade.
proofSteps: For each coefficient, its equality set is closed, since the representations are continuous and the coefficient field is Hausdorff discrete. It is conjugation invariant and contains C. A100 therefore extends equality to every element of G_F.

Apply A99 over kbar. If one semisimplification is the single simple module rho_1, the other module has composition length one, so it is already simple and isomorphic, without a separate semisimplicity assumption on the chosen lattice reduction.

An intertwining matrix has finitely many entries algebraic over the common finite field; they generate a finite extension. Its determinant is nonzero there. In A47 this produces the actual residual GL_n isomorphism before the polarized square-class alignment; p>2 is needed by that later polarized step, not by this recognition argument.

tests.name: A101.unipotent_boundary
tests.statement: A reducible semisimplification cannot upgrade to an isomorphism of original modules: the C_p Jordan-block example in A99 remains a counterexample.

tests.name: A101.rank_one
tests.statement: For n=1 characteristic polynomial equality gives equality of the characters on the dense Frobenius set and then on all of G_F.

tests.name: A101.no_small_prime_exclusion
tests.statement: The recognition step remains valid in characteristic2; only the later polarized square-root statements retain their p>2 hypothesis.

items.name: Finite modules over complete coefficient DVRs have the expected topology
items.statement: Let O be a complete DVR with finite residue field and uniformizer pi, equipped with its valuation topology. For every finite O-module M, the pi-adic topology is Hausdorff, compact and complete and equals the quotient topology for every O-linear surjection O^r→M. Every O-linear map between finite such modules is continuous. If T is a nonzero finite local O-algebra with maximal ideal m, its pi-adic and m-adic topologies coincide, so T is a complete Noetherian local ring. T and M may have O-torsion.
items.locator: CHT Proposition3.4.4 author PDF108 and A46/A48 coefficient-ring topology; explicit finite-module adapter to pinned L03/L07/L83.
proofSteps: Choose finite generators and q:O^r→M. For every a≥0, q(pi^a O^r)=pi^a M. These submodules are neighborhood bases and q is surjective, continuous and open for the pi-adic topology, proving precisely the quotient-topology assertion.

L03 gives separation because M is finite over the Noetherian local ring O. L07 identifies its completion with O-hat tensor_O M=M; thus completeness is inherited from O. L83 makes O compact, so M is compact as a continuous image of O^r. An O-linear f maps pi^a M into pi^a N, proving continuity directly; no unverified module-topology instance is needed.

T is Noetherian because it is finite over O. The element pi is not a unit in a nonzero finite O-algebra: otherwise pi T=T and Nakayama over O gives T=0. Hence pi∈m. The finite-dimensional local k-algebra T/pi T is Artinian. The descending powers of its maximal ideal stabilize, and Nakayama for that stabilized finite module forces it to vanish. Thus m^d⊂pi T for some d≥1.

Taking a-th powers yields m^(da)⊂pi^a T⊂m^a for every a≥0. The two topologies therefore coincide. This also applies to the common-residue ring A46 and to T in A48. Finite residue is used for compactness, not for the displayed cofinality inclusions or finite-module completeness.

tests.name: A102.torsion
tests.statement: M=O/(pi^2) has the finite discrete topology and is complete; freeness is unnecessary.

tests.name: A102.dual_numbers
tests.statement: For T=O[e]/(e^2), m=(pi,e) and m^2⊂pi T; in general m^a is not equal to pi^a T.

tests.name: A102.infinite_residue
tests.statement: For O=C[[t]], O is complete and separated but not compact: its continuous residue quotient is the infinite discrete field C. Compactness requires the finite residue hypothesis.

tests.name: A102.embedding_not_open
tests.statement: The diagonal O→O×O is a closed embedding but not an open map. The quotient-map assertion above is for surjections.

items.name: Finite integral Hecke algebras are closed in their coefficient products
items.statement: Let O be as in A102 and T a finite O-algebra with its pi-adic topology. Let A be a Hausdorff topological O-algebra with continuous addition and scalar multiplication, and j:T→A an injective O-algebra map. Then j is continuous and a closed embedding. Equivalently, a finite O-subalgebra of such A is closed. If A is the finite coefficient product or the common-residue subring in A46, its intrinsic coefficient topology agrees with the induced topology.
items.locator: CHT Proposition3.4.4 author PDF108, closed integral trace-ring step; explicit finite-O coefficient adapter.
proofSteps: Write T as a quotient of O^r using finite generators t_i. The composite O^r→A is (a_i)↦sum a_i j(t_i), hence continuous by finite sums and scalar continuity. A102 identifies the topology on T with the quotient topology, so j is continuous.
A102 makes T compact. L86 applied to j gives the closed embedding. Alternatively view j(T) as a finitely generated O-submodule of A and apply L82, then compact sets are closed in a Hausdorff space.

For A46, the finite O-module congruence subring has its pi-adic topology and the injective coordinate map into the Hausdorff product. This argument identifies that topology with the subspace topology. Combining A102 with its explicit unit criterion gives the m-adic topology required by A45/A48.

tests.name: A103.proper_congruence_ring
tests.statement: T={(x,y)∈O²:x≡y mod pi} is closed in O² and has the induced topology, although it is not the full product.

tests.name: A103.hausdorff_required
tests.statement: The injective identity from compact O with its valuation topology to the same ring with indiscrete topology is continuous but is not an embedding; the target Hausdorff hypothesis matters.

tests.name: A103.finite_generation_required
tests.statement: The prime subring Z⊂Z_p is dense and proper, so an arbitrary subring need not be closed. It is not a finite Z_p-submodule.

items.name: Characters of the compact adele-class group and Fourier uniqueness
items.statement: Let F be a number field with adeles A, and fix a nontrivial continuous unitary character psi of A trivial on F. Then gamma↦psi_gamma, psi_gamma(x)=psi(gamma x), is a group isomorphism from F onto the Pontryagin dual of the compact group F\A. Consequently, if h is a continuous function on F\A all of whose Fourier coefficients integral_{F\A} h(x) psi_gamma(x)^(-1) dx vanish for every gamma in F, then h=0. The same holds with F\A replaced by any of the successive additive quotients (F\A)^r arising from the unipotent filtration of N_n, the characters there being indexed by F^r. This is the uniqueness half only: no statement about pointwise convergence of the Fourier series is asserted.
items.locator: Cogdell, L-functions and Converse Theorems for GL_n, author-hosted PCMI notes (2002), Lecture1, printed6/PDF10: 'by standard duality theory the additive characters of the compact group k\A are isomorphic to k via the map gamma in k ↦ psi_gamma', with the parenthetical abelian-Fourier expansion immediately above. Cogdell cites Weil, Basic Number Theory, and Gelfand–Graev–Piatetski-Shapiro for the duality. Author PDF SHA-256 09b82f9aed494d28327ed9692f5bf37e6bed229cf470e80927e0cc10ce70932a, read 23 September 2026 (printed page = PDF page - 4).
proofSteps: Self-duality of A pairs A with its own dual through psi; the annihilator of the discrete cocompact subgroup F is F itself under that pairing, so the dual of F\A is F. AL.0 already owns self-duality of the local additive groups and the adelic restricted tensor product, which is what this specialises.

F\A is compact abelian, so its characters span a dense subspace of C(F\A) for the uniform norm by Stone–Weierstrass, the character group separating points. A continuous function orthogonal to every character is therefore orthogonal to a dense subspace of C(F\A) in L^2, hence is 0 in L^2 and, being continuous, is identically 0.

For the iterated case, the successive quotients of the unipotent filtration of N_n are F-vector groups of finite rank, so their adelic quotients are finite products of copies of F\A and the duality is the r-fold product of the rank-one statement. This is the form A67 and A68 consume when they peel one row at a time.

tests.name: A104.rank_one_is_circle
tests.statement: For F=Q, F\A is the solenoid whose dual is Q with the discrete topology; a continuous function with all Fourier coefficients zero vanishes.

tests.name: A104.continuity_required
tests.statement: An L^1 function on a compact abelian group with all Fourier coefficients zero is zero only almost everywhere, so the pointwise conclusion needs the continuity hypothesis that cusp forms supply.

tests.name: A104.nontrivial_psi_required
tests.statement: If psi were trivial then every psi_gamma would be trivial and the map gamma↦psi_gamma would not be injective; the nontriviality hypothesis is used.

items.name: Compatible invariant probability measures on the unipotent adelic quotients
items.statement: Let N be the unipotent radical of a standard parabolic of GL_n over a number field F. Then N(F)\N(A) is compact, N(A) and N(F) are unimodular, and there is a unique N(A)-invariant Radon measure on N(F)\N(A) of total mass 1. For a normal subgroup filtration N=N^(0)⊃N^(1)⊃…⊃N^(r)=1 with abelian successive quotients, the probability measures on the quotients N^(i)(F)\N^(i)(A) are compatible with the invariant probability measure on N(F)\N(A) through Weil's integration formula, so iterated integration along the filtration computes the integral over N(F)\N(A) in any order permitted by the filtration.
items.locator: A66 fixes 'the invariant probability quotient measure, compatible with the successive additive quotients'; this item is that hypothesis made explicit. Cogdell, PCMI notes (2002), Lecture1, printed5–7/PDF9–11, where the integrals over k\A and over N(k)\N(A) are taken and iterated without further comment. Author PDF SHA-256 09b82f9a…0932a, read 23 September 2026.
proofSteps: N is unipotent, so N(A) is unimodular, and N(F) is discrete hence unimodular. AA.2 already constructs invariant quotient measures by Weil's integral formula and proves their independence of the choice of measurable fundamental domain; specialising it to this pair gives an invariant Radon measure on the quotient, unique up to positive scalar.

N(F)\N(A) is compact — the standard fundamental domain is a product of copies of a fundamental domain for F\A, which is compact — so the invariant measure has finite total mass and may be normalised to 1. Uniqueness of the invariant probability measure follows from uniqueness up to scalar.

For the filtration, apply Weil's formula to each of the two stages N^(i+1)(F)\N^(i+1)(A) ⊂ N^(i)(F)\N^(i)(A). The compatibility is the assertion that the three normalisations agree, which holds because each is the unique invariant probability measure and the pushforward of an invariant probability measure is one. Iterating gives the Fubini statement used in A67 and A68.

tests.name: A105.GL2_case
tests.statement: For n=2, N_2(F)\N_2(A) is F\A and the measure is the invariant probability measure used for the psi-Fourier coefficient in A66.

tests.name: A105.unimodularity_used
tests.statement: For the full Borel B of GL_2, B(A) is not unimodular and no invariant quotient measure on B(F)\B(A) exists; the hypothesis that N is unipotent is what makes the construction available.

tests.name: A105.compactness_for_normalisation
tests.statement: GL_n(F)\GL_n(A) is not compact, so no invariant probability measure exists there; the normalisation is specific to the unipotent quotients.

items.name: The Whittaker integral is continuous on the smooth globalization
items.statement: Let A^infinity(GL_n(F)\GL_n(A)) be the space of smooth automorphic forms of uniform moderate growth, and for a compact open L in the finite part let (A^infinity)^L carry the Fréchet topology defined by the uniform moderate-growth seminorms. Then for each g the map phi↦W_psi(phi)(g) of A66 is a continuous linear functional on (A^infinity)^L, and phi↦W_psi(phi) is continuous into the corresponding space of Whittaker functions. In particular the functional Lambda of A70 is continuous, not merely linear, and is defined on the smooth globalization rather than on the K_infinity-finite Harish–Chandra module.
items.locator: Cogdell, Lectures on L-functions, Converse Theorems, and Functoriality for GL_n, Fields Institute notes (2003), section on smooth automorphic representations, printed24/PDF27: 'The spaces (A^infinity)^L all carry compatible limits of smooth Fréchet topologies coming from the uniform moderate growth semi-norms on A^infinity and the representation of G_infinity on these spaces are limits of smooth Fréchet representation of moderate growth.' Author PDF SHA-256 2c5ec050a6db216dcd2104b7fe266ddc03e4db7c7d300239e60d6ee9c40618a7, read 23 September 2026 (printed page = PDF page - 3).
proofSteps: A105 gives a probability measure on the compact domain N_n(F)\N_n(A). The integrand is bounded by the supremum of |phi| over the compact set N_n(F)\N_n(A)·g, so |W_psi(phi)(g)| is bounded by one of the defining seminorms of the Fréchet topology evaluated on a compact set. That is continuity of the functional.

AF.1 owns the construction of the smooth moderate-growth Fréchet globalization and its uniqueness; this item only records that the Whittaker integral is continuous for that topology, which is what makes 'nonzero continuous functional' meaningful in A70.

Continuity into the space of Whittaker functions follows because the estimate is uniform for g in a compact set, so convergence in the Fréchet topology gives locally uniform convergence of the transforms.

tests.name: A106.seminorm_bound
tests.statement: |W_psi(phi)(g)| <= sup over the compact N_n(F)\N_n(A)·g of |phi|, since the measure is a probability measure and |psi_N|=1.

tests.name: A106.smooth_vs_K_finite
tests.statement: A linear functional on the K_infinity-finite subspace need not extend continuously to the globalization, which is why A70 is stated for the smooth globalization; the distinction is the point of this item.

tests.name: A106.moderate_growth_used
tests.statement: Without a growth condition the integral over a compact quotient still converges, but the family of seminorms would not control it uniformly in g, so the second conclusion fails.

items.name: One-place abstract factorization of a smooth automorphic representation
items.statement: Let Pi be an irreducible smooth automorphic representation of GL_n(A_F) and v a finite place. Then there are an irreducible admissible smooth representation Pi_v of GL_n(F_v) and a complex vector space V^v carrying a smooth action of the away-from-v part, with an isomorphism of GL_n(F_v)-representations V_Pi ≅ V_(Pi_v) tensor_C V^v under which GL_n(F_v) acts only on the first factor. This is the one-place form of Flath's decomposition theorem, and it is an ABSTRACT isomorphism of representations: it does not factor automorphic forms into products of functions on the local groups.
items.locator: Cogdell, Fields Institute notes (2003), Theorem3.2 (Decomposition Theorem) and Corollary3.2.1, printed23–24/PDF27; the caveat is Cogdell's own, immediately after the corollary: 'the decomposition given in this corollary is an abstract decomposition. It does not give a factorization of automorphic forms into a product of functions on the local groups G(k_v)'. The smooth version is Theorem3.4, printed24–25/PDF28, which gives Pi = Pi_infinity tensor-hat Pi_f with Pi_f the restricted tensor product over the finite places. Author PDF SHA-256 2c5ec050…18a7, read 23 September 2026.
proofSteps: AF.2 already owns restricted tensor-product factorization for irreducible admissible constituents and uniqueness of almost-everywhere spherical vectors. This item extracts the single-place consequence: group the restricted tensor product as the v-factor tensored with the restricted tensor product over the remaining places, and take V^v to be the latter.

For the smooth globalization the grouping is Theorem3.4's Pi = Pi_infinity tensor-hat Pi_f followed by splitting Pi_f = Pi_v tensor (restricted product away from v); the archimedean factor is absorbed into V^v, which is why V^v is only required to carry a smooth action and no topology is asserted on it.

Record the caveat explicitly, because A71 uses only the abstract isomorphism: it chooses w in V^v to detect a given global functional, which is legitimate for an abstract tensor decomposition, whereas a factorization of automorphic forms into local functions is not available and is not claimed.

tests.name: A107.grouping_is_associativity
tests.statement: For a restricted tensor product over all places, grouping off one finite place is an isomorphism of representations of the group at that place, the remaining factor being the restricted product over the complement.

tests.name: A107.abstract_only
tests.statement: An automorphic form is not in general a product of local functions; Cogdell states this immediately after the corollary, so no such conclusion may be drawn from this item.

tests.name: A107.spherical_almost_everywhere
tests.statement: The restricted product is taken with respect to the almost-everywhere spherical vectors whose uniqueness AF.2 supplies; without that choice the restricted product is not defined.

items.name: Eventual coefficients of a rational Hilbert series
items.statement: For a characteristic-zero field F, p∈F[T], e≥0, and n>natDegree(p), the coefficient of T^n in p(T)/(1−T)^e equals Polynomial.hilbertPoly p e evaluated at n; this eventual polynomial is unique. Apply with F=Q to integer-valued length series. The ring or residue field whose module lengths are counted may have arbitrary characteristic.

items.name: Length additivity in an exact sequence
items.statement: For R-modules and R-linear maps N→M→P with the first injective, the second surjective and the pair exact, length_R(M)=length_R(N)+length_R(P) in N∪{∞}. Passing to natural or rational numbers requires proving these lengths finite.

items.name: Length under a surjective scalar map
items.statement: Let S→R be a surjective homomorphism of commutative rings, M an R-module with compatible restricted S-action. Then length_S(M)=length_R(M). In particular use S→S/I only on a module actually annihilated by I.

items.name: Length of a finite-dimensional vector space
items.statement: For a division ring K and a finite K-module V, length_K(V) equals finrank_K(V), with the latter cast to N∪{∞}.

items.name: Artin–Rees stabilization of an induced ideal filtration
items.statement: For a commutative Noetherian ring R, ideal I, finite R-module M and submodule N, there is c≥0 such that for every n≥c, I^n M∩N=I^(n−c)(I^c M∩N). No assertion that the induced filtration equals I^n N is made.

items.name: Zero-dimensional Noetherian rings are Artinian
items.statement: A commutative Noetherian ring of Krull dimension at most zero is Artinian. Use this for R/I when R is Noetherian local and √I is its maximal ideal.

items.name: Finiteness of the minimal primes
items.statement: The set of minimal prime ideals of a commutative Noetherian ring is finite.

items.name: Finite prime avoidance
items.statement: For a finite set of prime ideals p_i in a commutative ring, an ideal J contained setwise in their union is contained in one p_i. The pinned statement permits two exceptional nonprime ideals; only its all-prime specialization is used here.
items.note: Actual statement and ambient hypotheses read at the pinned commit. This imports existing mathematics; no new Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Noetherianity of a finite-variable polynomial ring
items.statement: For a finite variable type and a commutative Noetherian coefficient ring A, MvPolynomial variables A is Noetherian. Consequently a finite module over it is Noetherian and its submodules are finite.
items.note: Actual statement and ambient hypotheses read at the pinned commit. This imports existing mathematics; no new Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Finiteness of homogeneous polynomial pieces
items.statement: Over a commutative semiring A, with a finite variable type, the degree-n homogeneous submodule of the multivariate polynomial algebra is finitely generated as an A-module.
items.note: Actual statement and ambient hypotheses read at the pinned commit. This imports existing mathematics; no new Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Ideal powers from homogeneous polynomials in generators
items.statement: For a tuple x:ι→R in a commutative semiring and n≥0, the nth power of the ideal generated by x is the image, under polynomial evaluation at x, of the degree-n homogeneous polynomial submodule. This identifies the actual powers used in the descending filtration.
items.note: Actual statement and ambient hypotheses read at the pinned commit. This imports existing mathematics; no new Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Counting monomials by multisets
items.statement: For a finite type α and n≥0, the number of multisets of size n on α is binom(card(α)+n−1,n), with natural subtraction. For e=card(α)≥1 this is binom(n+e−1,e−1). The zero-variable case is treated directly: one monomial in degree zero and none in positive degree.
items.note: Actual statement and ambient hypotheses read at the pinned commit. This imports existing mathematics; no new Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Finite length from the two chain conditions
items.statement: An R-module has finite length if and only if it is both Noetherian and Artinian. In particular finite modules over an Artinian commutative ring have finite length.
items.note: Actual statement and ambient hypotheses read at the pinned commit. This imports existing mathematics; no new Lean implementation is asserted.

items.name: Ideal-adic associated graded module
items.statement: For a commutative ring R, ideal I and R-module M, construct gr_I(M)=⊕_(n≥0) I^n M/I^(n+1)M over gr_I(R)=⊕_(n≥0) I^n/I^(n+1). The degree-zero coefficient ring is R/I, acting through quotient scalars. If I and M are finite, generators of I in degree one and of M/IM in degree zero give a surjection (R/I)[X1,…,Xe]^r→gr_I(M) of graded modules. Every degree is finite over R/I. No section R/I→R is assumed.
items.locator: Stacks 00K8, proof of Proposition10.59.5; 00K0, Lemma10.58.6; explicit quotient-carrier adapter.
proofSteps: Use the quotient of the submodule I^n M by the embedded submodule I^(n+1)M, not a quotient of unrelated ambient types. For a∈I^i and m∈I^j M, changing either representative by one filtration step changes am by an element of I^(i+j+1)M. The product and module action therefore descend, and their laws follow on representatives.

I annihilates every degree quotient. Define the R/I-action by quotient lifting of the R-action; independence of lifts uses precisely this annihilation. The identity of degree zero acts as the identity, also when I=R and all pieces vanish.

Evaluate homogeneous polynomials in a fixed finite generating tuple of I. L97 shows their degree-n images generate I^n. Multiply by fixed generators of M, then pass modulo I^(n+1)M. Coefficients reduce modulo I, proving surjectivity of the displayed graded free-module map.

Each source degree is a finite direct sum of L96 homogeneous pieces, so its quotient is finite. Module maps and compatible maps of ring/ideal/module triples descend degree by degree. Taking M=R and I=m gives Z66; it must consume this construction rather than independently invent it.
