items.name: Closed submodules of complete Noetherian Tate modules
items.statement: Let A be a complete Hausdorff commutative topological Tate ring. Let V be a complete Hausdorff uniform additive group with countably generated uniformity, an A-module with continuous scalar multiplication, and Noetherian as an A-module. Every A-submodule N of V is closed. No canonical module topology on V needs to be assumed; its complete topology is part of the hypotheses.
items.note: Read ambient binders and proof. This supplies ideal closedness after Tate-algebra Noetherianity and the norm/topology carrier comparison, not those premises themselves.

items.name: Completeness of the finite-module topology
items.statement: If A is a complete first-countable topological ring with compatible uniform additive group structure and M is a finite A-module, the canonical right uniformity of moduleTopology A M is complete. Hausdorffness of M is a separate conclusion requiring a closed presentation kernel.

items.name: Separatedness of the finite-module topology over a Tate ring
items.statement: For a complete Hausdorff Noetherian commutative topological Tate ring A and a finite A-module M, moduleTopology A M is Hausdorff.

items.name: Strictness of finite-module linear maps over a Tate ring
items.statement: Let A be a complete Hausdorff commutative topological Tate ring with countably generated uniformity. Let M,N be complete Hausdorff uniform additive groups with countably generated uniformities and continuous A-actions. If M is a finite A-module and N a Noetherian A-module, every A-linear map M→N is continuous and open onto its image, without a continuity assumption on that map.

items.name: Open mapping over a Tate ring
items.statement: Let A be a commutative topological Tate ring, M a complete uniform additive A-module with countably generated uniformity, nonarchimedean additive topology and continuous scalar multiplication, and N a complete Hausdorff uniform additive A-module with countably generated uniformity and continuous multiplication by each fixed scalar. A surjective A-linear map f:M→N that is continuous at zero is open and a quotient map. The source need not be Hausdorff.

items.name: The unique complete finite-module topology
items.statement: Let A be a complete commutative nonarchimedean Tate ring with compatible uniform additive group structure and countably generated uniformity. Every finite A-module M carrying a complete Hausdorff uniform additive topology with countably generated uniformity and continuous A-action has IsModuleTopology A M. No Noetherianity hypothesis on A is required for this uniqueness assertion.

items.name: Normed complete quotients by closed ideals
items.statement: Let R be a complete commutative normed ring and I a closed ideal. The quotient R/I has the quotient norm inf_{i∈I} ||r+i||, its topology is the quotient topology, it is a normed commutative ring and it is complete. If R is a normed K-algebra, R/I inherits that structure. The general declarations provide arbitrarily close norm lifts, not a norm-minimizing lift.

items.name: Completed restricted series recover the complete coefficient-series carrier
items.statement: For a commutative nonarchimedean topological ring A, if the one-weight restricted-series ring is complete and Hausdorff, restrictedMvPowerSeriesCompletion k A is canonically A-algebra-isomorphic to that restricted-series ring. Both directions are uniformly continuous and the equivalence fixes every restricted series inserted by the completion map.
items.note: The same file proves completeness from complete coefficients and separatedness from separated coefficients. The Gauss norm identification remains Z81; this is not a second Tate-algebra carrier.

items.name: Vanishing is detected at maximal localizations
items.statement: For a commutative ring R and r∈R, if r maps to zero in R_m for every maximal ideal m, then r=0.

items.name: Continuity of linear maps from a finite-dimensional space
items.statement: Over a complete nontrivially normed field K, every K-linear map from a finite-dimensional Hausdorff topological K-vector space E to a topological K-vector space F is continuous. The topologies are additive group topologies with continuous scalar multiplication.

items.name: Noetherianity of strict Tate algebras
items.statement: For a complete nontrivially valued nonarchimedean field K and n≥0, T_n(K)=K⟨X₁,…,X_n⟩ is Noetherian.
items.locator: Bosch Münster notes §1.2 Proposition13, printed15/PDF17; upstream AdicSpaces Layer0.5(4)–(5)
items.note: Already an explicit upstream milestone. No new route or second proof owner. The pinned strong-Noetherian class assumes this field theorem; it does not prove it.
proofSteps: Induct on n; T_0=K. For I=0 there is nothing to generate. Otherwise choose 0≠g∈I, make it distinguished using Z48, and use Z49 to make T_n/(g) a finite module over T_(n−1). If g is a unit then I=T_n and use the generator 1.

The image I/(g) is finite over the Noetherian T_(n−1). Lift finitely many generators and adjoin g. This generates I as a T_n-ideal. Apply L21 for quotients. Do not use the discrete-topology instance of IsStronglyNoetherian for a nontrivially valued field.

items.name: Gauss topology comparison for the existing restricted-series carrier
items.statement: For a complete nontrivially valued nonarchimedean field K and finitely many variables, the one-weight restricted-series topology on the existing Tau Ceti carrier is the topology of ||Σ a_ν X^ν||=max_ν |a_ν| (zero series has norm zero). Transporting along L109 gives the same Banach K-algebra as the usual strict Tate algebra. Constants and all coordinate variables are preserved.
items.locator: Bosch §1.2 definition of T_n and Gauss norm, PDF10–11; Tau Ceti WeightedRestrictedSeries/Basic and Complete; upstream AdicSpaces Layer0.5(1)–(2)
items.note: A norm/topology comparison on the existing carrier, not a proposed replacement. It is still a planning adapter and has not been elaborated.
proofSteps: Restrictedness means the coefficients tend to zero cofinitely. Their norms attain a maximum unless all vanish. The ultrametric inequality bounds each convolution coefficient, so the maximum norm is submultiplicative. Scalar multiplication has the required norm equality.

At weight one, the defining basic neighborhood associated to an open additive coefficient subgroup U consists exactly of series with every coefficient in U. Coefficient balls and these subgroups are cofinal in the normed-field case. This identifies the topologies, not merely the underlying series.

A Gauss-Cauchy sequence has coefficientwise limits; uniform smallness outside one finite support shows those limits still tend to zero. The convergence is uniform in the Gauss norm. Polynomials are dense by finite-support truncation. L109 supplies the canonical completion equivalence.

items.name: Closed ideals of strict Tate algebras
items.statement: Let K be complete, nontrivially valued and nonarchimedean. Every ideal of T_n(K) is closed for the Gauss topology.
items.locator: Bosch §1.3 Corollary8 and §1.4 Proposition4, PDF23,25; generic proof via pinned L102/L108; upstream AdicSpaces Layer0.6
items.note: The general closed-submodule result is library item L102. This is its affine specialization, imported from the existing upstream layer.
proofSteps: Apply L102 to the Tate algebra acting on itself: Z80 supplies Noetherianity; Z81 supplies the complete Hausdorff countably based topology. A scalar 0<|π|<1 is a topologically nilpotent unit, giving the Tate hypothesis.

items.name: Quotient Banach algebra topology on a strict affinoid presentation
items.statement: For a strict affinoid presentation A=T_n(K)/I over a complete nontrivially valued nonarchimedean field, the quotient norm inf_{i∈I} ||f+i|| is a complete nonarchimedean K-algebra norm and induces the quotient topology. The projection T_n→A is continuous, open and contractive. This item does not assert that every infimum is attained.
items.locator: Bosch §1.4 Proposition4(i)–(ii), PDF25; Mathlib quotient-norm declarations L108
proofSteps: Use Z82 and L108. To retain the ultrametric inequality, lift two quotient classes to representatives with norms arbitrarily close to their quotient norms; apply the ultrametric inequality upstairs and let the positive errors tend to zero. Scalar equality follows by rescaling representatives for a nonzero scalar.

The general quotient construction already gives the topology and completeness. Openness is L67. Norm-attaining representatives in Bosch4(iii) need the stronger strict-closedness result and are not used by this branch.

items.name: Finite jets at maximal ideals of a strict affinoid
items.statement: For a strict K-affinoid A and a maximal ideal m, A/m^r is finite-dimensional over K for each integer r≥1. This does not assert the existence of a coefficient-field section A/m→A/m^r.
items.locator: Bosch §1.4 Proposition3 and Lemma18 proof, PDF24,32; explicit filtration proof below
items.note: Existing owner AdicSpacesPartII:R0. Gives the finite-dimensional targets in the automatic-continuity proof.
proofSteps: A/m is a finite extension of K by Z51. Choose finitely many generators of m using Z80. Products of j such generators span m^j/m^(j+1) over A/m, so each graded piece has finite K-dimension. This uses its natural quotient scalar action, not a chosen embedding of A/m into A.
Induct using 0→m^(r−1)/m^r→A/m^r→A/m^(r−1)→0 and finite-dimensionality in an exact sequence. If A=0 there are no maximal ideals, and the quantified statement is vacuous.

items.name: Joint separation by maximal-ideal jets
items.statement: For a Noetherian commutative ring A, the family A→A/m^r over all maximal ideals m and integers r≥1 is jointly injective. No Jacobson, reducedness or coefficient-field hypothesis is needed.
items.locator: Bosch §1.4 Lemma18 final paragraph, PDF32; pinned Krull separation L03 and localization detection L110
items.note: Generic algebraic adapter owned by SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0; consumed by affinoid continuity, not an analytic-specific duplicate.
proofSteps: If a maps to zero in every jet quotient, its image in every A_m lies in every power of mA_m. The localized ring is Noetherian local, so L03 makes this image zero.
Apply L110. For the zero ring the conclusion still holds. Residue fields alone would only detect the Jacobson radical, so retain all r.

items.name: Automatic continuity of morphisms of strict affinoids
items.statement: Every K-algebra homomorphism f:A→B between strict K-affinoid algebras over a complete nontrivially valued nonarchimedean field is continuous for the quotient Banach topologies of any two chosen presentations.
items.locator: Bosch §1.4 Proposition19 and its closed-graph alternative, PDF33; full closed-graph argument below
items.note: Existing owner AdicSpacesPartII:R0. The proof supplies the alternative Bosch mentions; it is a source-level proof, not Lean code.
proofSteps: For each maximal m⊂B and r≥1, let g:A→B/m^r be the composite. Its kernel is an ideal of A, hence closed by Z105. The algebraic quotient A/ker(g) injects into the finite-dimensional K-space B/m^r and is finite-dimensional. Both quotient topologies are Hausdorff. L111 makes the induced linear map continuous, so g is continuous.

The graph of f in A×B is the intersection of the closed kernels of the continuous linear maps (a,b)↦g(a)−b mod m^r. Z85 gives equality with that intersection; no reducedness is used. Thus the graph is a closed, hence complete, nonarchimedean Banach K-subspace.

The first projection from the graph to A is continuous, linear and bijective. L106 makes its inverse continuous. Compose that inverse with the second projection to obtain continuity of f. If B=0 the map is already continuous.

items.name: Independence and functoriality of strict affinoid presentation topology
items.statement: Any two strict Tate-algebra quotient presentations of a K-affinoid algebra A induce the same topology. The identity between the two resulting Banach algebras is bicontinuous. Every algebra isomorphism of strict affinoids is bicontinuous. For an ideal J⊂A, the quotient topology agrees with that from the composed Tate-algebra presentation of A/J.
items.locator: Bosch §1.4 Proposition19, PDF33; Conrad Exercise2.2.3(1), PDF13
proofSteps: Apply Z86 to the identity in both directions and likewise to an algebra isomorphism and its inverse. Equality of the topologies follows from the two continuity assertions.

The two-step quotient map T_n→A→A/J is an open quotient map by L67 and composition. The algebraic quotient by the preimage of J has exactly this topology. This proves compatibility for each specific quotient map, rather than only an abstract homeomorphism.

items.name: Finite-module completion is tensoring with the completed ring
items.statement: For a Noetherian commutative ring R, ideal I and finite R-module M, the canonical map R̂_I⊗_R M→M̂_I is an R̂_I-linear equivalence and sends 1⊗m to the completion image of m.

items.name: Finite-type algebras over a Noetherian ring are Noetherian
items.statement: For commutative rings R,S with an R-algebra structure, if R is Noetherian and S is finite type over R, S is Noetherian.

items.name: Finite type is preserved by tensor base change
items.statement: For commutative R-algebras A,B, if A is finite type over R, then B⊗_R A is finite type over B.

items.name: Restricted integral series as polynomial-adic completion
items.statement: For a complete DVR O with uniformizer π and a finite variable set X, O⟨X⟩ is canonically the π-adic completion of O[X]. For each r≥1, reduction of coefficients identifies O⟨X⟩/π^r with (O/π^r)[X], preserving constants, variables and all transition maps. Its restricted-series topology is its π-adic topology.
items.locator: Conrad AWS Exercise3.3.1, PDF30; explicit coefficient proof
items.note: Existing owner AdicSpacesPartII:F0. This finite-level calculation never commutes localization with an arbitrary inverse limit.
proofSteps: A compatible family of polynomials modulo π^r gives, for each monomial, a compatible family of coefficients and hence an element of O. For fixed r only finitely many coefficients are nonzero modulo π^r, since the rth member is a polynomial. Thus the coefficient family is restricted.

Conversely reduce a restricted coefficient family modulo π^r; only finitely many coefficients survive. The constructions are inverse and preserve sums and convolution, since each fixed convolution coefficient uses finitely many pairs of monomials.

The reduction kernel consists of series whose coefficients lie in π^r O. Divide all coefficients by π^r; restrictedness is preserved by this fixed shift of valuation. Thus the kernel is exactly π^r O⟨X⟩, which identifies the neighborhood bases as well as the quotients. Use L109 for the existing completed carrier.

items.name: Completion respects finite-type polynomial presentations
items.statement: For O,π as in Z88, a finite variable set X and ideal I⊂O[X], the canonical map O⟨X⟩→(O[X]/I)̂_(π) is surjective with kernel I O⟨X⟩. It induces an O-algebra isomorphism O⟨X⟩/I O⟨X⟩≅(O[X]/I)̂_(π), preserving the π-adic topologies and the canonical maps from O[X]/I. Reduction modulo π^r agrees with (O[X]/I)/π^r for every r≥1.
items.locator: Conrad §3.3 and Exercise3.3.1, PDF30; algebraic exactness L06 and tensor comparison L112
items.note: Existing owner AdicSpacesPartII:F0. Finite-type presentation is essential to this particular exactness argument.
proofSteps: Set S=O[X]. It is Noetherian by L113. Apply L06 to the exact sequence 0→I→S→S/I→0; I is finite because S is Noetherian. Z88 identifies Ŝ with O⟨X⟩.

L112 identifies Î with Ŝ⊗_S I. Its image under the completed inclusion is exactly the ideal generated by the images of I, so the kernel is IŜ, not an unspecified closure. First-isomorphism and completed surjectivity yield the algebra equivalence.

L22 identifies each completed topology with the topology of the extended principal ideal. A surjective O-algebra map carries π^r times its source onto π^r times its target, so the isomorphism preserves both π-adic topologies. Alternatively, quotient Z88 at level r by the polynomial relations: both sides are S/(I+(π^r)).

items.name: Bounded denominators identify the generic restricted-series algebra
items.statement: Let O be a complete DVR with uniformizer π and fraction field K. For finitely many variables X, coefficient localization gives O⟨X⟩[1/π]≅K⟨X⟩. The topology induced by the open lattice O⟨X⟩ is the Gauss topology. After quotienting by any ideal I of O[X], it induces (O⟨X⟩/I O⟨X⟩)[1/π]≅K⟨X⟩/I K⟨X⟩ with the corresponding affinoid quotient topology.
items.locator: Conrad AWS Exercise3.3.1, PDF30; explicit bounded-denominator and quotient proof
items.note: Existing owner AdicSpacesPartII:F0. Uniform boundedness of denominators is the surjectivity argument; unrestricted formal K-power series would fail it.
proofSteps: A restricted K-coefficient family tends to zero; all but finitely many coefficients lie in O, and the finitely many remaining valuations have a common lower bound. A single π^N therefore clears every denominator. Conversely, dividing a restricted O-series by a fixed π^N leaves a restricted K-series. These maps preserve coefficients and convolution and are mutually inverse.
The O-series are exactly the Gauss unit ball, and π^r O⟨X⟩ for r∈Z form the usual Gauss neighborhood basis. This proves the topology assertion before quotienting.

Localization of a quotient is the quotient of the localization by the extended ideal. Its presentation agrees with Z83; Z87 ensures this is the intended presentation-independent affinoid topology. No assertion about localization of arbitrary inverse limits is used.

items.name: Finite-level comparison for integral completed tensor products
items.statement: Let B_i be a finite family of finite-type O-algebras over a complete DVR O, and C_i their π-adic completions. Put P=⊗_O B_i, with P=O for the empty family. For each r≥1 there is a canonical factor-compatible isomorphism P/π^r≅⊗_(O/π^r)(C_i/π^r), compatible with r. Thus P̂_(π) is the π-adic completed tensor product of the C_i, defined by the inverse limit of the right-hand side. This is an isomorphism of complete topological O-algebras.
items.locator: Conrad Exercise3.3.8, PDF32, specialized to finite-type affine models; LLHLM23 Theorem3.7.1 PDF79–80; explicit finite-quotient proof
items.note: Existing owner AdicSpacesPartII:F0. Together with Z89/Z90 and the quotient presentation Z52, this supplies the integral and generic identifications in Z55.
proofSteps: By Z89 replace C_i/π^r with B_i/π^r, respecting each factor map. The universal property of the ordinary algebra tensor product identifies the tensor of these reductions with P/π^r. The two maps are induced by the same factor inclusions, so they commute with every reduction transition.

Take inverse limits of this isomorphism of inverse systems. The limit maps are inverse because they are inverse at every finite level; their topologies have the same kernels of finite-level projections. The empty system of factors gives lim_r O/π^r=O by completeness.

Equivalently the ordinary tensor Q=⊗_O C_i satisfies Q/π^r≅⊗_(O/π^r)(C_i/π^r). This comparison does not assert that Q itself is Noetherian; the Noetherian ring used for subsequent completion-flatness is P.

items.name: Flatness descends along faithfully flat scalar extension
items.statement: For a commutative ring R, commutative R-algebra S and R-module M, if S is faithfully flat over R and S⊗_R M is flat over S, then M is flat over R.

items.name: Regularity of polynomial rings over regular rings
items.statement: If R is a commutative regular Noetherian ring, R[X] and the polynomial algebra in any finite variable type over R are regular Noetherian rings.

items.name: A flat local ring map is faithfully flat
items.statement: For commutative local rings A,B and an A-algebra structure on B, if B is A-flat and A→B is a local homomorphism, then B is faithfully flat over A.

items.name: Noetherian modules descend along faithfully flat base change
items.statement: Let A be a faithfully flat commutative R-algebra and M an R-module. If A⊗_R M is Noetherian as an A-module, then M is Noetherian as an R-module. Taking M=R gives descent of Noetherianity of rings.
items.note: Continuation note (issue #1254): library citations corrected against the pinned Mathlib commit, where the previously recorded names do not exist; the declarations now cited do.

items.name: Regularity descends along flat local maps
items.statement: If A→B is a flat local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings and B is regular, then A is regular.
items.locator: Stacks00OF, Lemma10.110.9, statement and full proof read 23 September2026
items.note: The former Z78 text incorrectly suggested descending a free resolution of κ_B. This proof instead base changes a resolution of κ_A and descends flatness of one finite syzygy. Z100/Z101 expose the remaining homological suppliers.
proofSteps: The map is faithfully flat by L117. Let d=dim B. If d=0, B is a field; locality gives m_A B=0 and faithfulness gives m_A=0, so A is a field.

For d>0, start with a resolution of the A-residue field κ_A by finite free A-modules, formed by successively choosing generators of kernels over the Noetherian ring A. Tensor that A-resolution with B. Flatness preserves exactness and the terminal module is B⊗_A κ_A, not necessarily κ_B.

The global-dimension bound Z100 makes its dth syzygy projective over B. The syzygy is finite, hence free over local B. L115 descends flatness of this syzygy to A, and L81 makes the finite A-syzygy free. Therefore κ_A has a finite free resolution, and Z101 makes A regular.

items.name: Faithfully flat descent of regular ring maps
items.statement: Let A→B→C be homomorphisms of commutative rings. If A→C is regular and B→C is faithfully flat, then A→B is regular. Regularity here includes Noetherian, geometrically regular fibres as in Z76.
items.locator: Stacks07NT, Lemma15.42.7, statement and full proof read 23 September2026
items.note: This is descent of a map, whereas Z78 is descent of a ring property. The extra field-extension quantifier is essential.
proofSteps: To prove A-flatness of B, tensor an injection of A-modules with B and then with C over B. The composite is tensoring with the A-flat module C and remains injective; faithful flatness of C over B reflects injectivity. This establishes the flatness criterion for B.

For a prime p⊂A, the map B⊗_A κ(p)→C⊗_A κ(p) is faithfully flat, as is its base change along every finite field extension L/κ(p). The targets are regular Noetherian by regularity of A→C; Z78 descends both properties to the sources. This gives the full geometric fibre condition.

items.name: Identical completions for a flat local map with identical closed fibre
items.statement: Let A→B be a flat local map of Noetherian local rings such that m_A B=m_B and κ_A→κ_B is an isomorphism. It induces an isomorphism Â_(m_A)→B̂_(m_B), respecting A and all finite quotient maps.
items.locator: Stacks0AGX, Lemma15.44.9, statement and full proof read; finite-quotient alternative supplied here
proofSteps: Flatness identifies (m_A^r/m_A^(r+1))⊗_A B with m_B^r/m_B^(r+1). Since the first graded piece is annihilated by m_A and the residue fields agree, the map between these graded pieces is an isomorphism for every r.
Start with the residue-field isomorphism for r=1. Induct on r using the exact rows 0→m^r/m^(r+1)→A/m^(r+1)→A/m^r→0 and their B versions. The outside isomorphisms give the middle one.

These finite-quotient isomorphisms commute with reduction because all come from A→B. Their inverse limit is the required algebra isomorphism, with inverse continuous for the completion topologies. This argument explicitly proves the comparison used in Z57.

items.name: Regularity of ring maps is local at target maximal ideals
items.statement: For A→B with B Noetherian, the map is regular exactly when A_p→B_q is regular for every prime q of B and its contraction p; it suffices to test maximal q and their contractions (the contractions need not be maximal in A).
items.locator: Stacks07C0, Lemma15.42.2, statement and proof read 23 September2026
proofSteps: Flatness is local on target and source local rings. For each residue field and each finite field extension, regularity of the Noetherian fibre is tested on its local rings.

Localizing a regular map preserves flatness and the regularity of every geometrically extended fibre. Every target prime is contained in a maximal ideal, so the maximal-local test supplies every local test. No maximality of the contracted prime is inserted.

items.name: Regular local rings and their maximal-ideal completions
items.statement: For a Noetherian local ring A, A is regular if and only if its maximal-ideal completion is regular.
items.locator: Stacks07NY, Lemma15.44.4, statement and complete proof read 23 September2026
items.note: The same upstream ModularCurves §4D local completion-regularity atom already supplies Z23/Z28. Z96 names its coefficient-field-free equivalence, not a second proof owner. Import the foundational atom without a dependency on modular-curve applications.
proofSteps: Z25 gives a Noetherian completion; L08 identifies its maximal ideal as m_A Â. If A is regular, generators of m_A on dim A elements generate m_Â. Z28 preserves dimension, so L18/L19 give regularity of the completion.
Conversely apply Z92 to the flat local completion map, using L11 and L08. This proof neither assumes nor concludes that an arbitrary I-adic completion is local.

items.name: Derivations extend to adic completion
items.statement: For a derivation D:R→R of a commutative ring and an ideal I, there is a canonical continuous derivation D̂:R̂_I→R̂_I extending D. For r≥1 it satisfies D̂((I R̂)^(r+1))⊂(I R̂)^r when these powers give the completion topology.
items.locator: Stacks07PE, Lemma15.49.1(1), statement and full proof read 23 September2026
proofSteps: The Leibniz rule gives D(I^(r+1))⊂I^r. Thus D induces compatible additive maps R/I^(r+1)→R/I^r. Passing to the inverse limit gives D̂ with one step of precision loss.

Addition and Leibniz hold after every finite projection, hence hold in the separated inverse limit. The same precision bound gives continuity and uniqueness among continuous extensions because R is dense. Do not assert D(I^r)⊂I^r.

items.name: A derivation detects regular hypersurface quotients
items.statement: Let R be a regular Noetherian commutative ring and f∈R. If a derivation D:R→R sends f to an element whose image is a unit in R/(f), then R/(f) is regular.
items.locator: Stacks07PF, Lemma15.49.2, statement and full proof read 23 September2026
proofSteps: Localize at a prime containing f, extending D by the quotient rule. If f lay in the square of the local maximal ideal, Leibniz would put D(f) in the maximal ideal, contradicting its invertibility modulo f.

Thus f has nonzero cotangent class and belongs to a minimal generating set of the maximal ideal. Apply Z103 with one generator. Primes not containing f do not occur in the quotient. If f is a unit the quotient is zero, which is regular by the empty-prime condition.

items.name: Characteristic-zero formal fibres in the one-polynomial-variable reduction
items.statement: Let R be a complete regular local domain with fraction field K of characteristic zero. Let q⊂R[x] be maximal over m_R and r⊂q prime with r∩R=0. Then R[x]_q̂⊗_(R[x]) κ(r) is geometrically regular over κ(r).
items.locator: Corrected characteristic-zero step in Stacks07PV, using 07PE and 07PF; source finding E60
items.note: This is a source-level correction proof. No claim that the entire G-ring stability proof, especially its characteristic-p branch, is closed or implemented. Passing from a regular local ring to regularity of all its localizations uses the existing R03.3 regular-local/global-dimension package (Z100), rather than an unprovided instance at the pin.
proofSteps: Polynomial regularity is L116. Localize at q, complete using Z96, then invert R minus zero. The resulting Noetherian ring C=R[x]_q̂⊗_R K is regular. Localizations of regular rings are regular by the prime-local definition.

If r=0, the fibre further localizes C by the nonzero elements of K[x]. If r≠0, rK[x]=(g) for a nonconstant irreducible g∈K[x], and the fibre is C/(g), not a localization of the completion. In characteristic zero g is separable, so Bezout for g,g′ makes g′ a unit modulo g.

The R-derivation d/dx extends to R[x]_q and its completion using the quotient rule and Z97, and then to C. It sends g to g′. Apply Z98 to obtain regularity of C/(g). Finally a Noetherian algebra over a characteristic-zero field is geometrically regular when it is regular, since finite field extensions are separable. The finite-separable base-change supplier remains recorded in the regularity gap, rather than replaced by an assertion for imperfect fields.

items.name: Global-dimension bound for a regular local ring
items.statement: A regular local ring of Krull dimension d has global dimension at most d. In particular, for any module, the dth syzygy in a projective resolution is projective.
items.locator: Stacks00O7, Proposition10.110.1 (global-dimension consequence), and its cited dimension-shifting criterion
items.note: Import the existing R03.3 depth-auslander-buchsbaum-and-dimension-bounds node. This continuation exposes the inner source-proof contracts; their remaining atom/declaration adapters are listed in analytic-regularity-suppliers. No formal implementation is claimed.
proofSteps: Z116 bounds pd for finite modules by d. Z118 passes to all modules using the well-ordered extension lemma Z117.
Iterating the pinned one-step syzygy equivalence L122, with L121 at dimension zero, makes the dth syzygy in any projective resolution projective. For d=0 the module itself is projective.

items.name: Finite projective dimension of the residue field forces regularity
items.statement: If (A,m,κ) is a Noetherian local ring and κ has finite projective dimension over A, then A is a regular local ring.
items.locator: Stacks00OC, Proposition10.110.5, implication(1)⇒(3), statement and full outer proof read
items.note: Import the existing R03.3 depth-auslander-buchsbaum-and-dimension-bounds node. This continuation exposes the inner source-proof contracts; their remaining atom/declaration adapters are listed in analytic-regularity-suppliers. No formal implementation is claimed.
proofSteps: Z125 gives embdim R≤pd_R κ; Z128 gives pd_R κ≤dim R. The opposite inequality dim R≤embdim R is already available in the regular-local supplier chain.
Hence dim R=embdim R, and L19 identifies this with regularity. The proof uses a possibly nonexact Koszul source and a minimal exact target; it does not assume regularity of the generators beforehand.

items.name: Smooth algebras over arbitrary fields are regular
items.statement: For any field k, every smooth finitely presented k-algebra S is a regular Noetherian ring. No perfection assumption on k is required.
items.locator: Stacks00TT, Lemma10.140.3 final assertion, complete proof read 23 September2026
proofSteps: After extending to an algebraically closed field and choosing a geometric point over a given prime, smoothness remains true by L60. In a standard smooth presentation the invertible Jacobian minor makes the cotangent dimension equal the local dimension; the corresponding local ring is regular.

The map from the original local ring to that geometric local ring is flat local. Apply Z92 to descend regularity. The standard-smooth Jacobian and finite-type dimension inputs are shared with Z41–Z44 and remain in the source/declaration audit queue. This is not the converse asserting that every regular algebra over an imperfect field is smooth.

items.name: Quotient by part of a regular system of parameters
items.statement: Let A be a Noetherian regular local ring of dimension d and let x₁,…,x_d minimally generate its maximal ideal. For 0≤c≤d, A/(x₁,…,x_c) is a regular local ring of dimension d−c.
items.locator: Stacks00NQ, Lemma10.106.3, statement and complete proof read 23 September2026
items.note: Existing generic owner DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.3: this parameter-system specialization consumes the existing regular-sequence carrier and supplies the regular-local homological branch. It is not a new SchemeAndStackFoundations target.
proofSteps: For c=0 use A itself. For c=1 with d>0, the chosen x₁ is nonzero, and Z62 makes it a non-zero-divisor. The local quotient is Noetherian and its maximal ideal is generated by the remaining d−1 elements. The principal-quotient dimension bound and L18 give dimension exactly d−1, hence regularity by L19.

Repeat on the quotient: the remaining generators are minimal because their number equals its dimension. At c=d the quotient is the residue field. This proves the quotient regularity and dimension assertion; the separate regular-sequence consequence is Z104.

items.name: Closed ideals of strict affinoid quotients
items.statement: For every ideal I of T_n(K), every ideal of A=T_n(K)/I is closed in the quotient Banach topology. This includes the zero quotient.
items.locator: Bosch Münster notes §1.4 Proposition4, printed23/PDF25; upstream AdicSpaces Layer0.6
proofSteps: For an ideal J of A, its inverse image under T_n(K)→A is an ideal and is closed by Z82. The projection is a quotient map by Z83/L67. The quotient-topology criterion therefore makes J closed. This argument also covers A=0.
items.note: Existing upstream owner; separate from Tate closedness and quotient completeness so that each downstream proof can cite the required conclusion.

items.name: Regular systems of parameters are regular sequences
items.statement: In a Noetherian regular local ring A of dimension d, every minimal generating sequence x₁,…,x_d of the maximal ideal is an A-regular sequence. The empty sequence for a field is included.
proofSteps: By Z103, each quotient by an initial segment is regular local of the expected dimension. It is a domain by Z62. If the next parameter exists, its cotangent class is nonzero because the remaining system is minimal, so it is a non-zero-divisor in that domain. The final quotient is the nonzero residue field. This proves the regular-sequence conditions, including properness.
items.note: Existing generic owner DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.3: this parameter-system specialization consumes the existing regular-sequence carrier and supplies the regular-local homological branch. It is not a new SchemeAndStackFoundations target.

items.name: Projective dimension of a regular-sequence quotient
items.statement: For a commutative Noetherian local ring R, a list rs forming an R-regular sequence has pd_R(R/(rs))=length(rs). The pinned categorical statement uses ModuleCat and a universe shrink with Small R.
items.note: The carrier and quotient projective-dimension formula already exist, as AUDIT-17 records. This alone does not assert the global-dimension criterion Z100 or its converse Z101.

items.name: Affine root subgroups in a conjugated Iwahori
items.statement: Fix x ∈ A0. If w̃ ∈ W̃ and we set z̃ = w̃^* ∈ W̃^∨, then (for α ∈ Φ and m ∈ Z) U_{−α,m} ⊂ z̃^{-1} I_F z̃ if and only if ⟨w̃(x), α^∨⟩ < m.
items.note: Added: numbered result without an item. Until now only M12's statement restated it, inside a construction item located at 'Lemmas 4.2.7–8'. The lemma has two assertions. The paper proves only this one and says 'The proof of the second part is similar', so the second assertion is M39. Proof (PDF85): write w̃^{-1} = s t_ν. Lemma 4.2.7 (M12), applied to w̃^{-1} with (w̃^{-1})^* = z̃^{-1} (* reverses products, E1), turns the condition into U_{−s(α), m+⟨ν,α^∨⟩} ⊂ I_F. That means m + ⟨ν,α^∨⟩ ≥ δ_{s(α)>0} = ⌈⟨x, s(α)^∨⟩⌉, i.e. m > ⟨s^{-1}(x) − ν, α^∨⟩ = ⟨w̃(x), α^∨⟩. I checked this against the page image.

uses.how: At w̃ = e it gives U_{−α,m} ⊂ I_F iff ⟨x,α^∨⟩ < m, the lower bound in (4.3).
In the proof of Theorem 4.2.4 (PDF87), in its Lie-algebra form, v L^∇_a(N_{w̃*}) ∈ (w̃^*)^{-1} Lie I_F w̃^* is equivalent to v^{⌊⟨w̃(x),α^∨⟩⌋} dividing each −α-entry.
The proof of Lemma 4.3.8 (PDF91) gets v Lie L_α ⊂ (z̃′)^{-1} Lie I_F z̃′ from |⟨(z̃′)^*(x), ±α^∨⟩| < 1.

items.name: Affine root subgroups in a conjugated negative loop group
items.statement: Fix x ∈ A0. If w̃ ∈ W̃ and we set z̃ = w̃^* ∈ W̃^∨, then (for α ∈ Φ and m ∈ Z) U_{−α,m} ⊂ z̃^{-1} L^{--}G_F z̃ if and only if m < ⟨w̃(x), α^∨⟩.
items.note: Added: numbered result without an item. This is the second assertion of Lemma 4.2.8, and its proof is only called 'similar'. The same reduction through Lemma 4.2.7 turns the condition into U_{−s(α), m+⟨ν,α^∨⟩} ⊂ L^{--}G_F. By the criterion on PDF84 (U_{β,k} ⊂ L^{--}G_F iff k ≤ −δ_{β>0}), this is m + ⟨ν,α^∨⟩ ≤ −δ_{s(α)<0} = ⌊⟨x, s(α)^∨⟩⌋. Since ⟨x, s(α)^∨⟩ is not an integer, this is equivalent to m < ⟨w̃(x), α^∨⟩. I checked this derivation; the paper does not print it.

uses.how: Gives the upper bound m < ⟨w̃(x),α^∨⟩ in (4.3). Proposition 4.2.10 is proved 'from the definition of N_z̃ and Lemma 4.2.8'.

items.name: Finite Weyl invariance of ambient Schubert closures
items.statement: Let s̃, w, w̃1 be as in Proposition 4.3.6 (s̃ ∈ W̃, w̃1 ∈ W̃1^+, s̃ (n−1)-generic, w ∈ W). Then the closure of S°_F(w̃1, e, s̃) equals the closure of S°_F(w̃1, e, s̃w^{-1}), where closure is taken in Fl.
items.note: Added: numbered result without an item. It was named only inside M23's statement and in a route gap note ('proof-only input leaves (including 4.3.7–4.3.8 …)'). Proof (PDF90): translating by (s̃^*)^{-1} reduces to s̃ = e. It then suffices that the closure of S°(w̃1^*w0) = I_F\I_F w̃1^*w0 I_F is stable under right multiplication by W^∨. The product w̃1^*w′ is reduced for every w′ ∈ W^∨ (gallery argument; * preserves length), so [45, Prop. 2.8] puts each I_F\I_F w̃1^* I_F w′ I_F in that closure. The Bruhat decomposition L^+GL_n = ∪_{w′} I_F w′ I_F then identifies the closure with that of I_F\I_F w̃1^* L^+GL_n, which is W^∨-stable. The genericity hypothesis is not used.

uses.how: The proof of Proposition 4.3.6 (PDF91) uses it to show that S^{∇0}(w̃1,e,s̃) ∩ S°(w̃1,e,s̃s_α) is open in S^{∇0}(w̃1,e,s̃).

items.name: Adjacent fixed point in the differential closure
items.statement: Let s̃, w̃1 be as in Proposition 4.3.6 (s̃ ∈ W̃, w̃1 ∈ W̃1^+, s̃ (n−1)-generic). If s_α is a simple reflection for α ∈ Δ, then w̃1^* w0 s_α s̃^* ∈ S^{∇0}_F(w̃1, e, s̃).
items.note: Added: numbered result without an item. It was named only inside M23's statement. Proof (PDF90–91): let z̃ = w̃1^*w0 and z̃′ = z̃s_α. By Lemma 2.1.4, z̃′ ≤ z̃ and ℓ(z̃′) = ℓ(z̃) − 1. Let L_α be the minimal standard Levi containing U_{±α,0}. Then X_α := I_F\I_F z̃′ L_α ≅ P^1_F lies in the closure of S°(z̃) ([67, Prop. 8.8]). Next, X_α s̃^* ⊆ Fl^{∇0} by (4.8). With s̃^* = s^{-1}t_μ we have v(d/dv)(s̃^*)(s̃^*)^{-1} = Diag(s^{-1}(μ)), so it suffices that v Lie L_α ⊂ (z̃′)^{-1} Lie I_F z̃′. That follows from M38, because 0 < ⟨w̃1(x), −w0(α)^∨⟩ < 1 gives |⟨(z̃′)^*(x), ±α^∨⟩| < 1. Since X_α ∩ S°(z̃) is dense in X_α, X_α s̃^* ⊂ S^{∇0}(w̃1,e,s̃), and z̃′s̃^* is the stated point. The genericity hypothesis is not used.

uses.how: The proof of Proposition 4.3.6 (PDF91) uses the point to show that S^{∇0}(w̃1,e,s̃) ∩ S°(w̃1,e,s̃s_α) is nonempty.

items.name: Serre-labelled components lie in the crystalline special fibre
items.statement: Lemma 7.4.4. Setting of §7.4: K/Q_p finite unramified, zeta in X^*(Z), lambda in X_*(T)^J regular dominant with lambda_j in [0,h]^n, and tau = tau(s, mu+eta) with lowest alcove presentation (s,mu). Assume that mu is (4n+h)-deep in C_0. Let sigma in JH(W(lambda-eta) ⊗ sigmabar(tau)). Then C_sigma ⊂ X^{lambda,tau} ⊂ X^{<=lambda,tau}; that is, the reduced component C_sigma of X_{n,red} is contained in X^{lambda,tau}_red. Proof: by Proposition 2.3.7 (noting the eta-shift), sigma is 4n-deep. Every rhobar of the form (7.15) for sigma is then 4n-generic, and it lies in X^{lambda,tau}(Fbar) by Proposition 6.2.9. Such points are dense in C_sigma.
items.note: Added: numbered result without an item. The proof on PDF159 contains a harmless typo ('any such rhobar of lies').

uses.how: Lower bound: X^{lambda,tau} has at least #JH(W(lambda-eta) ⊗ sigmabar(tau)) irreducible components of dimension d_J.
Shows that Xtilde^{<=lambda,tau}_red exhausts the top-dimensional components of the naive local model.

items.name: Lowest-alcove depth is P_m-genericity
items.statement: Suppose that G = GL_n^J. Let P_m(X_1,…,X_n) = ∏_{i=1}^n ∏_{j=1}^m (X_i − X_{i+1} − j), where X_{n+1} is understood to be X_1. Then, for λ with λ − η ∈ C_0, λ − η is m-deep if and only if λ is P_m-generic (Definition 2.1.10(4), in every embedding).
items.note:
Added: numbered result without an item. Attached to N17 (polynomial genericity, Definition 2.1.10(4)); N17's api entry PolyGeneric.Pm_iff_deep already names it, so keep one owner. No proof is printed. Check from the page: with 0<⟨λ,α^∨⟩

0, the factors i

uses.how: §8.4.1, PDF174: P̃_{η,e} = P_{η,e}·P_{7n−3} 'see … Remark 2.1.11(2)', so P̃_{η,e}-genericity includes (7n−3)-depth.
Remark 9.1.7(1), PDF184: the factor P_{6n−2} of the polynomial in Theorem 9.1.6 comes from Remark 2.1.11.
Lemma 9.1.9 proof, PDF184: P = QP_{4n} makes ρ̄ 4n-generic, as Proposition 7.4.7(3) needs.
Lemma 9.1.10 proof, PDF185: P_{6n−2} | P gives the (6n−2)-genericity for Proposition 6.2.3.

items.name: Zero-monodromy inclusion of inertial parameters
items.statement: Both inertial L-parameters and Weil–Deligne inertial L-parameters are denoted τ (similarly for inertial types). There is a natural inclusion from the set of (tame) inertial L-parameters (resp. inertial types) to the set of (tame) Weil–Deligne L-parameters (resp. Weil–Deligne inertial types), sending an inertial L-parameter τ (resp. inertial type) to the Weil–Deligne inertial L-parameter (resp. Weil–Deligne inertial type) with ρ_τ = τ and N_τ = 0. Through this inclusion the (tame) inertial L-parameters (resp. inertial types) are regarded as a subset of the (tame) Weil–Deligne ones. There is also a surjective map in the other direction, given by forgetting the nilpotent element, for which the inclusion is a section.
items.note: Added: numbered result without an item. Attached to N56 (Weil–Deligne inertial parameter, Definition 2.5.1). N56's api WDInertialType.ofInertial and its test zero_N record the same map; keep one owner. Injectivity: conjugating (τ,0) conjugates τ. With N=0 the Weil–Deligne condition is vacuous once τ extends to the Weil group, which holds by the definition of an inertial L-parameter.

uses.how: Definition 6.2.1(I), PDF127: 'whenever τ is an inertial L-parameter (so N = 0 as in Remark 2.5.2)'; R_∞(λ,τ) is formed with the WD type (τ,0).
Definition 6.2.1(IV), PDF127: the set S of types (λ+η,τ) with τ inertial (so N_τ = 0).
§8.1, PDF163: types (λ+η,τ) have τ a WD inertial type; the minimal extremal types are those with N_τ = 0, i.e. the images of inertial types.

api.name: InertialType.toWD
api.statement: An inertial L-parameter (resp. inertial type) τ gives the Weil–Deligne inertial L-parameter (resp. type) (ρ_τ, N_τ) = (τ, 0).

api.name: WDInertialType.forgetN
api.statement: (ρ_τ, N_τ) ↦ ρ_τ is a surjection from (tame) Weil–Deligne inertial L-parameters (resp. types) onto (tame) inertial L-parameters (resp. types).

api.name: WDInertialType.forgetN_toWD
api.statement: forgetN (toWD τ) = τ, so toWD is a section of forgetN.

api.name: InertialType.toWD_injective
api.statement: toWD is injective on G^∨(E)-conjugacy classes.

api.name: InertialType.isTame_toWD
api.statement: toWD τ is tame iff τ is tame, since tameness only concerns ρ_τ.

tests.name: InertialType.toWD_GL1
tests.statement: For G = GL_1 every nilpotent element of Lie G^∨ is 0, so toWD and forgetN are inverse bijections.

tests.name: WDInertialType.fibre_trivial_GL2
tests.statement: For GL_2 and τ trivial on inertia, the fibre of forgetN over τ has exactly two classes, (1,0) = toWD τ and (1,[[0,1],[0,0]]), the restriction of Steinberg.

tests.name: WDInertialType.forgetN_not_injective
tests.statement: forgetN is not injective for n ≥ 2: (1,0) and (1,[[0,1],[0,0]]) have the same image, so toWD is not surjective.

tests.name: InertialType.toWD_regular
tests.statement: N_τ commutes with ρ_τ(I) (‖g‖ = 1 on inertia); if τ is a sum of pairwise distinct characters, the only WD type over τ is toWD τ.

items.name: Smallness bounds the cell coordinate degrees
items.statement: Fix x ∈ A_0, and for w̃ ∈ W̃ and α ∈ Φ let d_{α,w̃} = ⌊⟨w̃(x),α^∨⟩⌋ − ⌈⟨x,α^∨⟩⌉. If w̃ is m-small, then d_{α,w̃} ≤ m for any α ∈ Φ.
items.note: Added: numbered result without an item. Attached to M14, which defines d_{α,w̃}. If S1 splits M14, attach it to the Corollary 4.2.12 part. No proof is printed. Check: write w̃ = s t_ν. Then ⟨w̃(x),α^∨⟩ = ⟨ν,s^{-1}α^∨⟩ + ⟨x,s^{-1}α^∨⟩, where the first term is an integer ≤ h_ν ≤ m and the second lies in (−1,1). So the floor is ≤ m, and ⌈⟨x,α^∨⟩⌉ = δ_{α>0} ≥ 0.

uses.how: Theorem 4.2.4 proof, PDF87: 'By Remark 4.2.11, d_{α,w̃} ≤ m for all −α ∈ Supp(N_{w̃*})', so m-genericity of ā makes i+δ_{α>0}+⟨ā,α^∨⟩ ≠ 0 for i < d_{α,w̃}, and the lower coefficients c_{α,i} can be solved for.

items.name: Equidimensionality of the naive special fibre (claimed without proof)
items.statement: (In the setting of Theorem 4.6.2.) One can show that M^nv_J(≤λ,∇_a)_F is equidimensional of dimension d_J when λ is regular, using arguments similar to those of the proof of Theorem 4.3.9. The paper says it will not need this and does not pursue it.
items.note: Added: numbered result without an item. Attached to M30 (Theorem 4.6.2). The paper gives no proof. Remark 7.4.3(4) nevertheless uses it, and G34's statement includes that strengthening (sourceIssue: gap). A proof must show that each lower-dimensional piece S°(w̃*) ∩ Fl^{∇_a}, for w̃ ∈ Adm(λ) non-regular (Theorem 4.2.4, Corollary 4.2.6), lies in the closure of a d_J-dimensional one. Part (2) of the remark is unused (see kept).

uses.how: Remark 7.4.3(4), PDF159: 'Using the fact that M^nv_J(≤λ,∇_{a_τ})_F is equidimensional (cf. Remark 4.6.3)', Theorem 7.4.2(1) strengthens to X^{≤λ,τ}_red = ∪_σ C_σ, and X^{≤λ,τ}_F is equidimensional.

items.name: Covering read off from torus-fixed points of components
items.statement: If σ, σ′ are two Serre weights for which Proposition 4.7.3 holds (P_{w̃_{1,j}}(ω_j) ≢ 0 mod p for all j ∈ J, for their ζ-compatible lowest alcove presentations), then Proposition 2.3.12 shows that σ covers σ′ if and only if all the T^{∨,J}-fixed points of C^ζ_{σ′} lie in C^ζ_σ.
items.note: Added: numbered result without an item. Attached to M33 (Proposition 4.7.3). By Proposition 4.7.3 each fixed-point set is {w̃^* t_ω : w̃ ≤ w_0w̃_1} = (t_ω W̃_{≤w_0w̃_1})^*, using that * is order-preserving and anti-multiplicative (E1). So inclusion of fixed-point sets is the interval inclusion of Proposition 2.3.12(3) (N47). The depth hypotheses of Proposition 2.3.12 are left implicit: covering is only defined for 3h_η-deep weights, and compatible presentations are needed. Both applications concern generic, hence (6n−2)-deep, weights. Remark 4.7.4(1) says that whether P_{w̃_{1,j}}(ω_j) ≢ 0 mod p does not depend on the representative (w̃_1,ω). That is what makes 'σ for which Proposition 4.7.3 holds' well defined. It is not cited separately and is folded in here.

uses.how: Remark 8.6.4, PDF179: 'σ ∈ W^?(ρ̄) by Proposition 2.3.12(3) (see Remark 4.7.4(2)) and Theorem 4.7.6(2)'.
Lemma 9.1.10 proof, PDF186: ρ̄ ∈ C_{σ′} for some σ′ that σ covers, 'Then ρ̄ ∈ C_σ by Remark 4.7.4(2)'.

items.name: Standard parameters for the étale comparison diagram
items.statement: In Proposition 5.4.7 (τ with lowest alcove presentation (s,μ), μ (h+1)-deep in C_0, and λ_j ∈ [0,h]^n) there is a natural choice of a, b, z̃, namely a = 0, b = h and z̃ = s^{-1}t_{μ+η} = w̃^*(τ). To compare multiple types it can be convenient to make other choices.
items.note: Added: numbered result without an item. Attached to K34 (Proposition 5.4.7). The remark only names the choice. That it satisfies the hypotheses of Proposition 5.4.7 is immediate: ν = μ is (b−a+1) = (h+1)-deep by the hypothesis on τ, and (Gr̃^{[0,h],J}_{G,F})w̃^*(τ) ⊂ Fl̃^{[0,h]}_{J,w̃^*(τ)} holds by the definition of the latter.

uses.how: Proposition 5.5.7 proof, PDF123: 'the diagram in Proposition 5.4.7 with a = 0, b = h and z̃ = w̃^*(τ)'.
§7.4, diagram (7.16), PDF160: 'Proposition 5.4.7 specialized with a = 0, b = h and z̃ = w̃^*(τ)', used for Theorem 7.4.2(2) and Proposition 7.4.7.

items.name: No n-generic tame parameters when p divides 2n
items.statement: For our purposes, the hypothesis p ∤ 2n is often implicitly assumed, since if p | 2n then there are no n-generic tame inertial L-parameters.
items.note: Added: numbered result without an item. Attached to P10 (Proposition 6.2.4(1), which assumes p ∤ 2n). The paragraph after the remark imposes p ∤ 2n for the rest of §6.2 on this ground. As printed the claim needs n ≥ 2 (sourceIssue). For n ≥ 2, an n-deep μ in C_0 has ⟨μ+η,α_i^∨⟩ ≥ n+1 on each simple root and ⟨μ+η,θ^∨⟩ < p−n on the highest root, so p > (n−1)(n+1)+n = n²+n−1 > 2n. For n = 1 there are no roots, and every tame character is n-generic, including when p = 2.

uses.how: Proposition 6.2.6, PDF129: the standing assumption p ∤ 2n, justified by this remark, supplies the hypothesis of Proposition 6.2.4 used in its proof.
Theorem 8.4.10(1), PDF173: minimal patching functors for (6n−2)-generic ρ̄ are obtained from §6.2 without a separate p ∤ 2n hypothesis; the genericity forces it.

items.name: Only generic weights occur in polynomial-generic types
items.statement: If σ is not generic (Definition 8.4.6), then σ ∉ JH(σ̄(λ,τ)) for any (λ+η,τ) ∈ S_{P,Λ,t}. Hence any σ such that Z_σ occurs in Corollary 8.4.12 must be generic.
items.note: Added: numbered result without an item. Attached to B28 (Lemma 8.4.11; Corollary 8.4.12). If S3 splits B28, attach it to the Corollary 8.4.12 part. The first sentence is immediate from the definition of S_{P,Λ,t} (PDF173: types all of whose Jordan–Hölder constituents are generic). The second means that the cycles of non-generic σ in Corollary 8.4.12 are unconstrained and may be set to 0.

uses.how: Corollary 8.5.2 proof, PDF176: Z_σ(ρ̄) := 0 for non-generic σ, and (8.2) for (λ+η,τ) ∈ S_{P,Λ,t} with N_τ = 0 follows from Theorem 8.4.10(2) and Proposition 8.2.1.

items.name: Rees theorem: regular sequences detected by Ext
items.statement: For a commutative Noetherian R, a finite ModuleCat R object M, an ideal I with IM strictly smaller than M and n∈N, Ext^i_R(R/I,M)=0 for i<n iff an M-regular list of length n lies in I. The full TFAE also permits finite N with support V(I). Keep Small/universe shrink and the strict IM<M hypothesis.
items.locator: Mathlib/RingTheory/Depth/Rees.lean:158–191 at 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174; statement and surrounding binders freshly read

items.name: Projectivity detected by Ext in degree one
items.statement: In an abelian category with the indicated Ext universe, X is projective iff Ext^1(X,Y) vanishes for every Y. The equivalent predicate HasProjectiveDimensionLE X 0 and general Ext-vanishing predicate are already defined.
items.locator: Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Abelian/Projective/Dimension.lean:41–157 at 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174; statement and surrounding binders freshly read

items.name: Projective-dimension bounds along short exact sequences
items.statement: For a short exact X1→X2→X3 in an abelian category, the existing LT predicates give the three projective-dimension bounds. If X2 is projective, pd(X3)≤n+1 iff pd(X1)≤n, for n∈N. This is the one-step syzygy shift; it does not assert finite global dimension for an arbitrary ring.
items.locator: Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Abelian/Projective/Dimension.lean:183–227 at 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174; statement and surrounding binders freshly read

items.name: Finite flat modules over local rings are free
items.statement: For a commutative local R and finite R-module M, flatness of M implies freeness. Projective modules are flat by the pinned instance, so finite projective modules are free. No Noetherian hypothesis is required for this import.
items.locator: Mathlib/RingTheory/LocalRing/Module.lean and Mathlib/RingTheory/Flat/Basic.lean:304–308 and 227–231 at 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174; statement and surrounding binders freshly read

items.name: Exterior-power basis of a free module
items.statement: For a basis b of an R-module indexed by a linearly ordered type I over a commutative ring, the n-element finite subsets of I index a basis of the nth exterior power. Its vectors are the ordered wedges of b. No characteristic restriction is imposed.
items.locator: Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/ExteriorPower/Basis.lean:87–107 at 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174; statement and surrounding binders freshly read

items.name: Lifting from a projective object through an exact short complex
items.statement: In an abelian category, if S is exact and f:P→S.X2 satisfies S.g∘f=0 with P projective, there is a lift P→S.X1 composing with S.f to f. Exactness of a second source complex is not a hypothesis.
items.locator: Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/ShortComplex/Exact.lean:856–969 at 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174; statement and surrounding binders freshly read

items.name: Associated primes and zero divisors at the pin
items.statement: Over a commutative Noetherian ring the associated primes of a nonzero module form a nonempty set, and their union is the set of scalars killing a nonzero element. For a finite module this set of primes is finite. These supply the prime-avoidance step together with L94.
items.locator: Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/AssociatedPrime/Basic.lean and Finiteness.lean:220–241 and 158–166 at 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174; statement and surrounding binders freshly read

items.name: Nakayama vanishing for a finite submodule
items.statement: If a finitely generated submodule N satisfies N≤I N and I is contained in the Jacobson radical of zero, then N=0. Apply this to the kernel of a finite free presentation when xK=K and x belongs to the maximal ideal.
items.locator: Mathlib/RingTheory/Nakayama.lean:118–121 at 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174; statement and surrounding binders freshly read

items.name: Depth with its zero-module convention
items.statement: For an ideal I in R and finite M, use the existing R03.3 plan for depth_I(M)∈N∪{∞}: if IM≠M it is the supremum of lengths of M-regular lists in I; if IM=M it is ∞. Local depth uses I=m. In particular depth(0)=∞.
items.note: Exact refinement of existing depth-auslander-buchsbaum-and-dimension-bounds; reuse the pinned regular-list carrier. This is not a new depth implementation.
uses: Z107 bounds depth for nonzero finite modules
Z109 and Z115 require zero-module branches
api: depth_eq_top_of_smul_top: IM=M ⇒ depth_I(M)=∞
depth_ge_iff_regular_list: IM≠M ⇒ n≤depth_I(M) iff a regular list of length n lies in I, in the Noetherian setting
depth_congr: linear equivalence preserves depth
depth_local: depth(M)=depth_m(M)
depth_ext_iff: connect to L120 without redefining Ext
unitTests: For a field k and M=k, depth_(0)(k)=0
For any local R, depth_m(0)=∞, not zero
For R=k[[t]], depth_m(R)=1 and depth_m(k)=0
For I=R and finite M, depth_I(M)=∞

items.name: Depth is bounded by support dimension
items.statement: For a nonzero finite module over a Noetherian local ring, depth(M)≤dim Supp(M)≤dim R. Both depth and support dimension are finite here; the zero module is excluded.
proofSteps: Induct on the dimension of the support. In dimension zero the maximal ideal is associated, so it kills a nonzero element and no regular element lies in m.
For a nonempty regular list, quotient by its first element. Z129 drops support dimension by one; apply induction to the remaining list and take the supremum.

items.name: Depth is the first nonvanishing residue-field Ext
items.statement: For nonzero finite M over Noetherian local (R,m,κ), depth(M) is the least i with Ext^i_R(κ,M)≠0.
items.locator: Stacks00LW, Lemma10.72.5; pinned Rees theorem gives an alternative direct bridge
proofSteps: Nakayama gives mM≠M. Apply L120 with I=m: regular lists of length n exist exactly when all Ext degrees below n vanish.

Z107 bounds all such lengths, so their finite supremum e is attained; vanishing holds below e, whereas vanishing also at e would yield a list of length e+1. Thus Ext^e is nonzero. This avoids a circular use of the later depth-drop lemma.

items.name: The three depth inequalities
items.statement: For a short exact sequence 0→M1→M2→M3→0 of nonzero finite modules over Noetherian local R, depth M2≥min(depth M1,depth M3), depth M1≥min(depth M2,depth M3+1), and depth M3≥min(depth M2,depth M1−1), with the last integer lower bound interpreted without underflow.
proofSteps: Use the long exact sequence of Ext_R(κ,−). Below each indicated minimum the two groups adjacent to the relevant group vanish, forcing that group to vanish.
Translate through Z108. If a term is zero, use the induced isomorphism of the other terms separately; do not subtract from an infinity encoded as a natural number.

items.name: Depth drops by one along a regular element
items.statement: For nonzero finite M over Noetherian local R and x∈m regular on M, depth(M/xM)=depth(M)−1. Every M-regular list in m extends to length depth(M).
proofSteps: Nakayama makes M/xM nonzero. Apply Z109 to 0→M→M→M/xM→0 to get the lower bound.
Prepending x to every regular list on M/xM gives the reverse bound. Attainment from Z107 lets one extend a given list repeatedly, including the empty list.

items.name: Cohen–Macaulay and maximal Cohen–Macaulay modules
items.statement: Use the existing R03.3 CM plan: for nonzero finite M over Noetherian local R, CM means depth M=dim Supp M; maximal CM means depth M=dim R. Ring CM applies to R as a module. Keep zero modules separate in freeness and syzygy statements rather than imposing the finite-depth equality on them.
uses: Z112 parameter sequences on CM modules
Z114 freeness and Z115 syzygy depth
api: maximalCM_implies_CM: depth M=dim R ⇒ depth M=dim Supp M
CM_quotient_regular: quotient by a regular x∈m has depth and support dimension one less
regularLocal_is_CM: use Z104 and Z107
CM_congr: linear equivalence preserves the property
free_maximalCM: nonzero finite free module over CM local R is maximal CM
unitTests: Over k[[x,y]], R is maximal CM of depth2
The R-module R/(x) is CM of depth1 but not maximal CM
A field as its own module is maximal CM of depth0
The zero module takes the separate trivial branch, not a claimed finite-depth equality

items.name: Dimension-cutting parameters on a Cohen–Macaulay module are regular
items.statement: For nonzero finite CM M of support dimension d over Noetherian local R, if g1,…,gc∈m and dim Supp(M/(g1,…,gc)M)=d−c with c≤d, then the list is M-regular and extends to length d.
items.locator: Stacks00N6 Proposition10.103.4, with 00N5 and 00N4 inner proofs read
proofSteps: The principal dimension bound forces every intermediate support cut to drop dimension by exactly one.

For one cut, use the good-element induction of 00N4/00N5: in dimension1 the kernel has finite length and a regular parameter acts injectively, hence surjectively on it, so Nakayama kills it. In higher dimension prime avoidance supplies a simultaneous good parameter h; reduce modulo h, apply induction, and permute the regular pair.

Iterate on successive quotients and extend using Z110. Z129 supplies the support cuts, Z130 the finite-length kernel, and L128 the pair permutation. No new versions of those library carriers are planned.

items.name: Freeness lifts across a module-regular element
items.statement: Let R be Noetherian local, x∈m, and M finite with x injective on M. If M/xM is free over R/xR, then M is free over R. Regularity of x on R is not required.
items.locator: Mathlib/RingTheory/Regular/Free.lean:35–69 at 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174; entire statement and proof read; specializes Stacks00NS
proofSteps: Lift a finite basis modulo x. Nakayama shows the resulting map R^r→M is surjective.
Its kernel K is finite. Any relation a reduces to zero modulo x, so a=xb. Injectivity of x on M implies b is a relation. Hence K=xK, and L127 gives K=0.
items.note: Already at the pin with the more general finite-presentation/Jacobson-radical hypotheses. No new freeness-lifting theorem is planned; the Noetherian local specialization remains under its source ID.

items.name: Maximal Cohen–Macaulay modules over a regular local ring are free
items.statement: A nonzero finite M with depth(M)=dim R over a Noetherian regular local R is free; the zero module is free separately.
proofSteps: Induct on d=dim R. If d=0, R is a field. Otherwise take the first element x of a regular system of parameters.

The system is a system of parameters on M: the final quotient is finite-dimensional over κ and nonzero by Nakayama, and Z107 forces dim Supp M=d. Z112 makes x regular on M. Z103 makes R/xR regular local; Z110 gives the quotient maximal CM of dimension d−1.
Apply induction to M/xM and lift freeness by Z113.

items.name: Syzygy depth over a Cohen–Macaulay local ring
items.statement: Over a Noetherian CM local R of dimension d, a nonzero finite M of depth e admits a finite free partial resolution whose (d−e)th syzygy is either zero or maximal CM. When e=d take that syzygy to be M and use no free terms.
items.locator: Stacks00NE and 00NG, with explicit zero-syzygy convention
proofSteps: Choose finite free surjections successively; Noetherianity makes every kernel finite. If 0→K→F→M→0 has all terms nonzero, Z109 gives depth K≥min(d,depth M+1).

If a kernel vanishes, terminate with a shorter free resolution. Otherwise depth rises until d by at most d−e steps; once it reaches d it remains there. Zero M is resolved trivially outside the finite-e formula.

items.name: Finite free resolution length over a regular local ring
items.statement: For regular local R of dimension d and nonzero finite M of depth e, M has a finite free resolution of length at most d−e. The zero module has the zero resolution.
proofSteps: Z104 and Z107 show R is CM. Use Z115 and then Z114 on the final nonzero syzygy; if it vanishes, keep the shorter resolution.
For e=d this says M is already free. The natural-number subtraction d−e is justified by Z107, never applied to depth(0)=∞.

items.name: Projective-dimension bounds survive well-ordered extensions
items.statement: Let M be the union of submodules M_e well-ordered by inclusion. If every M_e/(union of M_f for f<e) has projective dimension at most n, then pd M≤n. No finiteness or Noetherian hypothesis on the ring is required.
proofSteps: For n=0 split each successive quotient. The direct sum of these projectives maps bijectively to M: largest nonzero support proves injectivity, and transfinite induction proves surjectivity.

For n>0 use the free module on the underlying set of each M_e and its kernel. Transition maps are inclusions. Quotienting by the earlier union gives an exact sequence with free middle term; L122 lowers each kernel-quotient bound to n−1.

Apply induction to the kernel union and L122 once more. L129 supplies direct-sum projectivity. Exactness of the unions is elementwise: each finite-support relation belongs to one stage, where its preimage or kernel witness exists. A quotient of free modules on nested underlying sets is free on the set difference. This does not claim arbitrary filtered colimits preserve projectivity.

items.name: Cyclic modules detect the global-dimension bound
items.statement: For a ring R and n≥0, the following are equivalent: every R-module has pd≤n; every finite R-module has pd≤n; every cyclic R/I has pd≤n (left ideals in the noncommutative version).
proofSteps: The forward implications are restrictions. Conversely well-order a generating set of M and filter by initial segments. Each successive quotient is cyclic or zero. Apply Z117.
Thus the finite-module result Z116 implies the all-module result Z100; this passage does not follow solely by writing M as a filtered union.

items.name: Finite free resolutions from finite projective dimension
items.statement: A finite module M over a commutative Noetherian local R with pd M≤n admits a resolution 0→F_n→…→F_0→M→0 with all F_i finite free.
items.locator: Stacks0CXF,0CXE,0CXC,00LP; finite-resolution specialization of the existing P7 perfect-complex plan
proofSteps: For n=0 use projectivity and L123. For n>0 choose n finite free surjections; their kernels stay finite by Noetherianity.
Iterating L122 makes the nth syzygy projective; L123 makes it free. The n=1 kernel is ker(F0→M); for n≥2 it is ker(F_(n−1)→F_(n−2)).

items.name: Minimal finite free complexes over a local ring
items.statement: Import the existing P7 minimal-complex plan: a finite free complex over local (R,m,κ) is minimal when each differential has image in m times the next term, equivalently all differentials after tensoring with κ vanish. For a minimal resolution of nonzero M, the largest nonzero term detects pd M.
uses: Z125 compares cotangent and resolution ranks
Z128 controls the top minor ideal
api: minimal_iff_residue_differential_zero: equivalent tests
split_contractible_unit: remove an adjacent R→R identity summand
minimal_resolution_top: nonzero F_n and vanishing above n imply pd M=n
minimal_F0_residue: F0/mF0≅M/mM
minimal_invariant_basis: changing finite free bases preserves minimality
unitTests: The complex R --1→ R splits off entirely and is not minimal
Over a DVR, R --π→ R is a minimal length1 resolution of κ
A module free in degree0 gives a minimal length0 resolution
The zero complex has no largest nonzero term; do not assign pd0=0 from that rule

items.name: Split off an invertible differential coefficient
items.statement: A finite free complex containing a unit matrix coefficient in one differential splits as an identity complex R→R and a complex with both adjacent ranks decreased by one. Repetition over a local ring yields a minimal complex without changing homology.
items.locator: Stacks00MT, Lemma10.102.2; existing P7 minimal-complex node
proofSteps: Use invertible row and column operations to make the coefficient a 1 with every other entry in its row and column zero.

The identities d²=0 force the incoming and outgoing maps to have zero components at the isolated coordinates. Split the two-term identity summand. The sum of finite ranks decreases by two, so repetition terminates.

items.name: Finite Koszul complex used by the residue-field comparison
items.statement: For a finite list x1,…,xn in a commutative R, use the shared finite Koszul precursor to DD.1: K_i=exterior^i R^n, with differential deleting the ath basis vector with coefficient (−1)^(a+1)x_ja in one-based indexing. H0=R/(x1,…,xn). No regular-sequence hypothesis is required to construct K or identify H0.
items.locator: Stacks00OA displayed complex; shared Koszul model of DerivedDeRhamCohomology:DD.1
items.note: Import the finite algebraic precursor only. Do not put derived completion, animation or the whole DD.1 layer ahead of R03.3. Prismatic, A_inf, derived-de Rham and local-cohomology uses must share this complex; quadratic-algebra Koszul duality is a different notion.
uses: Z123 needs a projective source complex, not an exact one
api: koszul_d_basis: alternating deletion formula
koszul_d_squared: pairwise cancellation gives zero over every commutative ring
koszul_H0: cokernel of d1 is the quotient by the list ideal
koszul_baseChange: termwise tensor transport with list images
koszul_nil: empty list gives R in degree0
koszul_regular_resolution: acyclicity is a separate theorem requiring regularity
unitTests: For the empty list, H0=R and positive terms vanish
For list[0] over nonzero R, d1=0 and H1=R, so K is not a resolution of H0
For list[a,b], d2(e1∧e2)=a e2−b e1 and d1d2=0
The same two-element identity holds in characteristic2 with the signs interpreted in R

items.name: Comparison from a projective complex into a resolution
items.statement: For a nonnegative augmented complex K of projective R-modules, a resolution F→N, and an augmentation-compatible module map M→N, construct a chain map K→F lifting it. K→M need not be exact. Two such lifts are chain homotopic.
items.locator: Stacks00LS, Lemma10.71.4, free-module version; projective extension uses pinned L125
proofSteps: Lift K0→N through F0→N. Inductively the desired map K_i→F_(i−1) lies in the differential kernel; exactness of F and L125 supply its lift to F_i.
For uniqueness subtract the two maps. Lift the difference in degree0 through d1, then subtract the previous homotopy correction at each degree and repeat. Source exactness is nowhere used.
The pinned ProjectiveResolution.lift requires both arguments to be resolutions, so that stronger bundled input cannot be applied directly to a possibly nonexact Koszul complex.

items.name: Characteristic-free injection of the alternating deletion map
items.statement: For a field κ, an ordered basis e1,…,en of V and 1≤i≤n, δ_i:exterior^i V→exterior^(i−1)V tensor V, e_J↦Σ_a(−1)^(a+1)e_(J minus ja) tensor e_ja, is injective, including when char κ divides i.
items.locator: Stacks00OA final linear-algebra check, expanded here by a basis-coordinate left inverse
proofSteps: Define a linear retraction on basis pairs (S,j): send e_S tensor e_j to e_(j followed by S) if j is strictly smaller than every member of S, and to zero otherwise. For empty S the condition is vacuous.
For an ordered nonempty J exactly its least-element deletion survives, with coefficient +1. Hence retraction∘δ_i=id over any commutative coefficient ring.
Do not use the wedge composite as the retraction: it is a signed multiple i of the identity and may vanish in characteristic dividing i.

items.name: Embedding dimension is bounded by residue-field projective dimension
items.statement: For Noetherian local (R,m,κ), dim_κ(m/m²)≤pd_R κ. The infinite-pd case is immediate; the finite-pd case works in every residue characteristic.
proofSteps: Lift a basis of m/m² to minimal generators x. Build K(x) and a minimal finite free resolution F of κ. Z123 gives K→F inducing id_κ.

Induct on i that K_i⊗κ→F_i⊗κ is injective. Degree0 follows from the augmentation. All differentials land in m, so modulo m² the comparison square has top map δ_i after identifying the x classes with the cotangent basis.

Z124 makes the top map injective; the right vertical map stays injective after tensoring over κ. Thus the left map is injective. In degree n=dim m/m² the exterior source is nonzero, forcing F_n≠0 and pdκ≥n.

items.name: Determinantal rank and the ideal of maximal nonzero minors
items.statement: For a map φ:R^a→R^b between finite free modules over a nonzero commutative ring, let r be the largest size of a nonzero minor and I(φ) the ideal of r-minors. Include r=0 with the empty minor1, hence I(0)=R. This is the exterior-power rank of Stacks00MV; it is not assumed constant under base change.
uses: Z127 needs rank preservation before localizing I(φ)
Z128 needs I(φ_n) proper for a nonzero top term
api: minorIdeal_basisChange: invertible changes of bases preserve the ideal of each fixed-size minor
rank_baseChange_le: rank can drop after a ring map
fixedMinorIdeal_baseChange: fixed-size minor ideals commute with base change
maximalMinor_baseChange: require the same rank before identifying I(φ) after base change
splitExact_rank: ranks are alternating sums of term ranks and I(φ)=R
unitTests: For φ=[t] over k[t], rank1 and I=(t), but after t↦0 rank0 and I=R
For an identity block of size r, the r-minor ideal is R
For the zero matrix, rank0 and the empty-minor ideal is R
A unit row or column operation changes individual minors but preserves their generated ideal

items.name: Necessary determinantal depth bounds for a finite free resolution
items.statement: For an exact finite free complex 0→R^n_e→…→R^n_0 over Noetherian local R, the rank of φ_i equals r_i=Σ_(j=i)^e(−1)^(j−i)n_j, and for each i≥1 its ideal of r_i-minors is either R or contains an R-regular sequence of length i.
items.locator: Stacks00N1, Proposition10.102.9, necessary direction; inner00MY,00MW,00MZ,0311 read
proofSteps: Remove unit summands. Localize at associated primes: there the maximal ideal kills a nonzero element. Exactness of the highest nonzero differential forces a unit coefficient; repeatedly split. The resulting split complex has the alternating-sum ranks and unit maximal-minor ideals.

The map R→product_(q in Ass R) R_q is injective (0311), so these prescribed ranks hold over R too. Only then identify the localizations of I(φ_i). Prime avoidance provides a nonzerodivisor x in the product of these ideals.

Reduce modulo x. The homology sequence leaves exactness in degrees≥2; remove degree0 and induct on the length. For i≥2 the inductive rank formula on the shortened complex is still r_i, so its maximal-minor ideal equals the image of the fixed r_i-minor ideal. Lift the regular list of length i−1 and prepend x. For i=1, x alone suffices. If the original positive-degree complex is zero the assertion is vacuous; otherwise minimality makes the product ideal proper, so x lies in m.
Only this necessary direction is used for Z128. The converse Buchsbaum–Eisenbud criterion was read but is not asserted as a closed supplier here.

items.name: Finite residue-field projective dimension is bounded by Krull dimension
items.statement: For a Noetherian local R with finite pd_R κ=n, one has n≤dim R.
proofSteps: If n=0 the inequality is immediate. Otherwise choose a minimal finite free resolution of κ of length n with F_n nonzero.
Z127 gives rank φ_n=rank F_n>0. Every coefficient of φ_n lies in m, so its positive-size minor ideal lies in m and is proper. It contains a regular sequence of length n.
Therefore depth R≥n by Z106, and Z107 bounds this by dim R.

items.name: Permutation of regular sequences on a Noetherian local module
items.statement: For a module M over a commutative local R with IsNoetherian R M, every permutation of an M-regular list remains M-regular. A weakly regular list needs the separate containment-in-maximal-ideal hypothesis.
items.locator: Mathlib/RingTheory/Regular/RegularSequence.lean:645–669 at 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174; statement and surrounding binders freshly read

items.name: Direct sums of projective modules are projective
items.statement: Over a semiring R and any index type, a direct sum of R-modules is projective iff every summand is projective. The arbitrary index universe is already supported by the pinned declaration.
items.locator: Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Projective.lean:290–303 at 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174; statement and surrounding binders freshly read

items.name: Support and quotient support of a finite module
items.statement: For a finite module M over a commutative ring, its support is V(Ann M), and Supp(M/IM)=Supp(M)∩V(I). The principal QuotSMulTop specialization is also present.
items.locator: Mathlib/RingTheory/Support.lean:217–220 and 249–283 at 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174; statement and surrounding binders freshly read

items.name: Support dimension under a principal cut
items.statement: For nonzero finite M over Noetherian local R and x∈m, dim Supp(M/xM)≤dim Supp M≤dim Supp(M/xM)+1. If x avoids every minimal prime of Supp M, in particular if x is M-regular, the second inequality is an equality.
items.locator: Stacks0B52 with00L3 and00KW, full statements and proofs read
proofSteps: L130 identifies the quotient support with the principal cut. For each irreducible component V(p), lift a system of parameters from (R/p)/(x); adding x gives an ideal of definition in R/p, so the parameter-number bound gives the inequality. Take the maximum over the finitely many components.

If x avoids the minimal primes, each prime chain in the cut can be extended strictly downward by a minimal prime of Supp M. Combine the inequalities. The ideal-of-definition characterization of dimension is the parameter-chain argument already recorded in Z64; this does not use Z107.

items.name: Finite length for a module supported only at the closed point
items.statement: A finite module M over Noetherian local R with Supp M⊆{m} has finite length, including M=0.
items.locator: Source step in Stacks00N4; explicit derivation from pinned support, zero-dimensional Artinian and finite-length inputs
proofSteps: For M≠0, L130 identifies Spec(R/Ann M) with the nonempty support {m}; hence R/Ann M is Noetherian and zero-dimensional.

L92 makes this quotient Artinian. M is finite over it, so L99 gives finite length. Submodules and composition factors are the same whether scalars are R or its annihilator quotient. The zero module has length zero.
