A79/A81 specify the regular-algebraic normalization t_i=(m_i+b_i−n−1)/2 and its integral cyclotomic polynomial conversion. A80 imports the already planned polarized cuspidal realization theorem at AG2.2.

Reuse the pure automorphic base-change and GL residual-spectrum owners. Labesse5.3 supplies the compact-unitary branch with [F+:Q]>1 and split-place comparison; Speh classification remains ET.7a, not a new patching or Galois roadmap. Exact Galois realization and twist comparison stay in AG2.2.

Add the GL_n-specific Whittaker integral, mirabolic injectivity and finite-place tensor restriction to the existing automorphic-function/cusp-form direction. AF.3 owns the global construction and cuspidality argument; AF.2 owns restricted tensor products and the one-place restriction adapter. Import AL.0 Fourier uniqueness, AA.2 quotient measures and the existing SR.5 local functional carrier. This is a source refinement, not a claim that the current AF.3 text already explicitly states global genericity for GL_n, and not a genericity claim for every reductive group. AF.5 identifies algebraic modular forms on compact-at-infinity groups with coefficient functions on finite adelic double cosets; A74 is its refinement by a smooth K-type factor at p (the sigma(lambda,tau)^* coefficients of LLHLM23 AppendixA). Continuation cc-d67081: AF.1 added to the stage list because A106 records that the Whittaker integral is continuous for the smooth moderate-growth Fréchet topology that AF.1 constructs, and A107 is the one-place grouping of the restricted tensor product AF.2 already owns, kept explicitly abstract as Cogdell states it.

The determinant-twist identity belongs to the shared local Whittaker-functional API, whose classical complex comparison is already requested by AL.3. It is an elementary identity of the N-action over characteristic zero, not a new integral co-Whittaker theorem, not an invocation of Helm in coefficient characteristic p, and not an automorphic construction.

AL.0 owns Schwartz–Bruhat spaces, self-duality of the local additive groups, the restricted tensor-product adelic space, Fourier inversion and adelic Poisson summation. A104 is the specialisation those already imply and that the Whittaker theory consumes: the characters of the COMPACT quotient F\A are indexed by F, so a continuous function on it with all Fourier coefficients zero vanishes. Route 20's reason already named 'AL.0 Fourier uniqueness' as an import; this route supplies the item that name referred to. Only the uniqueness half is asked for, not pointwise convergence.

AA.2 states in terms that it will 'construct invariant quotient measures by Weil's integral formula and prove their independence of measurable fundamental-domain choices'. A105 is the specialisation to unipotent radicals: the quotient is compact so the invariant measure normalises to a probability measure, and the normalisations along a filtration with abelian successive quotients agree, which is what licenses the iterated integration of A67 and A68. Route 20's reason already named 'AA.2 quotient measures' as an import; this route supplies that item. The unimodularity hypothesis is recorded, since the Borel gives no invariant quotient measure.

The existing R09.1 description includes Hilbert polynomials in the Noetherian setting, and its reviewed AUDIT-01 row explicitly assigns the missing graded-module Hilbert–Serre theorem here. These items give the finite-length coefficient specialization and monomial-rank bridge needed by SF.4’s local Hilbert–Samuel proof. Plan once here and import into SF.4; retain the full Noetherian/coherent-sheaf scope for R09.1’s other consumers. This source addition neither duplicates the library rational-series formula nor creates a private local Hilbert-polynomial owner.

sourceIssues.printed: traces of powers of generators of G uniquely characterize V
sourceIssues.correction: Use all group elements (and only claim semisimplification without a semisimplicity hypothesis); powers of a chosen generating set are insufficient.
sourceIssues.reason: Over C let G=C2*C2=<s,t|s²=t²=1>. Put rho_a(s)=diag(1,−1) and rho_a(t)=[[a,1],[1−a²,−a]] for a=0,2. Both matrices are involutions with eigenvalues1,−1. Both representations are irreducible: the only s-invariant lines are the coordinate axes, and neither is t-invariant since both off-diagonal entries are nonzero. sourceIssues.printed: would have dimension n!
sourceIssues.correction: Do not assert dimension n! for all irreducible admissible archimedean representations. A dimension theorem needs a restricted representation class and an exact algebraic Whittaker convention. For this application use the continuous functional constructed by the integral; no algebraic dimension count is needed.
sourceIssues.reason: Take the one-dimensional trivial irreducible admissible representation of GL_2(R). On its Harish–Chandra module the positive-root Lie algebra acts by zero. For ψ(x)=exp(2πix), an algebraic Whittaker functional λ would satisfy 0=λ(dπ(E12)v)=dψ(E12)λ(v)=2πiλ(v), so λ=0. Thus the dimension is zero, not 2!=2. The group-equivariant version likewise vanishes since ψ is nontrivial. This disproves the unqualified generality; it does not dispute a theorem for an appropriately restricted generic/principal-series class.

sourceIssues.locator: Proposition B.0.2(2) proof, PDF206 (page image checked); components of the special fibre listed on PDF206
sourceIssues.printed: Next we show that U(z̃, λ, ∇_{(a,b,0)})^nm is O-flat. For this, we first observe that U(z̃, λ, ∇_{(a,b,0)})^nm is topologically flat over O. … Finally, since U(z̃, λ, ∇_{(a,b,0)})^nm is O-flat with reduced special fiber, U(z̃, λ, ∇_{(a,b,0)})^nm is normal [69, Proposition 8.2].
sourceIssues.correction: Supply two missing checks. Write U = U(z̃,λ,∇_{(a,b,0)}) and U^nm for its partial normalization. (a) Topological flatness. By the identification O(U(z̃,λ,∇)^nm) = O(U(z̃,λ,∇))[−t d21/c22] stated on PDF204, the element W is integral over the chart, with unit leading coefficient (a−1)(b−1)(a−b). Since O(U(z̃,λ,∇))[1/t] is a regular domain (proof of Proposition B.0.1), W lies in it, so U^nm[1/p] ≅ U[1/p]. Let Z be the closure of the generic fibre in U^nm. Z is O-flat and finite over U, and it maps onto U because U is O-flat (part (1)). Z_F is equidimensional of dimension 3 and dominates each of the seven components of U_F. The seven components of U^nm_F listed on PDF206 all have dimension 3 = dim U_F, and by Table 1 each is the only top-dimensional component over its image. So Z_F contains all of them, and Z_F = U^nm_F as sets. (b) Normal generic fibre, which the criterion of [69] also needs: U^nm[1/p] ≅ U[1/p] is the fibre over (−p,a,b) of U(z̃,λ,∇)|_{X^0×V}. That scheme is open in (P_λ\GL_n) × X^0 × A^2 by Proposition 3.3.4 (U19), the input already used in the proof of Proposition B.0.1, so the fibre is smooth over E.
sourceIssues.reason: Topological flatness is not formal here. U^nm → U is an isomorphism only where c22 ≠ 0, and four of the seven components of U^nm_F listed on PDF206 lie in V(c22): (c22, …), (d31, c22, d21, W), (c22, d21, c12, …) and (c22, c13, c12, …). The O-flatness step (a ϖ-power-torsion function would be nilpotent) rests on it. A scheme that is flat over O with reduced special fibre is normal only if its generic fibre is normal, and the proof never checks this. mathlib:HenselianRing.is_henselian.statement:
class HenselianRing (R : Type*) [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) : Prop where
  jac : I ≤ Ideal.jacobson ⊥
  is_henselian :
    ∀ (f : R[X]) (_ : f.Monic) (a₀ : R) (_ : f.eval a₀ ∈ I)
      (_ : IsUnit (Ideal.Quotient.mk I (f.derivative.eval a₀))), ∃ a : R, f.IsRoot a ∧ a - a₀ ∈ I

mathlib:LinearMap.BilinForm.dualSubmodul.statement:
def dualSubmodule (N : Submodule R M) : Submodule R M where
  carrier := { x | ∀ y ∈ N, B x y ∈ (1 : Submodule R S) }
  add_mem' {a b} ha hb y hy := by simpa using add_mem (ha y hy) (hb y hy)
  zero_mem' y _ := by rw [B.zero_left]; exact zero_mem _
  smul_mem' r a ha y hy := by
    convert! (1 : Submodule R S).smul_mem r (ha y hy)
    rw [← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_smul S r a]
    simp only [algebraMap_smul, map_smul_of_tower, LinearMap.smul_apply]

lemma dualSubmodule_span_of_basis {ι} [Finite ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (hB : B.Nondegenerate) (b : Basis ι S M) :
    B.dualSubmodule (Submodule.span R (Set.range b)) =
      Submodule.span R (Set.range <| B.dualBasis hB b) := by
  cases nonempty_fintype ι

lemma dualSubmodule_dualSubmodule_flip_of_basis {ι : Type*} [Finite ι]
    (hB : B.Nondegenerate) (b : Basis ι S M) :
    B.dualSubmodule (B.flip.dualSubmodule (Submodule.span R (Set.range b))) =
      Submodule.span R (Set.range b) := by
  classical

lemma dualSubmodule_flip_dualSubmodule_of_basis {ι : Type*} [Finite ι]
    (hB : B.Nondegenerate) (b : Basis ι S M) :
    B.flip.dualSubmodule (B.dualSubmodule (Submodule.span R (Set.range b))) =
      Submodule.span R (Set.range b) := by
  classical

mathlib:Module.free_of_flat_of_isLocalRi.statement:
theorem free_of_flat_of_isLocalRing [Module.Finite R P] [Flat R P] : Free R P :=
  let w := Free.chooseBasis k (k ⊗[R] P)
  have ⟨v, eq⟩ := (TensorProduct.mk_surjective R P k Quotient.mk_surjective).comp_left w
  .of_basis <| .mk (IsLocalRing.linearIndependent_of_flat _ (eq ▸ w.linearIndependent)) <| by
    exact (span_eq_top_of_tmul_eq_basis _ w <| congr_fun eq).ge

mathlib:IsLocalRing.linearCombination_bi.statement:
theorem IsLocalRing.linearCombination_bijective_of_flat [Module.Finite R M] [Flat R M] {ι : Type u}
    (v : ι → M) (h : Function.Bijective (linearCombination k (TensorProduct.mk R k M 1 ∘ v))) :
    Function.Bijective (linearCombination R v) := by
  use linearIndependent_of_flat _ h.1
  rw [← LinearMap.range_eq_top, range_linearCombination]
  refine span_eq_top_of_tmul_eq_basis _ (.mk h.1 ?_) fun _ ↦ ?_
  · simpa only [top_le_iff, ← range_linearCombination, LinearMap.range_eq_top] using h.2
  · simp

mathlib:IsHausdorff.of_isLocalRing.statement:
variable {R : Type*} [CommRing R] (I : Ideal R) (M : Type*) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
variable [IsNoetherianRing R] [Module.Finite R M]

lemma IsHausdorff.of_le_jacobson (h : I ≤ Ideal.jacobson ⊥) : IsHausdorff I M :=
  ⟨fun x hx ↦ (Ideal.iInf_pow_smul_eq_bot_of_le_jacobson I h).le (by simpa [SModEq.zero] using hx)⟩

theorem IsHausdorff.of_isLocalRing [IsLocalRing R] (h : I ≠ ⊤) : IsHausdorff I M :=
  of_le_jacobson I M ((le_maximalIdeal h).trans (maximalIdeal_le_jacobson _))

instance [IsLocalRing R] : IsHausdorff (maximalIdeal R) M :=
  .of_le_jacobson _ _ (maximalIdeal_le_jacobson _)

mathlib:IsPrecomplete.prec.statement:
theorem IsPrecomplete.prec (_ : IsPrecomplete I M) {f : ℕ → M} :
    (∀ {m n}, m ≤ n → f m ≡ f n [SMOD (I ^ m • ⊤ : Submodule R M)]) →
      ∃ L : M, ∀ n, f n ≡ L [SMOD (I ^ n • ⊤ : Submodule R M)] :=
  IsPrecomplete.prec' _

requests.statement: Let A be an Artinian commutative ring and N a finite N-graded module over A[X1,…,Xe], with every Xi of degree one. Put H_N(T)=Σ_n length_A(N_n)T^n. There is p∈Z[T] with H_N=p/(1−T)^e in Q[[T]], and the graded-piece lengths eventually agree with a rational polynomial. For e=0 the series is a polynomial and its eventual coefficient polynomial is zero. This is a finite-length specialization of R09.1’s general Noetherian graded Hilbert-polynomial supplier; no restriction on char(A) is imposed.

For a commutative ring A and e≥1 variables of degree one, the homogeneous degree-n piece of A[X1,…,Xe] is finite free on the monomials X^a with Σ_i a_i=n, a family of cardinality binom(n+e−1,e−1). With no variables the degree-zero piece is A and all positive pieces vanish.
